text_mt: Having spoken to Medhātithi with the words of the gods, / he took Medhātithi and went to Mount Mānasa.

sanskrit_iast:
sendrā devagaṇāḥ sarve munayaśca tapodhanāḥ |
sādhyā vidyādharā yakṣā gandharvāśca samāgatāḥ || 96 ||
meaning:
सेन्द्रा देवगणाः सर्वे मुनयश्च तपोधनाः |
साध्या विद्याधरा यक्षा गन्धर्वाश्च समागताः || 96 ||
text_mt: All the hosts of gods headed by Indra, and the sages rich in austerities, / the Sādhyas, Vidyādharas, Yakṣas, and Gandharvas assembled.

sanskrit_iast:
devāśca sarve devyaśca ye devānucarāstathā |
te sarve mānasaprasthaṃ yātāścānye ca jantavaḥ || 97 ||
meaning:
देवाश्च सर्वे देव्यश्च ये देवानुचरास्तथा |
ते सर्वे मानसप्रस्थं याताश्चान्ये च जन्तवः || 97 ||
text_mt: All the gods and goddesses, and likewise the attendants of the gods, / and other living beings—all went to the plateau of Mānasa.

sanskrit_iast:
atha bhūte samāje tu devānāṃ kamalāsanaḥ |
medhātithiṃ muniṃ vākyamidamāhātideśayan || 98 ||
meaning:
अथ भूते समाजे तु देवानां कमलासनः |
मेधातिथिं मुनिं वाक्यमिदमाहातिदेशयन् || 98 ||
text_mt: Then, when the assembly of the gods had gathered, the lotus-seated Brahmā / spoke these instructing words to the sage Medhātithi:

sanskrit_iast: brahmovāca
meaning: ब्रह्मोवाच

sanskrit_iast:
medhātithe vasiṣṭhāya putrīṃ te caritavratām |
dehi brāhmaṇe vidhinā samāje tridivaukasām || 99 ||
meaning:
मेधातिथे वसिष्ठाय पुत्रीं ते चरितव्रताम् |
देहि ब्राह्मणे विधिना समाजे त्रिदिवौकसाम् || 99 ||
text_mt: "Medhātithi, give your daughter, who has accomplished her vows, / to the brāhmaṇa Vasiṣṭha according to the sacred rite, in the assembly of the heaven-dwellers.

sanskrit_iast:
vadhūvaratvamanayoḥ pūrvaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ mayaiva hi |
hariṇāṃ cāpyanujñātaṃ karma caitat samañjasam || 100 ||
meaning:
वधूवरत्वमनयोः पूर्वं सृष्टं मयैव हि |
हरिणां चाप्यनुज्ञातं कर्म चैतत् समञ्जसम् || 100 ||
text_mt: Indeed, their status as bride and groom was created by me in the past; / and it has been approved by Hari; this act is entirely fitting."

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ kṛte tava kule bhaviṣyati mahadyaśaḥ |
hitaṃ ca sarvabhūtānāṃ dehi tvāṃ māṃ ciraṃ kṛthāḥ || 101 ||
meaning:
एवं कृते तव कुले भविष्यति महद्यशः |
हितं च सर्वभूतानां देहि त्वां मां चिरं कृथाः || 101 ||
text_mt: “When this is done, there will be great glory for your lineage, / and welfare for all beings. Give [her]! Do not delay!”

sanskrit_iast:
tato brahmavacaṃ śrutvā hyatipramodito muniḥ |
evamastviti covāca natvā tān surapuṅgavān || 102 ||
meaning:
ततो ब्रह्मवचं श्रुत्वा ह्यतिप्रमोदितो मुनिः |
एवमस्त्विति चोवाच नत्वा तान् सुरपुङ्गवान् || 102 ||
text_mt: Then, having heard Brahmā's word, the sage was exceedingly delighted; / and bowing to those foremost of gods, he said, “So be it.”

sanskrit_iast:
eṣā tu vacanāt putrīmādāyārundhatī muniḥ |
dhyānasthasya vasiṣṭhasya devaiḥ saha jagāma ha || 103 ||
meaning:
एषा तु वचनात् पुत्रीमादायारुन्धती मुनिः |
ध्यानस्थस्य वसिष्ठस्य देवैः सह जगाम ह || 103 ||
text_mt: At that word, taking his daughter Arundhatī, the sage / went together with the gods to Vasiṣṭha, who was absorbed in meditation.

sanskrit_iast:
gatvā vasiṣṭhanikaṭaṃ devaiḥ parivṛto muniḥ |
brāhmaśriyā dīpyamāna jvalantamiva pāvakam || 104 ||
meaning:
गत्वा वसिष्ठनिकटं देवैः परिवृतो मुनिः |
ब्राह्मश्रिया दीप्यमान ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम् || 104 ||
text_mt: Having approached Vasiṣṭha, surrounded by the gods, the sage / saw the sage seated in a cave of Mount Mānasa, / blazing with Brahmanic splendor like a flaming fire,

sanskrit_iast:
dharmārthakāmamokṣeṣu dhṛtabuddhi pṛthak pṛthak |
dadarśa munimāsīnaṃ mānasācalakandare || 105 ||
meaning:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षेषु धृतबुद्धि पृथक् पृथक् |
ददर्श मुनिमासीनं मानसाचलकन्दरे || 105 ||
text_mt: holding his intellect firmly and distinctly upon duty, wealth, pleasure, and liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
vasiṣṭhamojasvivara bālasūryamivoditam |
atha putrīmagragatā kṛtvā medhātithirmuniḥ |
vasiṣṭha niyatātmānamuvācārundhatīpitā || 106 ||
meaning:
वसिष्ठमोजस्विवर बालसूर्यमिवोदितम् |
अथ पुत्रीमग्रगता कृत्वा मेधातिथिर्मुनिः |
वसिष्ठ नियतात्मानमुवाचारुन्धतीपिता || 106 ||
text_mt: To Vasiṣṭha, the foremost of the radiant, like a newly risen morning sun, / placing his daughter before him, Medhātithi the sage, / the father of Arundhatī, addressed him who had restrained his self:

sanskrit_iast: ṛṣiruvāca
meaning: ऋषिरुवाच

sanskrit_iast:
bhagavan brahmaṇaḥ putra putrīṃ me caritavratām |
dattāṃ pratigṛhāṇaināṃ mayā brāhmeṇa dharmataḥ || 107 ||
meaning:
भगवन् ब्रह्मणः पुत्र पुत्रीं मे चरितव्रताम् |
दत्तां प्रतिगृहाणैनां मया ब्राह्मेण धर्मतः || 107 ||
text_mt: “O venerable son of Brahmā, accept my daughter, who has performed her vows, / given by me according to duty through the Brāhma rite.

sanskrit_iast:
yatra yatrāśrame brahman svecchayā nivasiṣyasi |
tvadbhaktyaiṣā bhavitrī cacchāyevānugatā tava || 108 ||
meaning:
यत्र यत्राश्रमे ब्रह्मन् स्वेच्छया निवसिष्यसि |
त्वद्भक्त्यैषा भवित्री चच्छायेवानुगता तव || 108 ||
text_mt: In whatever hermitage you will dwell at your will, O holy one, / through devotion to you she will be your follower like a shadow.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra tatraiva me putrī samānavratacāriṇī | pativratā varārohā śuśrūṣāṃ te kariṣyati ||
109 ||
meaning:
तत्र तत्रैव मे पुत्री समानव्रतचारिणी | पतिव्रता वरारोहा शुश्रूषां ते करिष्यति ||
109 ||
text_mt: Wherever [you are], my daughter, practicing the same vows, / a pativratā of beautiful hips, will render service to you.”

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
iti śrutvā vasiṣṭhastu munermedhātithervacaḥ |
dṛṣṭvā samāgatān devān brahmaviṣṇuśivādikān || 110 ||
meaning:
इति श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठस्तु मुनेर्मेधातिथेर्वचः |
दृष्ट्वा समागतान् देवान् ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवादिकान् || 110 ||
text_mt: Having heard these words of the sage Medhātithi, / and seeing the assembled gods headed by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva,

sanskrit_iast:
avaśyametadbhāvīti niścitya divyacakṣuṣā |
brahmaṇaḥ sammate putrīṃ tadā medhātithermuneḥ |
vasiṣṭhaḥ pratijagrāha vāḍhamityuktavāṃśca ha || 111 ||
meaning:
अवश्यमेतद्भावीति निश्चित्य दिव्यचक्षुषा |
ब्रह्मणः सम्मते पुत्रीं तदा मेधातिथेर्मुनेः |
वसिष्ठः प्रतिजग्राह वाढमित्युक्तवांश्च ह || 111 ||
text_mt: ascertaining with divine sight that this was destined to be, / Vasiṣṭha accepted the daughter of the sage Medhātithi / with the consent of Brahmā, and said, “So be it.”

sanskrit_iast:
gṛhītapāṇiḥ sā devī vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā |
patyuḥ pādayuge cakṣuryugaṃ nyastavatī satī || 112 ||
meaning:
गृहीतपाणिः सा देवी वसिष्ठेन महात्मना |
पत्युः पादयुगे चक्षुर्युगं न्यस्तवती सती || 112 ||
text_mt: Her hand taken by the high-souled Vasiṣṭha, the virtuous woman, / a satī, cast both her eyes upon her husband’s feet.

sanskrit_iast:
tato brahmā ca viṣṇuśca rudraścānye tathāmarāḥ |
vivāhavidhinā tau tu modayāñcakrurutsavaiḥ || 113 ||
meaning:
ततो ब्रह्मा च विष्णुश्च रुद्रश्चान्ये तथामराः |
विवाहविधिना तौ तु मोदयाञ्चक्रुरुत्सवैः || 113 ||
text_mt: Then Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, and the other immortals / delighted the two with festivities according to the marriage rite.

sanskrit_iast:
sāvitrīpramukhā devyo devāścendrādayastathā |
dakṣādyāḥ kaśyapādyāstu munayo'titapodhanāḥ || 114 ||
meaning:
सावित्रीप्रमुखा देव्यो देवाश्चेन्द्रादयस्तथा |
दक्षाद्याः कश्यपाद्यास्तु मुनयोऽतितपोधनाः || 114 ||
text_mt: Goddesses led by Sāvitrī, and gods led by Indra, / and the ascetics rich in penance headed by Dakṣa and Kaśyapa,

sanskrit_iast:
unmucya brahmavacanādvalkalañcājinaṃ jaṭāḥ |
mandākinījalenāśu snāpayitvā sutaṃ vidheḥ || 115 ||
meaning:
उन्मुच्य ब्रह्मवचनाद्वल्कलञ्चाजिनं जटाः |
मन्दाकिनीजलेनाशु स्नापयित्वा सुतं विधेः || 115 ||
text_mt: at Brahmā's word removed the bark garments, black antelope skin, and matted hair; / and quickly bathing the son of Vidhi with the water of the Mandākinī,

sanskrit_iast:
jāmbunadaistathā divyairbhūṣaṇaiśca manoharaiḥ |
vasiṣṭhaṃ bhūṣayāṃcakrustathaivārundhatīṃ satīm || 116 ||
meaning:
जाम्बुनदैस्तथा दिव्यैर्भूषणैश्च मनोहरैः |
वसिष्ठं भूषयांचक्रुस्तथैवारुन्धतीं सतीम् || 116 ||
text_mt: they adorned Vasiṣṭha with gold and divine, charming ornaments, / and likewise Arundhatī, the virtuous woman.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūṣayitvātha tau tatra samāpya munibhirvidhim |
vivāhāvabhṛthaṃ cakrustayorvidhiharīśvarāḥ || 117 ||
meaning:
भूषयित्वाथ तौ तत्र समाप्य मुनिभिर्विधिम् |
विवाहावभृथं चक्रुस्तयोर्विधिहरीश्वराः || 117 ||
text_mt: Then, having adorned the two there and concluded the rite with the sages, / Vidhi, Hari, and Īśvara performed the post-marital ablution for them.

sanskrit_iast:
nidhāya sarvatīrthānāṃ toyaṃ jāmbunade ghaṭe |
āśīrvādakarairmantrairgāyatryā drupadādibhiḥ || 118 ||
meaning:
निधाय सर्वतीर्थानां तोयं जाम्बुनदे घटे |
आशीर्वादकरैर्मन्त्रैर्गायत्र्या द्रुपदादिभिः || 118 ||
text_mt: Placing water from all sacred fords in a golden vessel, / with blessing mantras, the Gāyatrī, and the Drupadā and other [hymns],

sanskrit_iast:
svayaṃ tau snāpayāñcakrurbrahmāviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ |
tato maharṣayaścānye tathā devarṣayaśca ye || 119 ||
meaning:
स्वयं तौ स्नापयाञ्चक्रुर्ब्रह्माविष्णुमहेश्वराः |
ततो महर्षयश्चान्ये तथा देवर्षयश्च ये || 119 ||
text_mt: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara themselves bathed the two. / Then the other great sages and whatever divine sages [were present],

sanskrit_iast:
te sarve ṛgyajuḥsāmavedabhāgairmahāsvaraiḥ |
gaṅgādi saritāṃ toyaiścakruḥ śāntiṃ tayormuhuḥ || 120 ||
meaning:
ते सर्वे ऋग्यजुःसामवेदभागैर्महास्वरैः |
गङ्गादि सरितां तोयैश्चक्रुः शान्तिं तयोर्मुहुः || 120 ||
text_mt: all of them, with parts of the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma Vedas in loud voices, / repeatedly performed rites of appeasement for the two with waters of the Gaṅgā and other rivers.

sanskrit_iast:
bhuvanatrayasañcāri vimānaṃ sūryavarcasam |
avyāhatagatiṃ brahmā satoyañca kamaṇḍalum || 121 ||
meaning:
भुवनत्रयसञ्चारि विमानं सूर्यवर्चसम् |
अव्याहतगतिं ब्रह्मा सतोयञ्च कमण्डलुम् || 121 ||
text_mt: Brahmā gave [them] an aerial chariot of solar splendor, moving unobstructed / across the three worlds, and a water-pot filled with water.

sanskrit_iast:
tābhyāṃ dāyaṃ dadau viṣṇurduṣprāpaṃ sthānamuttamam |
yadūrdhvaṃ sarvadevānāṃ marīcyādeḥ samīpataḥ || 122 ||
meaning:
ताभ्यां दायं ददौ विष्णुर्दुष्प्रापं स्थानमुत्तमम् |
यदूर्ध्वं सर्वदेवानां मरीच्यादेः समीपतः || 122 ||
text_mt: Viṣṇu gave them as a dowry an supreme abode hard to attain, / which is above all the gods, in the vicinity of Marīci and the others.

sanskrit_iast:
saptakalpāntajīvitvaṃ rudraḥ prādāttayorvaram |
aditiḥ kuṇḍalayugaṃ brahmaṇā nirmitaṃ svakam |
dadau svakarṇādākṛṣya putryai medhātithestadā || 123 ||
meaning:
सप्तकल्पान्तजीवित्वं रुद्रः प्रादात्तयोर्वरम् |
अदितिः कुण्डलयुगं ब्रह्मणा निर्मितं स्वकम् |
ददौ स्वकर्णादाकृष्य पुत्र्यै मेधातिथेस्तदा || 123 ||
text_mt: Rudra granted them the boon of living until the end of seven kalpas. / Aditi then drew from her own ears her own pair of earrings, fashioned by Brahmā, / and gave it to Medhātithi's daughter.

sanskrit_iast:
pativratātvaṃ sāvitrī bahulā bahuputratām |
devendro bahuratnāni dhaneśena samaṃ dadau || 124 ||
meaning:
पतिव्रतात्वं सावित्री बहुला बहुपुत्रताम् |
देवेन्द्रो बहुरत्नानि धनेशेन समं ददौ || 124 ||
text_mt: Sāvitrī gave the status of a pativratā; Bahulā gave many sons; / and Devendra together with the lord of wealth gave many jewels.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ devāśca munayo devyaścānye ca ye sthitāḥ |
dadustatra yathāyogyaṃ dāyaṃ tābhyāṃ pṛthak pṛthak || 125 ||
meaning:
एवं देवाश्च मुनयो देव्यश्चान्ये च ये स्थिताः |
ददुस्तत्र यथायोग्यं दायं ताभ्यां पृथक् पृथक् || 125 ||
text_mt: Thus the gods, sages, goddesses, and whoever else were present / gave appropriate gifts to the two there, each individually.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ vivāhya vidhivat sauvarṇe mānasācale |
arundhatī vasiṣṭhastu modamāpa tayā saha || 126 ||
meaning:
एवं विवाह्य विधिवत् सौवर्णे मानसाचले |
अरुन्धती वसिष्ठस्तु मोदमाप तया सह || 126 ||
text_mt: Having thus married Arundhatī according to rule on the golden Mount Mānasa, / Vasiṣṭha experienced delight with her.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra yat patitaṃ goyaṃ mānasācalakandare |
vivāhāvabhṛthārthāya śāntyarthe ca surāhṛtam || 127 ||
meaning:
तत्र यत् पतितं गोयं मानसाचलकन्दरे |
विवाहावभृथार्थाय शान्त्यर्थे च सुराहृतम् || 127 ||
text_mt: The water brought by the gods for the post-marital ablution / and for the rite of appeasement that fell there into the cave of Mount Mānasa,

sanskrit_iast:
brahmaviṣṇumahādevapāṇibhiḥ samudīritam |
tattoyaṃ saptadhā bhūtvā patitaṃ mānasācalāt || 128 ||
meaning:
ब्रह्मविष्णुमहादेवपाणिभिः समुदीरितम् |
तत्तोयं सप्तधा भूत्वा पतितं मानसाचलात् || 128 ||
text_mt: poured forth by the hands of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Mahādeva— / that water divided into seven parts and fell from Mount Mānasa.

sanskrit_iast:
himādreḥ kandare sānau sarasyāñca pṛthak pṛthak |
tattoyaṃ patitaṃ śipre devabhogye sarovare || 129 ||
meaning:
हिमाद्रेः कन्दरे सानौ सरस्याञ्च पृथक् पृथक् |
तत्तोयं पतितं शिप्रे देवभोग्ये सरोवरे || 129 ||
text_mt: Separately into a cave, a ridge, and a lake of the snowy mountain [it fell]. / That water fell into the Śiprā, a lake enjoyed by the gods;

sanskrit_iast:
tena śiprānadījātā viṣṇunā preritā kṣitau |
mahākauṣī prapāte tu yadvāri patitaṃ tu vai || 130 ||
meaning:
तेन शिप्रानदीजाता विष्णुना प्रेरिता क्षितौ |
महाकौषी प्रपाते तु यद्वारि पतितं तु वै || 130 ||
text_mt: by that the Śiprā river was born, set in motion on earth by Viṣṇu. / But the water that fell at the cascade of the Mahākauṣī

sanskrit_iast:
kauṣikī nāma sā jātā viśvāmitrāvatāritā |
umā kṣetre yat patitaṃ toyaṃ tena mahānadī || 131 ||
meaning:
कौषिकी नाम सा जाता विश्वामित्रावतारिता |
उमा क्षेत्रे यत् पतितं तोयं तेन महानदी || 131 ||
text_mt: became the Kauṣikī by name, brought down by Viśvāmitra. / The water that fell in the domain of Umā became a great river;

sanskrit_iast:
kāverī nāma sā jātā kāverasarasaḥ sṛtā |
mahākāle saraḥśreṣṭhe patitaṃ tajjalaṃ gireḥ || 132 ||
meaning:
कावेरी नाम सा जाता कावेरसरसः सृता |
महाकाले सरःश्रेष्ठे पतितं तज्जलं गिरेः || 132 ||
text_mt: issuing from Lake Kāvera, it became known by the name Kāverī. / That mountain water which fell into Mahākāla, the foremost of lakes,

sanskrit_iast:
himādreḥ pārśvabhāge tu dakṣiṇe śaṃbhusannidhau |
gomatī nāma tairjātā nadī gomadudīritā || 133 ||
meaning:
हिमाद्रेः पार्श्वभागे तु दक्षिणे शंभुसन्निधौ |
गोमती नाम तैर्जाता नदी गोमदुदीरिता || 133 ||
text_mt: on the southern slope of the snowy mountain in the presence of Śambhu, / became the river named Gomatī, declared by them to bring herds of cattle.

sanskrit_iast:
maināko nāma yaḥ putraḥ śailarājasya tatsamaḥ |
tasmin sānau samutpanno menakodātaḥ purā || 134 ||
meaning:
मैनाको नाम यः पुत्रः शैलराजस्य तत्समः |
तस्मिन् सानौ समुत्पन्नो मेनकोदातः पुरा || 134 ||
text_mt: The peak of the king of mountains that equals him, named Maināka, / produced formerly from Menakā—

sanskrit_iast:
yattatra patitaṃ toyaṃ tena jātā mahānadī |
devikākhyā mahādevapreritā sāgaraṃ prati || 135 ||
meaning:
यत्तत्र पतितं तोयं तेन जाता महानदी |
देविकाख्या महादेवप्रेरिता सागरं प्रति || 135 ||
text_mt: the water that fell upon that [peak] became the great river / called Devikā, sent towards the ocean by Mahādeva.

sanskrit_iast:
yattoyaṃ saṃgataṃ daryāṃ haṃsāvatārasannidhau |
tenābhūt sarayūrnāmnā nadī puṇyatamā smṛtā || 136 ||
meaning:
यत्तोयं संगतं दर्यां हंसावतारसन्निधौ |
तेनाभूत् सरयूर्नाम्ना नदी पुण्यतमा स्मृता || 136 ||
text_mt: The water that gathered in a cave near the descent of the Haṃsa / became the river named Sarayū, remembered as most sacred.

sanskrit_iast:
yānyambhāṃsi mahākhāṇḍavāraṇyasannidhau |
himavatkandare yāmye irāyā hradamadhyataḥ || 137 ||
meaning:
यान्यम्भांसि महाखाण्डवारण्यसन्निधौ |
हिमवत्कन्दरे याम्ये इराया ह्रदमध्यतः || 137 ||
text_mt: Those waters which fell near the great Khāṇḍava forest, / in the southern cave of Himavat, from the middle of the pool of Irā,

sanskrit_iast:
irāvatīnāma nadī tairjātā ca saridvarā |
etāḥ sarvāḥ snānapānasevanairjāhnavī yathā || 138 ||
meaning:
इरावतीनाम नदी तैर्जाता च सरिद्वरा |
एताः सर्वाः स्नानपानसेवनैर्जाह्नवी यथा || 138 ||
text_mt: became through them the excellent river named Irāvatī. / All these [rivers], by bathing, drinking, and resorting [to them], just like the Jāhnavī,

sanskrit_iast:
phalaṃ dadati martyānāṃ dakṣiṇodadhigāḥ sadā |
dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ bījabhūtāḥ sanātanāḥ || 139 ||
meaning:
फलं ददति मर्त्यानां दक्षिणोदधिगाः सदा |
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां बीजभूताः सनातनाः || 139 ||
text_mt: give reward to mortals, flowing always to the southern ocean, / being the eternal seeds of duty, wealth, pleasure, and liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
mahānadyastu saptaitāḥ sarvadā devabhogadāḥ |
evaṃ nadyaḥ saptajātāḥ sadāpuṇyatamodakāḥ || 140 ||
meaning:
महानद्यस्तु सप्तैताः सर्वदा देवभोगदाः |
एवं नद्यः सप्तजाताः सदापुण्यतमोदकाः || 140 ||
text_mt: These seven great rivers grant always the enjoyment of the gods. / Thus the seven rivers were born, having ever most sacred waters,

sanskrit_iast: arundhatyā vasiṣṭhasya vivāhe devasannidhau || 141 ||
meaning: अरुन्धत्या वसिष्ठस्य विवाहे देवसन्निधौ || 141 ||
text_mt: at the marriage of Arundhatī and Vasiṣṭha in the presence of the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ vivāhya sa tadā vasiṣṭhastāmarundhatīm |
devairdattaṃ tadā sthānaṃ vimānena jagāma ha || 142 ||
meaning:
एवं विवाह्य स तदा वसिष्ठस्तामरुन्धतीम् |
देवैर्दत्तं तदा स्थानं विमानेन जगाम ह || 142 ||
text_mt: Having thus married that Arundhatī, Vasiṣṭha then / went by aerial chariot to the place given by the gods,

sanskrit_iast: brahmaviṣṇumaheśānāṃ vacanānmunisattamaḥ || 143 ||
meaning: ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेशानां वचनान्मुनिसत्तमः || 143 ||
text_mt: by the word of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśāna, the best of sages,

sanskrit_iast:
hitāya sarvajagatāṃ triṣu lokuṣu sarvadā |
yasmin yasmin yuge yādṛk strīṇāṃ bhavati tādṛśam || 144 ||
meaning:
हिताय सर्वजगतां त्रिषु लोकुषु सर्वदा |
यस्मिन् यस्मिन् युगे यादृक् स्त्रीणां भवति तादृशम् || 144 ||
text_mt: for the welfare of all the worlds across the three realms always, / such as women become in each successive age.

sanskrit_iast:
veśaṃ bhāvaṃ śarīraṃ ca kṛtvā dharme niyojanam |
vicaratyeṣa lokāṃstrīnapramattaḥ prasannadhīḥ || 145 ||
meaning:
वेशं भावं शरीरं च कृत्वा धर्मे नियोजनम् |
विचरत्येष लोकांस्त्रीनप्रमत्तः प्रसन्नधीः || 145 ||
text_mt: having assumed dress, disposition, and a body / suited to each respective age, and engaging them in dharma, / she wanders unconfused through the three worlds, her mind serene.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ purā vasiṣṭhena pariṇītā tvarundhatī |
sā hitārthāya jagatāṃ devānāṃ vacanāt purā || 146 ||
meaning:
एवं पुरा वसिष्ठेन परिणीता त्वरुन्धती |
सा हितार्थाय जगतां देवानां वचनात् पुरा || 146 ||
text_mt: In this way Arundhatī was formerly wed by Vasiṣṭha / long ago, at the command of the gods, for the welfare of the worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
ya idaṃ śṛṇuyānnityamākhyānaṃ dharmasādhanam |
sarvakalyāṇasaṃyuktaṃ cirāyurvittavān bhavet || 147 ||
meaning:
य इदं शृणुयान्नित्यमाख्यानं धर्मसाधनम् |
सर्वकल्याणसंयुक्तं चिरायुर्वित्तवान् भवेत् || 147 ||
text_mt: Whoever constantly hears this narrative, which accomplishes dharma / and brings all auspiciousness, will live long and possess wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
yā strī śṛṇoti satatamarundhatyāḥ kathā mimām |
pativratā sā bhūtveha paratra svargamāpnuyāt || 148 ||
meaning:
या स्त्री शृणोति सततमरुन्धत्याः कथा मिमाम् |
पतिव्रता सा भूत्वेह परत्र स्वर्गमाप्नुयात् || 148 ||
text_mt: Any woman who constantly hears this tale of Arundhatī / becomes a pativratā in this world and attains heaven in the next.

sanskrit_iast:
idaṃ paraṃ svastyayanamidaṃ dharmapradaṃ param |
ākhyānaṃ sarvadā kīrtiryaśaḥ puṇyavivardhanam || 149 ||
meaning:
इदं परं स्वस्त्ययनमिदं धर्मप्रदं परम् |
आख्यानं सर्वदा कीर्तिर्यशः पुण्यविवर्धनम् || 149 ||
text_mt: This is the supreme blessing, this is the supreme giver of dharma; / this narrative ever increases renown, fame, and merit.

sanskrit_iast:
vivāhe puṃsi yātrāyāṃ yaḥ śrāddhe śrāvayettathā |
sthairyaṃ puṃsavanaṃ siddhiḥ pitṛprītiścajāyate || 150 ||
meaning:
विवाहे पुंसि यात्रायां यः श्राद्धे श्रावयेत्तथा |
स्थैर्यं पुंसवनं सिद्धिः पितृप्रीतिश्चजायते || 150 ||
text_mt: One who recites it at a wedding, on [begetting] a male child, on a journey, or at a śrāddha / gains stability, the birth of a son, success, and the pleasure of the ancestors.

sanskrit_iast:
iti vaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ |
arundhatī yathābhūtā bhāryā vāpi pativratā || 151 ||
meaning:
इति वः कथितं सर्वं वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः |
अरुन्धती यथाभूता भार्या वापि पतिव्रता || 151 ||
text_mt: Thus all has been related to you: / how Arundhatī became the wife and pativratā of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha,

sanskrit_iast:
yasya vā tanayā jātā yathotpannā ca yatra ca |
yathā brahmaharīśānāṃ vacanāt sa vṛtaḥ patiḥ || 152 ||
meaning:
यस्य वा तनया जाता यथोत्पन्ना च यत्र च |
यथा ब्रह्महरीशानां वचनात् स वृतः पतिः || 152 ||
text_mt: whose daughter she was born to be, and how and where she was born, / and how he was chosen as her husband at the word of Brahmā, Hari, and Īśāna.

sanskrit_iast:
etat vaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ guhyādguhyataraṃ param |
puṇyadaṃ pāpaharaṇamāyurārogyavardhanam || 153 ||
meaning:
एतत् वः सर्वमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं परम् |
पुण्यदं पापहरणमायुरारोग्यवर्धनम् || 153 ||
text_mt: All this, supreme and more secret than the secret, / bestowing merit, removing sin, and increasing life and health, has been told to you.

sanskrit_iast:
iti vipulavṛṣaudhakṣemakārītihāsaṃ sadasi sakṛdapīha śrāvayedyo dvijānām |
sa bhavati kaluṣaurghairhīnadehaḥ sameto munivarasahacaryāṃ pretya gīrvāṇa eva || 154 ||
meaning:
इति विपुलवृषौधक्षेमकारीतिहासं सदसि सकृदपीह श्रावयेद्यो द्विजानाम् |
स भवति कलुषौर्घैर्हीनदेहः समेतो मुनिवरसहचर्यां प्रेत्य गीर्वाण एव || 154 ||
text_mt: Whoever recites this history, which bestows extensive righteousness and prosperity, even once in an assembly of twice-born men, / becomes free in body from streams of defilement and, after death, attends upon the best of sages as a god.

sanskrit_iast:
iti śrīkālikāpurāṇe vasiṣṭhārundhatīvivāhe trayoviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ || 23 ||
caturviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
इति श्रीकालिकापुराणे वसिष्ठारुन्धतीविवाहे त्रयोविंशोऽध्यायः || 23 ||
चतुर्विंशोऽध्यायः
text_mt:
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, on the marriage of Vasiṣṭha and Arundhatī, in the glorious Kālikāpurāṇa.
Chapter Twenty-Four

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
tato himavataḥ prasthe gireḥ śiprasarastīre |
upaviṣṭo mahādevastansaro'paśyadantike || 1 ||
meaning:
ततो हिमवतः प्रस्थे गिरेः शिप्रसरस्तीरे |
उपविष्टो महादेवस्तन्सरोऽपश्यदन्तिके || 1 ||
text_mt: Then Mahādeva, seated on a plateau of the Himavat mountain / on the shore of Lake Śipra, looked at that lake nearby.

sanskrit_iast:
punaḥ punaḥ preṣyamāṇo brahmaṇā hariṇā ca saḥ |
dhyānaṃ kartuṃ tatra manaḥ sthiraṃ kṛtvā dṛḍhātmavān || 2||
meaning:
पुनः पुनः प्रेष्यमाणो ब्रह्मणा हरिणा च सः |
ध्यानं कर्तुं तत्र मनः स्थिरं कृत्वा दृढात्मवान् || 2||
text_mt: Urged again and again by Brahmā and Hari, / he, firm of self, made his mind steady there to perform meditation.

sanskrit_iast:
ātmānamātmanā draṣṭumātmanyeva viśeṣataḥ |
paramaṃ yatnamakarod yānena smaraṇaśāsanaḥ || 3 ||
meaning:
आत्मानमात्मना द्रष्टुमात्मन्येव विशेषतः |
परमं यत्नमकरोद् यानेन स्मरणशासनः || 3 ||
text_mt: In order to see the Self by the Self, especially within the Self alone, / the subduer of Smara made the utmost effort through contemplation.

sanskrit_iast:
dhyāne praviṣṭacittantu taṃ dṛṣṭvā druhiṇādayaḥ |
hare praviṣṭāṃ māyākhyāṃ tuṣṭuvuryatamānasāḥ || 4 ||
meaning:
ध्याने प्रविष्टचित्तन्तु तं दृष्ट्वा द्रुहिणादयः |
हरे प्रविष्टां मायाख्यां तुष्टुवुर्यतमानसाः || 4 ||
text_mt: Seeing him with his mind absorbed in meditation, Druhiṇa and the others, / their minds restrained, praised [the goddess] called Māyā who had entered Hara:

sanskrit_iast:
māyayā mohito bhargaḥ satīśokākulo bhṛśam |
vilapatyeva tāṃ tasmin mohayatuṃ jagatprasūm || 5 ||
meaning:
मायया मोहितो भर्गः सतीशोकाकुलो भृशम् |
विलपत्येव तां तस्मिन् मोहयतुं जगत्प्रसूम् || 5 ||
text_mt: “Deluded by Māyā and greatly agitated by grief for Satī, / Bharga continually laments. In order to delude him into [remembering] the mother of the world,

sanskrit_iast:
stutvā śambhuśarīrāttu niḥsāryenāṃ nirākulām |
śambhucittaṃ kariṣyāmo dhyānāsaktaṃ nirañjanam || 6 ||
meaning:
स्तुत्वा शम्भुशरीरात्तु निःसार्येनां निराकुलाम् |
शम्भुचित्तं करिष्यामो ध्यानासक्तं निरञ्जनम् || 6 ||
text_mt: praising her and drawing her undisturbed out of Śambhu's body, / we shall make Śambhu's mind taintless and attached to meditation.

sanskrit_iast:
yāvat satī punardehaṃ gṛhītvā harabhāminī |
bhavitrī tāvadevaiṣa viśoko dhyātu niṣkalam || 7 ||
meaning:
यावत् सती पुनर्देहं गृहीत्वा हरभामिनी |
भवित्री तावदेवैष विशोको ध्यातु निष्कलम् || 7 ||
text_mt: Until Satī again takes a body and is to become / the wife of Hara, let him, free from grief, meditate upon the partless [reality].”

sanskrit_iast:
iti sañcintya manasā brahmādyāstridivaukasaḥ |
yoganidrāṃ mahāmāyā stotumevaṃ samārabhana || 8 ||
meaning:
इति सञ्चिन्त्य मनसा ब्रह्माद्यास्त्रिदिवौकसः |
योगनिद्रां महामाया स्तोतुमेवं समारभन || 8 ||
text_mt: Reflecting thus in their minds, the dwellers of heaven headed by Brahmā / began to praise Yoganidrā, Mahāmāyā, in this manner.

sanskrit_iast: devā ūcuḥ
meaning: देवा ऊचुः

sanskrit_iast:
śrīśakti pāvanī tāntu puṣṭiṃ paramaniṣkalām |
vayaṃ stumo mahābhaktyā mahadavyaktarūpiṇīm || 9 ||
meaning:
श्रीशक्ति पावनी तान्तु पुष्टिं परमनिष्कलाम् |
वयं स्तुमो महाभक्त्या महदव्यक्तरूपिणीम् || 9 ||
text_mt: With great devotion we praise that auspicious energy, the purifier, / nourishment, the supreme partless one, who has the form of the great unmanifest;

sanskrit_iast:
śivāṃ śivakarī śuddhāṃ sthūlāṃ sūkṣmāṃ parāvarām |
antarvidyāmavidyākhyāṃ prītimekāgrayoganim || 10 ||
meaning:
शिवां शिवकरी शुद्धां स्थूलां सूक्ष्मां परावराम् |
अन्तर्विद्यामविद्याख्यां प्रीतिमेकाग्रयोगनिम् || 10 ||
text_mt: the benevolent, bestower of benevolence, pure, gross, subtle, higher and lower, / the inner knowledge named ignorance, delight, the one-pointed yoginī.

sanskrit_iast:
tvaṃ medhā tvaṃ dhṛtistvaṃ hrīstvaekā sarvagocarā |
tvaṃ dīdhitiḥ sūryagatā suprapañcaprakāśinī || 11 ||
meaning:
त्वं मेधा त्वं धृतिस्त्वं ह्रीस्त्वएका सर्वगोचरा |
त्वं दीधितिः सूर्यगता सुप्रपञ्चप्रकाशिनी || 11 ||
text_mt: You are intelligence, you are steadfastness, you are modesty, you alone are perceived by all; / you are the ray of light abiding in the sun, illuminating the manifest world.

sanskrit_iast:
yā tu brahmāṇḍasaṃsthānaṃ jagadbījeṣu yā jagat |
āpyāyayati brahmādīṃstambāntān yā tvamāpagā || 12 ||
meaning:
या तु ब्रह्माण्डसंस्थानं जगद्बीजेषु या जगत् |
आप्याययति ब्रह्मादींस्तम्बान्तान् या त्वमापगा || 12 ||
text_mt: You who abide in the cosmic egg, who in the seeds of the universe / nourish the universe from Brahmā down to a clump of grass—you are the river.

sanskrit_iast:
ya ekaḥ sarvajagatāṃ prāṇabhūtaḥ sadāgatiḥ |
devānāñca ya ādhāraḥ sa nabhasvāṃstavāṃśakaḥ || 13 ||
meaning:
य एकः सर्वजगतां प्राणभूतः सदागतिः |
देवानाञ्च य आधारः स नभस्वांस्तवांशकः || 13 ||
text_mt: That wind, the sole breath of life of all the worlds, the ever-moving, / who is the support of the gods, is a portion of you.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ visāri yattejaḥ sarvatraiva samidhyate |
tatte rūpaṃ jagadbījaṃ bahudhā yacca dṛśyate || 14 ||
meaning:
एवं विसारि यत्तेजः सर्वत्रैव समिध्यते |
तत्ते रूपं जगद्बीजं बहुधा यच्च दृश्यते || 14 ||
text_mt: Likewise, that spreading radiance which is kindled everywhere / is your form, the seed of the universe, which is seen in manifold ways.

sanskrit_iast:
yā brahmalokapātālasāntarālagatā sadā |
sā tvaṃ viyanmadhyabahirbrahmāṇḍasya ca sarvataḥ || 15 ||
meaning:
या ब्रह्मलोकपातालसान्तरालगता सदा |
सा त्वं वियन्मध्यबहिर्ब्रह्माण्डस्य च सर्वतः || 15 ||
text_mt: You who ever dwell in the world of Brahmā, the netherworld, and the intermediate space, / you are the atmosphere, inside and outside the cosmic egg on every side.

sanskrit_iast:
acalācalacakreṇa yantritā yā prapañcasūḥ |
jagaddhātrī lokamātā sā ca tvaṃ mādhavī kṣitiḥ || 16 ||
meaning:
अचलाचलचक्रेण यन्त्रिता या प्रपञ्चसूः |
जगद्धात्री लोकमाता सा च त्वं माधवी क्षितिः || 16 ||
text_mt: Restrained by the wheel of mountains, giving birth to the manifest world, / sustainer of the universe, mother of the worlds, you are the earth, beloved of Mādhava.

sanskrit_iast:
tvaṃ buddhistvaṃ tadviṣayā tvaṃ mātā chandasāṃ gatiḥ |
gāyatrī tvaṃ vedamātā tvaṃ sāvitrī sarasvatī || 17 ||
meaning:
त्वं बुद्धिस्त्वं तद्विषया त्वं माता छन्दसां गतिः |
गायत्री त्वं वेदमाता त्वं सावित्री सरस्वती || 17 ||
text_mt: You are intellect, you are its object, you are the mother, the path of the metres; / you are Gāyatrī, the mother of the Vedas, you are Sāvitrī and Sarasvatī.

sanskrit_iast:
tvaṃ mātā sarvajagatāṃ tvaṃ trayī kāmarūpiṇī |
tvaṃ hi nidrāsvarūpeṇa prāṇino nirjarādayaḥ |
ye svargādyokasaḥ sarvān sukhayantī pramohasi || 18 ||
meaning:
त्वं माता सर्वजगतां त्वं त्रयी कामरूपिणी |
त्वं हि निद्रास्वरूपेण प्राणिनो निर्जरादयः |
ये स्वर्गाद्योकसः सर्वान् सुखयन्ती प्रमोहसि || 18 ||
text_mt: You are the mother of all the worlds, you are the three Vedas, assuming forms at will; / in the form of sleep, you delight and thoroughly enchant / living beings, the undying gods, and all who dwell in heaven and other realms.

sanskrit_iast:
tvaṃ lakṣmīḥ puṇyakartrīṇāṃ pāpināṃ tvaṃ hi yātanā |
tathā nītibhṛtāṃ śrīśca sukhadānaiśikī dhṛti || 19 ||
meaning:
त्वं लक्ष्मीः पुण्यकर्त्रीणां पापिनां त्वं हि यातना |
तथा नीतिभृतां श्रीश्च सुखदानैशिकी धृति || 19 ||
text_mt: You are Lakṣmī to those who perform meritorious deeds, and you are torment to sinners; / likewise, you are prosperity to the virtuous and nocturnal steadfastness giving happiness.

sanskrit_iast:
tvaṃ śāntiḥ sarvajagatāṃ tvaṃ kāntiścandragocarā |
tvaṃ dhātrī sarvabhūtānāṃ lakṣmīstvaṃ viṣṇumohinī || 20 ||
meaning:
त्वं शान्तिः सर्वजगतां त्वं कान्तिश्चन्द्रगोचरा |
त्वं धात्री सर्वभूतानां लक्ष्मीस्त्वं विष्णुमोहिनी || 20 ||
text_mt: You are peace to all the worlds, you are the radiance abiding in the moon; / you are the supporter of all beings, you are Lakṣmī who enchants Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
tvaṃ tattvarūpā bhūtānāṃ pañcānāmapi sārakṛt |
tvaṃ trilokī mahāmāyāṃ tvaṃ nītirmohakāriṇī || 21 ||
meaning:
त्वं तत्त्वरूपा भूतानां पञ्चानामपि सारकृत् |
त्वं त्रिलोकी महामायां त्वं नीतिर्मोहकारिणी || 21 ||
text_mt: You have the form of reality, creating the essence even of the five elements; / you are the three worlds, Mahāmāyā, you are conduct, causing delusion.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃsāracakreṣvāropya sarvabhūtaṃ maheśvaraḥ |
bhrāmayannasti ca yathā sā tvaṃ māyā maheśvari || 22 ||
meaning:
संसारचक्रेष्वारोप्य सर्वभूतं महेश्वरः |
भ्रामयन्नस्ति च यथा सा त्वं माया महेश्वरि || 22 ||
text_mt: Placing all beings upon the wheels of worldly existence, / Maheśvara whirls them about; you are that Māyā, O Maheśvarī!

sanskrit_iast:
jayantī jayayuktānāṃ hrīrvidyāṃ nītiruttamā |
gītistvaṃ sāmavedasya granthistvaṃ yajuṣāṃ hutiḥ || 23 ||
meaning:
जयन्ती जययुक्तानां ह्रीर्विद्यां नीतिरुत्तमा |
गीतिस्त्वं सामवेदस्य ग्रन्थिस्त्वं यजुषां हुतिः || 23 ||
text_mt: You are Jayantī to the victorious, modesty, knowledge, excellent conduct; / you are the chant of the Sāmaveda, the prose-knot of the Yajurveda, the oblation.

sanskrit_iast:
samastagīrvāṇagaṇasya śaktistamomayī sattvaguṇaikadṛśyā |
rajaḥprapañcānubhavaikakāriṇī yā na stutā bhavyakarīha sāstu || 24 ||
meaning:
समस्तगीर्वाणगणस्य शक्तिस्तमोमयी सत्त्वगुणैकदृश्या |
रजःप्रपञ्चानुभवैककारिणी या न स्तुता भव्यकरीह सास्तु || 24 ||
text_mt: The power of the entire host of gods, consisting of darkness, seen only through the quality of purity, / the sole cause of experiencing the manifestation of passion—may she, who is not praised [adequately], bestow auspiciousness here.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃsārasāgarakarālataraṅgaduḥkhanistārakāritaraṇiścirītihīnā |
yāṣṭāṅgarūpaparapāvanakeligītavikṣepakāriṇī girau praṇanāma tāṃ vai || 25 ||
meaning:
संसारसागरकरालतरङ्गदुःखनिस्तारकारितरणिश्चिरीतिहीना |
याष्टाङ्गरूपपरपावनकेलिगीतविक्षेपकारिणी गिरौ प्रणनाम तां वै || 25 ||
text_mt: A boat rescuing one from the sorrow of the fierce waves of the ocean of rebirth, free from long-standing afflictions, / having the form of the eight limbs [of yoga], dispersing the playful chants of the supreme purifying [truth]—to her on the mountain we bow.

sanskrit_iast:
nāsākṣivaktrabhujavakṣasi mānase ca dhṛtvā sukhāni vidadhāti sadaiva jantoḥ |
nidreti yāti subhagā jagatībhavānāṃ sā naḥ prasīdatu dhṛtismṛtivṛttirūpā || 26 ||
meaning:
नासाक्षिवक्त्रभुजवक्षसि मानसे च धृत्वा सुखानि विदधाति सदैव जन्तोः |
निद्रेति याति सुभगा जगतीभवानां सा नः प्रसीदतु धृतिस्मृतिवृत्तिरूपा || 26 ||
text_mt: Holding them in the nose, eyes, mouth, arms, chest, and mind, she ever bestows joys upon creatures; / going about as sleep, beautiful, of those who exist in the world, may she, possessing the form of firmness, memory, and mental activity, be gracious to us.

sanskrit_iast:
sṛṣṭisthityantarūpā yā sṛṣṭisthityantakāriṇī |
sṛṣṭisthityantaśaktiryā sā māyā naḥ prasīdatu || 27 ||
meaning:
सृष्टिस्थित्यन्तरूपा या सृष्टिस्थित्यन्तकारिणी |
सृष्टिस्थित्यन्तशक्तिर्या सा माया नः प्रसीदतु || 27 ||
text_mt: She who has the form of creation, preservation, and dissolution, who causes creation, preservation, and dissolution, / who is the power of creation, preservation, and dissolution—may that Māyā be gracious to us!

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
yoganindrā mahāmāyā saṃstuteyaṃ tadā suraḥ |
harasya hṛdayāt kṣipraṃ niḥsasāra tadāñjasā || 28 ||
meaning:
योगनिन्द्रा महामाया संस्तुतेयं तदा सुरः |
हरस्य हृदयात् क्षिप्रं निःससार तदाञ्जसा || 28 ||
text_mt: When praised thus by the gods, Yoganidrā, Mahāmāyā, / quickly and easily issued forth from the heart of Hara.

sanskrit_iast:
viniḥsṛtāyāṃ tasyāṃ tu viveśa madhusūdanaḥ |
śambhoranta svayaṃ tasya śāntyarthaṃ viśvarūpadhṛk || 29 ||
meaning:
विनिःसृतायां तस्यां तु विवेश मधुसूदनः |
शम्भोरन्त स्वयं तस्य शान्त्यर्थं विश्वरूपधृक् || 29 ||
text_mt: When she had come forth, Madhusūdana, bearing the universal form, / entered within Śambhu of his own accord for the sake of his peace.

sanskrit_iast:
praviśya hṛdayaṃ tasya kalpe kalpe yathābhavat |
sṛṣṭi sthitistathaivāntastathādarśayadacyutaḥ || 30 ||
meaning:
प्रविश्य हृदयं तस्य कल्पे कल्पे यथाभवत् |
सृष्टि स्थितिस्तथैवान्तस्तथादर्शयदच्युतः || 30 ||
text_mt: Having entered his heart, Acyuta showed him / how creation, preservation, and dissolution take place in aeon after aeon;

sanskrit_iast:
yathā satī tasya jāyāṃ bhūtā sā yā ca yatsutā |
tat sarvaṃ darśayāmāsa muktadehā ca sā yathā || 31 ||
meaning:
यथा सती तस्य जायां भूता सा या च यत्सुता |
तत् सर्वं दर्शयामास मुक्तदेहा च सा यथा || 31 ||
text_mt: and how Satī had become his wife, who she was, whose daughter she was, / and how she cast off her body—all that he showed [him].

sanskrit_iast:
bahirvyakta tu niḥsāraṃ prapañca rajasaṃ bahu |
darśayitvā paraṃ jyotirgatacitaṃ tadākarot || 32 ||
meaning:
बहिर्व्यक्त तु निःसारं प्रपञ्च रजसं बहु |
दर्शयित्वा परं ज्योतिर्गतचितं तदाकरोत् || 32 ||
text_mt:
Having shown the manifested exterior—unreal, a vast manifestation of passion—
he then made his mind fixed upon the supreme light.

sanskrit_iast:
tato haro'pi tān sarvān prapañcān vīkṣya cāsakṛt |
niḥsārāṃśca tadā matvā sāre cittaṃ nyaveśayat || 33 ||
meaning:
ततो हरोऽपि तान् सर्वान् प्रपञ्चान् वीक्ष्य चासकृत् |
निःसारांश्च तदा मत्वा सारे चित्तं न्यवेशयत् || 33 ||
text_mt:
Then Hara also, looking repeatedly at all those manifestations,
and deeming them to be without substance, fixed his mind upon reality.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmādīnāṃ tadā māyā devānāṃ taiḥ pariṣṭutā |
pratiśrutya ca kartavyaṃ tatraivāntardadhe drutam || 34 ||
meaning:
ब्रह्मादीनां तदा माया देवानां तैः परिष्टुता |
प्रतिश्रुत्य च कर्तव्यं तत्रैवान्तर्दधे द्रुतम् || 34 ||
text_mt:
Then Māyā, praised by the gods headed by Brahmā,
promised what was to be done and immediately vanished right there.

sanskrit_iast:
bhagavānapi vaikuṇṭhaḥ śambhościttaṃ pade pade |
saṃyamya niḥsṛtaḥ kāyādrājeva ravimaṇḍalāt || 35 ||
meaning:
भगवानपि वैकुण्ठः शम्भोश्चित्तं पदे पदे |
संयम्य निःसृतः कायाद्राजेव रविमण्डलात् || 35 ||
text_mt:
The Blessed Lord Vaikuṇṭha too, having curbed Śambhu's mind at every step,
emerged from his body like the sun from its orb.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtakṛtyāstadā devā brahmanārāyaṇādayaḥ |
svaṃ svaṃ sthānaṃ yayuḥ prītiyutāstyaktvā haraṃ girau || 36 ||
meaning:
कृतकृत्यास्तदा देवा ब्रह्मनारायणादयः |
स्वं स्वं स्थानं ययुः प्रीतियुतास्त्यक्त्वा हरं गिरौ || 36 ||
text_mt:
Having achieved their purpose, the gods led by Brahmā and Nārāyaṇa
went each to his own abode, filled with joy, leaving Hara on the mountain.

sanskrit_iast:
dhyānāsaktaṃ mahādevaṃ praṇamyendrādayaḥ surāḥ |
vijñāpya mauninaṃ devaṃ jagmuḥ sthānaṃ svakaṃ svakam || 37 ||
meaning:
ध्यानासक्तं महादेवं प्रणम्येन्द्रादयः सुराः |
विज्ञाप्य मौनिनं देवं जग्मुः स्थानं स्वकं स्वकम् || 37 ||
text_mt:
Bowing to Mahādeva absorbed in meditation, the gods headed by Indra,
having addressed the silent god, went to their respective abodes.

sanskrit_iast:
yāteṣu teṣu deveṣu kapardī vṛṣavāhanaḥ |
sahasraṃ divyamānena dadhyau jyotiḥ paraṃ samāḥ || 38 ||
meaning:
यातेषु तेषु देवेषु कपर्दी वृषवाहनः |
सहस्रं दिव्यमानेन दध्यौ ज्योतिः परं समाः || 38 ||
text_mt:
When those gods had departed, the matted-haired one, whose mount is the bull,
meditated upon the supreme light for a thousand divine years.

sanskrit_iast: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
meaning: ऋषय ऊचुः

sanskrit_iast:
kathaṃ madhuripuḥ śambhoḥ praviśya hṛdaye'ñjasā |
kalpe kalpe sthitiṃ sṛṣṭiṃ saṃyamañcāpyadarśayat || 36 ||
meaning:
कथं मधुरिपुः शम्भोः प्रविश्य हृदयेऽञ्जसा |
कल्पे कल्पे स्थितिं सृष्टिं संयमञ्चाप्यदर्शयत् || 36 ||
text_mt:
How did Madhuripu, entering into the heart of Śambhu easily,
show maintenance, creation, and also destruction in kalpa after kalpa?

sanskrit_iast:
yathā jagatprapañcāya rajasā jagatīṃ gatāḥ |
niḥsāratā kathaṃ teṣāṃ darśitā kaiṭabhāriṇā || 40 ||
kinnu sārataraṃ guhyaṃ paraṃ jyotiḥ sanātanam |
darśitaṃ tena tat satyamācakṣva dvijasattama || 41 ||
meaning:
यथा जगत्प्रपञ्चाय रजसा जगतीं गताः |
निःसारता कथं तेषां दर्शिता कैटभारिणा || 40 ||
किन्नु सारतरं गुह्यं परं ज्योतिः सनातनम् |
दर्शितं तेन तत् सत्यमाचक्ष्व द्विजसत्तम || 41 ||
text_mt:
How, when they entered the earth through passion for the cosmic manifestation,
was their lack of substance shown by the enemy of Kaiṭabha?
What is that most essential, secret, supreme, eternal light
shown by him? Tell that truly, O best of the twice-born!

sanskrit_iast:
śrotumicchāma iti te munīndrādbhūtamuttamam |
vistarādidamākhyāhi dharma niḥśreyasaṃ param || 42 ||
meaning:
श्रोतुमिच्छाम इति ते मुनीन्द्राद्भूतमुत्तमम् |
विस्तरादिदमाख्याहि धर्म निःश्रेयसं परम् || 42 ||
text_mt:
We wish to hear from you, O king of sages, this wonderful and supreme [teaching];
relate in detail this supreme, highest good, which is righteous.

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
ādisargamahaṃ vakṣye vārāhaṃ dvijasattamāḥ |
kalpe kalpe yathā sṛṣṭirvārāhe yādṛśī bhavet || 43 ||
meaning:
आदिसर्गमहं वक्ष्ये वाराहं द्विजसत्तमाः |
कल्पे कल्पे यथा सृष्टिर्वाराहे यादृशी भवेत् || 43 ||
text_mt:
I shall explain the primeval creation of the Boar [Kalpa], O best of the twice-born,
how creation takes place in kalpa after kalpa, and of what nature it is in the Vārāha [Kalpa].

sanskrit_iast:
ādisṛṣṭi darśayitvā pratisargaṃ tathā hariḥ |
śambhavaṃ darśayāmāsa pralayādīn nibodhataḥ || 44 ||
meaning:
आदिसृष्टि दर्शयित्वा प्रतिसर्गं तथा हरिः |
शम्भवं दर्शयामास प्रलयादीन् निबोधतः || 44 ||
text_mt:
Having shown the primeval creation, Hari then showed
the secondary creation relating to Śambhu, along with dissolution and the rest; understand [this].

sanskrit_iast:
pralaya prathamaṃ vakṣye sargamādi tataḥ param |
pratisarga tato viprā vārāhaṃ vinibodhataḥ || 45 ||
meaning:
प्रलय प्रथमं वक्ष्ये सर्गमादि ततः परम् |
प्रतिसर्ग ततो विप्रा वाराहं विनिबोधतः || 45 ||
text_mt:
First I shall explain dissolution, and then the primeval creation,
and then secondary creation, O brahmins; understand that of the Boar [Kalpa].

sanskrit_iast:
nimeṣo nāma kālāṃśo netronmeṣavilakṣitaḥ |
tairaṣṭādaśabhiḥ kāṣṭhā kāṣṭhānāṃ triṃśatā kalā || 46 ||
meaning:
निमेषो नाम कालांशो नेत्रोन्मेषविलक्षितः |
तैरष्टादशभिः काष्ठा काष्ठानां त्रिंशता कला || 46 ||
text_mt:
The fraction of time termed a nimeṣa is defined by the twinkling of an eye;
eighteen of them make a kāṣṭhā; thirty kāṣṭhās make a kalā.

sanskrit_iast:
kalābhistāvatībhistu kṣaṇākhyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ |
kṣaṇairdvādaśabhiḥ prokto muhūrtastaistu triṃśatā || 47 ||
meaning:
कलाभिस्तावतीभिस्तु क्षणाख्यः परिकीर्तितः |
क्षणैर्द्वादशभिः प्रोक्तो मुहूर्तस्तैस्तु त्रिंशता || 47 ||
text_mt:
By as many kalās, what is called a kṣaṇa is proclaimed;
by twelve kṣaṇas a muhūrta is said [to be formed], and by thirty of those,

sanskrit_iast:
mānuṣaḥ syādahorātraḥ pakṣaste daśa pañca ca |
pakṣābhyāṃ mānuṣo māsaḥ pitṝṇāṃ tadaharniśam || 48 ||
meaning:
मानुषः स्यादहोरात्रः पक्षस्ते दश पञ्च च |
पक्षाभ्यां मानुषो मासः पितॄणां तदहर्निशम् || 48 ||
text_mt:
is a human day and night; fifteen of those are a fortnight;
by two fortnights a human month [is formed]; that is a day and night of the ancestors.

sanskrit_iast:
māsairdvādaśabhirvarṣo devānāṃ tadaharniśam |
kṛṣṇapakṣaḥ pitṝṇāṃ tu karmārthaṃ divaso mataḥ || 49 ||
meaning:
मासैर्द्वादशभिर्वर्षो देवानां तदहर्निशम् |
कृष्णपक्षः पितॄणां तु कर्मार्थं दिवसो मतः || 49 ||
text_mt:
By twelve months is a year; that is a day and night of the gods;
the dark fortnight is considered the day of the ancestors for their rites,

sanskrit_iast:
svapnārthaṃ śuklapakṣastu rajanī parikīrtitā |
devānāṃ tu dinaṃ proktaṃ ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇam || 50 ||
meaning:
स्वप्नार्थं शुक्लपक्षस्तु रजनी परिकीर्तिता |
देवानां तु दिनं प्रोक्तं षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् || 50 ||
text_mt:
and the bright fortnight is proclaimed their night for sleep.
The six months of the northern course are said to be the day of the gods,

sanskrit_iast:
rātriḥ svapnāya devānāṃ ṣaṇmāsā dakṣiṇāyaṇam |
dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāntu māsābhyāmarkajābhyāmṛtuḥ smṛtaḥ || 51 ||
meaning:
रात्रिः स्वप्नाय देवानां षण्मासा दक्षिणायणम् |
द्वाभ्यां द्वाभ्यान्तु मासाभ्यामर्कजाभ्यामृतुः स्मृतः || 51 ||
text_mt:
and the six months of the southern course are their night for sleep.
A season is known to consist of two solar months each.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛtubhiścāyanaṃ proktaṃ tribhistanmānuṣaṃ matam |
ṛtubhirvatsaraḥ ṣaḍbhistāṃśca śṛṇu pṛthak pṛthak || 52 ||
meaning:
ऋतुभिश्चायनं प्रोक्तं त्रिभिस्तन्मानुषं मतम् |
ऋतुभिर्वत्सरः षड्भिस्तांश्च शृणु पृथक् पृथक् || 52 ||
text_mt:
A solstice is said to consist of three seasons; that is considered human;
a year consists of six seasons; hear of them individually:

sanskrit_iast:
caitrādi-māsayugalaiḥ saṃjñābhedād dvijottamāḥ |
vasantaścaitravaiśākho grīṣmo jyeṣṭhaḥ śucistathā || 53 ||
meaning:
चैत्रादि-मासयुगलैः संज्ञाभेदाद् द्विजोत्तमाः |
वसन्तश्चैत्रवैशाखो ग्रीष्मो ज्येष्ठः शुचिस्तथा || 53 ||
text_mt:
By pairs of months beginning with Caitra, according to different names, O best of the twice-born:
spring is Caitra and Vaiśākha; summer is Jyeṣṭha and Śuci [Āṣāḍha];

sanskrit_iast:
prāvṛṭ nabhonabhasyau tu śarat syādiṣa-kārtikau |
sahaḥ pauṣau ca hemantaḥ śiśiro māghaphālgunau || 54 ||
meaning:
प्रावृट् नभोनभस्यौ तु शरत् स्यादिष-कार्तिकौ |
सहः पौषौ च हेमन्तः शिशिरो माघफाल्गुनौ || 54 ||
text_mt:
the rainy season is Nabhas and Nabhasya [Śrāvaṇa and Bhādrapada]; autumn is Iṣa and Kārtika [Āśvina and Kārttika];
Sahas and Pauṣa [Mārgaśīrṣa and Pauṣa] are winter; the dewy season is Māgha and Phālguna.

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaḍime ṛtavaḥ proktā yajñādau vihitāḥ pṛthak |
nṛṇāṃ mānena daśabhirlakṣaiḥ saptabhiruttaraiḥ |
aṣṭāviṃśatisāhasraimaniṃ kṛtayugasya tu || 55 ||
meaning:
षडिमे ऋतवः प्रोक्ता यज्ञादौ विहिताः पृथक् |
नृणां मानेन दशभिर्लक्षैः सप्तभिरुत्तरैः |
अष्टाविंशतिसाहस्रैमनिं कृतयुगस्य तु || 55 ||
text_mt:
These six seasons are proclaimed, ordained separately for sacrifices and the like.
By the measure of men, seventeen hundred thousand
and twenty-eight thousand [years] is the duration of the Kṛta age.

sanskrit_iast:
sandhyā catuḥśatānīha varṣāṇāmantarālataḥ |
sandhyāṃśastāvatā proktastadantargata īpsitaḥ || 56 ||
meaning:
सन्ध्या चतुःशतानीह वर्षाणामन्तरालतः |
सन्ध्यांशस्तावता प्रोक्तस्तदन्तर्गत ईप्सितः || 56 ||
text_mt:
Four hundred [divine] years are here the dawn in the interval,
and its twilight fraction is declared to be of the same length, included within it as desired.

sanskrit_iast:
tretā dvādaśabhirlakṣairmānuṣairvatsarairbhavet |
ṣaṇṇavatyā sahasraiśca sandhyā cāsya śatatrayam || 57 ||
meaning:
त्रेता द्वादशभिर्लक्षैर्मानुषैर्वत्सरैर्भवेत् |
षण्णवत्या सहस्रैश्च सन्ध्या चास्य शतत्रयम् || 57 ||
text_mt:
Tretā consists of twelve hundred thousand human years
and ninety-six thousand, and its dawn is three hundred [divine years].

sanskrit_iast:
śatatrayaṃ tu sandhyāṃśastadantaḥ parikīrtitaḥ |
catuḥṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi lakṣyāṇyaṣṭau pramāṇataḥ || 58 ||
meaning:
शतत्रयं तु सन्ध्यांशस्तदन्तः परिकीर्तितः |
चतुःषष्टिसहस्राणि लक्ष्याण्यष्टौ प्रमाणतः || 58 ||
text_mt:
The twilight fraction within it is proclaimed to be three hundred.
Eight hundred thousand and sixty-four thousand in measure

sanskrit_iast:
bhavedyugaṃ dvāparākhyaṃ teṣu sandhyā śatadvayam |
śatadvayaṃ tu sandhyāṃśastadantargata iṣyate || 59 ||
meaning:
भवेद्युगं द्वापराख्यं तेषु सन्ध्या शतद्वयम् |
शतद्वयं तु सन्ध्यांशस्तदन्तर्गत इष्यते || 59 ||
text_mt:
is the age named Dvāpara; in it the dawn is two hundred [divine years],
and two hundred is desired as the twilight fraction contained within it.

sanskrit_iast: dvātriṃśattu sahasrāṇi caturlakṣāṇi vai kaleḥ || 60 ||
meaning: द्वात्रिंशत्तु सहस्राणि चतुर्लक्षाणि वै कलेः || 60 ||
text_mt: Four hundred thousand and thirty-two thousand [years] are indeed of Kali.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃvatsarairbhavenmānaṃ sandhyaikaṃ procyate śatam |
vatsarāṇāmekaśataṃ saṃdhyāṃśaśca tadantare || 61 ||
meaning:
संवत्सरैर्भवेन्मानं सन्ध्यैकं प्रोच्यते शतम् |
वत्सराणामेकशतं संध्यांशश्च तदन्तरे || 61 ||
text_mt:
Its measure is in years; the dawn is declared to be one hundred,
and the twilight fraction within it is one hundred years.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ kṛtaśca tretā ca dvāparaśca tathā kaliḥ |
mānuṣeṇa pramāṇena bhaved yugacatuṣṭayam || 62 ||
meaning:
एवं कृतश्च त्रेता च द्वापरश्च तथा कलिः |
मानुषेण प्रमाणेन भवेद् युगचतुष्टयम् || 62 ||
text_mt:
Thus Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, and Kali—
such is the cycle of four ages by human measure.

sanskrit_iast:
tricatvāriṃśatā lakṣairmānañcāturyugaṃ bhavet |
sahasrairapi viṃśatyā saṃdhyā saṃdhyāṃśasaṃyutam || 63 ||
meaning:
त्रिचत्वारिंशता लक्षैर्मानञ्चातुर्युगं भवेत् |
सहस्रैरपि विंशत्या संध्या संध्यांशसंयुतम् || 63 ||
text_mt:
The measure of the four ages is forty-three hundred thousand
and twenty thousand [years], together with the dawns and twilight fractions.

sanskrit_iast:
daivaṃ dinaṃ vatsareṇa mānuṣeṇa sarātrakam |
evaṃ kramaṃ gaṇitvā tu mānuṣīyaiścaturyugaiḥ |
daivaṃ dvādaśasāhasraṃ vatsarāṇāṃ prakīrttitam || 64 ||
meaning:
दैवं दिनं वत्सरेण मानुषेण सरात्रकम् |
एवं क्रमं गणित्वा तु मानुषीयैश्चतुर्युगैः |
दैवं द्वादशसाहस्रं वत्सराणां प्रकीर्त्तितम् || 64 ||
text_mt:
A divine day with its night equals one human year.
Counting in this sequence by the human four ages,
twelve thousand divine years are proclaimed.

sanskrit_iast:
devairdvādaśasāhasrairvatsaraidaivikaṃ yugam |
tadvai caturyugaṃ nṛṇāṃ saṃdhyā saṃdhyāṃśasaṃyutam || 65 ||
meaning:
देवैर्द्वादशसाहस्रैर्वत्सरैदैविकं युगम् |
तद्वै चतुर्युगं नृणां संध्या संध्यांशसंयुतम् || 65 ||
text_mt:
Twelve thousand divine years constitute a divine age;
that indeed is the four ages of men, together with the dawns and twilight fractions.

sanskrit_iast:
devānāṃ tu kṛte tretādvāparādivyavasthayā |
na yugavyavahāro'sti na ca dharmādibhinnatā || 66 ||
meaning:
देवानां तु कृते त्रेताद्वापरादिव्यवस्थया |
न युगव्यवहारोऽस्ति न च धर्मादिभिन्नता || 66 ||
text_mt:
For the gods, according to the division into Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, and the rest,
there is no use of ages, nor any differentiation in virtue and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
kintu cāturyugaṃ nāraṃ bhaveddaivayugaṃ sadā |
daivikairekasaptatyā yugairmanvantaraṃ bhavet || 67 ||
meaning:
किन्तु चातुर्युगं नारं भवेद्दैवयुगं सदा |
दैविकैरेकसप्तत्या युगैर्मन्वन्तरं भवेत् || 67 ||
text_mt:
Rather, the human four-age cycle is always a single divine age.
By seventy-one divine ages a manvantara is formed.

sanskrit_iast:
daivayugasahasre dve brahmaṇaḥ syādaharniśam |
caturyugasahasre dve nṛṇāṃ mānena tadbhavet || 68 ||
meaning:
दैवयुगसहस्रे द्वे ब्रह्मणः स्यादहर्निशम् |
चतुर्युगसहस्रे द्वे नृणां मानेन तद्भवेत् || 68 ||
text_mt:
Two thousand divine ages constitute a day and night of Brahmā;
by the measure of men, that equals two thousand four-age cycles.

sanskrit_iast:
ekasmin brāhmadivase manava syuścaturdaśa |
evaṃ brāhmaṇe mānena divasaistu tribhiḥ śataiḥ |
sa-ṣaṣṭibhirvatsaraḥ syād brāhmo varṣo nṛṇāṃ yathā || 69 ||
meaning:
एकस्मिन् ब्राह्मदिवसे मनव स्युश्चतुर्दश |
एवं ब्राह्मणे मानेन दिवसैस्तु त्रिभिः शतैः |
स-षष्टिभिर्वत्सरः स्याद् ब्राह्मो वर्षो नृणां यथा || 69 ||
text_mt:
In a single day of Brahmā there are fourteen Manus.
Thus, by Brahmā's measure, three hundred and sixty days
make a year of Brahmā, just as [it is] a year for humans.

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmai pañcaśatā varṣaiḥ parārdhaḥ parikīrtitaḥ |
tadīśvarasya divasastāvatī rātrīrīḍyate || 70 ||
meaning:
ब्राह्मै पञ्चशता वर्षैः परार्धः परिकीर्तितः |
तदीश्वरस्य दिवसस्तावती रात्रीरीड्यते || 70 ||
text_mt:
Five hundred years of Brahmā are proclaimed to be a parārdha;
that is a day of Īśvara, and of equal length is the night praised [as his].

sanskrit_iast:
śatena brahmaṇo varṣo kālaḥ syād dviparārdhakaḥ |
parārdhadvitaye'tīte brahmaṇaḥ pralayo bhavet || 71 ||
meaning:
शतेन ब्रह्मणो वर्षो कालः स्याद् द्विपरार्धकः |
परार्धद्वितयेऽतीते ब्रह्मणः प्रलयो भवेत् || 71 ||
text_mt:
By one hundred years of Brahmā the time consists of two parārdhas;
when the two parārdhas have passed, the dissolution of Brahmā occurs.

sanskrit_iast:
pralīne brahmaṇi pare jagatāṃ prākṛto layaḥ |
samastajagadādhāramavyayaṃ yat parātparam || 72 ||
meaning:
प्रलीने ब्रह्मणि परे जगतां प्राकृतो लयः |
समस्तजगदाधारमव्ययं यत् परात्परम् || 72 ||
text_mt:
When the supreme Brahmā is dissolved, there occurs the elemental dissolution of the worlds.
That which is the foundation of the entire universe, imperishable, higher than the highest,

sanskrit_iast:
tasya brahmasvarūpasya divārātrasya yad bhavet |
tatparaṃ nāma tasyārdhaṃ parārdhaṃmabhidhīyate || 73 ||
meaning:
तस्य ब्रह्मस्वरूपस्य दिवारात्रस्य यद् भवेत् |
तत्परं नाम तस्यार्धं परार्धंमभिधीयते || 73 ||
text_mt:
of that essential nature of Brahman, whatever day and night there may be,
that is called a para; half of that is termed a parārdha.

sanskrit_iast:
jagatsvarūpī bhagavān paramātmākṣayo'vyayaḥ |
sthūlāt sthūlatamaḥ sūkṣmād yastu sūkṣmatamo mataḥ |
na tasyāsti divārātrivyavahāro na vatsaraḥ || 74 ||
meaning:
जगत्स्वरूपी भगवान् परमात्माक्षयोऽव्ययः |
स्थूलात् स्थूलतमः सूक्ष्माद् यस्तु सूक्ष्मतमो मतः |
न तस्यास्ति दिवारात्रिव्यवहारो न वत्सरः || 74 ||
text_mt: The Blessed Lord, whose form is the world, the imperishable and undecaying supreme self, / who is considered the grossest of the gross and the subtlest of the subtle, / has no dealing with day and night, nor with the year.

sanskrit_iast:
kintu paurāṇikaiḥ pūrvairasmābhirapi tādṛśaiḥ |
sṛṣṭipralayabodhārthaṃ kalpyate tadaharniśam || 75 ||
meaning:
किन्तु पौराणिकैः पूर्वैरस्माभिरपि तादृशैः |
सृष्टिप्रलयबोधार्थं कल्प्यते तदहर्निशम् || 75 ||
text_mt: Yet by ancient puranic authors, and likewise by us, / for the sake of understanding creation and dissolution, day and night are conceived for him.

sanskrit_iast:
sa eva rātriḥ sa divā sa varṣaḥ sa vai kṣitiḥ sṛṣṭikaro haraśca |
sa viṣṇurūpī puruṣaḥ purāṇastasmin samastañca vibhāti tadvat || 76 ||
meaning:
स एव रात्रिः स दिवा स वर्षः स वै क्षितिः सृष्टिकरो हरश्च |
स विष्णुरूपी पुरुषः पुराणस्तस्मिन् समस्तञ्च विभाति तद्वत् || 76 ||
text_mt: He indeed is night, he is day, he is the year, he indeed is earth, and Hara the creator; / he is the ancient Puruṣa having the form of Viṣṇu, and everything likewise shines within him.

sanskrit_iast:
tato brahmaṇi līne tu paramātmani śāśvate |
jagat sarvaṃ krameṇaiva tadrūpatvāya gacchati || 77 ||
meaning:
ततो ब्रह्मणि लीने तु परमात्मनि शाश्वते |
जगत् सर्वं क्रमेणैव तद्रूपत्वाय गच्छति || 77 ||
text_mt: Then, when Brahmā dissolves into the eternal supreme self, / the entire world gradually proceeds to attain his form.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmaṇaḥ śatavarṣānte rudrarūpī janārdanaḥ |
jagadantaṃ svayaṃ kṛtvā parame līnameti vai || 78 ||
meaning:
ब्रह्मणः शतवर्षान्ते रुद्ररूपी जनार्दनः |
जगदन्तं स्वयं कृत्वा परमे लीनमेति वै || 78 ||
text_mt: At the end of a hundred of Brahmā's years, Janārdana taking the form of Rudra, / having brought an end to the universe himself, indeed attains dissolution in the Supreme.

sanskrit_iast:
prathamaṃ savitā sarvaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ tathā |
tīvraiḥ karaiḥ śoṣayitvā jalaṃ sarvaṃ grahīṣyati || 79 ||
meaning:
प्रथमं सविता सर्वं स्थावरं जङ्गमं तथा |
तीव्रैः करैः शोषयित्वा जलं सर्वं ग्रहीष्यति || 79 ||
text_mt: First the sun, drying up everything stationary as well as moving / with fierce rays, will take away all water.

sanskrit_iast:
śuṣkā vṛkṣāstṛṇagaṇāḥ prāṇinaḥ parvatāstathā |
cūrṇīkṛtvā viśīrṇā syurdivyavarṣaśatena tu || 80 ||
meaning:
शुष्का वृक्षास्तृणगणाः प्राणिनः पर्वतास्तथा |
चूर्णीकृत्वा विशीर्णा स्युर्दिव्यवर्षशतेन तु || 80 ||
text_mt: Trees, clumps of grass, living beings, and likewise mountains, having dried up, / ground to dust, will be shattered within a hundred divine years.

sanskrit_iast:
tato dvādaśasūryasya raśmayaḥ prabalā bhṛśam |
abhavan dvādaśādityā jagadbhogyopabṛṃhitāḥ || 81 ||
meaning:
ततो द्वादशसूर्यस्य रश्मयः प्रबला भृशम् |
अभवन् द्वादशादित्या जगद्भोग्योपबृंहिताः || 81 ||
text_mt: Then the rays of the twelve-fold sun became intensely powerful; / the twelve Ādityas arose, magnified by all that the world had possessed.

sanskrit_iast:
raśmidvāreṇa sakalāssūryāste bhuvanāni ca |
adahan pṛthivī dyauśca medinī coṣṇatāṃ gatā || 82 ||
meaning:
रश्मिद्वारेण सकलास्सूर्यास्ते भुवनानि च |
अदहन् पृथिवी द्यौश्च मेदिनी चोष्णतां गता || 82 ||
text_mt: By means of their rays, all those suns burned the worlds; / the earth and the heavens and the soil reached extreme heat.

sanskrit_iast:
tato vinaṣṭe sakale sthāvare jaṅgame tathā |
ādityaraśmitau devo rudrarūpī janārdanaḥ || 83 ||
meaning:
ततो विनष्टे सकले स्थावरे जङ्गमे तथा |
आदित्यरश्मितौ देवो रुद्ररूपी जनार्दनः || 83 ||
text_mt: Then, when all stationary and moving things were destroyed, / heated by the rays of the sun, the god Janārdana, bearing the form of Rudra,

sanskrit_iast: niḥsṛtya prathamaṃ yātaḥ pātālatalamunnataḥ || 84 ||
meaning: निःसृत्य प्रथमं यातः पातालतलमुन्नतः || 84 ||
text_mt: came forth and first went down to the depths of the netherworld, raised high.

sanskrit_iast:
saptapātālasaṃsthāṃstu nāgagandharvarākṣasān |
devānṛṣīṃśca śeṣañca jaghāna varaśūladhṛk || 85 ||
meaning:
सप्तपातालसंस्थांस्तु नागगन्धर्वराक्षसान् |
देवानृषींश्च शेषञ्च जघान वरशूलधृक् || 85 ||
text_mt: Bearing the excellent trident, he slew the serpent-demons, gandharvas, and rākṣasas residing in the seven netherworlds, / as well as the gods, the sages, and Śeṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ svarge ca pātāle pṛthivyāṃ sāgareṣu ca |
ye prāṇinastān samastān jaghāna sa janārdanaḥ || 86 ||
meaning:
एवं स्वर्गे च पाताले पृथिव्यां सागरेषु च |
ये प्राणिनस्तान् समस्तान् जघान स जनार्दनः || 86 ||
text_mt: Thus, in heaven, in the netherworld, on earth, and in the oceans, / whatever living beings existed, Janārdana slew them all.

sanskrit_iast:
tato mukhānmahāvāyuṃ rudraśca sṛṣṭavān svayam |
so'vyāhatagatirgāḍhaṃ sasāra bhuvanatraye || 87 ||
meaning:
ततो मुखान्महावायुं रुद्रश्च सृष्टवान् स्वयम् |
सोऽव्याहतगतिर्गाढं ससार भुवनत्रये || 87 ||
text_mt: Then Rudra himself emitted a great wind from his mouth; / with unobstructed course, it swept forcefully through the three worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
yāvadvarṣaśataṃ vāyurbhraman bhuvanagarbhagaḥ |
sarvamutsārayāmāsa yat kiñcattulārāśivat || 88 ||
meaning:
यावद्वर्षशतं वायुर्भ्रमन् भुवनगर्भगः |
सर्वमुत्सारयामास यत् किञ्चत्तुलाराशिवत् || 88 ||
text_mt: Wandering within the belly of the world for a hundred years, / the wind blew away whatever existed, like a heap of cotton.

sanskrit_iast:
samastaṃ tat samutsārya jagadvarti samantataḥ |
viveśa dvādaśādityān sa vāyurjavanādhikaḥ || 89 ||
meaning:
समस्तं तत् समुत्सार्य जगद्वर्ति समन्ततः |
विवेश द्वादशादित्यान् स वायुर्जवनाधिकः || 89 ||
text_mt: Having scattered all that was found on every side in the world, / that wind, surpassing all in swiftness, entered into the twelve Ādityas.

sanskrit_iast:
praviśya maṇḍalaṃ teṣāṃ tejobhiḥ saha mārutaḥ |
mahāmeghān samārebhe rudreṇa pratiyojitaḥ || 90 ||
meaning:
प्रविश्य मण्डलं तेषां तेजोभिः सह मारुतः |
महामेघान् समारेभे रुद्रेण प्रतियोजितः || 90 ||
text_mt: Having entered their orb together with their fiery energies, the wind, / urged on by Rudra, set about forming the great clouds.

sanskrit_iast:
tataste preritā meghāstena vātena veginā |
rudreṇāpyatiraudreṇa paryāvavurnabhastalam || 99 ||
meaning:
ततस्ते प्रेरिता मेघास्तेन वातेन वेगिना |
रुद्रेणाप्यतिरौद्रेण पर्याववुर्नभस्तलम् || 99 ||
text_mt: Then those clouds, driven by that swift-moving wind / and by Rudra most terrible, surrounded the vault of the sky.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃvartākhyā mahāmeghā bhinnāñjanacayopamāḥ |
keciddhūmrā śoṇavarṇāḥ śuklāścitrāśca bhīṣaṇāḥ || 92 ||
meaning:
संवर्ताख्या महामेघा भिन्नाञ्जनचयोपमाः |
केचिद्धूम्रा शोणवर्णाः शुक्लाश्चित्राश्च भीषणाः || 92 ||
text_mt: The great clouds named Saṃvarta, resembling heaps of split collyrium, / some smoky, crimson-coloured, white, and variegated, were terrifying.

sanskrit_iast:
kecicca parvatākārāḥ kecinnāgasamaprabhāḥ |
prāsādasadṛśāḥ kecit krauñcavarṇāvibhīṣaṇāḥ || 93 ||
meaning:
केचिच्च पर्वताकाराः केचिन्नागसमप्रभाः |
प्रासादसदृशाः केचित् क्रौञ्चवर्णाविभीषणाः || 93 ||
text_mt: Some had the shape of mountains, some had the lustre of elephants, / some resembled palaces, and some were frightening with the colour of krauñca birds.

sanskrit_iast:
garjantste mahāmeghā varṣāṇāmadhikaṃ śatam |
vavṛṣustrīnatho lokān plāvayanto mahāsvanāḥ || 94 ||
meaning:
गर्जन्त्स्ते महामेघा वर्षाणामधिकं शतम् |
ववृषुस्त्रीनथो लोकान् प्लावयन्तो महास्वनाः || 94 ||
text_mt: Roaring, those great clouds, making a tremendous sound, / rained for more than a hundred years, submerging the three worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
atha stambhapramāṇena dhārāpātena vai dṛḍham |
dhārāsāreṇa mahatā pūritaṃ bhuvanatrayam || 95 ||
meaning:
अथ स्तम्भप्रमाणेन धारापातेन वै दृढम् |
धारासारेण महता पूरितं भुवनत्रयम् || 95 ||
text_mt: Then, by a downpour of streams as thick as pillars, / by a vast torrent of rain, the three worlds were completely filled.

sanskrit_iast:
ādhru vasthānamāsādya toyarāśau sthite tataḥ |
sa mukhādasṛjadvāyuṃ rudrarūpī janārdanaḥ || 96 ||
meaning:
आध्रु वस्थानमासाद्य तोयराशौ स्थिते ततः |
स मुखादसृजद्वायुं रुद्ररूपी जनार्दनः || 96 ||
text_mt: When the mass of waters reached as far as the pole-star's abode, / Janārdana in the form of Rudra then released a wind from his mouth.

sanskrit_iast:
tenaughavāyunākṣiptā meghāḥ saṃvatsarāñchatam |
avyāhatagatenāśu vidhvastā abhavaṃstataḥ || 97 ||
meaning:
तेनौघवायुनाक्षिप्ता मेघाः संवत्सराञ्छतम् |
अव्याहतगतेनाशु विध्वस्ता अभवंस्ततः || 97 ||
text_mt: Dispersed for a hundred years by that torrent-wind / of unobstructed course, the clouds were then quickly annihilated.

sanskrit_iast:
naṣṭeṣu teṣu megheṣu janalokādikaṃ punaḥ |
rudrastvābrahmabhuvanaṃ dhvaṃsayāmāsa nirdayaḥ || 98 ||
meaning:
नष्टेषु तेषु मेघेषु जनलोकादिकं पुनः |
रुद्रस्त्वाब्रह्मभुवनं ध्वंसयामास निर्दयः || 98 ||
text_mt: When those clouds were destroyed, merciless Rudra / then laid waste to the worlds from Janaloka onward, up to the realm of Brahmā.

sanskrit_iast:
vidhvasteṣu samasteṣu bhuvaneṣu viśeṣataḥ |
vinaṣṭe brahmaloke ca rudro'gād dvādaśāruṇān || 99 ||
meaning:
विध्वस्तेषु समस्तेषु भुवनेषु विशेषतः |
विनष्टे ब्रह्मलोके च रुद्रोऽगाद् द्वादशारुणान् || 99 ||
text_mt: When all the worlds were especially shattered / and the world of Brahmā was destroyed, Rudra went to the twelve suns.

sanskrit_iast:
sa gatvā dvādaśādityān vegena mahatā hariḥ |
agrasaccātijajvāla tairgarbhasthairdivākaraiḥ || 100 ||
meaning:
स गत्वा द्वादशादित्यान् वेगेन महता हरिः |
अग्रसच्चातिजज्वाल तैर्गर्भस्थैर्दिवाकरैः || 100 ||
text_mt: Having approached the twelve Ādityas with great speed, Hari / swallowed them, and he blazed exceedingly with those suns residing within his belly.

sanskrit_iast:
tato brahmāṇḍamāsādya rudraḥ kālāntakopamaḥ |
cūrṇīcakāra sakalaṃ muṣṭipeṣaṃ mahābalaḥ || 101 ||
meaning:
ततो ब्रह्माण्डमासाद्य रुद्रः कालान्तकोपमः |
चूर्णीचकार सकलं मुष्टिपेषं महाबलः || 101 ||
text_mt: Then, approaching the cosmic egg, Rudra, resembling the Death that ends a cosmic age, / mighty in strength, ground the whole of it to powder, like crushing it with a fist.

sanskrit_iast:
cūrṇīkurvantu brahmāṇḍaṃ pṛthivyapi vicūrṇitā |
toyāni ca samastāni sa dadhre yogato hariḥ || 102 ||
meaning:
चूर्णीकुर्वन्तु ब्रह्माण्डं पृथिव्यपि विचूर्णिता |
तोयानि च समस्तानि स दध्रे योगतो हरिः || 102 ||
text_mt: While the cosmic egg was being pulverized, the earth too was crushed, / and Hari by his yoga sustained all the waters.

sanskrit_iast:
yad brahmāṇḍādbahistoyaṃ sthitaṃ pūrvaṃ samantataḥ |
yadvābhyantargataṃ toyaṃ tat sarvañcaikatāṃ gatam || 103 ||
meaning:
यद् ब्रह्माण्डाद्बहिस्तोयं स्थितं पूर्वं समन्ततः |
यद्वाभ्यन्तर्गतं तोयं तत् सर्वञ्चैकतां गतम् || 103 ||
text_mt: The water that had stood previously on all sides outside the cosmic egg, / and the water that had been inside—it all became one.

sanskrit_iast:
ekībhūteṣu toyeṣu sarvavyāpiṣu sarvataḥ |
brahmāṇḍakhaṇḍapūrṇaudhaḥ plavannāsīt sa nauriva || 104 ||
meaning:
एकीभूतेषु तोयेषु सर्वव्यापिषु सर्वतः |
ब्रह्माण्डखण्डपूर्णौधः प्लवन्नासीत् स नौरिव || 104 ||
text_mt: When the waters had united, all-pervading in every direction, / the mass filled with fragments of the cosmic egg floated like a boat.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ pṛthivyāḥ sārantu gandhaṃ tanmātrakaṃ kramāt |
ambho jagrāha sakalaṃ vinaṣṭā pṛthivī tataḥ || 105 ||
meaning:
ततः पृथिव्याः सारन्तु गन्धं तन्मात्रकं क्रमात् |
अम्भो जग्राह सकलं विनष्टा पृथिवी ततः || 105 ||
text_mt: Then the water gradually absorbed the essence of earth, the subtle element of smell, / in its entirety; thereupon the earth was destroyed.

sanskrit_iast:
punaḥ sa rudrastejāṃsi garbhasthāni svakāyataḥ |
niḥsārayāmāsa punaḥ puñjobhūtāni bhīṣaṇaḥ || 106 ||
meaning:
पुनः स रुद्रस्तेजांसि गर्भस्थानि स्वकायतः |
निःसारयामास पुनः पुञ्जोभूतानि भीषणः || 106 ||
text_mt: Then that terrifying Rudra brought forth the fiery energies / that were within his belly out of his own body again, accumulated in a mass.

sanskrit_iast:
tāni tejāṃsi sakalaṃ jagṛhuḥ sarvataḥ sthitam |
antarbahiśca brahmāṇḍāttejo yaccānyato gatam || 107 ||
meaning:
तानि तेजांसि सकलं जगृहुः सर्वतः स्थितम् |
अन्तर्बहिश्च ब्रह्माण्डात्तेजो यच्चान्यतो गतम् || 107 ||
text_mt: Those fiery energies absorbed all that was located on all sides, / inside and outside the cosmic egg, and whatever fire had gone elsewhere.

sanskrit_iast:
jagadgataṃ sarvatejo gṛhītvā caikato jvalan |
raudrabrahmāṇḍakhaṇḍāni tejo'tha nyadahajjale || 108 ||
meaning:
जगद्गतं सर्वतेजो गृहीत्वा चैकतो ज्वलन् |
रौद्रब्रह्माण्डखण्डानि तेजोऽथ न्यदहज्जले || 108 ||
text_mt: Having absorbed all the fire found in the world and blazing as one, / the terrible fire then consumed the fragments of the cosmic egg in the water.

sanskrit_iast:
dagdhvā brahmāṇḍacūrṇāni tejāṃsyujjvalitāni ca |
jalebhyo rasatanmātraṃ sārabhūtaṃ tato'grahīt |
gṛhītasārāstā āpaḥ pranaṣṭāstejasā tataḥ || 109 ||
meaning:
दग्ध्वा ब्रह्माण्डचूर्णानि तेजांस्युज्ज्वलितानि च |
जलेभ्यो रसतन्मात्रं सारभूतं ततोऽग्रहीत् |
गृहीतसारास्ता आपः प्रनष्टास्तेजसा ततः || 109 ||
text_mt: Having burned the dust of the cosmic egg, the ignited fiery energies / then absorbed from the waters the subtle element of taste, which was their essence; / stripped of their essence, those waters were then destroyed by the fire.

sanskrit_iast:
apsu naṣṭāsu tattejaḥ praviśyātha sadāgatiḥ |
ekībhūto mahābhāgo rūpaṃ tanmātramagrahīt || 110 ||
meaning:
अप्सु नष्टासु तत्तेजः प्रविश्याथ सदागतिः |
एकीभूतो महाभागो रूपं तन्मात्रमग्रहीत् || 110 ||
text_mt: When the waters were destroyed, that fire entered the wind, / and becoming one, the glorious [wind] absorbed the subtle element of form.

sanskrit_iast:
gṛhīte rūpatanmātre tejāṃsi sakalānyatha |
vinaṣṭāni tato vāyuḥ prabalo'bhūdavāritaḥ || 111 ||
meaning:
गृहीते रूपतन्मात्रे तेजांसि सकलान्यथ |
विनष्टानि ततो वायुः प्रबलोऽभूदवारितः || 111 ||
text_mt: When the subtle element of form was absorbed, all the fiery energies then / were destroyed; thereupon the wind became powerful and unrestrained.

sanskrit_iast:
mahāsvanaṃ tato vāyumāsādyāgniriva jvalan |
rudraḥ saṃkṣobhayāmāsa tadākāśaṃ svayaṃ tataḥ || 112 ||
meaning:
महास्वनं ततो वायुमासाद्याग्निरिव ज्वलन् |
रुद्रः संक्षोभयामास तदाकाशं स्वयं ततः || 112 ||
text_mt: Then, having reached the loudly roaring wind, Rudra, blazing like fire, / himself agitated space at that time.

sanskrit_iast:
tena saṃkṣubdhamākāśamagrahīnmarutastataḥ |
tadgataṃ sparśatanmātraṃ tato naṣṭaḥ prabhañjanaḥ || 113 ||
meaning:
तेन संक्षुब्धमाकाशमग्रहीन्मरुतस्ततः |
तद्गतं स्पर्शतन्मात्रं ततो नष्टः प्रभञ्जनः || 113 ||
text_mt: Agitated by him, space then absorbed the subtle element of touch / residing in the wind; thereupon the wind was destroyed.

sanskrit_iast:
naṣṭe vāyau tato rudra ākāśāt sāramagrahīt |
śabdatanmātrakaṃ tasmin gṛhīte vigataṃ viyat || 114 ||
meaning:
नष्टे वायौ ततो रुद्र आकाशात् सारमग्रहीत् |
शब्दतन्मात्रकं तस्मिन् गृहीते विगतं वियत् || 114 ||
text_mt: When the wind was destroyed, Rudra then absorbed from space its essence, / the subtle element of sound; when that was absorbed, space vanished.

sanskrit_iast:
naṣṭe nabhasi rudro'sau kāye brāhme tadāviśat |
brāhmaṃ tadākulaṃ kāyaṃ nirādhāraṃ nirākulam |
viveśa vaiṣṇave kāye śaṅkhacakragadādhare || 115 ||
meaning:
नष्टे नभसि रुद्रोऽसौ काये ब्राह्मे तदाविशत् |
ब्राह्मं तदाकुलं कायं निराधारं निराकुलम् |
विवेश वैष्णवे काये शङ्खचक्रगदाधरे || 115 ||
text_mt: When the sky was destroyed, that Rudra then entered the body of Brahmā; / that confused, supportless body of Brahmā became untroubled / and entered the body of Viṣṇu, who bears the conch, disc, and mace.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ śaurirmahātejāḥ kāyaṃ tat pāñcabhautikam |
śaṅkhacakragadāśārṅgavarāsidharamacyutam |
svaśaktyā saṃjāhārāśu sāramādāya sarvataḥ || 116 ||
meaning:
ततः शौरिर्महातेजाः कायं तत् पाञ्चभौतिकम् |
शङ्खचक्रगदाशार्ङ्गवरासिधरमच्युतम् |
स्वशक्त्या संजाहाराशु सारमादाय सर्वतः || 116 ||
text_mt: Then Śauri of great splendour, the imperishable one bearing the conch, disc, mace, Śārṅga bow, and excellent sword, / quickly retracted by his own power that elemental body, / having taken back its essence from everywhere.

sanskrit_iast:
nirādhāraṃ nirākāraṃ niḥsattvaṃ niravagraham |
ānandamayamadvaitaṃ dvaitahīnāviśeṣaṇam || 117 ||
meaning:
निराधारं निराकारं निःसत्त्वं निरवग्रहम् |
आनन्दमयमद्वैतं द्वैतहीनाविशेषणम् || 117 ||
text_mt: without support, without form, devoid of being, without restraint, / consisting of bliss, non-dual, free from duality and distinctions,

sanskrit_iast:
na sthūlaṃ na ca sūkṣmaṃ yajjñānaṃ nityaṃ nirañjanam |
ekamāsīt paraṃ brahma svaprakāśa samantataḥ || 118 ||
meaning:
न स्थूलं न च सूक्ष्मं यज्ज्ञानं नित्यं निरञ्जनम् |
एकमासीत् परं ब्रह्म स्वप्रकाश समन्ततः || 118 ||
text_mt: neither gross nor subtle, which is eternal and untainted consciousness: / the one Supreme Brahman existed, self-luminous on all sides.

sanskrit_iast:
nāho na rātrirna viyanna pṛthvī nāsīttamo jyotirabhūnnacānyat |
śrotrādibuddhyādyupalabhyamekaṃ prādhānikaṃ brahma pumāṃstadāsīt || 119 ||
meaning:
नाहो न रात्रिर्न वियन्न पृथ्वी नासीत्तमो ज्योतिरभून्नचान्यत् |
श्रोत्रादिबुद्ध्याद्युपलभ्यमेकं प्राधानिकं ब्रह्म पुमांस्तदासीत् || 119 ||
text_mt: There was neither day nor night, neither sky nor earth; there was no darkness, nor was there light, nor anything else. / At that time, Brahman alone existed as Puruṣa, the source of pradhāna, knowable through hearing, the intellect, and the rest.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ yāvatsthitāṃ sṛṣṭistāvat kālamasṛṣṭikam |
āsīdekaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ tataḥ sṛṣṭiḥ pravartate || 120 ||
meaning:
एवं यावत्स्थितां सृष्टिस्तावत् कालमसृष्टिकम् |
आसीदेकं परं तत्त्वं ततः सृष्टिः प्रवर्तते || 120 ||
text_mt: As long as creation remains, for so long a period without creation / the one Supreme Reality existed; from it creation proceeds.

sanskrit_iast:
prakṛtau saṃsthito yasmāt sarvatanmātrasañcayaḥ |
ahaṅkāraṃ mahattattvaṃ gato yat prākṛto layaḥ || 121 ||
meaning:
प्रकृतौ संस्थितो यस्मात् सर्वतन्मात्रसञ्चयः |
अहङ्कारं महत्तत्त्वं गतो यत् प्राकृतो लयः || 121 ||
text_mt: Because the collection of all subtle elements is deposited in Prakṛti, / [and because] the 'I'-maker and the principle of the Great dissolve [into it], it is a cosmic dissolution (prākṛtalaya).

sanskrit_iast:
prakṛtau saṃsthitaṃ vyaktamatīta pralayantu tat |
tasmāt prākṛtasaṃjño'yamucyate pratisañcaraḥ || 122 ||
meaning:
प्रकृतौ संस्थितं व्यक्तमतीत प्रलयन्तु तत् |
तस्मात् प्राकृतसंज्ञोऽयमुच्यते प्रतिसञ्चरः || 122 ||
text_mt: The manifest merges into Prakṛti when that dissolution has passed; / therefore this dissolution is called 'elemental' (prākṛta).

sanskrit_iast:
ayaṃ vaḥ kathito viprāḥ prākṛtākhyo mahālayaḥ |
ādisṛṣṭiṃ śṛṇuṣvemāṃ kathyamānāṃ mayā punaḥ || 123 ||
meaning:
अयं वः कथितो विप्राः प्राकृताख्यो महालयः |
आदिसृष्टिं शृणुष्वेमां कथ्यमानां मया पुनः || 123 ||
text_mt: This great dissolution, named elemental, has been related to you, O brāhmaṇas. / Hear now this original creation as it is told by me once more.

sanskrit_iast:
iti śrīkālikāpurāṇe saṃhārakathanaṃ nāma caturviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ || 24 ||
pañcaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
इति श्रीकालिकापुराणे संहारकथनं नाम चतुर्विंशोऽध्यायः || 24 ||
पञ्चविंशोऽध्यायः
text_mt: Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, named 'The Account of Dissolution', in the glorious Kālikāpurāṇa. / Twenty-fifth chapter.

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
kālo nāma svayaṃ devaḥ sṛṣṭisthityantakārakaḥ |
avicchinnaḥ sa pralayaṃ stena bhāgena kenacit || 1 ||
meaning:
कालो नाम स्वयं देवः सृष्टिस्थित्यन्तकारकः |
अविच्छिन्नः स प्रलयं स्तेन भागेन केनचित् || 1 ||
text_mt: Time itself is the god who brings about creation, maintenance, and destruction; / unbroken, it brought about dissolution through a certain portion of itself.

sanskrit_iast:
layabhāge vyatīte tu sisṛkṣā samajāyata |
jñānarūpasya ca tadā paramabrahmaṇo vibhoḥ || 2 ||
meaning:
लयभागे व्यतीते तु सिसृक्षा समजायत |
ज्ञानरूपस्य च तदा परमब्रह्मणो विभोः || 2 ||
text_mt: When the portion of dissolution had passed, the desire to create arose / in the all-pervading Supreme Brahman, whose nature is consciousness.

sanskrit_iast:
tato'sya prakṛtistena samyaksaṃkṣobhitā dhiyā |
sa kṣubdhā sarvakāryārthamabhūt sā triguṇātmikā || 3 ||
meaning:
ततोऽस्य प्रकृतिस्तेन सम्यक्संक्षोभिता धिया |
स क्षुब्धा सर्वकार्यार्थमभूत् सा त्रिगुणात्मिका || 3 ||
text_mt: Then His Prakṛti was thoroughly agitated by Him with intellect; / agitated, she, consisting of the three guṇas, became fit for all effects.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā sannidhimātreṇa gandhaḥ kṣobhāya jāyate |
manaso lokakartṛtvāttathāsau parameśvaraḥ || 4 ||
meaning:
यथा सन्निधिमात्रेण गन्धः क्षोभाय जायते |
मनसो लोककर्तृत्वात्तथासौ परमेश्वरः || 4 ||
text_mt: Just as an odor causes agitation of the mind / merely by its proximity, because He is the maker of the worlds, so does the Supreme Lord.

sanskrit_iast:
sa eva kṣobhako brahman kṣobhyaśca parameśvaraḥ |
sa saṃkocavikāśābhyāṃ pradhānatve'pi ca sthitaḥ || 5 ||
meaning:
स एव क्षोभको ब्रह्मन् क्षोभ्यश्च परमेश्वरः |
स संकोचविकाशाभ्यां प्रधानत्वेऽपि च स्थितः || 5 ||
text_mt: He alone is the agitator, O brāhmaṇa, and the Supreme Lord is also the agitated; / through contraction and expansion He abides even in the state of pradhāna.

sanskrit_iast:
icchāmātreṇa puruṣaḥ śṛṣṭyarthaṃ parameśvaraḥ |
tataḥ saṃkṣobhayāmāsa punareva jagatpatiḥ || 6 ||
meaning:
इच्छामात्रेण पुरुषः शृष्ट्यर्थं परमेश्वरः |
ततः संक्षोभयामास पुनरेव जगत्पतिः || 6 ||
text_mt: By mere desire, the Puruṣa, the Supreme Lord, for the sake of creation, / the Lord of the world, then agitated [Prakṛti] once again.

sanskrit_iast:
guṇasāmyāttatastasmāt kṣetrajñādhiṣṭhitāt tataḥ |
guṇavyañjanasaṃbhūtiḥ sargakāle babhūva ha || 7 ||
meaning:
गुणसाम्यात्ततस्तस्मात् क्षेत्रज्ञाधिष्ठितात् ततः |
गुणव्यञ्जनसंभूतिः सर्गकाले बभूव ह || 7 ||
text_mt: From that equilibrium of the guṇas, presided over by the Knower of the Field, / the emergence and manifestation of the guṇas occurred at the time of creation.

sanskrit_iast:
pradhānatattvādudbhutamīśvarecchāsamīritāt |
mahattatvaṃ prathamatastat pradhānaṃ samāvṛṇot || 8 ||
meaning:
प्रधानतत्त्वादुद्भुतमीश्वरेच्छासमीरितात् |
महत्तत्वं प्रथमतस्तत् प्रधानं समावृणोत् || 8 ||
text_mt: Arising from the principle of pradhāna impelled by the Lord's will, / the principle of the Great first emerged; pradhāna enveloped it.

sanskrit_iast:
pradhānenāvṛtāttasmādahaṅkāro vyajāyata |
vaikārikastaijasaśca bhūtādiścaiva tāmasaḥ || 9 ||
meaning:
प्रधानेनावृतात्तस्मादहङ्कारो व्यजायत |
वैकारिकस्तैजसश्च भूतादिश्चैव तामसः || 9 ||
text_mt: From that [Great principle] enveloped by pradhāna, the 'I'-maker was born: / the transforming (vaikārika), the energetic (taijasa), and the elemental (bhūtādi) which is tamasic.

sanskrit_iast:
trividho'yamahaṅkāro yo jāto mahato'grataḥ |
bhūtānāmindriyāṇāñca sa vai hetuḥ sanātanaḥ || 10 ||
meaning:
त्रिविधोऽयमहङ्कारो यो जातो महतोऽग्रतः |
भूतानामिन्द्रियाणाञ्च स वै हेतुः सनातनः || 10 ||
text_mt: This threefold 'I'-maker, which was born first from the Great, / is indeed the eternal cause of the elements and the senses.

sanskrit_iast:
sa mahāṃstamahaṅkāraṃ jātamātraṃ samāvṛṇot |
tanmātrāṇi tataḥ pañcajajñire'smāt samāvṛtāt || 11 ||
meaning:
स महांस्तमहङ्कारं जातमात्रं समावृणोत् |
तन्मात्राणि ततः पञ्चजज्ञिरेऽस्मात् समावृतात् || 11 ||
text_mt: That Great principle enveloped that 'I'-maker as soon as it was born; / from it, when enveloped, the five subtle elements were born.

sanskrit_iast:
prathamaṃ śabdatanmātraṃ sparśatanmātramantaram |
tṛtīyaṃ rūpatanmātraṃ rasatanmātrameva ca || 12 ||
meaning:
प्रथमं शब्दतन्मात्रं स्पर्शतन्मात्रमन्तरम् |
तृतीयं रूपतन्मात्रं रसतन्मात्रमेव च || 12 ||
text_mt: First the subtle element of sound, next the subtle element of touch, / third the subtle element of form, and the subtle element of taste,

sanskrit_iast:
pañcamaṃ gandhatanmātrametāni kramaśo'bhavan |
pratyekaṃ sarvatanmātramahaṅkāraḥ samāvṛṇot || 13 ||
meaning:
पञ्चमं गन्धतन्मात्रमेतानि क्रमशोऽभवन् |
प्रत्येकं सर्वतन्मात्रमहङ्कारः समावृणोत् || 13 ||
text_mt: and fifth the subtle element of smell: these came forth in succession. / The 'I'-maker enveloped each of all the subtle elements.

sanskrit_iast:
sasarja śabdatanmātrādākāśa śabdalakṣaṇam |
śabdamātraṃ tathākāśa bhūtādi sa samāvṛṇot || 14 ||
meaning:
ससर्ज शब्दतन्मात्रादाकाश शब्दलक्षणम् |
शब्दमात्रं तथाकाश भूतादि स समावृणोत् || 14 ||
text_mt: From the subtle element of sound, it created space characterised by sound; / the elemental enveloped that subtle sound and space.

sanskrit_iast:
śabdatanmātrasahitāt sparśatanmātratastataḥ |
vāyuṃ samabhavat sparśaguṇaḥ śabdasamanvitaḥ || 15 ||
meaning:
शब्दतन्मात्रसहितात् स्पर्शतन्मात्रतस्ततः |
वायुं समभवत् स्पर्शगुणः शब्दसमन्वितः || 15 ||
text_mt: From the subtle element of touch accompanied by the subtle element of sound, / wind arose, endowed with the quality of touch combined with sound.

sanskrit_iast:
ākāśavāyusaṃyuktādrūpatanmātratastataḥ |
tejaḥ samabhavaddīpta sarvatastadavardhataḥ || 16 ||
meaning:
आकाशवायुसंयुक्ताद्रूपतन्मात्रतस्ततः |
तेजः समभवद्दीप्त सर्वतस्तदवर्धतः || 16 ||
text_mt: From the subtle element of form joined with space and wind, / radiant fire arose; it grew in all directions.

sanskrit_iast:
tacchabdavat sparśavacca rūpavacca vyajāyata |
tato viyadvāyutejoyuktāttoyaṃ sasarja ha |
rasatanmātrataḥ samyak tena vyāpta samantaḥ || 17 ||
meaning:
तच्छब्दवत् स्पर्शवच्च रूपवच्च व्यजायत |
ततो वियद्वायुतेजोयुक्तात्तोयं ससर्ज ह |
रसतन्मात्रतः सम्यक् तेन व्याप्त समन्तः || 17 ||
text_mt: It came forth endowed with sound, touch, and form. / Then, from the subtle element of taste joined with space, wind, and fire, it created water; by it [all] was completely pervaded.

sanskrit_iast:
toyānyādhāraśaktiryā viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ |
sā dadhre'tha nirādhārāṇyanilāndolitāni vai || 18 ||
meaning:
तोयान्याधारशक्तिर्या विष्णोरमिततेजसः |
सा दध्रेऽथ निराधाराण्यनिलान्दोलितानि वै || 18 ||
text_mt: Then that supporting energy of Viṣṇu of boundless splendor / held the waters, which were without support and tossed by the wind.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣu bījaṃ prathamataḥ sasarja parameśvaraḥ |
tadaṇḍamabhavad haimaṃ sahasrāṃśusamaprabham || 19 ||
meaning:
तेषु बीजं प्रथमतः ससर्ज परमेश्वरः |
तदण्डमभवद् हैमं सहस्रांशुसमप्रभम् || 19 ||
text_mt: In them the Supreme Lord first cast a seed; / that became a golden egg, having the radiance of a thousand suns,

sanskrit_iast:
mahadādiviśeṣāntairārabdhaṃ sarvato vṛtam |
vārivahnyanilākāśaistamobhūtādinā bahiḥ |
vṛtaṃ daśaguṇairaṇḍaṃ bhūtādirmahatā tathā || 20 ||
meaning:
महदादिविशेषान्तैरारब्धं सर्वतो वृतम् |
वारिवह्न्यनिलाकाशैस्तमोभूतादिना बहिः |
वृतं दशगुणैरण्डं भूतादिर्महता तथा || 20 ||
text_mt: begun by [the principles] from the Great up to the specific [elements], enveloped on all sides / externally by water, fire, wind, space, and the tamasic elemental origin— / the egg was enveloped by ten times as much, and the elemental origin likewise by the Great.

sanskrit_iast:
bījaṃ yathā bāhyadalairvyāptamaṇḍaṃ tathā punah |
toyādibhistathā vyāptaṃ brahmāṇḍamatulaṃ dvijāḥ || 21 ||
meaning:
बीजं यथा बाह्यदलैर्व्याप्तमण्डं तथा पुनह् |
तोयादिभिस्तथा व्याप्तं ब्रह्माण्डमतुलं द्विजाः || 21 ||
text_mt: Just as a seed is covered by outer husks, so again was the egg; / the peerless cosmic egg was covered by water and the rest, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
tadaṇḍamadhye svayameva viṣṇurbrahmasvarūpaṃ vinidhāya kāyam |
divyena mānena sa varṣamekaṃ sthito'grahīdbījagaṇaṃ svabuddhyā || 22 ||
meaning:
तदण्डमध्ये स्वयमेव विष्णुर्ब्रह्मस्वरूपं विनिधाय कायम् |
दिव्येन मानेन स वर्षमेकं स्थितोऽग्रहीद्बीजगणं स्वबुद्ध्या || 22 ||
text_mt: Within that egg, Viṣṇu Himself, placing His body in the form of Brahmā, / remained for one year by divine reckoning, and grasped the collection of seeds with His intellect.

sanskrit_iast:
dhyānena cāṇḍaṃ svayameva kṛtvā dvidhā sa tasthau kṣaṇamātramasmin |
tadaiva tanmātragaṇaiḥ samastairgandhottarairbhūramunaiva sṛṣṭā || 23 ||
meaning:
ध्यानेन चाण्डं स्वयमेव कृत्वा द्विधा स तस्थौ क्षणमात्रमस्मिन् |
तदैव तन्मात्रगणैः समस्तैर्गन्धोत्तरैर्भूरमुनैव सृष्टा || 23 ||
text_mt: Having split the egg in two Himself through meditation, He remained within it for just a moment; / then the earth was created by Him alone out of all the groups of subtle elements, with smell predominant.

sanskrit_iast:
sparśasya śabdasya samastarūpaguṇasya gandhasya rasasya caiṣā |
ādhārabhūtā sakalaiḥ kṛtā yattanmātravargairakhilā dharitrī || 24 ||
meaning:
स्पर्शस्य शब्दस्य समस्तरूपगुणस्य गन्धस्य रसस्य चैषा |
आधारभूता सकलैः कृता यत्तन्मात्रवर्गैरखिला धरित्री || 24 ||
text_mt: Because this entire earth was made by all the classes of subtle elements, / it is the support of touch, of sound, of all qualities of form, of smell, and of taste.

sanskrit_iast:
jātastadutthaiḥ kanakacalo'sau jarāyubhiḥ parvatasañcayo'bhūt |
garbhādikaiḥ saptapayodhayastu skandhadvayena tridaśālayo'bhūt || 25 ||
meaning:
जातस्तदुत्थैः कनकचलोऽसौ जरायुभिः पर्वतसञ्चयोऽभूत् |
गर्भादिकैः सप्तपयोधयस्तु स्कन्धद्वयेन त्रिदशालयोऽभूत् || 25 ||
text_mt: From its inner parts arose the golden mountain; from the caul came the mass of mountains; / from the embryonic fluids came the seven oceans; from the two upper halves came the abode of the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
skandhadvayenāparadeśajena saptābhavannāgagṛhāṇi tāni |
pātālasaṃjñāni mahāsukhāni yatra svayaṃ syāt parato maheśaḥ || 26 ||
meaning:
स्कन्धद्वयेनापरदेशजेन सप्ताभवन्नागगृहाणि तानि |
पातालसंज्ञानि महासुखानि यत्र स्वयं स्यात् परतो महेशः || 26 ||
text_mt: From the two halves produced in the lower region arose those seven abodes of the Nāgas, / called Pātālas, full of great pleasures, where the Great Lord Himself resides beyond.

sanskrit_iast:
