meaning:
प्रसाद्यमानो धरया हरिर्णारायणोऽव्ययः |
शङ्खाग्रेण तदा पुत्रं पस्पर्श नरकाह्वयम् || 92 ||
text_mt: Being propitiated by the Earth, the imperishable Hari, Nārāyaṇa, / then touched her son named Naraka with the tip of his conch.

sanskrit_iast:
spṛṣṭamātro'tha hariṇā narako'bhūt sudarśanaḥ |
dṛṣṭaścotsāhavāṃścaiva balavān samapadyata || 93 ||
meaning:
स्पृष्टमात्रोऽथ हरिणा नरकोऽभूत् सुदर्शनः |
दृष्टश्चोत्साहवांश्चैव बलवान् समपद्यत || 93 ||
text_mt: As soon as he was touched by Hari, Naraka became fair to look upon; / and having regained his sight, he became energetic and strong.

sanskrit_iast:
tata utthāya narako hariṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum |
bhaktyā praṇamya govindaṃ sāṣṭāṅga ca muhurmuhuḥ || 94 ||
meaning:
तत उत्थाय नरको हरिं नारायणं प्रभुम् |
भक्त्या प्रणम्य गोविन्दं साष्टाङ्ग च मुहुर्मुहुः || 94 ||
text_mt: Then, rising up, Naraka bowed with devotion to Hari, the lord Nārāyaṇa, / prostrating with eight limbs before Govinda again and again.

sanskrit_iast:
nanāma pṛthivīṃ vīro jātasampratyayāstadā |
praṇamya ca mahābhāgāṃ bhaktyā paramayā yutaḥ || 95 ||
meaning:
ननाम पृथिवीं वीरो जातसम्प्रत्ययास्तदा |
प्रणम्य च महाभागां भक्त्या परमया युतः || 95 ||
text_mt: Then the hero, whose conviction had arisen, bowed to the Earth; / and having bowed to the highly fortunate one, endowed with supreme devotion,

sanskrit_iast:
prāñjaliḥ puratastasthau noktvā kiñcana vai bhiyā |
tatastadarthe pṛthivī mādhavaṃ samayācata || 96 ||
meaning:
प्राञ्जलिः पुरतस्तस्थौ नोक्त्वा किञ्चन वै भिया |
ततस्तदर्थे पृथिवी माधवं समयाचत || 96 ||
text_mt: he stood before [them] with folded hands, saying nothing out of fear. / Then on his behalf the Earth pleaded with Mādhava:

sanskrit_iast:
prasīda devadeveśa samayaṃ pratipālaya |
tvayāhaṃ tanayo datto mama sarvaṃ jagatpate |
etadarthe pratijñātaṃ yaddattaṃ pratipālaya || 97 ||
meaning:
प्रसीद देवदेवेश समयं प्रतिपालय |
त्वयाहं तनयो दत्तो मम सर्वं जगत्पते |
एतदर्थे प्रतिज्ञातं यद्दत्तं प्रतिपालय || 97 ||
text_mt: "Be gracious, O god of the lords of gods; protect the stipulation! / By you, O lord of the universe, a son was given to me, my all; / what was promised for his sake, which was granted, fulfill that!"

sanskrit_iast: bhagavānuvāca
meaning: भगवानुवाच

sanskrit_iast:
bhavatī yat suputrārthe māmayācata purā mayā |
tat sarvaṃt ava dattaṃ vai rājyaṃ dattaṃ ca vatsute || 98 ||
meaning:
भवती यत् सुपुत्रार्थे मामयाचत पुरा मया |
तत् सर्वंत् अव दत्तं वै राज्यं दत्तं च वत्सुते || 98 ||
text_mt: "What you requested of me formerly for the sake of your good son, / all that has indeed been given to you, and a kingdom has been given to your son."

sanskrit_iast:
ityuktvā bhagavān viṣṇurādāya narakāhvayam |
sārddhaṃ pṛthivyā gaṅgāyāṃ mamajja jagatāṃ prabhuḥ || 99 ||
meaning:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान् विष्णुरादाय नरकाह्वयम् |
सार्द्धं पृथिव्या गङ्गायां ममज्ज जगतां प्रभुः || 99 ||
text_mt: Having spoken thus, the lord Viṣṇu, the master of the worlds, / took the one named Naraka and submerged into the Gaṅgā together with the Earth.

sanskrit_iast:
nimajya kṣaṇamātreṇa prāgjyotiṣapuraṃ gataḥ |
madhyagaṃ kāmārūpasya kāmākhyā yatra nāyikāḥ || 100 ||
meaning:
निमज्य क्षणमात्रेण प्राग्ज्योतिषपुरं गतः |
मध्यगं कामारूपस्य कामाख्या यत्र नायिकाः || 100 ||
text_mt: Having dived, in just a moment he went to the city of Prāgjyotiṣa, / situated in the center of Kāmarūpa, where Kāmākhyā is the presiding mistress.

sanskrit_iast:
sa ca deśaḥ svarājyārthe pūrvaṃ suptaśca śambhunā |
kirātairbalibhiḥ krūrairajñerapi ca vāsitaḥ || 101 ||
meaning:
स च देशः स्वराज्यार्थे पूर्वं सुप्तश्च शम्भुना |
किरातैर्बलिभिः क्रूरैरज्ञेरपि च वासितः || 101 ||
text_mt: That region had previously been reserved by Śambhu for his own kingdom, / and it was inhabited by strong, cruel, and ignorant Kirātas.

sanskrit_iast:
rukmastambhanibhāṃstatra kirātān jñānavarjitān |
anarthamuṇḍitān madyamāṃsāśanaikatatparān || 102 ||
meaning:
रुक्मस्तम्भनिभांस्तत्र किरातान् ज्ञानवर्जितान् |
अनर्थमुण्डितान् मद्यमांसाशनैकतत्परान् || 102 ||
text_mt: There [were] the Kirātas resembling pillars of gold, devoid of knowledge, / uselessly shaven-headed, intent solely on consuming liquor and meat.

sanskrit_iast:
dadarśa viṣṇuḥ kupitān viṣṇuṃ dṛṣṭvā dvijarṣabhāḥ |
teṣāmadhipatistatra ghaṭako nāma vīryavān |
rukmastambhanibhastatraḥ pradīpta iva pāvakaḥ || 103 ||
meaning:
ददर्श विष्णुः कुपितान् विष्णुं दृष्ट्वा द्विजर्षभाः |
तेषामधिपतिस्तत्र घटको नाम वीर्यवान् |
रुक्मस्तम्भनिभस्तत्रः प्रदीप्त इव पावकः || 103 ||
text_mt: Viṣṇu saw them enraged upon seeing Viṣṇu, O best of the twice-born. / Their leader there, named Ghaṭaka, was mighty, / resembling a pillar of gold, like a blazing fire.

sanskrit_iast:
sa kroddhāccaturaṅgena balena mahatā yutaḥ |
āsasāda jagannāthaṃ narakaṃ ca mahāvalam || 104 ||
meaning:
स क्रोद्धाच्चतुरङ्गेन बलेन महता युतः |
आससाद जगन्नाथं नरकं च महावलम् || 104 ||
text_mt: Out of anger, accompanied by a great fourfold army, / he approached the Lord of the World and the mighty Naraka.

sanskrit_iast:
āsādya śaravarṣeṇa vavarṣa prabhumavyayam |
kirātaiḥ sahito rājā ghaṭakākhyaḥ kirātarāṭ || 105 ||
meaning:
आसाद्य शरवर्षेण ववर्ष प्रभुमव्ययम् |
किरातैः सहितो राजा घटकाख्यः किरातराट् || 105 ||
text_mt: Having approached, the king called Ghaṭaka, ruler of the Kirātas, / along with the Kirātas showered the imperishable Lord with a rain of arrows.

sanskrit_iast:
mādhavopi tadā putraṃ narakaṃ vīryavattaram |
presyāmāsa yuddhāya kirātanṛpatestadā || 106 ||
meaning:
माधवोपि तदा पुत्रं नरकं वीर्यवत्तरम् |
प्रेस्यामास युद्धाय किरातनृपतेस्तदा || 106 ||
text_mt: Mādhava then dispatched his son Naraka, of superior prowess, / to fight against the king of the Kirātas.

sanskrit_iast:
narako dhanurādāya saha tairbalavattaraiḥ |
yuyudhe suciraṃ tatra śastrāstrairbahudheritaiḥ || 107 ||
meaning:
नरको धनुरादाय सह तैर्बलवत्तरैः |
युयुधे सुचिरं तत्र शस्त्रास्त्रैर्बहुधेरितैः || 107 ||
text_mt: Taking his bow, Naraka fought for a long time there against those very powerful [foes] / with weapons and missiles discharged in many ways.

sanskrit_iast:
tato'sau bhallamādāya yojayitā dhanurguṇaiḥ |
śiraḥ kirātarājasya ciccheda narako balī || 108 ||
meaning:
ततोऽसौ भल्लमादाय योजयिता धनुर्गुणैः |
शिरः किरातराजस्य चिच्छेद नरको बली || 108 ||
text_mt: Then, taking a broad-headed arrow and fitting it to his bowstring, / the mighty Naraka severed the head of the Kirāta king.

sanskrit_iast:
mukhyān mukhyān kirātāṃśca bahūn senādhipāṃstathā |
jaghāna kupito vīraḥ keśarīva mataṅgajān || 109 ||
meaning:
मुख्यान् मुख्यान् किरातांश्च बहून् सेनाधिपांस्तथा |
जघान कुपितो वीरः केशरीव मतङ्गजान् || 109 ||
text_mt: Enraged, the hero killed many principal Kirātas and army commanders, / just as a lion [kills] elephants.

sanskrit_iast:
hate'tha nṛpatau kecit palāyanaparāyaṇāḥ |
kirātāḥ kecana punarnarakaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ || 110 ||
meaning:
हतेऽथ नृपतौ केचित् पलायनपरायणाः |
किराताः केचन पुनर्नरकं शरणं गताः || 110 ||
text_mt: When their king was slain, some of the Kirātas took to flight, / while others sought refuge with Naraka.

sanskrit_iast:
nihatya yudhyamānāṃstu saṃrakṣya śaraṇaṃ gatān |
narakaḥ pitaraṃ gatvā praṇamyātha nyavedayat || 111 ||
meaning:
निहत्य युध्यमानांस्तु संरक्ष्य शरणं गतान् |
नरकः पितरं गत्वा प्रणम्याथ न्यवेदयत् || 111 ||
text_mt: Having killed those who fought on, but protecting those who surrendered, / Naraka went to his father, bowed, and reported:

sanskrit_iast: naraka uvāca
meaning: नरक उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
hatastāta kirātānāmadhipo ghaṭako mayā |
senādhipāśca tasyānye kimanyat kuravāṇyaham || 112 ||
meaning:
हतस्तात किरातानामधिपो घटको मया |
सेनाधिपाश्च तस्यान्ये किमन्यत् कुरवाण्यहम् || 112 ||
text_mt: “Father, Ghaṭaka, the leader of the Kirātas, has been killed by me, / as well as his other army commanders. What else shall I do?”

sanskrit_iast: śrībhagavānuvāca
meaning: श्रीभगवानुवाच

sanskrit_iast:
kirātān jahi yāvattvaṃ devīṃ dikkaravāsinīm |
palāyamānān vidrāvya pālaya śaraṇaṃ gatān || 113 ||
meaning:
किरातान् जहि यावत्त्वं देवीं दिक्करवासिनीम् |
पलायमानान् विद्राव्य पालय शरणं गतान् || 113 ||
text_mt: “[Continue to] slay the Kirātas as far as the goddess Dikkaravāsinī; / routing those who flee, protect those who seek refuge.”

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ sa narako vīraḥ samāruhya sitaṃ gajam |
caturdantaṃ mahākāyaṃ kirātādhipavāhanam || 114 ||
meaning:
ततः स नरको वीरः समारुह्य सितं गजम् |
चतुर्दन्तं महाकायं किराताधिपवाहनम् || 114 ||
text_mt: Then the heroic Naraka, mounting the white elephant / with four tusks and a huge body, the mount of the Kirāta king,

sanskrit_iast:
airāvatasamaṃ vīrye vegena garuḍopamam |
kirātān drāvayāmāsa yāvaddikkaravāsinīm || 115 ||
meaning:
ऐरावतसमं वीर्ये वेगेन गरुडोपमम् |
किरातान् द्रावयामास यावद्दिक्करवासिनीम् || 115 ||
text_mt: equal to Airāvata in prowess and like Garuḍa in speed, / drove away the Kirātas as far as Dikkaravāsinī.

sanskrit_iast: pitaraṃ punarāgatya vacanaṃ cedamabravīt |
meaning: पितरं पुनरागत्य वचनं चेदमब्रवीत् |
text_mt: Returning again to his father, he spoke these words:

sanskrit_iast: naraka uvāca
meaning: नरक उवाच

sanskrit_iast: vidrāvitāḥ kirātāste sāgarāntaṃ samāśritāḥ || 116 ||
meaning: विद्राविताः किरातास्ते सागरान्तं समाश्रिताः || 116 ||
text_mt: “Those Kirātas have been driven away and have taken refuge at the edge of the ocean.

sanskrit_iast:
hataśca gha'kākhyo hi kirātādhipatirmahān |
veginaṃ gajamāruhya airāvatasamaṃ guṇaiḥ |
yadanyat karaṇīyaṃ me tadājñāpaya samprati || 117 ||
meaning:
हतश्च घऽकाख्यो हि किराताधिपतिर्महान् |
वेगिनं गजमारुह्य ऐरावतसमं गुणैः |
यदन्यत् करणीयं मे तदाज्ञापय सम्प्रति || 117 ||
text_mt: And the great ruler of the Kirātas, called Ghaṭaka, has been slain, / mounted on the swift elephant equal to Airāvata in virtues. / What else is to be done by me, command that now.”

sanskrit_iast: bhagavānuvāca
meaning: भगवानुवाच

sanskrit_iast:
karatoyā sadā gaṅgā pūrvabhāgāvadhiśrayā |
yāvallalitakāntāsti tāvadeva puraṃ tava || 118 ||
meaning:
करतोया सदा गङ्गा पूर्वभागावधिश्रया |
यावल्ललितकान्तास्ति तावदेव पुरं तव || 118 ||
text_mt: “The Karatoyā, the eternal Gaṅgā, forms the boundary of the eastern region; / as far as Lalitakāntā extends, that alone is your city.

sanskrit_iast:
atra devī mahābhāgā yoganidrā jagatprasūḥ |
kāmākhyārūpamāsthāya sadā tiṣṭhati śobhanā || 119 ||
meaning:
अत्र देवी महाभागा योगनिद्रा जगत्प्रसूः |
कामाख्यारूपमास्थाय सदा तिष्ठति शोभना || 119 ||
text_mt: Here the illustrious goddess Yoganidrā, mother of the universe, / assuming the form of Kāmākhyā, always dwells, auspicious.

sanskrit_iast:
atrāsti nadarājo'yaṃ lauhityo brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ |
atraiva daśadikapālāḥ sve sve pīṭhe vyavasthitāḥ || 120 ||
meaning:
अत्रास्ति नदराजोऽयं लौहित्यो ब्रह्मणः सुतः |
अत्रैव दशदिकपालाः स्वे स्वे पीठे व्यवस्थिताः || 120 ||
text_mt: Here is this king of rivers, Lauhitya, the son of Brahmā; / right here the guardians of the ten directions are established, each at their own seat.

sanskrit_iast:
atra svayaṃ mahādevo brahmā cāhaṃ vyavasthitaḥ |
candraḥ sūryaśca satataṃ vasato'tra ca putraka || 121 ||
meaning:
अत्र स्वयं महादेवो ब्रह्मा चाहं व्यवस्थितः |
चन्द्रः सूर्यश्च सततं वसतोऽत्र च पुत्रक || 121 ||
text_mt: Here Mahādeva, Brahmā, and I myself dwell; / the Moon and the Sun also constantly dwell here, O son.

sanskrit_iast:
sarve krīḍārthamāyātā rahasyaṃ deśamuttamam |
atra śrīrvasate bhadrā bhogyamatra tathā bahu || 122 ||
meaning:
सर्वे क्रीडार्थमायाता रहस्यं देशमुत्तमम् |
अत्र श्रीर्वसते भद्रा भोग्यमत्र तथा बहु || 122 ||
text_mt: All have come for sport to this secret, supreme region. / Here auspicious Śrī resides, and here is much to be enjoyed.

sanskrit_iast:
asya madhye sthito brahmā praṅnakṣatraṃ sasarja ha |
tataḥ prāgjyotiṣākhyeyaṃ purī śakrapurīsamā || 123 ||
meaning:
अस्य मध्ये स्थितो ब्रह्मा प्रङ्नक्षत्रं ससर्ज ह |
ततः प्राग्ज्योतिषाख्येयं पुरी शक्रपुरीसमा || 123 ||
text_mt: Stationed in its center, Brahmā created the star in the east; / therefore this city, equal to Indra's city, is named Prāgjyotiṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
atra tvaṃ vasa bhadraṃ te hyabhiṣikto mayā svayam |
kṛtadāraḥ sahāmātyai rājā bhūtvā mahābalaḥ || 124 ||
meaning:
अत्र त्वं वस भद्रं ते ह्यभिषिक्तो मया स्वयम् |
कृतदारः सहामात्यै राजा भूत्वा महाबलः || 124 ||
text_mt: Dwell here—may good fortune attend you!—consecrated by me myself, / having taken a wife, along with your ministers, becoming a mighty king.”

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
evamuktvā svayaṃ viṣṇuḥ śambhoranumate tadā |
sarvān kirātān pūrvasyāṃ sāgarānte nyaveśayat || 125 ||
meaning:
एवमुक्त्वा स्वयं विष्णुः शम्भोरनुमते तदा |
सर्वान् किरातान् पूर्वस्यां सागरान्ते न्यवेशयत् || 125 ||
text_mt: Having spoken thus, Viṣṇu himself, with the consent of Śambhu, / then settled all the Kirātas in the east, on the shore of the ocean.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvaṃ lalitakāntāyāḥ samādāyāvadhiṃ punaḥ |
yāvat sāgaraparyantaṃ kirātāstāvadāvasan || 126 ||
meaning:
पूर्वं ललितकान्तायाः समादायावधिं पुनः |
यावत् सागरपर्यन्तं किरातास्तावदावसन् || 126 ||
text_mt: Taking the boundary eastward from Lalitakāntā / as far as the ocean, the Kirātas dwelt there.

sanskrit_iast:
paścāllalitakāntāyāḥ derśa kṛtvāvadhiṃ punaḥ |
karatoyā nadīṃ yāvat kāmākhyānilayaṃ tu tat || 127 ||
meaning:
पश्चाल्ललितकान्तायाः देर्श कृत्वावधिं पुनः |
करतोया नदीं यावत् कामाख्यानिलयं तु तत् || 127 ||
text_mt: West of Lalitakāntā, however, marking the boundary / as far as the river Karatoyā, that is the abode of Kāmākhyā.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmāt kirātānutsārya vedaśāstrātigān bahūn |
dvijātīn vāsayāmāsa tatra varṇān sanātanān || 128 ||
meaning:
तस्मात् किरातानुत्सार्य वेदशास्त्रातिगान् बहून् |
द्विजातीन् वासयामास तत्र वर्णान् सनातनान् || 128 ||
text_mt: Having expelled from there the Kirātas who transgressed the Vedas and the treatises, / he settled twice-born men, the eternal social classes, there in great numbers.

sanskrit_iast:
vedādhyayanadānādi satataṃ vartate yathā |
tathā cakāra bhagavān munibhirvāsayan vibhuḥ || 129 ||
meaning:
वेदाध्ययनदानादि सततं वर्तते यथा |
तथा चकार भगवान् मुनिभिर्वासयन् विभुः || 129 ||
text_mt: So that study of the Vedas, gift-giving, and other rites might continuously go on, / the omnipresent Lord brought that about by settling [the land] with sages.

sanskrit_iast:
vedavādaratāḥ sarve dānadharmaparāyaṇāḥ |
nacirādabhavaddeśaḥ kāmarūpāhvayastadā || 130 ||
meaning:
वेदवादरताः सर्वे दानधर्मपरायणाः |
नचिरादभवद्देशः कामरूपाह्वयस्तदा || 130 ||
text_mt: All were devoted to the teachings of the Vedas and dedicated to charity and righteousness; / soon thereafter that region came to be known as Kāmarūpa.

sanskrit_iast:
tato vidarbharājasya putrīṃ māyāhvayāṃ hariḥ |
putrārthe varayāmāsa narakasya samāṃ guṇaiḥ || 131 ||
meaning:
ततो विदर्भराजस्य पुत्रीं मायाह्वयां हरिः |
पुत्रार्थे वरयामास नरकस्य समां गुणैः || 131 ||
text_mt: Then Hari chose for his son the daughter of the king of Vidarbha, / named Māyā, who was equal to Naraka in good qualities.

sanskrit_iast:
tāmudvāhya hṛṣīkeśastasmin puravare svayam |
tayā samaṃ svatanayaṃ rājatvenābhyaṣecayat || 132 ||
meaning:
तामुद्वाह्य हृषीकेशस्तस्मिन् पुरवरे स्वयम् |
तया समं स्वतनयं राजत्वेनाभ्यषेचयत् || 132 ||
text_mt: Having married her, Hṛṣīkeśa himself in that foremost of cities / consecrated his son to kingship along with her.

sanskrit_iast:
sūguptāṃ ca purīṃ cakre giridurgeṇa mādhava |
jaladurgaṃ sarvato bhadraṃ devairapi durāsadam || 133 ||
meaning:
सूगुप्तां च पुरीं चक्रे गिरिदुर्गेण माधव |
जलदुर्गं सर्वतो भद्रं देवैरपि दुरासदम् || 133 ||
text_mt: Mādhava made the city well-protected by a mountain fortress, / a water fortress, auspicious on all sides, hard to approach even for the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ kirātarājasya caturdantāḥ sudantinaḥ |
pañcaviṃśatisāhasrā mahāmātrakuthairyutāḥ || 134 ||
meaning:
ततः किरातराजस्य चतुर्दन्ताः सुदन्तिनः |
पञ्चविंशतिसाहस्रा महामात्रकुथैर्युताः || 134 ||
text_mt: Then Naraka took all the Kirāta king's fine tusked elephants / with four tusks, twenty-five thousand in number, equipped with drivers and saddlecloths,

sanskrit_iast:
yāni ratnānyanekāni sainyāni vividhāni ca |
aśvāścābharaṇāścaiva tatsarvaṃ narako'grahīt || 135 ||
meaning:
यानि रत्नान्यनेकानि सैन्यानि विविधानि च |
अश्वाश्चाभरणाश्चैव तत्सर्वं नरकोऽग्रहीत् || 135 ||
text_mt: the many jewels, the diverse armies, / the horses and ornaments.

sanskrit_iast:
yadyat subhūṣaṇaṃ rājño dhvajāścābharaṇāni ca |
tāni tāni svayaṃ viṣṇustanayasya dadau tadā || 136 ||
meaning:
यद्यत् सुभूषणं राज्ञो ध्वजाश्चाभरणानि च |
तानि तानि स्वयं विष्णुस्तनयस्य ददौ तदा || 136 ||
text_mt: Whatever fine regalia, banners, and ornaments belonged to the king, / Viṣṇu himself then gave all of those to his son.

sanskrit_iast:
rathaṃ ca pradadau tasmai triṣu lokeṣu durlabham |
lohāṣṭacakrasañchannamardhayojanavistṛtam || 137 ||
meaning:
रथं च प्रददौ तस्मै त्रिषु लोकेषु दुर्लभम् |
लोहाष्टचक्रसञ्छन्नमर्धयोजनविस्तृतम् || 137 ||
text_mt: He also gave him a chariot difficult to obtain in the three worlds, / furnished with eight iron wheels, half a yojana in breadth,

sanskrit_iast:
yuktamaśvasahasraiśca tathāṣṭābhirmanojavaiḥ |
ratnakāñcanacitrāḍhyaṃ vedikābhāgavistaram || 138 ||
meaning:
युक्तमश्वसहस्रैश्च तथाष्टाभिर्मनोजवैः |
रत्नकाञ्चनचित्राढ्यं वेदिकाभागविस्तरम् || 138 ||
text_mt: yoked with eight thousand horses swift as thought, / adorned with diverse jewels and gold, with an expansive platform,

sanskrit_iast:
vajradhvajena mahatā kāñcanena virājitam |
hemadaṇḍapatākāḍhyaṃ vaidūryamaṇikūbaram || 139 ||
meaning:
वज्रध्वजेन महता काञ्चनेन विराजितम् |
हेमदण्डपताकाढ्यं वैदूर्यमणिकूबरम् || 139 ||
text_mt: splendid with a great golden thunderbolt banner, / furnished with golden staff and pennants, with a pole of lapis lazuli,

sanskrit_iast:
siṃhavyāghrasamudbhūtaiścarmabhiśchāditaṃ sadā |
lohajālaiśca sañchannaṃ kiṃṅkaṇījālamālinam |
sarvapraharaṇairyuktaṃ bahumāyāsamanvitam || 140 ||
meaning:
सिंहव्याघ्रसमुद्भूतैश्चर्मभिश्छादितं सदा |
लोहजालैश्च सञ्छन्नं किंङ्कणीजालमालिनम् |
सर्वप्रहरणैर्युक्तं बहुमायासमन्वितम् || 140 ||
text_mt: always covered with hides taken from lions and tigers, / draped with iron mail, adorned with garlands of jingling bells, / equipped with all manner of weapons, and endowed with many magical illusions.

sanskrit_iast:
śaktiṃ ca pradadau tasmai sarvaśatruviśātanīm |
jvālāmālābhidīptāṅgīṃ ripukakṣāgnirūpiṇīm || 141 ||
meaning:
शक्तिं च प्रददौ तस्मै सर्वशत्रुविशातनीम् |
ज्वालामालाभिदीप्ताङ्गीं रिपुकक्षाग्निरूपिणीम् || 141 ||
text_mt: He also gave him a spear that destroys all enemies, / its body blazing with garlands of flames, having the form of a fire to the dry grass of foes.

sanskrit_iast:
imaṃ ca samayaṃ proce narakāna mahātmane |
narakasya hitāyeśo vasudhāyāḥ samakṣataḥ || 142 ||
meaning:
इमं च समयं प्रोचे नरकान महात्मने |
नरकस्य हितायेशो वसुधायाः समक्षतः || 142 ||
text_mt: The Lord also made this stipulation to the great-souled Naraka / for Naraka's welfare, in the presence of the Earth:

sanskrit_iast: śrībhagavānuvāca
meaning: श्रीभगवानुवाच

sanskrit_iast:
imāṃ śaktiṃ na hi bhavān prāṇānāṃ saṃśayaṃ vinā |
prayokṣyati kadācittu mānuṣeṣu viśeṣataḥ || 143 ||
meaning:
इमां शक्तिं न हि भवान् प्राणानां संशयं विना |
प्रयोक्ष्यति कदाचित्तु मानुषेषु विशेषतः || 143 ||
text_mt: “You must never employ this spear except when your life is in danger, / especially against human beings.

sanskrit_iast:
eṣā bhāryā ca vaidarbhī bhavataḥ sadṛśī guṇaiḥ |
bhavato jīvanaṃ yāvattāvat sthāsyati śobhanā || 144 ||
meaning:
एषा भार्या च वैदर्भी भवतः सदृशी गुणैः |
भवतो जीवनं यावत्तावत् स्थास्यति शोभना || 144 ||
text_mt: And this wife from Vidarbha, equal to you in virtues— / this lovely woman will remain as long as your life lasts.

sanskrit_iast:
tvaṃ tu prajāyai tretāyāṃ yatnavān vai bhaviṣyasi |
dvāparānte tu samprāpte prajā tatra bhaviṣyati || 145 ||
meaning:
त्वं तु प्रजायै त्रेतायां यत्नवान् वै भविष्यसि |
द्वापरान्ते तु सम्प्राप्ते प्रजा तत्र भविष्यति || 145 ||
text_mt: You will make efforts for offspring in the Tretā age, / and when the end of the Dvāpara age arrives, offspring will be born to you there.”

sanskrit_iast:
virodho munibhiḥ sārdhaṃ brāhmaṇairapi putraka |
na kadācittvayā kāryaścirañjīvitumicchatā || 146 ||
meaning:
विरोधो मुनिभिः सार्धं ब्राह्मणैरपि पुत्रक |
न कदाचित्त्वया कार्यश्चिरञ्जीवितुमिच्छता || 146 ||
text_mt: Hostility with sages or with brāhmaṇas, my son, / must never be caused by you if you wish to live long.

sanskrit_iast:
na rājabhirna devaiśca virodho yujyate tava |
mahādurgasya ve madhye vasato hyaparājite || 147 ||
meaning:
न राजभिर्न देवैश्च विरोधो युज्यते तव |
महादुर्गस्य वे मध्ये वसतो ह्यपराजिते || 147 ||
text_mt: Neither with kings nor with gods is hostility proper for you, / dwelling in the midst of a great fortress, O unconquered one.

sanskrit_iast:
divyayoṣidgaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ vasamāno'tibhogavān |
svaparvate kāmarūpe ciraṃ tvaṃ tiṣṭha tutraka || 148 ||
meaning:
दिव्ययोषिद्गणैः सार्धं वसमानोऽतिभोगवान् |
स्वपर्वते कामरूपे चिरं त्वं तिष्ठ तुत्रक || 148 ||
text_mt: Dwelling together with groups of celestial women, enjoying great pleasures, / stay long upon your own mountain in Kāmarūpa, my son.

sanskrit_iast:
mahādevīṃ mahāmāyāṃ jaganmātaramambikām |
kāmākhyāṃ tvaṃ vinā putra nānyadevaṃ yajiṣyasi || 149 ||
meaning:
महादेवीं महामायां जगन्मातरमम्बिकाम् |
कामाख्यां त्वं विना पुत्र नान्यदेवं यजिष्यसि || 149 ||
text_mt: Except for the great goddess Mahāmāyā, Ambikā, the mother of the world, / Kāmākhyā, my son, you shall worship no other deity.

sanskrit_iast:
ito'nyathā tvaṃ viharan gataprāṇo bhaviṣyasi |
tasmānnāka yatrena samayaṃ pranipālaya || 150 ||
meaning:
इतोऽन्यथा त्वं विहरन् गतप्राणो भविष्यसि |
तस्मान्नाक यत्रेन समयं प्रनिपालय || 150 ||
text_mt: Behaving otherwise than this, you will become bereft of life; / therefore, with effort, protect this covenant.

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
ityuktvā bhagavān viṣṇurnarakaṃ tanayaṃ svakam |
tamapāsya rahasyenāṃ pṛthivīṃ vākyamabravīt || 151 ||
meaning:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान् विष्णुर्नरकं तनयं स्वकम् |
तमपास्य रहस्येनां पृथिवीं वाक्यमब्रवीत् || 151 ||
text_mt: Having spoken thus to his son Naraka, the blessed Viṣṇu / set him aside and spoke these words in secret to the Earth:

sanskrit_iast:
yad yat pūrvaṃ mayā proktaṃ kartavyaṃ tava sundari |
tat sarvaṃ narakāyāśu bhūtyai samupadeśaya || 152 ||
meaning:
यद् यत् पूर्वं मया प्रोक्तं कर्तव्यं तव सुन्दरि |
तत् सर्वं नरकायाशु भूत्यै समुपदेशय || 152 ||
text_mt: "Whatever has been declared by me before as what ought to be done, O beautiful woman, / teach all that quickly to Naraka for his prosperity.

sanskrit_iast:
yadainaṃ tvaṃ svayaṃ hantuṃ māṃ jagaddhātri bhāṣase |
tadā tu mānuṣaḥ kaścinnarakaṃ nihaniṣyati || 153 ||
meaning:
यदैनं त्वं स्वयं हन्तुं मां जगद्धात्रि भाषसे |
तदा तु मानुषः कश्चिन्नरकं निहनिष्यति || 153 ||
text_mt: When you yourself speak to me to slay him, O supporter of the world, / then indeed a certain human being will slay Naraka."

sanskrit_iast: pṛthivyuvāca
meaning: पृथिव्युवाच

sanskrit_iast:
prajārthameṣa yatno me nindyaḥ syāt santatiṃ vinā |
tasmānnātha prayantānme santatiṃ pālayiṣyasi || 154 ||
meaning:
प्रजार्थमेष यत्नो मे निन्द्यः स्यात् सन्ततिं विना |
तस्मान्नाथ प्रयन्तान्मे सन्ततिं पालयिष्यसि || 154 ||
text_mt: "This effort of mine was for offspring; it would be reproachable without descendants; / therefore, O Lord, protect my lineage with effort."

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
evamastviti tāṃ viṣṇuḥ pṛthivīṃ prati pāvanaḥ |
narakaṃ ca samābhāṣya tatrāntardhimagāt kṣaṇāt || 155 ||
meaning:
एवमस्त्विति तां विष्णुः पृथिवीं प्रति पावनः |
नरकं च समाभाष्य तत्रान्तर्धिमगात् क्षणात् || 155 ||
text_mt: Saying 'So be it' to the Earth, the pure Viṣṇu, / after addressing Naraka, vanished from there in an instant.

sanskrit_iast:
gate harau nijasthānaṃ pṛthivī tanaraṃ svakam |
yat pūrvaṃ hariṇā proktaṃ tatra taṃ vyanayat svayam || 156 ||
meaning:
गते हरौ निजस्थानं पृथिवी तनरं स्वकम् |
यत् पूर्वं हरिणा प्रोक्तं तत्र तं व्यनयत् स्वयम् || 156 ||
text_mt: When Hari had gone to his own abode, the Earth personally / led her son into that which had been previously spoken by Hari.

sanskrit_iast:
narako'pi tadā dhīmān vedaśāstrārthapāragaḥ |
brahmaṇyanītikuśalo vadānyo dānatatparaḥ || 157 ||
meaning:
नरकोऽपि तदा धीमान् वेदशास्त्रार्थपारगः |
ब्रह्मण्यनीतिकुशलो वदान्यो दानतत्परः || 157 ||
text_mt: Then the wise Naraka, having mastered the meaning of the Vedas and treatises, / devoted to brāhmaṇas, skilled in policy, generous, intent on giving,

sanskrit_iast:
kāmākhyāpūjanarato nīlakūṭe mahāgirau |
mahābhogī mahāśrīmān hīnabādhaśca śatrubhiḥ |
suciraṃ rājyamakarocchakravattridaśālaye || 158 ||
meaning:
कामाख्यापूजनरतो नीलकूटे महागिरौ |
महाभोगी महाश्रीमान् हीनबाधश्च शत्रुभिः |
सुचिरं राज्यमकरोच्छक्रवत्त्रिदशालये || 158 ||
text_mt: devoted to worshipping Kāmākhyā on the great mountain Nīlakūṭa, / possessing great enjoyment, greatly glorious, free from trouble by enemies, / ruled the kingdom for a very long time, like Śakra in the abode of the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
tato videharājo'pi śrutvaiva narakaśriyam |
saputrabhāryaḥ saguṇo narakaṃ draṣṭumabhyagāt || 159 ||
meaning:
ततो विदेहराजोऽपि श्रुत्वैव नरकश्रियम् |
सपुत्रभार्यः सगुणो नरकं द्रष्टुमभ्यगात् || 159 ||
text_mt: Then the king of Videha as well, hearing of Naraka's prosperity, / endowed with virtues, went to see Naraka together with his son and wife.

sanskrit_iast:
prāgjyotiṣaṃ puraṃ gatvā kāmarūpāntarasthitam |
dadarśa narakaṃ rājā śaraccandrasamaṃ śriyā || 160 ||
meaning:
प्राग्ज्योतिषं पुरं गत्वा कामरूपान्तरस्थितम् |
ददर्श नरकं राजा शरच्चन्द्रसमं श्रिया || 160 ||
text_mt: Having gone to the city of Prāgjyotiṣa situated within Kāmarūpa, / the king saw Naraka resembling the autumn moon in splendor.

sanskrit_iast:
prāgjyotiṣaṃ puraṃ mene sa rājā tvamarāvatīm |
devendraṃ narakaṃ mene satparicchadabhūṣaṇam || 161 ||
meaning:
प्राग्ज्योतिषं पुरं मेने स राजा त्वमरावतीम् |
देवेन्द्रं नरकं मेने सत्परिच्छदभूषणम् || 161 ||
text_mt: That king regarded the city of Prāgjyotiṣa as Amarāvatī, / and regarded Naraka, with his fine attendants and ornaments, as the lord of the gods.

sanskrit_iast: janaka uvāca
meaning: जनक उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
tato mahiṣyai tat sarvaṃ janako vākyamabravīt |
eṣa te pālitasutaḥ śrīmān narakasaṃjñakaḥ || 162 ||
meaning:
ततो महिष्यै तत् सर्वं जनको वाक्यमब्रवीत् |
एष ते पालितसुतः श्रीमान् नरकसंज्ञकः || 162 ||
text_mt: Then Janaka said all these words to his queen: / "This is your foster-son named glorious Naraka,

sanskrit_iast:
pṛthivyā dayitaḥ putraḥ sañjāto ghṛṣṭirūpiṇā |
viṣṇunā jagadīśena tvamenaṃ paśya saṅgatam || 163 ||
meaning:
पृथिव्या दयितः पुत्रः सञ्जातो घृष्टिरूपिणा |
विष्णुना जगदीशेन त्वमेनं पश्य सङ्गतम् || 163 ||
text_mt: the beloved son of the Earth, born from Viṣṇu, / the Lord of the world in the form of a boar; see him joined with her."

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
ityuktvā janako rājā yathā vṛttaṃ tathā purā |
vṛttāntaṃ kathayāmāsa narako jātavān yathā || 164 ||
meaning:
इत्युक्त्वा जनको राजा यथा वृत्तं तथा पुरा |
वृत्तान्तं कथयामास नरको जातवान् यथा || 164 ||
text_mt: Having spoken thus, King Janaka recounted the story / just as it had happened before, how Naraka was born.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastatra ciraṃ sthitvā prāgjyotiṣapure mudā |
videhādhipatī rājā narakeṇa prapūjitaḥ || 165 ||
meaning:
ततस्तत्र चिरं स्थित्वा प्राग्ज्योतिषपुरे मुदा |
विदेहाधिपती राजा नरकेण प्रपूजितः || 165 ||
text_mt: Then, having stayed there long with joy in the city of Prāgjyotiṣa, / the king, ruler of Videha, worshipped by Naraka,

sanskrit_iast: svasthānaṃ gatavāṃstasmāt svagaṇaiḥ parivāritaḥ || 166 ||
meaning: स्वस्थानं गतवांस्तस्मात् स्वगणैः परिवारितः || 166 ||
text_mt: went from there to his own place, surrounded by his own retinues.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ sa narako jātaḥ pṛthivyāstanayastadā |
hīnāsurasvabhāvaḥ saṃvijahāra ciraṃ kṣitau || 167 ||
meaning:
एवं स नरको जातः पृथिव्यास्तनयस्तदा |
हीनासुरस्वभावः संविजहार चिरं क्षितौ || 167 ||
text_mt: Thus Naraka was born as the son of the Earth at that time; / devoid of demonic nature, he sported for a long time on earth.

sanskrit_iast:
iti śrīkālikāpurāṇe narakābhiṣecane'ṣtatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ || 38 ||
ekonacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
इति श्रीकालिकापुराणे नरकाभिषेचनेऽष्तत्रिंशोऽध्यायः || 38 ||
एकोनचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः
text_mt:
Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, on the consecration of Naraka, in the glorious Kālikāpurāṇa.
Chapter thirty-nine

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
sa rājā narakaḥ śrīmāṃścirañjīvī mahābhujaḥ |
mānuṣeṇaiva bhāvena ciraṃ rājyamathākarot || 1 ||
meaning:
स राजा नरकः श्रीमांश्चिरञ्जीवी महाभुजः |
मानुषेणैव भावेन चिरं राज्यमथाकरोत् || 1 ||
text_mt: That king Naraka, glorious, long-lived, and mighty-armed, / then ruled the kingdom for a long time in a purely human manner.

sanskrit_iast:
tretāyāṃ ca vyatītāyāṃ dvāparasya tu śeṣataḥ |
abhavacchoṇitapure bāṇo nāma mahāsuraḥ || 2 ||
meaning:
त्रेतायां च व्यतीतायां द्वापरस्य तु शेषतः |
अभवच्छोणितपुरे बाणो नाम महासुरः || 2 ||
text_mt: When the Tretā age had passed and toward the end of the Dvāpara age, / in Śoṇitapura there lived a great asura named Bāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyāgnidurgaṃ nagaraṃ sa ca śambhusakho balī |
sahasrabāhurdurdharṣaḥ priyaḥ putraḥ sa vai baleḥ || 3 ||
meaning:
तस्याग्निदुर्गं नगरं स च शम्भुसखो बली |
सहस्रबाहुर्दुर्धर्षः प्रियः पुत्रः स वै बलेः || 3 ||
text_mt: His city was a fortress of fire; he was a friend of Śambhu, powerful, / thousand-armed, unassailable, and the beloved son of Bali.

sanskrit_iast:
narakeṇa samaṃ tasya mahāmaitrī vyajāyata |
amanāgamanānnityamanyonyānugrahaistathā |
tayorabhūd mahāprītiḥ pavanānalayoryathā || 4 ||
meaning:
नरकेण समं तस्य महामैत्री व्यजायत |
अमनागमनान्नित्यमन्योन्यानुग्रहैस्तथा |
तयोरभूद् महाप्रीतिः पवनानलयोर्यथा || 4 ||
text_mt: A great friendship arose between him and Naraka; / from constant visits and mutual favors, / there was great affection between the two, as between wind and fire.

sanskrit_iast:
sa ca bāṇaḥ samārādhya mahādevaṃ jagatprabhum |
āsureṇātha bhāvena vyacaraccākutobhayaḥ || 5 ||
meaning:
स च बाणः समाराध्य महादेवं जगत्प्रभुम् |
आसुरेणाथ भावेन व्यचरच्चाकुतोभयः || 5 ||
text_mt: And that Bāṇa, having propitiated Mahādeva, the lord of the world, / then roamed about with demonic nature, fearing nothing from anywhere.

sanskrit_iast:
tatsaṃsargāt sa narako dṛṣṭvā tasyādbhutāṃ kṛtim |
tenaiva saha bhāvena vihartumupacakrame || 6 ||
meaning:
तत्संसर्गात् स नरको दृष्ट्वा तस्याद्भुतां कृतिम् |
तेनैव सह भावेन विहर्तुमुपचक्रमे || 6 ||
text_mt: From associating with him and seeing his wondrous conduct, Naraka / began to behave with that very same nature.

sanskrit_iast:
na brāhmaṇān pūjayati yathā pūrvaṃ tathā dvijāḥ |
na ca yajñeṣu dāneṣu pūrvavanmuditaḥ sa ca || 7 ||
meaning:
न ब्राह्मणान् पूजयति यथा पूर्वं तथा द्विजाः |
न च यज्ञेषु दानेषु पूर्ववन्मुदितः स च || 7 ||
text_mt: He did not honor brāhmaṇas as before, O twice-born ones, / nor did he rejoice in sacrifices and gifts as he had done previously;

sanskrit_iast:
na tathā viṣṇumabhyeti pṛthivīṃ vāpi nārcati |
kāmākhyāyāṃ tathā bhaktistadā tasyātha nābhavat || 8 ||
meaning:
न तथा विष्णुमभ्येति पृथिवीं वापि नार्चति |
कामाख्यायां तथा भक्तिस्तदा तस्याथ नाभवत् || 8 ||
text_mt: he did not approach Viṣṇu in that way, nor did he worship the Earth; / nor was there his devotion to Kāmākhyā as before.

sanskrit_iast:
etasminnantare dhātustanayo munisattamaḥ |
vasiṣṭho nāma kāmākhyāṃ draṣṭuṃ prāgjyotiṣaṃ gataḥ || 9 ||
meaning:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे धातुस्तनयो मुनिसत्तमः |
वसिष्ठो नाम कामाख्यां द्रष्टुं प्राग्ज्योतिषं गतः || 9 ||
text_mt: In the meantime, the son of Dhātṛ, the best of sages, / named Vasiṣṭha, went to Prāgjyotiṣa to see Kāmākhyā.

sanskrit_iast:
tāṃ durgābhyantare nīlakūṭadevīṃ vyavasthitām |
draṣṭuṃ gantuṃ vasiṣṭhasya na dvāraṃ narako hyadāt || 10 ||
meaning:
तां दुर्गाभ्यन्तरे नीलकूटदेवीं व्यवस्थिताम् |
द्रष्टुं गन्तुं वसिष्ठस्य न द्वारं नरको ह्यदात् || 10 ||
text_mt: To Vasiṣṭha, who had come to see that goddess of Nīlakūṭa / established within the fortress, Naraka did not grant passage through the gate.

sanskrit_iast:
tato vasiṣṭhaḥ kupito vacanaṃ paruṣaṃ muniḥ |
jagāda narakaṃ vīraṃ garhayanmunisattamaḥ || 11 ||
meaning:
ततो वसिष्ठः कुपितो वचनं परुषं मुनिः |
जगाद नरकं वीरं गर्हयन्मुनिसत्तमः || 11 ||
text_mt: Then the sage Vasiṣṭha, enraged, spoke harsh words, / reviling the hero Naraka, best of sages:

sanskrit_iast: vasiṣṭha uvāca
meaning: वसिष्ठ उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
kathaṃ pṛthivyāstanayo varāhasya suto'ñjasā |
devīṃ draṣṭuṃ brāhmaṇasya na dadāsi tathāgataḥ || 12 ||
meaning:
कथं पृथिव्यास्तनयो वराहस्य सुतोऽञ्जसा |
देवीं द्रष्टुं ब्राह्मणस्य न ददासि तथागतः || 12 ||
text_mt: "How is it that, being the son of the Earth and the son of the Boar, / behaving in such a way, you do not allow a brāhmaṇa to see the Goddess?

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃ te kulocitaṃ karma tvaṃ karoṣi dharātmaja |
devīṃ prāgjyotiṣaṃ gatvā pūjayiṣye jaganmayīm || 13 ||
meaning:
किं ते कुलोचितं कर्म त्वं करोषि धरात्मज |
देवीं प्राग्ज्योतिषं गत्वा पूजयिष्ये जगन्मयीम् || 13 ||
text_mt: Are you performing an action appropriate to your lineage, O son of the Earth? / Having gone to Prāgjyotiṣa, I will worship the Goddess who consists of the world."

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ sa narako rājā prāptakālaḥ kṣite sutaḥ |
paruṣeṇātha vākyena tamākṣipya nirastavān || 14 ||
meaning:
ततः स नरको राजा प्राप्तकालः क्षिते सुतः |
परुषेणाथ वाक्येन तमाक्षिप्य निरस्तवान् || 14 ||
text_mt: Then that king Naraka, whose time had arrived, the son of the Earth, / having insulted him with harsh speech, turned him away.

sanskrit_iast: tato muniḥ sa kupitaḥ śaśāpa narakaṃ nṛpam |
meaning: ततो मुनिः स कुपितः शशाप नरकं नृपम् |
text_mt: Then that enraged sage cursed King Naraka:

sanskrit_iast: vaśiṣṭha uvāca
meaning: वशिष्ठ उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
nacirād yena jāto'si tena mānuṣarūpiṇā |
maraṇaṃ bhavitā pāpa varāhakulapāṃsana || 15 ||
meaning:
नचिराद् येन जातोऽसि तेन मानुषरूपिणा |
मरणं भविता पाप वराहकुलपांसन || 15 ||
text_mt: "Before long, by him from whom you were born, having assumed a human form, / your death will come to pass, O evil one, defiler of the Boar's lineage!

sanskrit_iast:
mṛte tvayi mahādevīṃ kāmākhyāṃ jagatāṃ prasūm |
pūjayiṣyāmyahaṃ pāpa tiṣṭha yāsye svamālayam || 16 ||
meaning:
मृते त्वयि महादेवीं कामाख्यां जगतां प्रसूम् |
पूजयिष्याम्यहं पाप तिष्ठ यास्ये स्वमालयम् || 16 ||
text_mt: When you are dead, I will worship the great goddess Kāmākhyā, / the mother of the worlds, O evil one! Stay; I shall go to my own abode.

sanskrit_iast:
tvaṃ yāvajjivitā pāpa kāmākhyāpi jagatprasūḥ |
sarvaiḥ parikaraiḥ sārdhamantardhānāya gacchatu || 17 ||
meaning:
त्वं यावज्जिविता पाप कामाख्यापि जगत्प्रसूः |
सर्वैः परिकरैः सार्धमन्तर्धानाय गच्छतु || 17 ||
text_mt: As long as you are alive, O evil one, may even Kāmākhyā, the mother of the world, / depart into invisibility along with all her attendants!"

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
ityuktvā brahmaputraḥ sa svasthānaṃ gatavān muniḥ |
vasiṣṭhastena bhaumena nirastaḥ kupito bhṛśam || 18 ||
meaning:
इत्युक्त्वा ब्रह्मपुत्रः स स्वस्थानं गतवान् मुनिः |
वसिष्ठस्तेन भौमेन निरस्तः कुपितो भृशम् || 18 ||
text_mt: Having spoken thus, that sage, the son of Brahmā, went to his own place; / Vasiṣṭha, turned away by that son of the Earth, was exceedingly enraged.

sanskrit_iast:
gate vasiṣṭhe narakaḥ śīghraṃ vismayasaṃyutaḥ |
jagāma devībhavanaṃ nīlakūṭaṃ mahāgirim || 19 ||
meaning:
गते वसिष्ठे नरकः शीघ्रं विस्मयसंयुतः |
जगाम देवीभवनं नीलकूटं महागिरिम् || 19 ||
text_mt: When Vasiṣṭha had departed, Naraka, filled with astonishment, / quickly went to the abode of the goddess on the great mountain Nīlakūṭa.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra gatvā na cāpaśyat kāmākhyā kāmarūpiṇīm |
na yonimaṇḍalaṃ tasyāḥ sarvān parikarāṃstathā || 20 ||
meaning:
तत्र गत्वा न चापश्यत् कामाख्या कामरूपिणीम् |
न योनिमण्डलं तस्याः सर्वान् परिकरांस्तथा || 20 ||
text_mt: Having gone there, he did not see Kāmākhyā who assumes forms at will, / nor her pubic region, nor all her attendants.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ sa vimanā bhūtvā kṣitiṃ sasmāra mātaram |
pitaraṃ ca jagannāthaṃ narakaḥ prabhumavyayam || 21 ||
meaning:
ततः स विमना भूत्वा क्षितिं सस्मार मातरम् |
पितरं च जगन्नाथं नरकः प्रभुमव्ययम् || 21 ||
text_mt: Then, downcast, Naraka remembered his mother, the Earth, / and his father, the imperishable Lord, master of the universe.

sanskrit_iast:
na tāvapi tadā yātau tasya pratyakṣatāṃ dvijāḥ |
vyutkrāntasamayasyeti nītihīnasya śambhave || 22 ||
meaning:
न तावपि तदा यातौ तस्य प्रत्यक्षतां द्विजाः |
व्युत्क्रान्तसमयस्येति नीतिहीनस्य शम्भवे || 22 ||
text_mt: O twice-born ones, neither of them appeared before him then, / because he, destitute of proper conduct, had violated the covenant regarding Śambhu.

sanskrit_iast:
ciraṃ pratīkṣya tau tatra bhaumo vajradhvajastadā |
aprāptakṣtiviṣṇuḥ sa saśokaḥ svaṃ niveśanam || 23 ||
meaning:
चिरं प्रतीक्ष्य तौ तत्र भौमो वज्रध्वजस्तदा |
अप्राप्तक्ष्तिविष्णुः स सशोकः स्वं निवेशनम् || 23 ||
text_mt: Having waited for them there for a long time, the earth-born Vajradhvaja then, / not having attained the Earth and Viṣṇu, went grieving to his own dwelling.

sanskrit_iast:
sa gacchan svagṛhaṃ bhaumaḥ purīṃ svāṃ dṛṣṭavāṃstu saḥ |
pūrvaśriyā parityaktāṃ malināṃ vanitāmiva || 24 ||
meaning:
स गच्छन् स्वगृहं भौमः पुरीं स्वां दृष्टवांस्तु सः |
पूर्वश्रिया परित्यक्तां मलिनां वनितामिव || 24 ||
text_mt: Going to his home, that son of the Earth saw his city, / bereft of its former splendour, like a bedraggled woman.

sanskrit_iast:
devyāmantarhitāyāṃ tu vedavādavivarjitam |
puṇyasvalpādarajanaṃ tat puraṃ samapadyata || 25 ||
meaning:
देव्यामन्तर्हितायां तु वेदवादविवर्जितम् |
पुण्यस्वल्पादरजनं तत् पुरं समपद्यत || 25 ||
text_mt: When the Goddess had vanished, that city became devoid of Vedic recitation, / its people having little regard for virtue.

sanskrit_iast:
na devāstatra gacchanti na viprā na maharṣayaḥ |
babhūva nagaraṃ tasya svalpayajñakriyotsavam || 26 ||
meaning:
न देवास्तत्र गच्छन्ति न विप्रा न महर्षयः |
बभूव नगरं तस्य स्वल्पयज्ञक्रियोत्सवम् || 26 ||
text_mt: Neither gods went there, nor brāhmaṇas, nor great seers; / his city became one where sacrificial rites and festivals were scarce.

sanskrit_iast:
ītayo bahavo jātā mṛtāśca bahavo janāḥ |
lauhityanadarājo'pi hīnatoyastadā'bhavat || 27 ||
meaning:
ईतयो बहवो जाता मृताश्च बहवो जनाः |
लौहित्यनदराजोऽपि हीनतोयस्तदाऽभवत् || 27 ||
text_mt: Many plagues arose, and many people died; / even the Lauhitya, the king of rivers, became diminished in water then.

sanskrit_iast:
bahūni viparītāni dṛṣṭvā sa narakastadā |
mene maraṇamāsannamatmano brahmaśāpataḥ || 28 ||
meaning:
बहूनि विपरीतानि दृष्ट्वा स नरकस्तदा |
मेने मरणमासन्नमत्मनो ब्रह्मशापतः || 28 ||
text_mt: Seeing many portents of doom, Naraka then / considered his own death to be near on account of the brāhmaṇa’s curse.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ prāgjyotiṣādhyakṣaḥ śokavihvalacetanaḥ |
cintayan manasā mitraṃ bāṇaṃ balisutaṃ yayau || 29 ||
meaning:
ततः प्राग्ज्योतिषाध्यक्षः शोकविह्वलचेतनः |
चिन्तयन् मनसा मित्रं बाणं बलिसुतं ययौ || 29 ||
text_mt: Then the ruler of Prāgjyotiṣa, his mind overwhelmed with sorrow, / turned his thoughts to his friend Bāṇa, son of Bali.

sanskrit_iast:
sakhā prāṇasamaḥ so'sya satatānyonyarakṣaṇe |
tatparau bāṇanarakau svarvaidyāvaśvināviva || 30 ||
meaning:
सखा प्राणसमः सोऽस्य सततान्योन्यरक्षणे |
तत्परौ बाणनरकौ स्वर्वैद्यावश्विनाविव || 30 ||
text_mt: He was a friend as dear as life itself, constantly devoted / to their mutual protection, like the Aśvins, the physicians of heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
etasminnantare bāṇo mitraṃ śambhusakho balī |
anukūlayitā mantrapradānena mahābudhaḥ || 31 ||
meaning:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे बाणो मित्रं शम्भुसखो बली |
अनुकूलयिता मन्त्रप्रदानेन महाबुधः || 31 ||
text_mt: In this interval, [he thought:] 'Bāṇa, the friend of Śambhu, powerful and very wise, / will act favorably toward me by giving advice.'

sanskrit_iast:
iti cāsīnmatistasya vajraketostadācalā |
dūtaṃ ca prāhiṇod dīptaṃ bāṇasya nagaraṃ prati || 32 ||
meaning:
इति चासीन्मतिस्तस्य वज्रकेतोस्तदाचला |
दूतं च प्राहिणोद् दीप्तं बाणस्य नगरं प्रति || 32 ||
text_mt: Such was the firm thought of Vajraketu then; / and he dispatched a splendid messenger to Bāṇa’s city.

sanskrit_iast:
sa śoṇitapuraṃ gatvā syandanenāśugāminā |
tato bhaumasya vṛttāntaṃ vāṇāyāśu nyavedayat || 33 ||
meaning:
स शोणितपुरं गत्वा स्यन्दनेनाशुगामिना |
ततो भौमस्य वृत्तान्तं वाणायाशु न्यवेदयत् || 33 ||
text_mt: Having gone to Śoṇitapura in a swift-moving chariot, / he quickly reported the news of the earth-born [king] to Bāṇa:

sanskrit_iast:
yathā śapto vasiṣṭhena yathā cāntarhitāmbikā |
yathā vighnaḥ puravare jātaḥ prāgjyotiṣāhvaye || 34 ||
meaning:
यथा शप्तो वसिष्ठेन यथा चान्तर्हिताम्बिका |
यथा विघ्नः पुरवरे जातः प्राग्ज्योतिषाह्वये || 34 ||
text_mt: how he was cursed by Vasiṣṭha, how Ambikā disappeared, / and how disaster arose in the excellent city called Prāgjyotiṣa;

sanskrit_iast:
samayasya vyatikrāntirbhūmimādhavayoryathā |
tathā sa dūto bhaumasya śaśaṃsa balisūnave || 35 ||
meaning:
समयस्य व्यतिक्रान्तिर्भूमिमाधवयोर्यथा |
तथा स दूतो भौमस्य शशंस बलिसूनवे || 35 ||
text_mt: and how the covenant of the Earth and Mādhava was breached— / thus that messenger of the earth-born [king] related [all] to Bali’s son.

sanskrit_iast:
sa samākāramitrasya samyag daivaparābhavam |
svayaṃ jagāma narakaṃ sabhājayitumīśvaraḥ || 36 ||
meaning:
स समाकारमित्रस्य सम्यग् दैवपराभवम् |
स्वयं जगाम नरकं सभाजयितुमीश्वरः || 36 ||
text_mt: Having understood completely the divine calamity of his friend, / the lord himself went to honour Naraka.

sanskrit_iast:
sa kāñcanavicitrāṅgaṃ yuktamaśvaśataistribhiḥ |
lohacakraṃ ca vaiyāghraṃ mayūradhajabhūṣitam || 37 ||
meaning:
स काञ्चनविचित्राङ्गं युक्तमश्वशतैस्त्रिभिः |
लोहचक्रं च वैयाघ्रं मयूरधजभूषितम् || 37 ||
text_mt: He mounted a great chariot, its frame adorned with gold, / yoked to three hundred horses, with iron wheels, draped in tiger skin, and adorned with peacock banners,

sanskrit_iast:
hemadaṇḍasitacchatracchaditaṃ kiṅkiṇīgaṇaiḥ |
nānāratanaugharacitamāruroha mahāratham || 38 ||
meaning:
हेमदण्डसितच्छत्रच्छदितं किङ्किणीगणैः |
नानारतनौघरचितमारुरोह महारथम् || 38 ||
text_mt: covered with a white parasol with a golden staff, hung with rows of small bells, / and fashioned with an array of various jewels.

sanskrit_iast:
sa sahasrabhujaḥ śrīmāṃścaturaṃgabalairyutaḥ |
prāgjyotiṣaṃ bhaumapuramacirādājagāma ha || 39 ||
meaning:
स सहस्रभुजः श्रीमांश्चतुरंगबलैर्युतः |
प्राग्ज्योतिषं भौमपुरमचिरादाजगाम ह || 39 ||
text_mt: He of a thousand arms, glorious, accompanied by a fourfold army, / soon arrived at Prāgjyotiṣa, the city of the earth-born [king].

sanskrit_iast:
tamāsādya mahābāhurbāṇaḥ prāgjyotiṣeśvaram |
hīnaṃ pūrvaśriyā mitramapaśyannagaraṃ ca tat || 40 ||
meaning:
तमासाद्य महाबाहुर्बाणः प्राग्ज्योतिषेश्वरम् |
हीनं पूर्वश्रिया मित्रमपश्यन्नगरं च तत् || 40 ||
text_mt: Approaching him, the mighty-armed Bāṇa saw the ruler of Prāgjyotiṣa, / his friend bereft of his former splendour, and saw that city.

sanskrit_iast:
sa tena tūjito bāṇo yathāyogyaṃ sutena koḥ |
papraccha kiṃ nimittaṃ te hīnaśrīkamabhūt puram || 41 ||
meaning:
स तेन तूजितो बाणो यथायोग्यं सुतेन कोः |
पप्रच्छ किं निमित्तं ते हीनश्रीकमभूत् पुरम् || 41 ||
text_mt: Suitably honoured by him, the son of the Earth, / Bāṇa asked: 'Why has your city become deprived of splendour?

sanskrit_iast: bāṇa uvāca
meaning: बाण उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
śarīraṃ ca yathāpūrvaṃ tathā na tava rājate |
manaśca te nāti hṛṣṭaṃ tatra hetuṃ vadasva me || 42 ||
meaning:
शरीरं च यथापूर्वं तथा न तव राजते |
मनश्च ते नाति हृष्टं तत्र हेतुं वदस्व मे || 42 ||
text_mt: 'Your body does not shine as before, / and your mind is not very glad; tell me the reason for that.'

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
evamādīni pṛṣṭaḥ sa narakaḥ kṣitinandanaḥ |
yathā vasiṣṭhaśāpo'bhūt tat sarvaṃ tasya cābravīt || 43 ||
meaning:
एवमादीनि पृष्टः स नरकः क्षितिनन्दनः |
यथा वसिष्ठशापोऽभूत् तत् सर्वं तस्य चाब्रवीत् || 43 ||
text_mt: Being asked these and other things, that Naraka, the delight of the Earth, / told him all about how Vasiṣṭha’s curse had come to pass.

sanskrit_iast:
yacchrutaṃ bhaumavadanāttaddūtāveditaṃ purā |
jñātvāṃ tathā taṃ provāca bāṇo vajradhvajaṃ punaḥ || 44 ||
meaning:
यच्छ्रुतं भौमवदनात्तद्दूतावेदितं पुरा |
ज्ञात्वां तथा तं प्रोवाच बाणो वज्रध्वजं पुनः || 44 ||
text_mt: Learning that what he heard from the mouth of the earth-born [king] was what the messenger had previously reported, / Bāṇa spoke again to Vajradhvaja:

sanskrit_iast: bāṇa uvāca
meaning: बाण उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
nahi manyustvayā kāryaḥ sukhe duḥkhe śarīriṇām |
cakravat parivartete naitābhyāṃ kau'pi hīyate || 45 ||
meaning:
नहि मन्युस्त्वया कार्यः सुखे दुःखे शरीरिणाम् |
चक्रवत् परिवर्तेते नैताभ्यां कौऽपि हीयते || 45 ||
text_mt: 'You must not grieve; pleasure and pain revolve like a wheel / for embodied beings; no one on earth is free of them.

sanskrit_iast:
paraṃ tatra pratīkāraḥ kāryo dhīrairvibhūtaye |
bhavānapi pratīkāraṃ kartumarhati samprati || 46 ||
meaning:
परं तत्र प्रतीकारः कार्यो धीरैर्विभूतये |
भवानपि प्रतीकारं कर्तुमर्हति सम्प्रति || 46 ||
text_mt: Yet a remedy should be undertaken by the resolute for the sake of prosperity; / you too ought to undertake a remedy now.

sanskrit_iast:
ya eṣa mānuṣaḥ pṛthvyāmasādhāraṇabhūtibhiḥ |
vardhate dānavo vāpi daityo vāpyathavāsuraḥ || 47 ||
meaning:
य एष मानुषः पृथ्व्यामसाधारणभूतिभिः |
वर्धते दानवो वापि दैत्यो वाप्यथवासुरः || 47 ||
text_mt: Whatever human, or Dānava, or Daitya, or Asura on this earth / grows with extraordinary prosperity,

sanskrit_iast:
rākṣasaḥ kinnaro vāpi śakrastān sahate nahi |
sa kauṭilyaṃ devagaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ kurvannitastataḥ |
yathā tathā prakāreṇa bhraṃśayatyeva taṃ śriyaḥ || 48 ||
meaning:
राक्षसः किन्नरो वापि शक्रस्तान् सहते नहि |
स कौटिल्यं देवगणैः सार्धं कुर्वन्नितस्ततः |
यथा तथा प्रकारेण भ्रंशयत्येव तं श्रियः || 48 ||
text_mt: or Rākṣasa, or Kinnara—Śakra does not tolerate them; / practicing deceit here and there together with the hosts of gods, / by some means or other he causes them to fall from fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya ceṣṭatamo devo viṣṇurnityaṃ sanātanaḥ |
sa na śaktasya kurute mano'niṣṭaṃ manāgapi || 49 ||
meaning:
तस्य चेष्टतमो देवो विष्णुर्नित्यं सनातनः |
स न शक्तस्य कुरुते मनोऽनिष्टं मनागपि || 49 ||
text_mt: His most beloved god is the eternal, imperishable Viṣṇu; / he does not cause even the slightest displeasure to Śakra.

sanskrit_iast:
yaḥ samārādhayed viṣṇuṃ śakrasyāniṣṭakārakaḥ |
tasmai varaṃ tu sacchidraṃ dattvā taṃ śātayatvitaḥ || 50 ||
meaning:
यः समाराधयेद् विष्णुं शक्रस्यानिष्टकारकः |
तस्मै वरं तु सच्छिद्रं दत्त्वा तं शातयत्वितः || 50 ||
text_mt: Whoever, worshiping Viṣṇu, causes harm to Śakra, / to him he grants a boon that has a loophole, and thereby ruins him.

sanskrit_iast:
ciramārādhito viṣṇuriṣṭān kāmān prayacchati |
mahatā kāyaduḥkhena pūjitaḥ samprasīdati || 51 ||
meaning:
चिरमाराधितो विष्णुरिष्टान् कामान् प्रयच्छति |
महता कायदुःखेन पूजितः सम्प्रसीदति || 51 ||
text_mt: Viṣṇu, worshiped for a long time, grants desired wishes; / worshiped with great bodily hardship, he becomes pleased.

sanskrit_iast:
vineṣṭadevatāpūjāṃ vibhūtimatulāṃ pumān |
kaḥ prāpnoti śrutaḥ pūrvaṃ na vā pūrvataraiḥ kvacit || 52 ||
meaning:
विनेष्टदेवतापूजां विभूतिमतुलां पुमान् |
कः प्राप्नोति श्रुतः पूर्वं न वा पूर्वतरैः क्वचित् || 52 ||
text_mt: Without the worship of one’s chosen deity, what man has ever attained / matchless prosperity, heard of formerly or by ancient ancestors anywhere?

sanskrit_iast:
tvayā nārādhitaḥ pūrvaṃ brahmā vā viṣṇurīśvaraḥ |
tena te'dya mahāvighnā utpannā viṣaye tava || 53 ||
meaning:
त्वया नाराधितः पूर्वं ब्रह्मा वा विष्णुरीश्वरः |
तेन तेऽद्य महाविघ्ना उत्पन्ना विषये तव || 53 ||
text_mt: You have not previously worshiped Brahmā, Viṣṇu, or Īśvara; / therefore today great obstacles have arisen in your realm.

sanskrit_iast:
yo vā viṣṇuḥ pālakaste na nisargānukampakaḥ |
kintu te sa kṣitervākyāttayā cārādhito muhuḥ || 54 ||
meaning:
यो वा विष्णुः पालकस्ते न निसर्गानुकम्पकः |
किन्तु ते स क्षितेर्वाक्यात्तया चाराधितो मुहुः || 54 ||
text_mt: Moreover, Viṣṇu who is your protector is not naturally compassionate, / but he was so at the request of the Earth, being worshiped repeatedly by her.

sanskrit_iast:
dattaṃ chidraṃ ca te viṣṇurnāparādhyāstvayā dvijāḥ |
ito'nyathā tvaṃ bhavitā hataśrīriti naḥ śrutam || 55 ||
meaning:
दत्तं छिद्रं च ते विष्णुर्नापराध्यास्त्वया द्विजाः |
इतोऽन्यथा त्वं भविता हतश्रीरिति नः श्रुतम् || 55 ||
text_mt: A loophole was given to you by Viṣṇu: "Brāhmaṇas are not to be offended by you; / otherwise you will become ruined in fortune"—so we have heard.

sanskrit_iast:
aparādhyastvayā bhūpa vasiṣṭhaḥ paramo muniḥ |
tena smaraṇamātreṇa nāyātau kṣitimādhavau || 56 ||
meaning:
अपराध्यस्त्वया भूप वसिष्ठः परमो मुनिः |
तेन स्मरणमात्रेण नायातौ क्षितिमाधवौ || 56 ||
text_mt: You have offended Vasiṣṭha, the supreme seer, O king; / therefore, at mere remembrance, the Earth and Mādhava did not come.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmāttvaṃ mitra budhyasva kauṭilyaṃ harimedhasaḥ |
nādhunā yujyate bhauma tavodāsīnatākṛtiḥ || 57 ||
meaning:
तस्मात्त्वं मित्र बुध्यस्व कौटिल्यं हरिमेधसः |
नाधुना युज्यते भौम तवोदासीनताकृतिः || 57 ||
text_mt: Therefore, O friend, realize the duplicity of Harimedhas; / an attitude of indifference does not befit you now, O son of the Earth.

sanskrit_iast:
yatte manasi tāto'yamiti sampratyayaḥ sa te |
varāha eva te tātaḥ sa lokāntaraṃ gataḥ || 58 ||
meaning:
यत्ते मनसि तातोऽयमिति सम्प्रत्ययः स ते |
वराह एव ते तातः स लोकान्तरं गतः || 58 ||
text_mt: As for your conviction in mind that "He is my father"— / the Boar alone was your father, and he has gone to another world.

sanskrit_iast:
vārāho'pi hareraṃśa iti yacchrūyate tvayā |
tasyāṃśa ityatukrośaḥ kena vo kriyate vada || 59 ||
meaning:
वाराहोऽपि हरेरंश इति यच्छ्रूयते त्वया |
तस्यांश इत्यतुक्रोशः केन वो क्रियते वद || 59 ||
text_mt: And as for what is heard by you, that the Boar is a portion of Hari— / tell me, who shows compassion to an incarnation simply because he is a portion?

sanskrit_iast:
tasmāttvaṃ kuru śambhorvā brahmaṇo vādhunārcanam |
sa te prasannaḥ paramamiṣṭakāmaṃ pradāsyati || 60 ||
meaning:
तस्मात्त्वं कुरु शम्भोर्वा ब्रह्मणो वाधुनार्चनम् |
स ते प्रसन्नः परममिष्टकामं प्रदास्यति || 60 ||
text_mt: Therefore perform now the worship of Śambhu or of Brahmā; / pleased, he will grant you your highest desired wish.

sanskrit_iast:
vighno vā muniśāpo vā mahetirvātipīḍakaḥ |
vidhau prasanne śambhau vā nacirātkṣayameṣyati || 61 ||
meaning:
विघ्नो वा मुनिशापो वा महेतिर्वातिपीडकः |
विधौ प्रसन्ने शम्भौ वा नचिरात्क्षयमेष्यति || 61 ||
text_mt: An obstacle, a sage’s curse, or a very oppressive calamity / will soon come to an end when Vidhi or Śambhu is pleased.'

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
jātasampratyayo bhaumo bāṇasya vacanāt tadā |
suprītaḥ samuvācedaṃ dhīraghargharaniḥsvanaḥ || 62 ||
meaning:
जातसम्प्रत्ययो भौमो बाणस्य वचनात् तदा |
सुप्रीतः समुवाचेदं धीरघर्घरनिःस्वनः || 62 ||
text_mt: Having gained conviction from Bāṇa’s words then, / the earth-born [king], very pleased, spoke these words with a deep, rumbling voice:

sanskrit_iast: bhauma uvāca
meaning: भौम उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
yat tvayā gaditaṃ bāṇa hitaṃ me mitravatsala |
tat kāryamacirādeva tapaścaraṇamuttamam || 63 ||
meaning:
यत् त्वया गदितं बाण हितं मे मित्रवत्सल |
तत् कार्यमचिरादेव तपश्चरणमुत्तमम् || 63 ||
text_mt: 'What you have spoken, O Bāṇa, affectionate to friends, is for my welfare; / the excellent performance of austerities must indeed be undertaken without delay.'

sanskrit_iast:
viṣṇurnārādhanīyo me tatra hetustvayoditaḥ |
navārādhyastathā śambhurantarguptaḥ sa me pure || 64 ||
meaning:
विष्णुर्नाराधनीयो मे तत्र हेतुस्त्वयोदितः |
नवाराध्यस्तथा शम्भुरन्तर्गुप्तः स मे पुरे || 64 ||
text_mt:
"I must not worship Viṣṇu; you have stated the reason for that.
Nor is Śambhu to be propitiated, for he remains hidden within my city.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmād brahmā samārādhyo vacanāt tava mitraka |
tatputrasya mahābāho lauhityasyāmbusannidhau || 65 ||
meaning:
तस्माद् ब्रह्मा समाराध्यो वचनात् तव मित्रक |
तत्पुत्रस्य महाबाहो लौहित्यस्याम्बुसन्निधौ || 65 ||
text_mt:
Therefore, Brahmā is to be propitiated at your word, my friend,
near the waters of his son, the Lauhitya, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit_iast:
bhavatādhyāpitaścāhaṃ śiṣyo'tha guruṇā yathā |
mitraṃ mitraṃ yathā dhīra sāmnā paramavalgunā || 66 ||
meaning:
भवताध्यापितश्चाहं शिष्योऽथ गुरुणा यथा |
मित्रं मित्रं यथा धीर साम्ना परमवल्गुना || 66 ||
text_mt:
I have been instructed by you just as a student is by a guru,
[and] as a wise friend [counsels] a friend with exceedingly pleasant conciliation."

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
ityuktvā sa mahābāhurbāṇaṃ vajradhvajastadā |
yathāvat pūjayāmāsa tanmitraṃ mitravatsalaḥ || 67 ||
meaning:
इत्युक्त्वा स महाबाहुर्बाणं वज्रध्वजस्तदा |
यथावत् पूजयामास तन्मित्रं मित्रवत्सलः || 67 ||
text_mt:
Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed Vajradhvaja then
duly honored that friend Bāṇa, affectionate toward his companion.

sanskrit_iast:
arcayitvā yathāyogyaṃ prasthāpya ca baleḥ sutam |
brahmārādhanamatyugraṃ kartumicchan kṣiteḥ sutaḥ || 68 ||
meaning:
अर्चयित्वा यथायोग्यं प्रस्थाप्य च बलेः सुतम् |
ब्रह्माराधनमत्युग्रं कर्तुमिच्छन् क्षितेः सुतः || 68 ||
text_mt:
Having worshipped the son of Bali fittingly and sent him off,
the son of the Earth, desiring to perform extremely fierce propitiation of Brahmā,

sanskrit_iast:
sa tīre nadarājasya lauhityasya mahātmanaḥ |
brahmācalaṃ samāruhya tapastaptumupasthitaḥ || 69 ||
meaning:
स तीरे नदराजस्य लौहित्यस्य महात्मनः |
ब्रह्माचलं समारुह्य तपस्तप्तुमुपस्थितः || 69 ||
text_mt:
stood upon Brahmācala on the bank of the great river-king Lauhitya,
prepared to perform austerities.

sanskrit_iast:
sa mānuṣeṇa mānena kṣitiputraḥ śataṃ samāḥ |
jalāhāravratenaiva samānarca pitāmaham || 70 ||
meaning:
स मानुषेण मानेन क्षितिपुत्रः शतं समाः |
जलाहारव्रतेनैव समानर्च पितामहम् || 70 ||
text_mt:
By human measure, for a hundred years,
the son of the Earth worshipped the Grandfather solely with the vow of consuming [only] water.

sanskrit_iast:
santuṣṭaḥ śatavarṣānte brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ |
pratyakṣībhūya narakasyāgrataḥ samupasthitaḥ || 71 ||
meaning:
सन्तुष्टः शतवर्षान्ते ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः |
प्रत्यक्षीभूय नरकस्याग्रतः समुपस्थितः || 71 ||
text_mt:
Gratified at the end of the hundred years, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds,
became visible and appeared before Naraka.

sanskrit_iast:
prīto'smi te varaṃ dāsye varaṃ varaya suvrata |
iti covāca narakaṃ sa tadā kamalāsanaḥ || 72 ||
meaning:
प्रीतोऽस्मि ते वरं दास्ये वरं वरय सुव्रत |
इति चोवाच नरकं स तदा कमलासनः || 72 ||
text_mt:
"I am pleased with you; I shall grant a boon. Choose a boon, O you of noble vows!"
Thus the lotus-seated one then spoke to Naraka.

sanskrit_iast:
sa dṛṣṭvā sarvalokeśaṃ pratyakṣaṃ kamalāsanam |
praṇamya prāñjaliḥ proce vinayānatakandharaḥ || 73 ||
meaning:
स दृष्ट्वा सर्वलोकेशं प्रत्यक्षं कमलासनम् |
प्रणम्य प्राञ्जलिः प्रोचे विनयानतकन्धरः || 73 ||
text_mt:
Seeing the lotus-seated lord of all the worlds visibly present,
he bowed with folded hands and, with his neck bent in humility, spoke:

sanskrit_iast: hauma uvāca
meaning: हौम उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
devāsurebhyo rakṣobhyaḥ sarvebhyo devayonitaḥ |
avadhyatvaṃ suraśreṣṭha varamekaṃ prayaccha me || 74 ||
meaning:
देवासुरेभ्यो रक्षोभ्यः सर्वेभ्यो देवयोनितः |
अवध्यत्वं सुरश्रेष्ठ वरमेकं प्रयच्छ मे || 74 ||
text_mt:
"Grant me one boon, O best of gods:
invulnerability from gods, asuras, rākṣasas, and all beings of divine origin.

sanskrit_iast:
avicchinnā santatirme yāvaccandro ravistapet |
tāvadbhavatu lokeśa dvitīyo'yaṃ varo mama || 75 ||
meaning:
अविच्छिन्ना सन्ततिर्मे यावच्चन्द्रो रविस्तपेत् |
तावद्भवतु लोकेश द्वितीयोऽयं वरो मम || 75 ||
text_mt:
May my lineage be unbroken as long as the moon and sun shine;
let this be my second boon, O lord of the worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
tilottamādyā yā devyaḥ sadrūpaguṇasaṃyutāḥ |
tāstā me dayitāḥ santu sahasrāṇi tu ṣoḍaśa || 76 ||
meaning:
तिलोत्तमाद्या या देव्यः सद्रूपगुणसंयुताः |
तास्ता मे दयिताः सन्तु सहस्राणि तु षोडश || 76 ||
text_mt:
May those goddesses, endowed with true beauty and virtues, beginning with Tilottamā,
numbering sixteen thousand, become my beloved wives.

sanskrit_iast:
ajeyatvaṃ sadā śrīrmā na jahātu kadācana |
iti pañca varā me'dya vṛtāstvattaḥ pitāmaha || 77 ||
meaning:
अजेयत्वं सदा श्रीर्मा न जहातु कदाचन |
इति पञ्च वरा मेऽद्य वृतास्त्वत्तः पितामह || 77 ||
text_mt:
May I have invincibility, and may fortune never abandon me.
In this way, these five boons are chosen by me from you today, O Grandfather."

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
māyayā mohito bhaumo muniśāpaṃ vismṛtya ca |
anyadvarāntaraṃ vavre muniśāpastathā sthitaḥ || 78 ||
meaning:
मायया मोहितो भौमो मुनिशापं विस्मृत्य च |
अन्यद्वरान्तरं वव्रे मुनिशापस्तथा स्थितः || 78 ||
text_mt:
Deluded by Māyā and forgetting the sage’s curse, Bhauma
chose different boons, and so the sage's curse remained in place.

sanskrit_iast:
evamastviti tān sarvān varān dattvā pitāmahaḥ |
uvācedaṃ dvāparānte sandhyāyāṃ surakanyakāḥ || 79 ||
meaning:
एवमस्त्विति तान् सर्वान् वरान् दत्त्वा पितामहः |
उवाचेदं द्वापरान्ते सन्ध्यायां सुरकन्यकाः || 79 ||
text_mt:
Having granted all those boons, saying, "So be it,"
the Grandfather spoke these words: "At the close of Dvāpara, in the twilight, the celestial maidens,

sanskrit_iast:
tilottamādyāste jāyā sambhaviṣyanti bhūtale |
na yāvannārado yāti vajradhvaja puraṃ tava |
tāvanna maithune yojyā bhavatā tākṣiteḥ suta || 80 ||
meaning:
तिलोत्तमाद्यास्ते जाया सम्भविष्यन्ति भूतले |
न यावन्नारदो याति वज्रध्वज पुरं तव |
तावन्न मैथुने योज्या भवता ताक्षितेः सुत || 80 ||
text_mt:
beginning with Tilottamā, will become your wives on the surface of the earth.
Until Nārada comes to your city, O Vajradhvaja,
so long must they not be united in sexual union by you, O son of the Earth."

sanskrit_iast:
ityuktvā sarvalokeśaḥ kṣaṇādantarhito'bhavat |
mudamāsādya paramāṃ svasthānaṃ narako'bhyagāt || 81 ||
meaning:
इत्युक्त्वा सर्वलोकेशः क्षणादन्तर्हितोऽभवत् |
मुदमासाद्य परमां स्वस्थानं नरकोऽभ्यगात् || 81 ||
text_mt:
Having spoken thus, the lord of all the worlds vanished in an instant.
Having attained supreme joy, Naraka returned to his own abode.

sanskrit_iast:
tato muditalokaṃ taṃ nagaraṃ śrīniṣevitam |
sadā sotsāhasampūrṇamītivighnavivarjitam || 82 ||
meaning:
ततो मुदितलोकं तं नगरं श्रीनिषेवितम् |
सदा सोत्साहसम्पूर्णमीतिविघ्नविवर्जितम् || 82 ||
text_mt:
Then that city, inhabited by delighted people and attended by prosperity,
ever filled with enterprise and free from calamities and obstacles,

sanskrit_iast:
abhavat paśusaṃghaiśca vājivāraṇakumbhakaiḥ |
sampūrṇaṃ devarājasya dayitevāmarāvatī || 83 ||
meaning:
अभवत् पशुसंघैश्च वाजिवारणकुम्भकैः |
सम्पूर्णं देवराजस्य दयितेवामरावती || 83 ||
text_mt:
became full of herds of livestock and the temples of horses and elephants,
like Amarāvatī, the beloved [city] of the king of gods.

sanskrit_iast:
uttīrṇatapasaṃ śrutvā bāṇo dattavaraṃ tathā |
svayaṃ punarupātiṣṭhad bhaumaṃ vajradhvajaṃ tadā || 84 ||
meaning:
उत्तीर्णतपसं श्रुत्वा बाणो दत्तवरं तथा |
स्वयं पुनरुपातिष्ठद् भौमं वज्रध्वजं तदा || 84 ||
text_mt:
Hearing that he had completed his austerities and received boons,
Bāṇa then personally approached Bhauma Vajradhvaja again.

sanskrit_iast:
sa gatvā bhaumanagaraṃ bāṇaḥ prāgjyotiṣāhvayam |
papraccha narakaṃ mitraṃ tapasaḥ sanniveśanam || 85 ||
meaning:
स गत्वा भौमनगरं बाणः प्राग्ज्योतिषाह्वयम् |
पप्रच्छ नरकं मित्रं तपसः सन्निवेशनम् || 85 ||
text_mt:
Having gone to Bhauma's city called Prāgjyotiṣa,
Bāṇa questioned his friend Naraka about the circumstances of his austerity:

sanskrit_iast:
kutra tvayā tapastaptaṃ kiṃ vā cīrṇaṃ tvayā vratam |
kīdṛśo vā varo labdhastvaṃ mamākhyātumarhasi || 86 ||
meaning:
कुत्र त्वया तपस्तप्तं किं वा चीर्णं त्वया व्रतम् |
कीदृशो वा वरो लब्धस्त्वं ममाख्यातुमर्हसि || 86 ||
text_mt:
"Where did you perform your austerity, or what vow did you observe?
What sort of boon was obtained? You ought to tell me.

sanskrit_iast:
dṛṣṭaṃ tava puraṃ sarvaṃ prahṛṣṭajanasaṅkulam |
vājivāraṇaratnaughaiḥ pūritaṃ maṅgalasvanaiḥ || 87 ||
meaning:
दृष्टं तव पुरं सर्वं प्रहृष्टजनसङ्कुलम् |
वाजिवारणरत्नौघैः पूरितं मङ्गलस्वनैः || 87 ||
text_mt:
Your entire city is seen crowded with overjoyed people,
filled with horses, elephants, hosts of jewels, and auspicious sounds.

sanskrit_iast:
dṛśyate'dya tvayā pālyaṃ śasyapūrṇamanāmayam |
kathyatāṃ vā kathaṃ brahmā varaṃ tubhyaṃ pradattavān || 88 ||
meaning:
दृश्यतेऽद्य त्वया पाल्यं शस्यपूर्णमनामयम् |
कथ्यतां वा कथं ब्रह्मा वरं तुभ्यं प्रदत्तवान् || 88 ||
text_mt:
Today it is seen being protected by you, filled with grain and free from disease.
Tell me, how did Brahmā grant the boon to you?"

sanskrit_iast: bhauma uvāca
meaning: भौम उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
brahmā svayaṃ parvatarūpadhārī
kāmeśvarīṃ dhartumihāvatīrṇaḥ |
tatra svayaṃ samprati ghasrameti
purā na yāvacchapate vasiṣṭhaḥ || 89 ||
meaning:
ब्रह्मा स्वयं पर्वतरूपधारी
कामेश्वरीं धर्तुमिहावतीर्णः |
तत्र स्वयं सम्प्रति घस्रमेति
पुरा न यावच्छपते वसिष्ठः || 89 ||
text_mt:
"Brahmā himself, bearing the form of a mountain,
descended here to support Kāmeśvarī.
There he presently spends his day,
until Vasiṣṭha formerly utters his curse.

sanskrit_iast:
so'yaṃ pure me baliputra rājate
devaughasevyo'pyamarottamāṃśaḥ |
tatrāhameko varatoyabhojano
varṣāṇyakārṣaṃ ca tapaḥ śatāni vai || 90 ||
meaning:
सोऽयं पुरे मे बलिपुत्र राजते
देवौघसेव्योऽप्यमरोत्तमांशः |
तत्राहमेको वरतोयभोजनो
वर्षाण्यकार्षं च तपः शतानि वै || 90 ||
text_mt:
This mountain shines in my city, O son of Bali,
served by hosts of gods, a portion of the highest of immortals.
There alone, consuming only the best water,
I indeed performed austerities for a hundred years.

sanskrit_iast:
lauhityatīre ghanavāyusevite
manohare prāṇabhṛtāṃ sukhaprade |
tapaḥpravṛttasya mukhaṃ samāgama-
ccharad yathaikā śaradāṃ śatāni me || 91 ||
meaning:
लौहित्यतीरे घनवायुसेविते
मनोहरे प्राणभृतां सुखप्रदे |
तपःप्रवृत्तस्य मुखं समागम-
च्छरद् यथैका शरदां शतानि मे || 91 ||
text_mt:
On the bank of the Lauhitya, visited by dense breezes,
charming and bestowing happiness upon living beings,
as I engaged in austerity, a hundred autumns passed for me
like a single autumn, bringing joy.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ sa tuṣṭaścaturānano'bhavat
pratyakṣato māṃ nyagadacca maddhitam |
tava prasanno'smi varaṃ yathepsitaṃ
dāsye gṛhāṇeti puro'tha bhūtvā || 92 ||
meaning:
ततः स तुष्टश्चतुराननोऽभवत्
प्रत्यक्षतो मां न्यगदच्च मद्धितम् |
तव प्रसन्नोऽस्मि वरं यथेप्सितं
दास्ये गृहाणेति पुरोऽथ भूत्वा || 92 ||
text_mt:
Then the four-faced one became pleased,
appeared visibly, and spoke what was for my benefit:
'I am pleased with you; standing before you, I shall grant
the boon as desired; receive it!'

sanskrit_iast:
avadhyatā me surayonitaḥ surā-
dacchinnasantānamajeyatā tathā |
sadā vibhūtirna jahātu māmiti
varāśca nāryo navayauvanānvitāḥ || 93 ||
meaning:
अवध्यता मे सुरयोनितः सुरा-
दच्छिन्नसन्तानमजेयता तथा |
सदा विभूतिर्न जहातु मामिति
वराश्च नार्यो नवयौवनान्विताः || 93 ||
text_mt:
'Invulnerability for me from those of divine origin, from gods,
an unbroken lineage, as well as invincibility,
and that sovereignty should never abandon me,
and women endowed with fresh youth as boons.'

sanskrit_iast:
ete varāḥ pañca mayā tato vṛtāḥ
so'pi pratiśrutya gato nijāspadam |
tato'hamabhyetya puraṃ nijaṃ mudā
mantripravīraiḥ sahitaḥ punastān || 94 ||
meaning:
एते वराः पञ्च मया ततो वृताः
सोऽपि प्रतिश्रुत्य गतो निजास्पदम् |
ततोऽहमभ्येत्य पुरं निजं मुदा
मन्त्रिप्रवीरैः सहितः पुनस्तान् || 94 ||
text_mt:
These five boons were chosen by me from him.
He too, having promised them, departed to his own abode.
Then, happily arriving at my own city,
I, together with the foremost ministers,

sanskrit_iast:
paurān sabandhūn sagaṇānamodayam
dānena mānena ca bhojanena || 95 ||
meaning:
पौरान् सबन्धून् सगणानमोदयम्
दानेन मानेन च भोजनेन || 95 ||
text_mt:
delighted those citizens, together with their kinsmen and companions,
with gifts, honor, and food."

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
itīritaṃ tasya baleḥ sutastadā
bhaumasya śrutvā mumude na tatkṣaṇāt |
idaṃ tadoce vacanaṃ kṣiteḥ sutaṃ
tatkālayuktaṃ na cca sūnṛtodbhavam || 96 ||
meaning:
इतीरितं तस्य बलेः सुतस्तदा
भौमस्य श्रुत्वा मुमुदे न तत्क्षणात् |
इदं तदोचे वचनं क्षितेः सुतं
तत्कालयुक्तं न च्च सूनृतोद्भवम् || 96 ||
text_mt:
Hearing that which was spoken by Bhauma,
the son of Bali did not rejoice at that moment.
He then spoke this speech to the son of the Earth,
suited to that time, but not arising from truth:

sanskrit_iast: bāṇa uvāca
meaning: बाण उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
na te muneḥ śāpamatītya gantuṃ
bhūtā matirmitra tadā vidheḥ puraḥ |
kathaṃ tu bhadraṃ bhavitā taveha
bhāvītyavaśyaṃ kṣitiputra nityam || 97 ||
meaning:
न ते मुनेः शापमतीत्य गन्तुं
भूता मतिर्मित्र तदा विधेः पुरः |
कथं तु भद्रं भविता तवेह
भावीत्यवश्यं क्षितिपुत्र नित्यम् || 97 ||
text_mt:
"Before Vidhi, O friend, you did not have the mind
to transcend the sage’s curse.
How indeed will good fortune come to you here?
What is to be, O son of the Earth, must always come to pass.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtasya karaṇaṃ nāsti daivādhiṣṭhitakarmaṇaḥ |
bhāvītyavaśyaṃ yadbhāvyaṃ tatra brahmāpyabādhakaḥ || 98 ||
meaning:
कृतस्य करणं नास्ति दैवाधिष्ठितकर्मणः |
भावीत्यवश्यं यद्भाव्यं तत्र ब्रह्माप्यबाधकः || 98 ||
text_mt:
There is no undoing of an action overseen by destiny;
whatever must happen will certainly occur, and even Brahmā cannot hinder it.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmāt tvaṃ sumahāvīrānasurān pāvakopamān |
sandhayāya ca puraskṛtya sācivye viniyojaya || 99 ||
meaning:
तस्मात् त्वं सुमहावीरानसुरान् पावकोपमान् |
सन्धयाय च पुरस्कृत्य साचिव्ये विनियोजय || 99 ||
text_mt:
Therefore, bringing forward immensely heroic asuras
resembling fire, make alliances and appoint them to ministerial posts.

sanskrit_iast:
dvāri saṃsthāpya vai vīrān devairap durāsadān |
atikramasva deveśaṃ yadi labdhavaro bhavān || 100 ||
meaning:
द्वारि संस्थाप्य वै वीरान् देवैरप् दुरासदान् |
अतिक्रमस्व देवेशं यदि लब्धवरो भवान् || 100 ||
text_mt:
Stationing at the gates heroes difficult to approach even by the gods,
challenge the lord of the gods, if you are one who has obtained boons.

sanskrit_iast:
vidhinā yo varo datto bhavate tat-parīkṣaṇam |
kartumarhasi jāyāyāmaputro janayātmajam || 101 ||
meaning:
विधिना यो वरो दत्तो भवते तत्-परीक्षणम् |
कर्तुमर्हसि जायायामपुत्रो जनयात्मजम् || 101 ||
text_mt:
You ought to test the boon that was granted to you by Vidhi:
being sonless, beget a son upon your wife!"

sanskrit_iast:
ityuktvā prayayau bāṇo yathāvat tena pūjitaḥ |
narako mitravacanaṃ kartuṃ samupacakrame || 102 ||
meaning:
इत्युक्त्वा प्रययौ बाणो यथावत् तेन पूजितः |
नरको मित्रवचनं कर्तुं समुपचक्रमे || 102 ||
text_mt:
Having spoken thus and being duly worshipped by him, Bāṇa departed.
Naraka set about carrying out the words of his friend.

sanskrit_iast:
iti śrīkālikāpurāṇe bhaumatapasyāyāṃ ekonacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ || 39 ||
catvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
इति श्रीकालिकापुराणे भौमतपस्यायां एकोनचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः || 39 ||
चत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः
text_mt:
Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, on Bhauma's austerity, in the glorious Kālikāpurāṇa.
Fortieth Chapter

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
ṛtumatyāṃ tu jāyāyāṃ kāle sa narakaḥ kramāt |
bhagadattaṃ mahāśīrṣaṃ madavantaṃ sumālinam || 1 ||
meaning:
ऋतुमत्यां तु जायायां काले स नरकः क्रमात् |
भगदत्तं महाशीर्षं मदवन्तं सुमालिनम् || 1 ||
text_mt:
In time, when his wife was in her fertile season, that Naraka in due course [begot]
Bhagadatta, Mahāśīrṣa, Madavant, and Sumālin.

sanskrit_iast:
caturo janayāmāsa putrānetān kṣiteḥ sutaḥ |
mahāsattvān mahāvīryān vīrairanyairdurāsadān || 2 ||
meaning:
चतुरो जनयामास पुत्रानेतान् क्षितेः सुतः |
महासत्त्वान् महावीर्यान् वीरैरन्यैर्दुरासदान् || 2 ||
text_mt: The son of the Earth fathered these four sons, / of great strength, great valour, and difficult for other heroes to overcome.

sanskrit_iast:
tato bāṇasya vacanād hayagrīvaṃ tathā murum |
sandhāyātha samānīya saināpatye'bhyas.ecayat || 3 ||
meaning:
ततो बाणस्य वचनाद् हयग्रीवं तथा मुरुम् |
सन्धायाथ समानीय सैनापत्येऽभ्यस्.एचयत् || 3 ||
text_mt: Then, on the advice of Bāṇa, he formed an alliance, brought Hayagrīva / and Muru, and consecrated them to the generalship of his army.

sanskrit_iast:
muruṃ sannihitaṃ śrutvā hayagrīvaṃ ca bhauminā |
ye ye kṣitau tadā hyāsannasurāste'pi saṅgatāḥ || 4 ||
meaning:
मुरुं सन्निहितं श्रुत्वा हयग्रीवं च भौमिना |
ये ये क्षितौ तदा ह्यासन्नसुरास्तेऽपि सङ्गताः || 4 ||
text_mt: Hearing that Muru and Hayagrīva had allied with the son of Bhūmi, / whatever asuras were on earth at that time joined them too.

sanskrit_iast:
hayagrīvaṃ muruṃ śrutvā narakeṇa samāgatam |
nisundasundanāmānāvasurau sainikaiḥ saha || 5 ||
meaning:
हयग्रीवं मुरुं श्रुत्वा नरकेण समागतम् |
निसुन्दसुन्दनामानावसुरौ सैनिकैः सह || 5 ||
text_mt: Hearing that Hayagrīva and Muru had united with Naraka, / the two asuras named Nisunda and Sunda, along with their troops,

sanskrit_iast:
virūpākṣastadā daityaḥ sarve tena samāgaman |
tataḥ sa paścimadvāri narakaḥ senayā saha || 6 ||
meaning:
विरूपाक्षस्तदा दैत्यः सर्वे तेन समागमन् |
ततः स पश्चिमद्वारि नरकः सेनया सह || 6 ||
text_mt: and the daitya Virūpākṣa—they all joined him then. / Then Naraka, together with his army, at the western gate

sanskrit_iast:
muruṃ dvārādhipaṃ cakre hayagrīvaṃ tathottare |
pūrvadvāri nisundantu virūpākṣaṃ tu dakṣiṇe || 7 ||
meaning:
मुरुं द्वाराधिपं चक्रे हयग्रीवं तथोत्तरे |
पूर्वद्वारि निसुन्दन्तु विरूपाक्षं तु दक्षिणे || 7 ||
text_mt: appointed Muru as keeper of the gate, and Hayagrīva at the north; / Nisunda at the eastern gate, and Virūpākṣa at the south.

sanskrit_iast:
madhye pañcajanaṃ sundaṃ saināpatye'bhyaṣecayat |
muruṃ kṣurāntān pāśāṃśca ṣaṭsahasrāṇyayojayat || 8 ||
meaning:
मध्ये पञ्चजनं सुन्दं सैनापत्येऽभ्यषेचयत् |
मुरुं क्षुरान्तान् पाशांश्च षट्सहस्राण्ययोजयत् || 8 ||
text_mt: In the centre he consecrated Pañcajana and Sunda to the generalship. / Muru prepared razor-edged nooses, six thousand of them,

sanskrit_iast:
dvāri tat purarakṣārthaṃ satkṛtaḥ kṣitisūnunā |
evaṃ pūrvān pūrvatarānavamatya sumantriṇaḥ || 9 ||
meaning:
द्वारि तत् पुररक्षार्थं सत्कृतः क्षितिसूनुना |
एवं पूर्वान् पूर्वतरानवमत्य सुमन्त्रिणः || 9 ||
text_mt: at the gate to protect that city, honoured by the son of the Earth. / Thus, disregarding his previous, highly experienced wise counsellors,

sanskrit_iast:
asuraireva satataṃ so'suro mudito'bhavat |
pūrvaṃ gṛhītaṃ bhāvaṃ sa parityajya kṣiteḥ sutaḥ || 10 ||
meaning:
असुरैरेव सततं सोऽसुरो मुदितोऽभवत् |
पूर्वं गृहीतं भावं स परित्यज्य क्षितेः सुतः || 10 ||
text_mt: that asura rejoiced only in the company of asuras continually. / Abandoning the disposition he had previously assumed, the son of the Earth,

sanskrit_iast:
āsuraṃ bhāvamāsādya bādhate tridivaukasaḥ |
na devān na munīn sarvān na ca jānāti kāṃścana || 11 ||
meaning:
आसुरं भावमासाद्य बाधते त्रिदिवौकसः |
न देवान् न मुनीन् सर्वान् न च जानाति कांश्चन || 11 ||
text_mt: taking on an asura nature, began tormenting the dwellers of heaven; / he had no regard for the gods, nor all the sages, nor anyone at all.

sanskrit_iast:
sureśvaraṃ jigāyāśu hayagrīvasahāyavān |
evaṃ sa cāsuraṃ bhāvaṃ tanvāno vicaran kṣitau || 12 ||
meaning:
सुरेश्वरं जिगायाशु हयग्रीवसहायवान् |
एवं स चासुरं भावं तन्वानो विचरन् क्षितौ || 12 ||
text_mt: With Hayagrīva as his ally, he swiftly conquered the lord of the gods. / Thus propagating an asura nature, wandering over the earth,

sanskrit_iast:
bāṇasya vacanācchakraṃ bādhayatyeva vai munīn |
deveśvaraṃ tridhā jitvā hayagrīva sahāyavān || 13 ||
meaning:
बाणस्य वचनाच्छक्रं बाधयत्येव वै मुनीन् |
देवेश्वरं त्रिधा जित्वा हयग्रीव सहायवान् || 13 ||
text_mt: at the prompting of Bāṇa he harassed Indra and the sages; / having defeated the lord of gods three times with Hayagrīva as his ally,

sanskrit_iast:
adityāḥ kuṇḍalayugaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam |
sarvaratnāmṛtasrāvi duḥkhavighnaharaṃ param || 14 ||
meaning:
अदित्याः कुण्डलयुगं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् |
सर्वरत्नामृतस्रावि दुःखविघ्नहरं परम् || 14 ||
text_mt: Naraka, born of Bhūmi, fearless of the sage's curse, / seized Aditi's pair of earrings, renowned through the three worlds,

sanskrit_iast: jahāra narako bhaumo nirbhīto muniśāpataḥ |
meaning: जहार नरको भौमो निर्भीतो मुनिशापतः |
text_mt: which yielded all gems and nectar, and removed all sorrow and obstacles.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ devān bādhamāno munīn viprān kṣiteḥ sutaḥ |
pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi rājyaṃ prāgjyotiṣe'karot || 15 ||
meaning:
एवं देवान् बाधमानो मुनीन् विप्रान् क्षितेः सुतः |
पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि राज्यं प्राग्ज्योतिषेऽकरोत् || 15 ||
text_mt: Thus harassing the gods, sages, and brahmins, the son of the Earth / ruled for five thousand years in Prāgjyotiṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
etasminnantare devī mahābhārārditā kṣitiḥ |
brahmaviṣṇumukhān devān rakṣārthaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatā |
idaṃ covāca dhātāraṃ praṇamyorvī samādhavam || 16 ||
meaning:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे देवी महाभारार्दिता क्षितिः |
ब्रह्मविष्णुमुखान् देवान् रक्षार्थं शरणं गता |
इदं चोवाच धातारं प्रणम्योर्वी समाधवम् || 16 ||
text_mt: Meanwhile, the goddess Earth, afflicted by a mighty burden, / went for protection to the gods led by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, / and bowing to Dhātṛ together with Mādhava, the Earth spoke these words:

sanskrit_iast: pṛthivyuvāca
meaning: पृथिव्युवाच

sanskrit_iast:
dānavā rākṣā datyā hariṇā ye ca sūditāḥ |
te rājñāṃ mandire jātā adhunā balagarvitāḥ || 17 ||
meaning:
दानवा राक्षा दत्या हरिणा ये च सूदिताः |
ते राज्ञां मन्दिरे जाता अधुना बलगर्विताः || 17 ||
text_mt: The dānavas, rākṣasas, and daityas who were slain by Hari / have now been born in the palaces of kings, arrogant in their strength.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣāṃ bhāramahaṃ soḍhuṃ na śaknomi mahattaram |
asaṃkhyātāśca te sarvetān saṃkhyātuṃ na cotsahe || 18 ||
meaning:
तेषां भारमहं सोढुं न शक्नोमि महत्तरम् |
असंख्याताश्च ते सर्वेतान् संख्यातुं न चोत्सहे || 18 ||
text_mt: I am not able to endure their exceedingly great burden; / they are all innumerable, and I am unable to count them.

sanskrit_iast:
aṣṭau śatasahasrāṇi teṣāṃ mukhyā mahābalāḥ |
teṣvapyatibalān voḍhuṃ na tāñchaknomi cādhunā || 19 ||
meaning:
अष्टौ शतसहस्राणि तेषां मुख्या महाबलाः |
तेष्वप्यतिबलान् वोढुं न ताञ्छक्नोमि चाधुना || 19 ||
text_mt: Eight hundred thousand are their chiefs, endowed with great might; / even among them, those of excessive strength I am now unable to bear:

sanskrit_iast:
bāṇaṃ baleḥ sutaṃ vīraṃ kaṃsa dhenukameva ca |
ariṣṭaṃ ca pralambaṃ ca sunāmānaṃ muruṃ śalam || 20 ||
meaning:
बाणं बलेः सुतं वीरं कंस धेनुकमेव च |
अरिष्टं च प्रलम्बं च सुनामानं मुरुं शलम् || 20 ||
text_mt: Bāṇa, the heroic son of Bali; Kaṃsa and Dhenuka; / Ariṣṭa, Pralamba, Sunāman, Muru, and Śala;

sanskrit_iast:
cāruṇamuṣṭikau mallau jarāsandhaṃ mahābalam |
narakaṃ ca hayagrīvaṃ nisundaṃ sundameva ca || 21 ||
meaning:
चारुणमुष्टिकौ मल्लौ जरासन्धं महाबलम् |
नरकं च हयग्रीवं निसुन्दं सुन्दमेव च || 21 ||
text_mt: the two wrestlers Cāṇūra and Muṣṭika; Jarāsandha of great might; / Naraka, Hayagrīva, Nisunda, and Sunda;

sanskrit_iast:
virūpākṣaṃ pañcajanaṃ hiḍimbaṃ ca bakaṃ balam |
jaṭāsuraṃ ca kirmīramanāyudhamalambuṣam || 22 ||
meaning:
विरूपाक्षं पञ्चजनं हिडिम्बं च बकं बलम् |
जटासुरं च किर्मीरमनायुधमलम्बुषम् || 22 ||
text_mt: Virūpākṣa, Pañcajana, Hiḍimba, Baka, Bala, / Jaṭāsura, Kirmīra, Anāyudha, Alambuṣa,

sanskrit_iast:
saubhākhyaṃ ca jarāsandhaṃ dvividaṃ cāpi vānaram |
śrutāyudhaṃ mahādaityaṃ śatāyudhamathāparam || 23 ||
meaning:
सौभाख्यं च जरासन्धं द्विविदं चापि वानरम् |
श्रुतायुधं महादैत्यं शतायुधमथापरम् || 23 ||
text_mt: Saubha, Jarāsandha, the monkey Dvivida, / the great daitya Śrutāyudha, and another, Śatāyudha;

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣyaśṛṅgasutaṃ caiva subāhumatibāhukam |
kālakañjāṃstathā daityān hiraṇyapuravāsinaḥ || 24 ||
meaning:
ऋष्यशृङ्गसुतं चैव सुबाहुमतिबाहुकम् |
कालकञ्जांस्तथा दैत्यान् हिरण्यपुरवासिनः || 24 ||
text_mt: the son of Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, Subāhu, Atibāhuka, / and the Kālakañja daityas dwelling in Hiraṇyapura.

sanskrit_iast:
eteṣāṃ tu padakṣobharviśīrṇāhaṃ dine dine |
lokān voḍhuṃ na śaknomi tānnighnantu surottamāḥ || 25 ||
meaning:
एतेषां तु पदक्षोभर्विशीर्णाहं दिने दिने |
लोकान् वोढुं न शक्नोमि तान्निघ्नन्तु सुरोत्तमाः || 25 ||
text_mt: Crushed day by day by the trampling of their feet, / I cannot bear the worlds; let the best of gods destroy them!

sanskrit_iast:
nacedrakṣāṃ prakurvanti bhavantaḥ surasattamāḥ |
tadā viśīrṇā yāsyāmi pātālamavaśā'dhunā || 26 ||
meaning:
नचेद्रक्षां प्रकुर्वन्ति भवन्तः सुरसत्तमाः |
तदा विशीर्णा यास्यामि पातालमवशाऽधुना || 26 ||
text_mt: If you, the best of gods, do not protect me, / then I, helpless, will crumble and sink into the netherworld now.

sanskrit_iast: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
meaning: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

sanskrit_iast:
tatastasyā vacaḥ śrutvā brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ |
ityūcuste kariṣyāmaḥ kṣite bhāravimokṣaṇam || 27 ||
meaning:
ततस्तस्या वचः श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः |
इत्यूचुस्ते करिष्यामः क्षिते भारविमोक्षणम् || 27 ||
text_mt: Then, having heard her speech, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara / replied to her: “O Earth, we shall remove your burden.”

sanskrit_iast:
visṛjya pṛthivīṃ devīṃ sarve devāḥ sanātanam |
mādhavaṃ toṣayāmāsurbhārāvataraṇaṃ prati || 28 ||
meaning:
विसृज्य पृथिवीं देवीं सर्वे देवाः सनातनम् |
माधवं तोषयामासुर्भारावतरणं प्रति || 28 ||
text_mt: Having sent away the goddess Earth, all the gods / propitiated the eternal Mādhava to descend and remove the burden.

sanskrit_iast:
sa tu tuṣṭaḥ surān sarvān svāṃśairavatarantu vai |
kṣitau bhārāvatārāyetyuktvā svayamiha prabhuḥ || 29 ||
meaning:
स तु तुष्टः सुरान् सर्वान् स्वांशैरवतरन्तु वै |
क्षितौ भारावतारायेत्युक्त्वा स्वयमिह प्रभुः || 29 ||
text_mt: Pleased, the Lord said to all the gods: “Descend indeed / to the earth with your portions to relieve the burden,” and here he himself

sanskrit_iast:
avatīrṇo'tha devakyā garbhe bhārāvatāraṇe |
viṣṇuṃ cāvatariṣyantaṃ jñātvā devāḥ sanātanam || 30 ||
meaning:
अवतीर्णोऽथ देवक्या गर्भे भारावतारणे |
विष्णुं चावतरिष्यन्तं ज्ञात्वा देवाः सनातनम् || 30 ||
text_mt: descended into the womb of Devakī to remove the burden. / And knowing that the eternal Viṣṇu was about to descend,

sanskrit_iast:
rambhātilottamādyāśca devyo rūpaguṇānvitāḥ |
kṣitāvutpādayāmāsuḥ sahasrāṇi tu ṣoḍaśa || 31 ||
meaning:
रम्भातिलोत्तमाद्याश्च देव्यो रूपगुणान्विताः |
क्षितावुत्पादयामासुः सहस्राणि तु षोडश || 31 ||
text_mt: the gods brought forth sixteen thousand goddesses, / endowed with beauty and virtues, headed by Rambhā and Tilottamā, upon the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
tāḥ sarvā himavatpṛṣṭhe krīḍamānā varastriyaḥ |
apaśyannarako bhaumastā jahāra tadā haṭhāt || 32 ||
meaning:
ताः सर्वा हिमवत्पृष्ठे क्रीडमाना वरस्त्रियः |
अपश्यन्नरको भौमस्ता जहार तदा हठात् || 32 ||
text_mt: As all those excellent women were sporting on the ridge of Himavat, / Naraka, born of Bhūmi, saw them and then carried them off by force.

sanskrit_iast:
tena tā dharṣitā devyo nītāḥ prāgjyotiṣaṃ prati |
narakaṃ prārthayāmāsuḥ samayaṃ maithunaṃ prati || 33 ||
meaning:
तेन ता धर्षिता देव्यो नीताः प्राग्ज्योतिषं प्रति |
नरकं प्रार्थयामासुः समयं मैथुनं प्रति || 33 ||
text_mt: Assaulted by him and taken to Prāgjyotiṣa, / the goddesses pleaded with Naraka for a period before union:

sanskrit_iast:
nārado yāvadāyāti nagaraṃ prati bhauma te |
asmākaṃ kuru rakṣāṃ ca tāvanno muñca maithune || 34 ||
meaning:
नारदो यावदायाति नगरं प्रति भौम ते |
अस्माकं कुरु रक्षां च तावन्नो मुञ्च मैथुने || 34 ||
text_mt: “O son of Bhūmi, until Nārada comes to your city, / keep us safe and spare us from union.

sanskrit_iast:
sa sameṣyati vīra tvāṃ na cirānno hyanugrahāt |
tena dṛṣṭā vayaṃ sārdhameṣyāmaḥ saṅgamaṃ tvayā || 35 ||
meaning:
स समेष्यति वीर त्वां न चिरान्नो ह्यनुग्रहात् |
तेन दृष्टा वयं सार्धमेष्यामः सङ्गमं त्वया || 35 ||
text_mt: O hero, he will soon visit you out of grace toward us; / seen by him, we will enter into union with you.”

sanskrit_iast:
iti samprārthitastābhirnarako bhūminandanaḥ |
brahmavākyaṃ tadā smṛtvā evamastūcivān muhuḥ || 36 ||
meaning:
इति सम्प्रार्थितस्ताभिर्नरको भूमिनन्दनः |
ब्रह्मवाक्यं तदा स्मृत्वा एवमस्तूचिवान् मुहुः || 36 ||
text_mt: Thus pleaded with by them, Naraka, the delight of the Earth, / then remembered Brahmā's words and repeatedly said, “So be it.”
