text_mt: in other [directions], the fallen, severed head grants prosperity. / Any chattering sound of teeth that occurs in a severed head

sanskrit_iast:
narāṇāṃ paśupakṣyādigrāhādīnāṃ ca rogadaḥ |
lotakaṃ cakṣuṣorjātaṃ yadi sravati mastake || 131 ||
meaning:
नराणां पशुपक्ष्यादिग्राहादीनां च रोगदः |
लोतकं चक्षुषोर्जातं यदि स्रवति मस्तके || 131 ||
text_mt: of men, beasts, birds, alligators, and the like causes disease. / If a tear arising from the eyes flows when the head

sanskrit_iast:
chinne narasya rājyasya tā hāniṃ vinirdiśet |
māhiṣe mastake netrād yadi sravati lotakam || 132 ||
meaning:
छिन्ने नरस्य राज्यस्य ता हानिं विनिर्दिशेत् |
माहिषे मस्तके नेत्राद् यदि स्रवति लोतकम् || 132 ||
text_mt: of a man is severed, one should foretell the loss of the kingdom. / If a tear flows from the eye in a buffalo's head

sanskrit_iast:
chinne niveditaṃ vairibhūpamṛtyuṃ tadādiśet |
anyeṣāmatha paśvādivalīnāṃ śiraso'rditāt || 133 ||
meaning:
छिन्ने निवेदितं वैरिभूपमृत्युं तदादिशेत् |
अन्येषामथ पश्वादिवलीनां शिरसोऽर्दितात् || 133 ||
text_mt: that is severed and presented, one should predict the death of the enemy king. / If from the wounded head of other victims, such as beasts,

sanskrit_iast:
nirgataṃ lotakaṃ dhatte parāṃ bhītiṃ gadaṃ tathā |
hasati cchinnaśīrṣaṃ cennāraṃ syāt tu ripukṣayaḥ || 134 ||
meaning:
निर्गतं लोतकं धत्ते परां भीतिं गदं तथा |
हसति च्छिन्नशीर्षं चेन्नारं स्यात् तु रिपुक्षयः || 134 ||
text_mt: a flowing tear emerges, it brings supreme terror and disease. / If the severed human head laughs, there will be destruction of enemies,

sanskrit_iast:
śrīvṛddhirāyuṣo vṛddhiḥ sadā dāturasaṃśayaḥ |
yad yadvākyaṃ nigadati tathā bhavati cācirāt || 135 ||
meaning:
श्रीवृद्धिरायुषो वृद्धिः सदा दातुरसंशयः |
यद् यद्वाक्यं निगदति तथा भवति चाचिरात् || 135 ||
text_mt: increase of prosperity, and increase of life constantly for the giver, without a doubt; / and whatever words it utters come to pass before long.

sanskrit_iast:
ūṅkārādrājyahāniḥ syācchūleṣmasrāvācca pañcatā |
devānāṃ yadi nāmāni bhāṣate chinnamastakaḥ || 136 ||
meaning:
ऊङ्काराद्राज्यहानिः स्याच्छूलेष्मस्रावाच्च पञ्चता |
देवानां यदि नामानि भाषते छिन्नमस्तकः || 136 ||
text_mt: From the sound 'ūṃ' there is loss of kingdom, and from the discharge of phlegm, death. / If the severed head utters the names of the gods,

sanskrit_iast:
vibhūtimatulāṃ vidyāt ṣaṇmāsābhyantare tadā |
rudhirādānakāle tu śakṛnmūtre yadi sravet || 137 ||
meaning:
विभूतिमतुलां विद्यात् षण्मासाभ्यन्तरे तदा |
रुधिरादानकाले तु शकृन्मूत्रे यदि स्रवेत् || 137 ||
text_mt: one should know that incomparable power [will arise] within six months. / If at the time of taking the blood, feces and urine should flow

sanskrit_iast:
kāyaṃ tadādhaścordhvaṃ vā dātuḥ syānmaraṇaṃ tadā |
ākṣepād vāmapādasya mahārogaḥ prajāyate || 138 ||
meaning:
कायं तदाधश्चोर्ध्वं वा दातुः स्यान्मरणं तदा |
आक्षेपाद् वामपादस्य महारोगः प्रजायते || 138 ||
text_mt: from the body then, below or above, the giver will die. / From a twitching of the left foot, great disease arises;

sanskrit_iast:
anyadākṣepacalanaiḥ kalyāṇamupajāyate |
māhiṣasya tu raktasya mānuṣasya tu sādhakaḥ || 139 ||
meaning:
अन्यदाक्षेपचलनैः कल्याणमुपजायते |
माहिषस्य तु रक्तस्य मानुषस्य तु साधकः || 139 ||
text_mt: from other twitching and movements, welfare arises. / The practitioner, with the blood of a buffalo or of a human,

sanskrit_iast:
aṅguṣṭhānāmikābhyāṃ tu kiṃciduddhṛtya bhūtale |
mahākauśikamantreṇa nikṣiped balimuttamam || 140 ||
meaning:
अङ्गुष्ठानामिकाभ्यां तु किंचिदुद्धृत्य भूतले |
महाकौशिकमन्त्रेण निक्षिपेद् बलिमुत्तमम् || 140 ||
text_mt: having taken up a little between the thumb and ring finger, / should cast the excellent offering onto the ground with the Mahākauśika mantra,

sanskrit_iast:
devebhyaḥ pūtanādibhyo nair-ṛtyāṃ diśī pūrvataḥ |
mahiṣaḥ pañcavarṣīyaḥ pañcaviṃśativārṣikaḥ || 141 ||
meaning:
देवेभ्यः पूतनादिभ्यो नैर्-ऋत्यां दिशी पूर्वतः |
महिषः पञ्चवर्षीयः पञ्चविंशतिवार्षिकः || 141 ||
text_mt: for the gods such as Pūtanā and others, in the south-west quarter, facing east. / A five-year-old buffalo and a twenty-five-year-old

sanskrit_iast:
balirdeyo naro devyai tasya raktaṃ tu bhūtaye |
netrabījatrayaṃ kāmabījaṃ hantā prajāpatiḥ || 142 ||
meaning:
बलिर्देयो नरो देव्यै तस्य रक्तं तु भूतये |
नेत्रबीजत्रयं कामबीजं हन्ता प्रजापतिः || 142 ||
text_mt: human should be offered as a victim to the goddess, and its blood [is] for prosperity. / Three netra-bījas, the kāma-bīja, 'hantā', Prajāpati,

sanskrit_iast:
vahnibījaṃ ṣaṭsvarābhyāṃ saṃpṛktaśca tathā paraḥ |
sa evaitāstathaitāvadādivargāntasaṃyutaḥ || 143 ||
meaning:
वह्निबीजं षट्स्वराभ्यां संपृक्तश्च तथा परः |
स एवैतास्तथैतावदादिवर्गान्तसंयुतः || 143 ||
text_mt: the vahni-bīja, connected with six vowels, and then the other; / that same, and then combined with the end of the initial group,

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṣṭhasvaraśikhābinduścandrayuktasthāparaḥ |
virmāsikābījakāntaḥ kauśikītyabhimantraṇam || 144 ||
meaning:
षष्ठस्वरशिखाबिन्दुश्चन्द्रयुक्तस्थापरः |
विर्मासिकाबीजकान्तः कौशिकीत्यभिमन्त्रणम् || 144 ||
text_mt: with the crest-bindu of the sixth vowel, joined with the moon, and then another; / ending with the bīja of the two nostrils, the consecration with 'Kauśikī',

sanskrit_iast:
eṣa baliḥ svāheti mantro'yaṃ kauśikī smṛtaḥ |
nṛpo vairibaliṃ dadyāt khaḍgamāmantrya pūrvataḥ || 145 ||
meaning:
एष बलिः स्वाहेति मन्त्रोऽयं कौशिकी स्मृतः |
नृपो वैरिबलिं दद्यात् खड्गमामन्त्र्य पूर्वतः || 145 ||
text_mt: 'eṣa baliḥ svāhā'—this mantra is remembered as Kauśikī. / A king should offer an enemy-victim, having first consecrated the sword;

sanskrit_iast:
mahiṣaṃ cātha chāgaṃ vā vairināmnābhimantrya ca |
sūtreṇa vadane baddhaṃ tridhā tasya tu mantrakaiḥ || 146 ||
meaning:
महिषं चाथ छागं वा वैरिनाम्नाभिमन्त्र्य च |
सूत्रेण वदने बद्धं त्रिधा तस्य तु मन्त्रकैः || 146 ||
text_mt: and having consecrated a buffalo or goat with the enemy's name, / tied around its mouth thrice with a thread by means of mantras,

sanskrit_iast:
chittvā tasyottamāṅgaṃ tu devyai dadyāt prayatnataḥ |
yadā yadā riporvṛddhirvalidānaṃ tadā param || 147 ||
meaning:
छित्त्वा तस्योत्तमाङ्गं तु देव्यै दद्यात् प्रयत्नतः |
यदा यदा रिपोर्वृद्धिर्वलिदानं तदा परम् || 147 ||
text_mt: Having cut off its head, he should carefully offer it to the goddess. / Whenever the enemy grows [in power], the supreme offering of sacrifice is then [prescribed].

sanskrit_iast:
dadyāt tadā śiraśchittvā ripostasya kṣayāya ca |
prāṇapratiṣṭhāṃ ca ripoḥ kuryāt tasmin paśāvaya || 148 ||
meaning:
दद्यात् तदा शिरश्छित्त्वा रिपोस्तस्य क्षयाय च |
प्राणप्रतिष्ठां च रिपोः कुर्यात् तस्मिन् पशावय || 148 ||
text_mt: He should then offer it after severing the head, for the destruction of that enemy. / And he should perform the installation of life-breath of the enemy into that animal.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmin kṣīṇe ripoḥ prāṇāḥ kṣīyante vipadā yutāḥ |
ādau viruddharūpiṇi caṇḍike ca tataḥ param || 149 ||
meaning:
तस्मिन् क्षीणे रिपोः प्राणाः क्षीयन्ते विपदा युताः |
आदौ विरुद्धरूपिणि चण्डिके च ततः परम् || 149 ||
text_mt: When it is destroyed, the enemy's life-breaths, accompanied by disaster, are destroyed. / First [the words] 'O Caṇḍikā of opposing form!', and thereafter,

sanskrit_iast:
vairiṇantvamukaṃ ceti yāhītyāmreḍitaṃ punaḥ |
vahnibhāryā tataḥ paścāt khaḍgamantraṃ prakīrtitam || 150 ||
meaning:
वैरिणन्त्वमुकं चेति याहीत्याम्रेडितं पुनः |
वह्निभार्या ततः पश्चात् खड्गमन्त्रं प्रकीर्तितम् || 150 ||
text_mt: 'go to the enemy so-and-so!', with 'go' repeated once again, / then followed by 'the wife of fire' (svāhā)—this is declared to be the sword-mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
svayaṃ sa vairī yo dveṣṭi tamimaṃ paśurūpiṇam |
vināśaya mahāmārī spheṃ spheṃ khādaya khādaya || 151 ||
meaning:
स्वयं स वैरी यो द्वेष्टि तमिमं पशुरूपिणम् |
विनाशय महामारी स्फें स्फें खादय खादय || 151 ||
text_mt: 'He himself is the enemy who hates; destroy him, this one in animal form, / O Mahāmārī! Spheṃ spheṃ, devour, devour!'

sanskrit_iast:
ityanena tu mantreṇa vadvyaḥ śirasi puṣpakam |
dadyāt tatastadrudhiraṃ dvyakṣarābhyāṃ nivedayet || 152 ||
meaning:
इत्यनेन तु मन्त्रेण वद्व्यः शिरसि पुष्पकम् |
दद्यात् ततस्तद्रुधिरं द्व्यक्षराभ्यां निवेदयेत् || 152 ||
text_mt: With this mantra, indeed, he should place a flower on the head of the victim. / Then he should offer its blood with the two-syllabled [mantra].

sanskrit_iast:
mahānavamyāṃ śaradi yadyevaṃ dīyate baliḥ |
tadā tadaṣṭāṅgabhavairmāṃsairhomaṃ samācaret || 153 ||
meaning:
महानवम्यां शरदि यद्येवं दीयते बलिः |
तदा तदष्टाङ्गभवैर्मांसैर्होमं समाचरेत् || 153 ||
text_mt: If the sacrifice is offered in this manner on Mahānavamī in autumn, / he should then perform an oblation with the meat derived from its eight limbs,

sanskrit_iast:
durgātantreṇa mantreṇa praṇīte dahane śucau |
evaṃ dattvā baliṃ martyo ripukṣayamavāpnuyāt || 154 ||
meaning:
दुर्गातन्त्रेण मन्त्रेण प्रणीते दहने शुचौ |
एवं दत्त्वा बलिं मर्त्यो रिपुक्षयमवाप्नुयात् || 154 ||
text_mt: into pure fire brought forth with the mantra of the Durgātantra. / By offering the sacrifice thus, a mortal obtains the destruction of his enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
nābheradhastādrudhiraṃ pṛṣṭhabhāgasya ca śriye |
svagātrarudhirai dadyānna kadācana sādhakaḥ || 155 ||
meaning:
नाभेरधस्ताद्रुधिरं पृष्ठभागस्य च श्रिये |
स्वगात्ररुधिरै दद्यान्न कदाचन साधकः || 155 ||
text_mt: A practitioner should never offer blood from below the navel, / or from the back, for the sake of prosperity, from his own bodily blood.

sanskrit_iast:
noṣṭhasya cibukasyāpi nendriyāṇāṃ ca mānavaḥ |
kaṇṭhādho nābhitaścordhvaṃ bāhvoḥ pāṇimṛte tathā || 156 ||
meaning:
नोष्ठस्य चिबुकस्यापि नेन्द्रियाणां च मानवः |
कण्ठाधो नाभितश्चोर्ध्वं बाह्वोः पाणिमृते तथा || 156 ||
text_mt: Nor [should] a man [offer blood] from the lip, from the chin, or from the sense organs; / [he may offer] from below the throat and above the navel, and from the two arms, except the hands;

sanskrit_iast:
pradadyādrudhiraṃ ghātaṃ nātikuryācca sādhakaḥ |
gaṇḍayośca lalāṭasya bhruvormadhyasya śoṇitam || 157 ||
meaning:
प्रदद्याद्रुधिरं घातं नातिकुर्याच्च साधकः |
गण्डयोश्च ललाटस्य भ्रुवोर्मध्यस्य शोणितम् || 157 ||
text_mt: the practitioner may offer blood, but he should not make too deep a wound. / The blood of the two cheeks, of the forehead, of the space between the eyebrows,

sanskrit_iast:
karṇāgrasya ca bāhvośca galayo rudarasya ca |
kaṇṭhādo nābhitaścordhvaṃ hṛdbhāgasya yatastataḥ || 158 ||
meaning:
कर्णाग्रस्य च बाह्वोश्च गलयो रुदरस्य च |
कण्ठादो नाभितश्चोर्ध्वं हृद्भागस्य यतस्ततः || 158 ||
text_mt: of the tip of the ear, of the two arms, of the two sides of the neck, and of the belly, / [and] from here and there in the region of the heart, below the throat and above the navel,

sanskrit_iast:
pārśvayoścāpi rudhiraṃ durgāyai vinivedayet |
na gulpato'sṛkpradadyānna jatrornāpi vaktrataḥ || 159 ||
meaning:
पार्श्वयोश्चापि रुधिरं दुर्गायै विनिवेदयेत् |
न गुल्पतोऽसृक्प्रदद्यान्न जत्रोर्नापि वक्त्रतः || 159 ||
text_mt: and also the blood of the two flanks, he should present to Durgā. / He should not offer blood from the ankle, nor from the collarbone, nor from the mouth,

sanskrit_iast:
na ca rogabilādaṅgānnānyaghātācca bhairava |
tadarthe ca kṛtāghātaḥ saśraddho'kṣubdhamānasaḥ || 160 ||
meaning:
न च रोगबिलादङ्गान्नान्यघाताच्च भैरव |
तदर्थे च कृताघातः सश्रद्धोऽक्षुब्धमानसः || 160 ||
text_mt: nor from a diseased cavity, nor from a limb wounded by another, O Bhairava. / Having made an incision for that purpose, endowed with faith, with an unagitated mind,

sanskrit_iast:
śrute raktaṃ pradadyāttu padmapuṣpasya patrake |
sauvarṇe rājate kāṃsye lauhe phāle na vā naraḥ || 161 ||
meaning:
श्रुते रक्तं प्रदद्यात्तु पद्मपुष्पस्य पत्रके |
सौवर्णे राजते कांस्ये लौहे फाले न वा नरः || 161 ||
text_mt: when it flows, a man should offer the blood in a lotus petal, / [or] in [a vessel] of gold, of silver, of bell-metal, or of iron, but not in an iron ploughshare.

sanskrit_iast:
nidhāya devyai dadyāt tu tadraktaṃ mantrapūrvakam |
khananaṃ kṣurikākhaḍgaśaṅkulādi yadastrakam || 162 ||
meaning:
निधाय देव्यै दद्यात् तु तद्रक्तं मन्त्रपूर्वकम् |
खननं क्षुरिकाखड्गशङ्कुलादि यदस्त्रकम् || 162 ||
text_mt: Having placed it, he should offer that blood to the goddess, preceded by mantras. / An incision [may be made with] a knife, a sword, a spear, or whatever weapon;

sanskrit_iast:
ghātena bṛhadastrasya mahāphalamavāpnuyāt |
padmapuṣpasya patraṃ tu yāvad gṛhṇāti śoṇitam || 163 ||
meaning:
घातेन बृहदस्त्रस्य महाफलमवाप्नुयात् |
पद्मपुष्पस्य पत्रं तु यावद् गृह्णाति शोणितम् || 163 ||
text_mt: by a wound from a large weapon, he obtains great fruit. / As much blood as a lotus petal can hold,

sanskrit_iast:
tatpramāṇe caturbhāgādhikaṃ raktaṃ tu sādhakaḥ |
na kadācit pradadyāttu nāṅgacchedamathācaret || 164 ||
meaning:
तत्प्रमाणे चतुर्भागाधिकं रक्तं तु साधकः |
न कदाचित् प्रदद्यात्तु नाङ्गच्छेदमथाचरेत् || 164 ||
text_mt: the practitioner should never offer blood exceeding that measure by a quarter part, / nor should he amputate a limb.

sanskrit_iast:
yaḥ svahṛdayasañjātamāṃsaṃ māṣapramāṇataḥ |
tilamudgapramāṇād vā devyai dadyāt tu bhaktitaḥ || 165 ||
meaning:
यः स्वहृदयसञ्जातमांसं माषप्रमाणतः |
तिलमुद्गप्रमाणाद् वा देव्यै दद्यात् तु भक्तितः || 165 ||
text_mt: He who offers flesh originating from his own heart, of the measure of a māṣa bean, / or of the measure of a sesame seed or a mudga bean, with devotion to the goddess,

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṇmāsābhyantare tasmāt kāmamiṣṭamavāpnuyāt |
bāhvostu skandhayorvāpi yo dadyād dīpavartikām || 166 ||
meaning:
षण्मासाभ्यन्तरे तस्मात् काममिष्टमवाप्नुयात् |
बाह्वोस्तु स्कन्धयोर्वापि यो दद्याद् दीपवर्तिकाम् || 166 ||
text_mt: obtains his desired wish from that within six months. / He who places a burning lamp-wick on his two arms or on his shoulders,

sanskrit_iast:
hṛdaye vā snehapātraṃ vinā bhaktyā tu sādhakaḥ |
kṣaṇamātreṇa taddīpapradānasya phalaṃ śṛṇu || 167 ||
meaning:
हृदये वा स्नेहपात्रं विना भक्त्या तु साधकः |
क्षणमात्रेण तद्दीपप्रदानस्य फलं शृणु || 167 ||
text_mt: or on his chest, without a vessel of oil, out of devotion, O practitioner— / hear the fruit of offering that lamp for merely a moment:

sanskrit_iast:
bhuktvā ca vipulān bhogān devīgehe yadṛcchayā |
kalpatrayaṃ tu saṃsthāya sārvabhaumo nṛpo bhavet || 168 ||
meaning:
भुक्त्वा च विपुलान् भोगान् देवीगेहे यदृच्छया |
कल्पत्रयं तु संस्थाय सार्वभौमो नृपो भवेत् || 168 ||
text_mt: having enjoyed abundant pleasures at will in the abode of the goddess, / and having remained there for three kalpas, he becomes a universal monarch.

sanskrit_iast:
mahiṣasya śiraśchinnaṃ sapradīpaṃ śivāpuraḥ |
hastābhyāṃ yaḥ samādāya ahorātraṃ tu tiṣṭhati || 169 ||
meaning:
महिषस्य शिरश्छिन्नं सप्रदीपं शिवापुरः |
हस्ताभ्यां यः समादाय अहोरात्रं तु तिष्ठति || 169 ||
text_mt: He who, having taken the severed head of a buffalo with a burning lamp in his two hands, / stands for a day and a night before Śivā,

sanskrit_iast:
sa cirāyuḥ pūtamūrtiriha bhuktvā manoramān |
bhogānte madgṛhago gaṇānāmadhipo bhavet || 170 ||
meaning:
स चिरायुः पूतमूर्तिरिह भुक्त्वा मनोरमान् |
भोगान्ते मद्गृहगो गणानामधिपो भवेत् || 170 ||
text_mt: he, of long life and purified form, having enjoyed charming [pleasures] in this world, / at the end of his pleasures goes to my abode and becomes a lord of the gaṇas.

sanskrit_iast:
narasya śīrṣamādāya sādhako dakṣiṇe kare |
vāmena raudhiraṃ pātraṃ gṛhītvā niśi jāgrataḥ || 171 ||
meaning:
नरस्य शीर्षमादाय साधको दक्षिणे करे |
वामेन रौधिरं पात्रं गृहीत्वा निशि जाग्रतः || 171 ||
text_mt: A practitioner who, holding a human head in his right hand / and a vessel of blood in his left, stays awake through the night—

sanskrit_iast:
yāvadrātraṃ sthito martyo rājā bhavati ceha vai |
mṛte mama gṛhaṃ prāpya gaṇānāmadhip bhavet || 172 ||
meaning:
यावद्रात्रं स्थितो मर्त्यो राजा भवति चेह वै |
मृते मम गृहं प्राप्य गणानामधिप् भवेत् || 172 ||
text_mt: for as long as the night the mortal stands, he indeed becomes a king in this world; / upon death, having attained my abode, he becomes a lord of the gaṇas.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣaṇamātraṃ valīnāṃ yaḥ śiroraktaṃ karadvaye |
gṛhītvā cintayed devīṃ purastiṣṭhati mānavaḥ || 173 ||
meaning:
क्षणमात्रं वलीनां यः शिरोरक्तं करद्वये |
गृहीत्वा चिन्तयेद् देवीं पुरस्तिष्ठति मानवः || 173 ||
text_mt: A man who, taking the head and blood of sacrificial victims in both hands / for merely a moment, stands before [the goddess] meditating upon her,

sanskrit_iast:
sa kāmāniha samprāpya devīloke mahīyate |
mahāmāye jagannāthe sarvakāmapradāyini || 174 ||
meaning:
स कामानिह सम्प्राप्य देवीलोके महीयते |
महामाये जगन्नाथे सर्वकामप्रदायिनि || 174 ||
text_mt: he, having attained his desires in this world, is exalted in the realm of the goddess: / 'O Mahāmāyā, O mistress of the universe, O giver of all desires!

sanskrit_iast:
dadāmi deharudhiraṃ prasīda varadā bhava |
ityuktvā mūlamantreṇa natipūrva vicakṣaṇaḥ || 175 ||
meaning:
ददामि देहरुधिरं प्रसीद वरदा भव |
इत्युक्त्वा मूलमन्त्रेण नतिपूर्व विचक्षणः || 175 ||
text_mt: I give my bodily blood; be pleased, be a giver of boons!' / Having spoken thus with the root-mantra, preceded by prostration, the wise,

sanskrit_iast:
svagātrarudhiraṃ dadyād mānavaḥ siddhasannibhaḥ |
yanātmamāṃsaṃ satyena dadāmīśvari bhūtaye || 176 ||
meaning:
स्वगात्ररुधिरं दद्याद् मानवः सिद्धसन्निभः |
यनात्ममांसं सत्येन ददामीश्वरि भूतये || 176 ||
text_mt: perfected-like man should offer his own bodily blood: / 'Since, by this truth, I give my own flesh, O Īśvarī, for prosperity,

sanskrit_iast:
nirvāṇaṃ tena satyena dehi haṃ haṃ namo namaḥ |
ityanena tu mantreṇa svamāṃsaṃ vitared budhaḥ || 177 ||
meaning:
निर्वाणं तेन सत्येन देहि हं हं नमो नमः |
इत्यनेन तु मन्त्रेण स्वमांसं वितरेद् बुधः || 177 ||
text_mt: by that truth grant me liberation! Haṃ haṃ, salutation, salutation!' / With this mantra the wise man should bestow his own flesh.

sanskrit_iast:
saubhāgyaṃ sukhasampannaṃ pradīpaṃ paramaṃ ruciḥ |
dīpayenmāṃsamiha taṃ dīpaṃ hnauṃ hnauṃ namo namaḥ || 178 ||
meaning:
सौभाग्यं सुखसम्पन्नं प्रदीपं परमं रुचिः |
दीपयेन्मांसमिह तं दीपं ह्नौं ह्नौं नमो नमः || 178 ||
text_mt: 'Endowed with fortune and happiness, the lamp is of supreme brilliance; / let it kindle that flesh here, the lamp! Hnauṃ hnauṃ, salutation, salutation!'

sanskrit_iast:
ityanena tu mantreṇa dīpaṃ dadyād vicakṣaṇaḥ |
mahānavamyāṃ śaradi rātrau skandaviśākhayoḥ || 179 ||
meaning:
इत्यनेन तु मन्त्रेण दीपं दद्याद् विचक्षणः |
महानवम्यां शरदि रात्रौ स्कन्दविशाखयोः || 179 ||
text_mt: With this mantra the discerning man should offer the lamp. / On Mahānavamī in autumn, at night, for Skanda and Viśākha,

sanskrit_iast:
yavacūrṇamayaṃ kṛtvā ripuṃ mṛnmayameva vā |
śiraśchittvā baliṃ dadyāt kṛtvā tasya tu mantrataḥ || 180 ||
meaning:
यवचूर्णमयं कृत्वा रिपुं मृन्मयमेव वा |
शिरश्छित्त्वा बलिं दद्यात् कृत्वा तस्य तु मन्त्रतः || 180 ||
text_mt: having fashioned an enemy made of barley flour or made of clay, / having severed its head, he should offer it as a sacrifice after consecrating it with mantras.

sanskrit_iast:
anenaiva tu mantreṇa khaḍgamāmantrya yatnataḥ |
raktaṃ kilikilī ghora ghorādhāravihiṃsakaḥ || 181 ||
meaning:
अनेनैव तु मन्त्रेण खड्गमामन्त्र्य यत्नतः |
रक्तं किलिकिली घोर घोराधारविहिंसकः || 181 ||
text_mt: Having carefully consecrated the sword with this very mantra: / 'Blood, kilikilī, terrible, destructive of the support of terror,

sanskrit_iast:
brahmaśiṣyāmbikāśiṣyamamukaṃ cārisattamam |
ānto visargasahitaḥ sa ca binduyuto'paraḥ || 182 ||
meaning:
ब्रह्मशिष्याम्बिकाशिष्यममुकं चारिसत्तमम् |
आन्तो विसर्गसहितः स च बिन्दुयुतोऽपरः || 182 ||
text_mt: disciple of Brahmā, disciple of Ambikā, such-and-such excellent enemy!' / Ending in ā with a visarga, and another endowed with a bindu,

sanskrit_iast:
śiraśchittvā valiṃ dadyāt kṛtvā tasya tu mantrataḥ |
anenaiva tu mantreṇa bindunā ca samanvitaḥ || 183 ||
meaning:
शिरश्छित्त्वा वलिं दद्यात् कृत्वा तस्य तु मन्त्रतः |
अनेनैव तु मन्त्रेण बिन्दुना च समन्वितः || 183 ||
text_mt: having cut off the head, he should offer the sacrifice, having consecrated it with the mantra, / joined with this very mantra and accompanied by a bindu.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmāgniryogacandreṇa bindunā ca samanvitaḥ |
phaḍanto valiṣu proktaḥ khaḍgaḥ skandaviśākhayoḥ || 184 ||
meaning:
ब्रह्माग्निर्योगचन्द्रेण बिन्दुना च समन्वितः |
फडन्तो वलिषु प्रोक्तः खड्गः स्कन्दविशाखयोः || 184 ||
text_mt: Brahmā's fire joined with the moon and accompanied by a bindu, / ending in phaṭ, is declared as the sword in sacrifices to Skanda and Viśākha.

sanskrit_iast:
raktadravyaiḥ śocayitvā kṛtrimaṃ taṃ valiṃ ripum |
kucandanasya tilakaṃ lalāṭe viniveśya ca || 185 ||
meaning:
रक्तद्रव्यैः शोचयित्वा कृत्रिमं तं वलिं रिपुम् |
कुचन्दनस्य तिलकं ललाटे विनिवेश्य च || 185 ||
text_mt: Having purified that artificial sacrificial victim, the enemy, with red substances, / and having placed a mark of red sandalwood on its forehead,

sanskrit_iast:
raktamālyāmbaraṃ kṛtvā raktavastradharaṃ tathā |
kaṇṭhe baddhvā raktasūtrairnābhau śalyaṃ ca kṛtrimam || 186 ||
meaning:
रक्तमाल्याम्बरं कृत्वा रक्तवस्त्रधरं तथा |
कण्ठे बद्ध्वा रक्तसूत्रैर्नाभौ शल्यं च कृत्रिमम् || 186 ||
text_mt: having adorned it with a red garland and garments, and making it wear red cloth, / having bound it at the neck with red threads, and having fixed an artificial dart in the navel,

sanskrit_iast:
dattvottaraśiraḥ skandhaṃ kṛtvā khaḍgena chedayet |
śirastasya tato dadyāt skandamantreṇa mantritam || 187 ||
meaning:
दत्त्वोत्तरशिरः स्कन्धं कृत्वा खड्गेन छेदयेत् |
शिरस्तस्य ततो दद्यात् स्कन्दमन्त्रेण मन्त्रितम् || 187 ||
text_mt: having placed its head and shoulder to the north, he should sever it with the sword. / Then he should offer its head, consecrated with the mantra of Skanda.

sanskrit_iast:
caturdaśasvarāgnibhyāṃ sampṛktaḥ stāt puraḥsakam |
parataḥ parataḥ pūrvaṃ candrabindusamanvitam || 188 ||
meaning:
चतुर्दशस्वराग्निभ्यां सम्पृक्तः स्तात् पुरःसकम् |
परतः परतः पूर्वं चन्द्रबिन्दुसमन्वितम् || 188 ||
text_mt: Combined with the fourteenth vowel and fire, preceded by s and t, / and further, as before, accompanied by the crescent moon and dot (candrabindu),

sanskrit_iast:
skandasya mūlamantro'yaṃ tena tasmai baliṃ sṛjet |
caturdaśasvarāgnibhyāṃ tṛtīyaṃ tu ca pūrvavat || 189 ||
meaning:
स्कन्दस्य मूलमन्त्रोऽयं तेन तस्मै बलिं सृजेत् |
चतुर्दशस्वराग्निभ्यां तृतीयं तु च पूर्ववत् || 189 ||
text_mt: this is the root-mantra of Skanda; with it he should offer the sacrifice to him. / With the fourteenth vowel and fire, the third [syllable is formed] as before.

sanskrit_iast:
prokto viśākhamantro'yaṃ tena tasmai baliṃ sṛjet |
kuṭilākṣo kṛṣṇapiṅgavarṇau raktāṅgadhāriṇau || 190 ||
meaning:
प्रोक्तो विशाखमन्त्रोऽयं तेन तस्मै बलिं सृजेत् |
कुटिलाक्षो कृष्णपिङ्गवर्णौ रक्ताङ्गधारिणौ || 190 ||
text_mt: This is declared to be the Viśākha mantra; with it one should offer sacrifice to him. / Having squinting eyes, black and reddish-brown in color, wearing red garments,

sanskrit_iast:
triśūlaṃ karavālaṃ ca pāṇibhyāṃ dakṣiṇe tathā |
bibhratau nṛkapālaṃ ca katrikāṃ cāti vāmataḥ || 191 ||
meaning:
त्रिशूलं करवालं च पाणिभ्यां दक्षिणे तथा |
बिभ्रतौ नृकपालं च कत्रिकां चाति वामतः || 191 ||
text_mt: holding a trident and a sword in their right hands, / and bearing a human skull and a knife on their left;

sanskrit_iast:
trinetrau naramuṇḍānāṃ mālāmurasi bibhratau |
vikaṭau daśanairbhīmairgaṇeśau dvārapālakau || 192 ||
meaning:
त्रिनेत्रौ नरमुण्डानां मालामुरसि बिभ्रतौ |
विकटौ दशनैर्भीमैर्गणेशौ द्वारपालकौ || 192 ||
text_mt: three-eyed, wearing a garland of human heads upon their chest, / fierce with terrible fangs—the two gaṇa-chiefs, the door-keepers,

sanskrit_iast:
dhyānena cintayed devyāḥ purataḥ saṃsthitau sadā |
caitre māsyasite pakṣe caturdaśyāṃ viśeṣataḥ || 193 ||
meaning:
ध्यानेन चिन्तयेद् देव्याः पुरतः संस्थितौ सदा |
चैत्रे मास्यसिते पक्षे चतुर्दश्यां विशेषतः || 193 ||
text_mt: one should always contemplate through meditation as standing before the Goddess, / especially in the month of Caitra, during the dark fortnight, on the fourteenth day.

sanskrit_iast:
valibhirmahiṣaiśchāgaiḥ māṃ ca bhairavarūpiṇam |
toṣayenmadhumirmāṃsaistena tuṣyāmyahaṃ sutau || 194 ||
meaning:
वलिभिर्महिषैश्छागैः मां च भैरवरूपिणम् |
तोषयेन्मधुमिर्मांसैस्तेन तुष्याम्यहं सुतौ || 194 ||
text_mt: With sacrifices of buffaloes and goats, and with wine and meat, / one should satisfy me in the form of Bhairava; by that I am pleased, O sons.

sanskrit_iast:
caṇḍikā validāne tu valiśīrṣaṃ jalena ca |
abhiṣicya tu mantreṇa mūlenaiva nivedayet || 195 ||
meaning:
चण्डिका वलिदाने तु वलिशीर्षं जलेन च |
अभिषिच्य तु मन्त्रेण मूलेनैव निवेदयेत् || 195 ||
text_mt: In the animal sacrifice to Caṇḍikā, having sprinkled the severed head of the sacrificial victim with water, / one should present it indeed with the root mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
īṣatprāṇaṃ tu bahudhā calitaṃ pūrvamarcitam |
vīkṣetkāyasamṛddhiṃ tu siddhabhāvaṃ ca sādhakaḥ || 196 ||
meaning:
ईषत्प्राणं तु बहुधा चलितं पूर्वमर्चितम् |
वीक्षेत्कायसमृद्धिं तु सिद्धभावं च साधकः || 196 ||
text_mt: Slightly breathing and twitching repeatedly, having been worshipped earlier, / the practitioner should observe the fullness of the body and the attainment of perfection.

sanskrit_iast:
sitapreto rathasteṣāṃ yogapīṭhasya sannibhaḥ |
dhyāyāmyasmin mahāmāye siddhiṃ bodhayate namaḥ || 197 ||
meaning:
सितप्रेतो रथस्तेषां योगपीठस्य सन्निभः |
ध्यायाम्यस्मिन् महामाये सिद्धिं बोधयते नमः || 197 ||
text_mt: ‘A white corpse is their chariot, resembling the yoga-seat; / I meditate upon this, O Mahāmāyā; obeisance to the one who reveals perfection.’

sanskrit_iast:
anenāmantritaṃ śīrṣaṃ na cirād yadi vepate |
tatkāryasya tadā siddhirasiddhistu viparyayāt || 198 ||
meaning:
अनेनामन्त्रितं शीर्षं न चिराद् यदि वेपते |
तत्कार्यस्य तदा सिद्धिरसिद्धिस्तु विपर्ययात् || 198 ||
text_mt: Consecrated with this [mantra], if the head soon trembles, / then there is success in that endeavor; but failure from the contrary.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ dadad vīro yathokta vidhinā'munā |
validānādeva caturvargamāpnotyasaṃśayam || 199 ||
meaning:
एवं ददद् वीरो यथोक्त विधिनाऽमुना |
वलिदानादेव चतुर्वर्गमाप्नोत्यसंशयम् || 199 ||
text_mt: Offering thus according to this prescribed rule, the hero / undoubtedly attains the four aims of life from the very offering of the sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ valipradānasya kramo rūpaṃ tathaiva ca |
kathito rudhirādhyāya upacārāñ śṛṇuṣva me || 200 ||
meaning:
एवं वलिप्रदानस्य क्रमो रूपं तथैव च |
कथितो रुधिराध्याय उपचाराञ् शृणुष्व मे || 200 ||
text_mt: Thus the order and the manner of offering animal sacrifice / has been explained in the Blood Chapter. Hear from me the ritual services.

sanskrit_iast:
iti śrīkālikāpurāṇe validānavivaraṇaṃ nāma aptaṣaṣṭitamo'dhyāyaḥ || 67 ||
aṣṭaṣaṣṭitamo'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
इति श्रीकालिकापुराणे वलिदानविवरणं नाम अप्तषष्टितमोऽध्यायः || 67 ||
अष्टषष्टितमोऽध्यायः
text_mt:
Thus ends the sixty-seventh chapter, named the Description of Animal Sacrifice, in the glorious Kālikāpurāṇa.
Chapter Sixty-eight.

sanskrit_iast: śrībhagavānuvāca
meaning: श्रीभगवानुवाच

sanskrit_iast:
upacārān pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu ṣoḍaśa bhairava |
yaḥ samyak tuṣyate devo devo'pyanyo hi bhaktitaḥ || 1 ||
meaning:
उपचारान् प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु षोडश भैरव |
यः सम्यक् तुष्यते देवो देवोऽप्यन्यो हि भक्तितः || 1 ||
text_mt: I will explain the sixteen ritual services; listen, O Bhairava, / by which the god is thoroughly pleased, and any other deity as well, through devotion.

sanskrit_iast:
āsanaṃ prathamaṃ dadyāt pauṣṇyaṃ dāravameva vā |
vāstraṃ vā cārmaṇaṃ kauśaṃ maṇḍalasyottare sṛjet || 2 ||
meaning:
आसनं प्रथमं दद्यात् पौष्ण्यं दारवमेव वा |
वास्त्रं वा चार्मणं कौशं मण्डलस्योत्तरे सृजेत् || 2 ||
text_mt: First one should offer a seat—made of flowers, of wood, / of cloth, of hide, or of kuśa grass; one should arrange it to the north of the maṇḍala.

sanskrit_iast:
yadaiva dīyate padme maṇḍalasya tadutsṛjet |
vākpuṣpatoyaiḥ kusumaṃ vinā yacchādakaṃ bhavet || 3 ||
meaning:
यदैव दीयते पद्मे मण्डलस्य तदुत्सृजेत् |
वाक्पुष्पतोयैः कुसुमं विना यच्छादकं भवेत् || 3 ||
text_mt: Whenever it is offered in the lotus of the maṇḍala, then one should discard / what serves as a covering without speech, flowers, and water.

sanskrit_iast:
padmasya tadbahirdeśe dvārādau vinivedayet |
arghyaṃ pādyaṃ cācamanaṃ snānīyaṃ netrarañjanam || 4 ||
meaning:
पद्मस्य तद्बहिर्देशे द्वारादौ विनिवेदयेत् |
अर्घ्यं पाद्यं चाचमनं स्नानीयं नेत्ररञ्जनम् || 4 ||
text_mt: Outside the lotus, at the entrance and other places, one should present it. / Water for respect, water for the feet, water for sipping, bath water, and eye salve,

sanskrit_iast:
madhuparkaṃ ca gandhaṃ ca puṣpaṃ padme nivedayet |
pratimāsu ca yadyogyaṃ gātre dātuṃ ca tat tanau || 5 ||
meaning:
मधुपर्कं च गन्धं च पुष्पं पद्मे निवेदयेत् |
प्रतिमासु च यद्योग्यं गात्रे दातुं च तत् तनौ || 5 ||
text_mt: madhuparka, fragrant paste, and flowers one should present on the lotus, / and on images, whatever is appropriate to place upon the body, [one should place] upon the form;

sanskrit_iast:
dadyād yogyaṃ tu purato naivedyaṃ bhojanādikam |
pauṣpāsanaṃ yad vihitaṃ yasya tad yadi garbhakam || 6 ||
meaning:
दद्याद् योग्यं तु पुरतो नैवेद्यं भोजनादिकम् |
पौष्पासनं यद् विहितं यस्य तद् यदि गर्भकम् || 6 ||
text_mt: and one should place before [the deity] the appropriate food offering consisting of a meal and the like. / If a flower-seat is prescribed, whatever is suitable for the interior,

sanskrit_iast:
nivedayet tadā padme vipulaṃ dvāri cotsṛjet |
pauṣpaṃ puṣpaugharacitaṃ kuśasūtrādisaṃyutam || 7 ||
meaning:
निवेदयेत् तदा पद्मे विपुलं द्वारि चोत्सृजेत् |
पौष्पं पुष्पौघरचितं कुशसूत्रादिसंयुतम् || 7 ||
text_mt: one should then present on the lotus, and discard a large one at the door. / A flower-seat made from a mass of flowers, joined with kuśa cord and other materials,

sanskrit_iast:
atiprītikaraṃ devyā mamāpynyasya bhairava |
yajñakāṣṭhasamudbhutamāsanaṃ masṛṇaṃ śubham || 8 ||
meaning:
अतिप्रीतिकरं देव्या ममाप्य्न्यस्य भैरव |
यज्ञकाष्ठसमुद्भुतमासनं मसृणं शुभम् || 8 ||
text_mt: causes great pleasure to the Goddess, and also to me and others, O Bhairava. / A seat made of sacrificial wood, smooth and auspicious,

sanskrit_iast:
nocchrāyaṃ nātivistīrṇamāsanaṃ viniyojayet |
anyad dārubhavaṃ cāpi dadyādāsanamuttamam || 9 ||
meaning:
नोच्छ्रायं नातिविस्तीर्णमासनं विनियोजयेत् |
अन्यद् दारुभवं चापि दद्यादासनमुत्तमम् || 9 ||
text_mt: neither very high nor very wide, one should employ; / or one may also give another excellent seat made of wood,

sanskrit_iast:
sakaṇṭakaṃ kṣīrayuta dārusāravivarjitam |
caityaśmaśānasambhūtaṃ varjayitvā vibhītakam || 10 ||
meaning:
सकण्टकं क्षीरयुत दारुसारविवर्जितम् |
चैत्यश्मशानसम्भूतं वर्जयित्वा विभीतकम् || 10 ||
text_mt: avoiding wood that is thorny, milky, devoid of pith, / or grown in sacred spots or cremation grounds, and avoiding the vibhītaka tree.

sanskrit_iast:
valkalaṃ koṣajaṃ śāṇaṃ vastrametat trayaṃ matam |
romajaṃ kambalaṃ aitadanena tu catuṣṭayam || 11 ||
meaning:
वल्कलं कोषजं शाणं वस्त्रमेतत् त्रयं मतम् |
रोमजं कम्बलं ऐतदनेन तु चतुष्टयम् || 11 ||
text_mt: Bark, silk, and hemp—these three are considered cloth; / woolen blanket made from hair makes four with these.

sanskrit_iast:
anena racitaṃ dadyādāsanaṃ ceṣṭabhūtaye |
iṃhavyāghratarakṣūṇāṃ chāgasya mahiṣasya vā || 12 ||
meaning:
अनेन रचितं दद्यादासनं चेष्टभूतये |
इंहव्याघ्रतरक्षूणां छागस्य महिषस्य वा || 12 ||
text_mt: One should give a seat fashioned from these for the desired prosperity. / From [the hide] of a lion, tiger, or hyena, or of a goat or buffalo,

sanskrit_iast:
gajānāṃ turagāṇāṃ ca kṛṣṇasārasya carmaṇaḥ |
sṛmarasyātha rāmasya mṛgāṇāṃ navabhedinām || 13 ||
meaning:
गजानां तुरगाणां च कृष्णसारस्य चर्मणः |
सृमरस्याथ रामस्य मृगाणां नवभेदिनाम् || 13 ||
text_mt: of elephants and of horses, and from the hide of a blackbuck, / of a sṛmara, or of a rāma, from nine varieties of deer—

sanskrit_iast:
carmabhiḥ sarvadevānāmāsanaṃ prītidaṃ śrutam |
vastreṣu kambalaṃ śastamāsanaṃ devatuṣṭaye || 14 ||
meaning:
चर्मभिः सर्वदेवानामासनं प्रीतिदं श्रुतम् |
वस्त्रेषु कम्बलं शस्तमासनं देवतुष्टये || 14 ||
text_mt: a seat made of the skins [of these] is traditionally held to give pleasure to all deities. / Among cloths, a blanket is praised as a seat for the satisfaction of the gods;

sanskrit_iast:
rāṅkavaṃ cārmaṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dāravaṃ candanodbhavam |
yaccāsanaṃ kuśamayaṃ tadāsanamanuttamam || 15 ||
meaning:
राङ्कवं चार्मणं श्रेष्ठं दारवं चन्दनोद्भवम् |
यच्चासनं कुशमयं तदासनमनुत्तमम् || 15 ||
text_mt: a rāṅkava woolen cloth is best, and among wooden ones, that derived from sandalwood; / and that seat which is made of kuśa grass is the unsurpassed seat.

sanskrit_iast:
sarveṣāmapi devānāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca yatātmanām |
yogapīṭhasya sadṛśamāsanaṃ sthānamucyate || 16 ||
meaning:
सर्वेषामपि देवानामृषीणां च यतात्मनाम् |
योगपीठस्य सदृशमासनं स्थानमुच्यते || 16 ||
text_mt: For all deities and for self-controlled sages, / a seat resembling a yoga-seat is called the place [of worship].

sanskrit_iast:
āsanasya pradānena saubhāgyaṃ muktimāpnuyāt |
śambaro rohito rāmo nyaṅkuraṅkuśaśā ruruḥ || 17 ||
meaning:
आसनस्य प्रदानेन सौभाग्यं मुक्तिमाप्नुयात् |
शम्बरो रोहितो रामो न्यङ्कुरङ्कुशशा रुरुः || 17 ||
text_mt: By giving a seat, one obtains good fortune and liberation. / The śambara, rohita, rāma, nyaṅku, raṅku, śaśa, ruru,

sanskrit_iast:
eṇaśca hariṇaśceti mṛgā navavidhā matāḥ |
hariṇaścāpi vijñeyo añcabhedo'tra bhairava || 18 ||
meaning:
एणश्च हरिणश्चेति मृगा नवविधा मताः |
हरिणश्चापि विज्ञेयो अञ्चभेदोऽत्र भैरव || 18 ||
text_mt: eṇa, and hariṇa—these are considered the nine kinds of deer. / And the hariṇa is also to be known as fivefold here, O Bhairava:

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣyah khaḍgo ruruścaiva pṛṣataśca magastathā |
ete valipradāneṣu carmadāneṣu kīrtitāḥ || 19 ||
meaning:
ऋष्यह् खड्गो रुरुश्चैव पृषतश्च मगस्तथा |
एते वलिप्रदानेषु चर्मदानेषु कीर्तिताः || 19 ||
text_mt: the ṛṣya, the rhinoceros, the ruru, the spotted deer, and the [ordinary] deer; / these are proclaimed in animal offerings and in the offerings of hides.

sanskrit_iast:
sarveṣāṃ taijasanāṃ ca āsanaṃ śreṣṭhamucyate |
āyasaṃ varjayitvā tu kāṃsyaṃ sīsakameva vā || 20 ||
meaning:
सर्वेषां तैजसनां च आसनं श्रेष्ठमुच्यते |
आयसं वर्जयित्वा तु कांस्यं सीसकमेव वा || 20 ||
text_mt: A seat made of any metallic substance is called excellent, / but avoiding iron, bronze, or lead.

sanskrit_iast:
śilāmayaṃ maṇimayaṃ tathā ratnamayaṃ matam |
āsana devatābhyastu bhuktyai muktyai samutsṛjet || 21 ||
meaning:
शिलामयं मणिमयं तथा रत्नमयं मतम् |
आसन देवताभ्यस्तु भुक्त्यै मुक्त्यै समुत्सृजेत् || 21 ||
text_mt: A seat made of stone, made of gems, and likewise made of jewels / one should offer to the deities for enjoyment and liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
atraiva sādhakānāṃ ca āsanaṃ śṛṇu bhairava |
yatrāsīnaḥ pūjayaṃstu sarvasiddhimavāpnuyāt || 22 ||
meaning:
अत्रैव साधकानां च आसनं शृणु भैरव |
यत्रासीनः पूजयंस्तु सर्वसिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् || 22 ||
text_mt: Here also listen, O Bhairava, regarding the seat of practitioners, / seated upon which in worship one attains all spiritual perfection.

sanskrit_iast:
aindhanaṃ cārmaṇaṃ vāstraṃ taijasaṃ ca catuṣṭayam |
āsanaṃ sādhakānāṃ ca satataṃ parikīrtitam || 23 ||
meaning:
ऐन्धनं चार्मणं वास्त्रं तैजसं च चतुष्टयम् |
आसनं साधकानां च सततं परिकीर्तितम् || 23 ||
text_mt: Made of wood, made of hide, made of cloth, and made of metal: this fourfold / seat of practitioners is continually praised.

sanskrit_iast:
at sarvamāsanaṃ śastaṃ pūjākarmaṇi sādhake |
na yatheṣṭāsano bhūyat pūjākarmaṇi sādhakaḥ || 24 ||
meaning:
अत् सर्वमासनं शस्तं पूजाकर्मणि साधके |
न यथेष्टासनो भूयत् पूजाकर्मणि साधकः || 24 ||
text_mt: All this is an approved seat for the practitioner in the rite of worship; / the practitioner should not sit as he pleases in the rite of worship.

sanskrit_iast:
kāṣṭhādikāsanaṃ kuryāt sitameva sadā budhaḥ |
caturviṃśatyaṅgulena dīrghaṃ kāṣṭhāsanaṃ matam || 25 ||
meaning:
काष्ठादिकासनं कुर्यात् सितमेव सदा बुधः |
चतुर्विंशत्यङ्गुलेन दीर्घं काष्ठासनं मतम् || 25 ||
text_mt: The wise person should always make a seat of wood and the like bright white; / a wooden seat is considered twenty-four finger-widths long,

sanskrit_iast:
ṣoḍaśāṅgulavistīrṇamucchrāyaṃ caturaṅgulam |
ṣaḍaṅgulaṃ vā kuryāt nocchritañcāta ācaret || 26 ||
meaning:
षोडशाङ्गुलविस्तीर्णमुच्छ्रायं चतुरङ्गुलम् |
षडङ्गुलं वा कुर्यात् नोच्छ्रितञ्चात आचरेत् || 26 ||
text_mt: sixteen finger-widths wide, and four finger-widths high; / or one may make it six finger-widths [high], but higher than that one should not make it.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvoktaṃ varjayed varjyamāsanaṃ pūjaneṣvapi |
vastraṃ dvihastānno dīrghaṃ sārdhahastānna vistṛtam || 27 ||
meaning:
पूर्वोक्तं वर्जयेद् वर्ज्यमासनं पूजनेष्वपि |
वस्त्रं द्विहस्तान्नो दीर्घं सार्धहस्तान्न विस्तृतम् || 27 ||
text_mt: One should avoid what was previously mentioned as forbidden, even in worship. / A cloth seat must not be longer than two cubits, nor wider than one and a half cubits;

sanskrit_iast:
na ryaṅgulāt tathocchrāyaṃ pūjākarmaṇi saṃśrayet |
yatheṣṭaṃ cārmaṇaṃ kuryāt pūrvoktaṃ siddhidāyakam || 28 ||
meaning:
न र्यङ्गुलात् तथोच्छ्रायं पूजाकर्मणि संश्रयेत् |
यथेष्टं चार्मणं कुर्यात् पूर्वोक्तं सिद्धिदायकम् || 28 ||
text_mt: in the rite of worship one should not resort to [a thickness] greater than three finger-widths. / As for a hide, one may make it as one pleases, as previously stated, conferring perfection;

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaḍaṅgulādhikaṃ kuryānnocchritaṃ ca kadācana |
kāmbalaṃ cārmaṇaṃ śailaṃ mahāmāyāprapūjane || 29 ||
meaning:
षडङ्गुलाधिकं कुर्यान्नोच्छ्रितं च कदाचन |
काम्बलं चार्मणं शैलं महामायाप्रपूजने || 29 ||
text_mt: one should make it exceeding six finger-widths, and never elevated. / A woolen, leather, or stone seat in the worship of Mahāmāyā,

sanskrit_iast:
praśastamāsanaṃ proktaṃ kāmākhyāyāstathaiva ca |
tripurāyāśca satataṃ viṣṇoścāpi kuśāsanam || 30 ||
meaning:
प्रशस्तमासनं प्रोक्तं कामाख्यायास्तथैव च |
त्रिपुरायाश्च सततं विष्णोश्चापि कुशासनम् || 30 ||
text_mt: and likewise of Kāmākhyā, is declared to be an approved seat; / and for Tripurā and Viṣṇu, a kuśa-grass seat at all times.

sanskrit_iast:
bahudīrghaṃ bahuṃcchrāyaṃ tathaiva bahuvistṛtam |
dāru bhūmisamaṃ proktamaśmāpi sarvakarmaṇi || 31 ||
meaning:
बहुदीर्घं बहुंच्छ्रायं तथैव बहुविस्तृतम् |
दारु भूमिसमं प्रोक्तमश्मापि सर्वकर्मणि || 31 ||
text_mt: Very long, very high, and likewise very wide / wood or stone is declared equal to the bare earth in all rites.

sanskrit_iast:
pṛthak pṛthak kalpayet tu bahirdvāri tathāsanam |
na patramāsanaṃ kuryāt kadācidapi pūjane || 32 ||
meaning:
पृथक् पृथक् कल्पयेत् तु बहिर्द्वारि तथासनम् |
न पत्रमासनं कुर्यात् कदाचिदपि पूजने || 32 ||
text_mt: One should arrange the seat individually outside at the door; / one should never make a leaf into a seat in worship,

sanskrit_iast:
na prāṇyaṅga-samudbhūtamasthijaṃ dviradādṛte |
mātaṅgadantasañjātaṃ kāmikeṣvāsanaṃ caret || 33 ||
meaning:
न प्राण्यङ्ग-समुद्भूतमस्थिजं द्विरदादृते |
मातङ्गदन्तसञ्जातं कामिकेष्वासनं चरेत् || 33 ||
text_mt: nor one derived from an animal body or born of bone, except for the elephant; / a seat produced from elephant tusk one may use in desire-prompted rites.

sanskrit_iast:
cārmaṃ pūrvoditaṃ grāhyaṃ tathā gandhamṛgasya ca |
salile yadi kurvīta devatānāṃ prapūjanam || 34 ||
meaning:
चार्मं पूर्वोदितं ग्राह्यं तथा गन्धमृगस्य च |
सलिले यदि कुर्वीत देवतानां प्रपूजनम् || 34 ||
text_mt: The skin [seat] mentioned before should be taken, as also that of a musk deer. / If one should perform the worship of deities in water,

sanskrit_iast:
tatrāpyāsana āsīno notthitastu kadācana |
toye śilāmayaṃ kuryādāsanaṃ kauśameva vā || 35 ||
meaning:
तत्राप्यासन आसीनो नोत्थितस्तु कदाचन |
तोये शिलामयं कुर्यादासनं कौशमेव वा || 35 ||
text_mt: even there, seated upon a seat, never standing up, / one should make a seat made of stone in the water, or one of kuśa grass,

sanskrit_iast:
dāravaṃ taijasaṃ vāpi nānyadāsanamācaret |
āsanāropasaṃsthānaṃ sthānābhāve tu pūjakaḥ || 36 ||
meaning:
दारवं तैजसं वापि नान्यदासनमाचरेत् |
आसनारोपसंस्थानं स्थानाभावे तु पूजकः || 36 ||
text_mt: or wooden, or metallic; one should not use any other seat. / But in the absence of a place, the worshipper, assuming the posture of ascending a seat,

sanskrit_iast:
āsanaṃ kalpayitvā tu manasā pūjayejjale |
yadyāsituṃ na saṃsthānaṃ vidyate toyamadhyataḥ || 37 ||
meaning:
आसनं कल्पयित्वा तु मनसा पूजयेज्जले |
यद्यासितुं न संस्थानं विद्यते तोयमध्यतः || 37 ||
text_mt: having mentally fashioned a seat, should worship in the water. / If there is no place to sit in the midst of the water,

sanskrit_iast:
anyatra vā tadā sthitvā devapūjāṃ samācaret |
ityetat kathitaṃ putra pūjyapūjakasaṅgatam || 38 ||
meaning:
अन्यत्र वा तदा स्थित्वा देवपूजां समाचरेत् |
इत्येतत् कथितं पुत्र पूज्यपूजकसङ्गतम् || 38 ||
text_mt: then, standing elsewhere, one should perform the worship of the god. / Thus this has been spoken, O son, concerning what pertains to the worshipped and the worshipper,

sanskrit_iast:
āsanaṃ pādyamadhunā śṛṇu vetāla bhairava |
pādārthamudakaṃ pādyaṃ kevalaṃ toyameva tat || 39 ||
meaning:
आसनं पाद्यमधुना शृणु वेताल भैरव |
पादार्थमुदकं पाद्यं केवलं तोयमेव तत् || 39 ||
text_mt: namely the seat. Now hear of the foot-washing water, O Vetāla and Bhairava. / Water for the feet is pādya; it is pure water alone.

sanskrit_iast:
tat taijasena pātreṇa śaṅkhenāpi pradāpayet |
dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ sasthānaṃ pādyamiṣyate || 40 ||
meaning:
तत् तैजसेन पात्रेण शङ्खेनापि प्रदापयेत् |
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां सस्थानं पाद्यमिष्यते || 40 ||
text_mt: One should offer it with a metallic vessel or with a conch shell. / Pādya is held to be the abode of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
tadāsanottaraṃ dadyānmūlamantreṇa sarvataḥ |
kuśapuṣpākṣataiścaiva siddhārthaiścandanaistathā || 41 ||
meaning:
तदासनोत्तरं दद्यान्मूलमन्त्रेण सर्वतः |
कुशपुष्पाक्षतैश्चैव सिद्धार्थैश्चन्दनैस्तथा || 41 ||
text_mt: One should offer it after the seat, with the root-mantra from all sides, / with kuśa grass, flowers, unbroken grains, mustard seeds, and sandalwood,

sanskrit_iast:
toyairgandhairyathālabdhairarghyaṃ dadyāt tu siddhaye |
arghyeṇa labhate kāmānarghyeṇa labhate dhanam || 42 ||
meaning:
तोयैर्गन्धैर्यथालब्धैरर्घ्यं दद्यात् तु सिद्धये |
अर्घ्येण लभते कामानर्घ्येण लभते धनम् || 42 ||
text_mt: with waters and perfumes, as obtained, one should offer the arghya for success. / Through arghya one attains desires; through arghya one attains wealth;

sanskrit_iast:
putrāyuḥsukhamokṣāṇi dānādarghyasya vai labhet |
na dadyād bhāskarāyārghyaṃ śaṅkhatoyairvicakṣaṇaḥ || 43 ||
meaning:
पुत्रायुःसुखमोक्षाणि दानादर्घ्यस्य वै लभेत् |
न दद्याद् भास्करायार्घ्यं शङ्खतोयैर्विचक्षणः || 43 ||
text_mt: indeed, one obtains sons, long life, happiness, and liberation from the giving of arghya. / A wise man should not offer arghya to the Sun with water from a conch shell,

sanskrit_iast:
tathā na śuktipātreṇa viṣṇave'rghyaṃ nivedayet |
dadyādācamanīyaṃ tu sugandhisalilaiḥ śubhaiḥ || 44 ||
meaning:
तथा न शुक्तिपात्रेण विष्णवेऽर्घ्यं निवेदयेत् |
दद्यादाचमनीयं तु सुगन्धिसलिलैः शुभैः || 44 ||
text_mt: nor likewise should one offer arghya to Viṣṇu with an oyster shell. / One should offer water for sipping with fragrant, auspicious waters,

sanskrit_iast:
karpūravāsitairvāpi kṛṣṇāguruvidhūpitaiḥ |
yathā tathā sugandhairvā prasaṅgaiḥ phenavarjitaiḥ || 45 ||
meaning:
कर्पूरवासितैर्वापि कृष्णागुरुविधूपितैः |
यथा तथा सुगन्धैर्वा प्रसङ्गैः फेनवर्जितैः || 45 ||
text_mt: scented with camphor or perfumed with black agallochum, / or fragrant in any manner, clear and free from foam.

sanskrit_iast:
tat taijasena pātreṇa śaṅkhenāpi pradāpayet |
udakaṃ dīyate yat tu prasannaṃ phenavarjitam || 46 ||
meaning:
तत् तैजसेन पात्रेण शङ्खेनापि प्रदापयेत् |
उदकं दीयते यत् तु प्रसन्नं फेनवर्जितम् || 46 ||
text_mt: One should offer it with a metallic vessel or with a conch shell. / The water that is given, clear and free from foam,

sanskrit_iast:
ācamanāya devebhyastadācamanamucyate |
kevalaṃ toyamātreṇa tad vā dadyānna miśritam || 47 ||
meaning:
आचमनाय देवेभ्यस्तदाचमनमुच्यते |
केवलं तोयमात्रेण तद् वा दद्यान्न मिश्रितम् || 47 ||
text_mt: for sipping to the gods—that is called ācamana. / Or one may give it with pure water alone, not mixed;

sanskrit_iast:
vāsitaṃ tu sugandhādyaiḥ kartavyaṃ yadi labhyate |
āyurbalaṃ yaśovṛddhiṃ pradāyācamanīyakam || 48 ||
meaning:
वासितं तु सुगन्धाद्यैः कर्तव्यं यदि लभ्यते |
आयुर्बलं यशोवृद्धिं प्रदायाचमनीयकम् || 48 ||
text_mt: it should be made perfumed with scents and the like, if it can be obtained. / Having offered sipping water, the practitioner continually obtains

sanskrit_iast:
labhate sādhako nityaṃ kāmāṃścaiva yathotthitān |
dadhirsarpirjala kṣaudraṃ sitā tābhiśca pañcabhiḥ || 49 ||
meaning:
लभते साधको नित्यं कामांश्चैव यथोत्थितान् |
दधिर्सर्पिर्जल क्षौद्रं सिता ताभिश्च पञ्चभिः || 49 ||
text_mt: long life, strength, increase of fame, and desires as they arise. / Curd, clarified butter, water, honey, and white sugar—with these five

sanskrit_iast:
procyate madhuparkastu sarvadevaughatuṣṭaye |
jalaṃ tu sarvataḥ svalpaṃ sitādadhighṛtaṃ samam || 50 ||
meaning:
प्रोच्यते मधुपर्कस्तु सर्वदेवौघतुष्टये |
जलं तु सर्वतः स्वल्पं सितादधिघृतं समम् || 50 ||
text_mt: the madhuparka is prescribed for the satisfaction of the host of all gods. / Water should be the smallest of all; white sugar, curd, and ghee should be equal;

sanskrit_iast:
sarvebhya ścādhikaṃ kṣaudraṃ madhuparkeprayojayet |
tad dadyāt kāṃsyapātreṇa raukmaśvetamayena vā || 51 ||
meaning:
सर्वेभ्य श्चाधिकं क्षौद्रं मधुपर्केप्रयोजयेत् |
तद् दद्यात् कांस्यपात्रेण रौक्मश्वेतमयेन वा || 51 ||
text_mt: and more honey than all of them one should use in the madhuparka. / One should offer it with a bell-metal vessel, or one made of gold or silver.

sanskrit_iast:
jyotiṣṭomāśvamedhādau pūrte ceṣṭe ca pūjane |
madhuparkaḥ pradiṣṭo'yaṃ sarvadevaughatuṣṭidaḥ || 52 ||
meaning:
ज्योतिष्टोमाश्वमेधादौ पूर्ते चेष्टे च पूजने |
मधुपर्कः प्रदिष्टोऽयं सर्वदेवौघतुष्टिदः || 52 ||
text_mt: In the Jyotiṣṭoma, Aśvamedha, and other [sacrifices], in public works, in sacrifices, and in worship, / this madhuparka is prescribed, bestowing satisfaction on the host of all gods.

sanskrit_iast:
dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ sādhakaḥ parikīrtitaḥ |
madhuparkaḥ saukhyabhogya-tuṣṭi-puṣṭi-pradāyakaḥ || 53 ||
meaning:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां साधकः परिकीर्तितः |
मधुपर्कः सौख्यभोग्य-तुष्टि-पुष्टि-प्रदायकः || 53 ||
text_mt: It is celebrated as achieving dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa; / madhuparka is the bestower of happiness, enjoyment, satisfaction, and nourishment.

sanskrit_iast:
piṣṭātako'tha kastūrī rocanaṃ kuṅkumaṃ tathā |
guḍaḥ kṣaudraṃ pañcagavyaṃ sarvauṣadhigaṇastathā || 54 ||
meaning:
पिष्टातकोऽथ कस्तूरी रोचनं कुङ्कुमं तथा |
गुडः क्षौद्रं पञ्चगव्यं सर्वौषधिगणस्तथा || 54 ||
text_mt: Scented powder, musk, yellow orpiment, and saffron, / molasses, honey, pañcagavya, and the collection of all medicinal herbs,

sanskrit_iast:
sitā nirṇejanaṃ tailaṃ snigdhastehena tattilāḥ |
prānte toyamiti proktaṃ snānīyaṃ kalpakovidaiḥ || 55 ||
meaning:
सिता निर्णेजनं तैलं स्निग्धस्तेहेन तत्तिलाः |
प्रान्ते तोयमिति प्रोक्तं स्नानीयं कल्पकोविदैः || 55 ||
text_mt: white sugar, cleansing agent, oil, and sesame seeds with an unctuous oily substance, / and water at the end: this is declared as the bath-water by those skilled in ritual rules.

sanskrit_iast:
svarṇaratnodakaṃ caiva karpūrādyadhivāsitam |
taijasaiḥ kāṃsyapātrairvā śaṅkhairvā tannivedayet || 56 ||
meaning:
स्वर्णरत्नोदकं चैव कर्पूराद्यधिवासितम् |
तैजसैः कांस्यपात्रैर्वा शङ्खैर्वा तन्निवेदयेत् || 56 ||
text_mt: Also water with gold and gems, perfumed with camphor and the like; / one should offer it in metallic or bell-metal vessels, or with conches.

sanskrit_iast:
aṇḍale keśare deyamādityapratimāsu ca |
śivaliṅge tathā bhoge pīṭhe devatanau tathā || 57 ||
meaning:
अण्डले केशरे देयमादित्यप्रतिमासु च |
शिवलिङ्गे तथा भोगे पीठे देवतनौ तथा || 57 ||
text_mt: It should be given on the maṇḍala, on the pericarp, and on images of the Sun, / on the Śiva-liṅga, and on the serpent, on the altar, and on the body of the deity.

sanskrit_iast:
adyaḥsnigdhaṃ ṛnmayaṃ vā sarpiḥsinduraje tathā |
śrīcandanapratiṣṭhe vā lepayet pratimātanau || 58 ||
meaning:
अद्यःस्निग्धं ऋन्मयं वा सर्पिःसिन्दुरजे तथा |
श्रीचन्दनप्रतिष्ठे वा लेपयेत् प्रतिमातनौ || 58 ||
text_mt: One should smear the body of the image, whether freshly oiled or made of clay, / or made of ghee and vermilion, or consecrated with sacred sandalwood;

sanskrit_iast:
vastikasthāpite khaḍge snāpayed darpaṇe'tha vā |
evaṃ dadyāt tu snānīyaṃ mahādevyai viśeṣataḥ || 59 ||
meaning:
वस्तिकस्थापिते खड्गे स्नापयेद् दर्पणेऽथ वा |
एवं दद्यात् तु स्नानीयं महादेव्यै विशेषतः || 59 ||
text_mt: or one should bathe [the deity] in a sword placed on a cloth, or in a mirror. / Thus one should offer bath-water, especially to the Great Goddess,

sanskrit_iast:
avi viṣṇuśivebhyo vā yatra tatra prapūjane |
pūjakaḥ snānadānāt ta cirāyurupajāyate || 60 ||
meaning:
अवि विष्णुशिवेभ्यो वा यत्र तत्र प्रपूजने |
पूजकः स्नानदानात् त चिरायुरुपजायते || 60 ||
text_mt: or to the Sun, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, wherever in worship. / From giving a bath, the worshipper becomes long-lived;

sanskrit_iast:
samyak snānapradānāt tu kalpāntaṃ svargabhāgbhavet |
yadeva dīyate pādyaṃ gandhapuṣpādikaṃ tathā || 61 ||
meaning:
सम्यक् स्नानप्रदानात् तु कल्पान्तं स्वर्गभाग्भवेत् |
यदेव दीयते पाद्यं गन्धपुष्पादिकं तथा || 61 ||
text_mt: and from offering a proper bath, one becomes a sharer of heaven until the end of a kalpa. / Whatever is given—pādya, perfumes, flowers, and the like,

sanskrit_iast:
upācārāṃstathā sarvānarghyapātrāhitairjalaiḥ |
amṛtīkaraṇādyaistu saṃskṛtaistvabhiṣicya taiḥ || 62 ||
meaning:
उपाचारांस्तथा सर्वानर्घ्यपात्राहितैर्जलैः |
अमृतीकरणाद्यैस्तु संस्कृतैस्त्वभिषिच्य तैः || 62 ||
text_mt: and all the services, sprinkling them with waters placed in the arghya-vessel / and consecrated with immortalisation and other rites—

sanskrit_iast:
pradadyādiṣṭadevebhyo gṛhṇāti ca tataḥ svayam |
arghyapātrāṇi taistoyairvinā yadvinivedanam || 63 ||
meaning:
प्रदद्यादिष्टदेवेभ्यो गृह्णाति च ततः स्वयम् |
अर्घ्यपात्राणि तैस्तोयैर्विना यद्विनिवेदनम् || 63 ||
text_mt: one should offer to the chosen deities, and then [the deity] receives it in person. / Any offering that is given to the chosen deities

sanskrit_iast:
dīyate ceṣṭadevebhyaḥ sarvaṃ tanniṣphalaṃ bhavet |
rāgāllobhāt pramādād vā hyarghyaṃ pātrāmṛtīkṛtam || 64 ||
meaning:
दीयते चेष्टदेवेभ्यः सर्वं तन्निष्फलं भवेत् |
रागाल्लोभात् प्रमादाद् वा ह्यर्घ्यं पात्रामृतीकृतम् || 64 ||
text_mt: without the waters from the arghya-vessels, all of that becomes fruitless. / If out of passion, greed, or negligence, the arghya-water, made immortal in the vessel,

sanskrit_iast:
toyaṃ srutaṃ syāt pātrāt tu punaḥ kuryāt tadā mṛtam |
svalpāvaśeṣatoye tu pātrasthe hyamṛtīkṛte || 65 ||
meaning:
तोयं स्रुतं स्यात् पात्रात् तु पुनः कुर्यात् तदा मृतम् |
स्वल्पावशेषतोये तु पात्रस्थे ह्यमृतीकृते || 65 ||
text_mt: should leak from the vessel, then one should make it immortal again. / When a little water remains in the vessel, once it has been made immortal,

sanskrit_iast:
tatrānyadudakaṃ dadyāt tattainaivāmṛtaṃ bhavet |
bahūni yadi puṣpāṇi mālā vā pracurā yadi || 66 ||
meaning:
तत्रान्यदुदकं दद्यात् तत्तैनैवामृतं भवेत् |
बहूनि यदि पुष्पाणि माला वा प्रचुरा यदि || 66 ||
text_mt: one should add other water there; that will become immortal by that very [remainder]. / If there are many flowers, or if there is an abundance of garlands,

sanskrit_iast:
dīyante cārghyapātrasthairjalaiḥ saṃsicya cotsṛjet |
anyatoyairyadutsṛṣṭamarghyapātrasthitetaraiḥ || 67 ||
meaning:
दीयन्ते चार्घ्यपात्रस्थैर्जलैः संसिच्य चोत्सृजेत् |
अन्यतोयैर्यदुत्सृष्टमर्घ्यपात्रस्थितेतरैः || 67 ||
text_mt: when they are offered, one should release them having sprinkled them with the waters in the arghya-vessel. / Whatever is released with other waters, distinct from that which is in the arghya-vessel,

sanskrit_iast:
tanna gṛhvātīṣṭadevo dattaṃ vidhiśatairapi |
saṃskṛte tvarghyapātre tu navabhiḥ pratipattibhiḥ || 68 ||
meaning:
तन्न गृह्वातीष्टदेवो दत्तं विधिशतैरपि |
संस्कृते त्वर्घ्यपात्रे तु नवभिः प्रतिपत्तिभिः || 68 ||
text_mt: the chosen deity does not accept, even if given with hundreds of rules. / In the arghya-vessel, when consecrated with the nine attentions,

sanskrit_iast:
tiṣṭhanti savatīrthāni pīyūṣāṇi ca sarvataḥ |
tasmāt tatra sthitaistoyairabhyukṣyopacārānutsṛjet || 69 ||
meaning:
तिष्ठन्ति सवतीर्थानि पीयूषाणि च सर्वतः |
तस्मात् तत्र स्थितैस्तोयैरभ्युक्ष्योपचारानुत्सृजेत् || 69 ||
text_mt: all sacred fords and nectars dwell on all sides. / Therefore, sprinkling with the waters residing there, one should offer the services;

sanskrit_iast:
na yogyamarghyapātreṣu nidhāya vinivedayet |
idaṃ te bhairava proktaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ caivāsanādikam |
vastrādi daśa vakṣyāmi śṛṇu vijñānavṛddhaye || 70 ||
meaning:
न योग्यमर्घ्यपात्रेषु निधाय विनिवेदयेत् |
इदं ते भैरव प्रोक्तं षट्कं चैवासनादिकम् |
वस्त्रादि दश वक्ष्यामि शृणु विज्ञानवृद्धये || 70 ||
text_mt: one should not offer an unsuitable [gift] having placed it in the arghya-vessels. / This hexad beginning with the seat has been declared to you, O Bhairava; / I shall speak of the ten [items] beginning with cloth; listen, for the increase of discernment.

sanskrit_iast:
iti śrīkālikāpurāṇe aṣṭaṣaṣṭitamo'dhyāyaḥ || 68 ||
ekonasaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ |
meaning:
इति श्रीकालिकापुराणे अष्टषष्टितमोऽध्यायः || 68 ||
एकोनसप्ततितमोऽध्यायः |
text_mt: Thus ends the sixty-eighth chapter in the glorious Kālikāpurāṇa. / The sixty-ninth chapter.

sanskrit_iast: śrībhagavānuvāca |
meaning: श्रीभगवानुवाच |

sanskrit_iast:
kārpāsaṃ kambalaṃ bālkaṃ kośajaṃ vastramiṣyate |
tatpūrvaṃ pūjayitvaiva mantrairdevāya cotsṛjet || 1 ||
meaning:
कार्पासं कम्बलं बाल्कं कोशजं वस्त्रमिष्यते |
तत्पूर्वं पूजयित्वैव मन्त्रैर्देवाय चोत्सृजेत् || 1 ||
text_mt: Cotton, woollen, bark-fibre, and silk garments are prescribed; / only having first worshipped it with mantras should one offer it to the god.

sanskrit_iast:
nirdaśaṃ malinaṃ jīrṇaṃ chinnaṃ gātrāaliṅgitam |
parakīyaṃ hyākhudaṣṭaṃ sūcīviddhaṃ tathoṣitam || 2 ||
meaning:
निर्दशं मलिनं जीर्णं छिन्नं गात्राअलिङ्गितम् |
परकीयं ह्याखुदष्टं सूचीविद्धं तथोषितम् || 2 ||
text_mt: A garment past ten days [from washing], dirty, worn-out, torn, touched by the body [of another], / belonging to another, gnawed by mice, pierced by a needle, or kept overnight,

sanskrit_iast:
ptaleśaṃ vidhautaṃ ca śleṣmamūtrādidūṣitam |
pradāne devatābhyaśca daive pitrye ca karmaṇi || 3 ||
meaning:
प्तलेशं विधौतं च श्लेष्ममूत्रादिदूषितम् |
प्रदाने देवताभ्यश्च दैवे पित्र्ये च कर्मणि || 3 ||
text_mt: stained, washed [by a washerman], or defiled by phlegm, urine, and the like, / in offering to the deities, in rites for gods or ancestors,

sanskrit_iast:
varjaet svopayogena yajñādāvupayojane |
uttarīyottarāsaṅgairnicolo modacelakaḥ || 4 ||
meaning:
वर्जएत् स्वोपयोगेन यज्ञादावुपयोजने |
उत्तरीयोत्तरासङ्गैर्निचोलो मोदचेलकः || 4 ||
text_mt: one should avoid for one's own use and for use in sacrifice and the like. / An upper garment, an uttarīya, a wrapper, an outer garment,

sanskrit_iast:
paridhānaṃ ca pañcaitānyasyūtāni prayojayet |
sāṇa vastraṃ niśāraṃ ca tathaivātapavāraṇam || 5 ||
meaning:
परिधानं च पञ्चैतान्यस्यूतानि प्रयोजयेत् |
साण वस्त्रं निशारं च तथैवातपवारणम् || 5 ||
text_mt: and a lower garment—these five unstitched [garments] one should use. / Hemp cloth, a blanket, and an umbrella,

sanskrit_iast:
caṇḍātakaṃ tathā dṛśyaṃ pañca syūtānyaduṣṭaye |
patākādhvajadaṇḍādau syūtaṃ vastraṃ prayojayet || 6 ||
meaning:
चण्डातकं तथा दृश्यं पञ्च स्यूतान्यदुष्टये |
पताकाध्वजदण्डादौ स्यूतं वस्त्रं प्रयोजयेत् || 6 ||
text_mt: a skirt, and a screen—these five stitched [garments] are for satisfaction. / On flags, banner-poles, and the like, one should use stitched cloth.

sanskrit_iast:
anyatrāvaraṇādau ca tadvināśasya tena tat |
raktaṃ kauśeyavastraṃ ca mahādevyai praśasyate || 7 ||
meaning:
अन्यत्रावरणादौ च तद्विनाशस्य तेन तत् |
रक्तं कौशेयवस्त्रं च महादेव्यै प्रशस्यते || 7 ||
text_mt: And elsewhere, for coverings and the like, sewn cloth [may be used], since by that it is ruined; / and red silk garment is praised for the Great Goddess.

sanskrit_iast:
pītaṃ tathaiva kauśeyaṃ āsudevāya cotsṛjet |
raktaṃ tu kambalaṃ dadyācchivāya paramātmane || 8 ||
meaning:
पीतं तथैव कौशेयं आसुदेवाय चोत्सृजेत् |
रक्तं तु कम्बलं दद्याच्छिवाय परमात्मने || 8 ||
text_mt: And in the same way, one should present yellow silk to Vāsudeva; / but one should offer a red blanket to Śiva, the Supreme Self.

sanskrit_iast:
vicitraṃ sarvadevebhyo devībhyoṃ'śu nivedayet |
kārpāsaṃ sarvatobhadraṃ dadyāt sarvebhya eva ca || 9 ||
meaning:
विचित्रं सर्वदेवेभ्यो देवीभ्योंऽशु निवेदयेत् |
कार्पासं सर्वतोभद्रं दद्यात् सर्वेभ्य एव च || 9 ||
text_mt: One should offer multi-coloured [garments] and rays of cloth to all the gods and goddesses; / and one should offer cotton, which is auspicious on all sides, to everyone.

sanskrit_iast:
naikāntaraktaṃ dadyāt tu vāsudevāya cailakam |
tathā naikāntanīlaṃ tu śivāya vinivedayet || 10 ||
meaning:
नैकान्तरक्तं दद्यात् तु वासुदेवाय चैलकम् |
तथा नैकान्तनीलं तु शिवाय विनिवेदयेत् || 10 ||
text_mt: But one should never offer an entirely red cloth to Vāsudeva; / likewise, one should not present an entirely dark blue one to Śiva.

sanskrit_iast:
nīlīraktaṃ tu yadvastraṃ tat sarvatra vivarjitam |
daive pitrye tūpayoge varjayet tu vicakṣaṇaḥ || 11 ||
meaning:
नीलीरक्तं तु यद्वस्त्रं तत् सर्वत्र विवर्जितम् |
दैवे पित्र्ये तूपयोगे वर्जयेत् तु विचक्षणः || 11 ||
text_mt: Any cloth that is dyed with indigo is rejected everywhere; / a wise man must avoid it in usage for the gods as well as for the ancestors.

sanskrit_iast:
nīlīraktaṃ pramādāttu yo dadyād viṣṇave budhaḥ |
niṣphalā tasya tatpūjā tadā bhavati bhairava || 12 ||
meaning:
नीलीरक्तं प्रमादात्तु यो दद्याद् विष्णवे बुधः |
निष्फला तस्य तत्पूजा तदा भवति भैरव || 12 ||
text_mt: If a wise person offers cloth dyed with indigo to Viṣṇu through heedlessness, / then his worship becomes fruitless, O Bhairava.

sanskrit_iast:
vicitre vāsasi punarlagnaṃ nīlīvirañjitam |
vastraṃ dadyānmahādevyai nānyasmai tu kadācana || 13 ||
meaning:
विचित्रे वाससि पुनर्लग्नं नीलीविरञ्जितम् |
वस्त्रं दद्यान्महादेव्यै नान्यस्मै तु कदाचन || 13 ||
text_mt: Moreover, one may offer cloth attached to a multi-coloured garment, coloured with indigo, / to the Great Goddess, but never to anyone else.

sanskrit_iast:
dvipadāṃ brāhmaṇo yadvaddevānāṃ vāsavo yathā |
tathā bhūṣaṇavargeṣu vastramuttamamucyate || 14 ||
meaning:
द्विपदां ब्राह्मणो यद्वद्देवानां वासवो यथा |
तथा भूषणवर्गेषु वस्त्रमुत्तममुच्यते || 14 ||
text_mt: Just as the brāhmaṇa is the best of bipeds, and Indra of the gods, / so cloth is called the foremost among the classes of ornaments.

sanskrit_iast:
vastreṇa jīryate lajjā vastreṇa hīyate tvadham |
vastrāt syāt sarvataḥ siddhiścaturvarga pradaṃ ca tat || 15 ||
meaning:
वस्त्रेण जीर्यते लज्जा वस्त्रेण हीयते त्वधम् |
वस्त्रात् स्यात् सर्वतः सिद्धिश्चतुर्वर्ग प्रदं च तत् || 15 ||
text_mt: By cloth shame is worn away, and by cloth sin is removed; / from cloth comes accomplishment in everything, and it grants the four aims of life.

sanskrit_iast:
vastraṃ te kathitaṃ putra sarvaprītipradāyakam |
bhogyaṃ bhūṣottamaṃ nityaṃ bhūṣaṇāni śṛṇuṣva me || 16 ||
meaning:
वस्त्रं ते कथितं पुत्र सर्वप्रीतिप्रदायकम् |
भोग्यं भूषोत्तमं नित्यं भूषणानि शृणुष्व मे || 16 ||
text_mt: Cloth has been described to you, my son, as granting all pleasure, / an enjoyable object and eternally the supreme ornament; now hear the ornaments from me:

sanskrit_iast:
kirīṭaṃ ca śiroratnaṃ kuṇḍalaṃ ca lalāṭikā |
tālapatraṃ ca hāraśca graiveyakamathormikā || 17 ||
meaning:
किरीटं च शिरोरत्नं कुण्डलं च ललाटिका |
तालपत्रं च हारश्च ग्रैवेयकमथोर्मिका || 17 ||
text_mt: a diadem, a head-gem, an earring, a forehead-ornament, / a palm-leaf earring, a necklace, a choker, and a ring,

sanskrit_iast:
prālambikāratnasūtramuttaṅgotarks'mālikā |
pārśvadyoto nakhadyoto hyaṅgulīcchādakastathā || 18 ||
meaning:
प्रालम्बिकारत्नसूत्रमुत्तङ्गोतर्क्स्ऽमालिका |
पार्श्वद्योतो नखद्योतो ह्यङ्गुलीच्छादकस्तथा || 18 ||
text_mt: a long pendent necklace, a jewel-string, a crest-garland, / a flank-brilliance, a nail-brilliance, and a finger-cover,

sanskrit_iast:
jūṭālakaṃ mānavako mūrdhatārā khalantikā |
aṅgado bāhuvalayaḥ śikhābhūṣaṇa iṅgikā || 19 ||
meaning:
जूटालकं मानवको मूर्धतारा खलन्तिका |
अङ्गदो बाहुवलयः शिखाभूषण इङ्गिका || 19 ||
text_mt: a crest-pendant, a mānavaka garland, a head-star, an anklet, / an armlet, an arm-bangle, a topknot ornament, an iṅgikā,

sanskrit_iast:
rāgdaṇḍabandhamudbhāsanābhipūro'tha mālikā |
saptakī śṛṅkhalaṃ caiva dantapatraṃ ca karṇakaḥ || 20 ||
meaning:
राग्दण्डबन्धमुद्भासनाभिपूरोऽथ मालिका |
सप्तकी शृङ्खलं चैव दन्तपत्रं च कर्णकः || 20 ||
text_mt: a chest-band, an illuminating navel-filler, a garland, / a seven-string necklace, a chain, an ivory earring, an ear-drop,

sanskrit_iast:
ūrusūtraṃ ca nīvīṃ ca muṣṭibandhaṃ prakīrṇakam |
pādāṅgadaṃ haṃsakaśca nūpuraṃ kṣudraghaṇṭikā || 21 ||
meaning:
ऊरुसूत्रं च नीवीं च मुष्टिबन्धं प्रकीर्णकम् |
पादाङ्गदं हंसकश्च नूपुरं क्षुद्रघण्टिका || 21 ||
text_mt: a thigh-chain, a waist-knot cloth, a wrist-band, a loose flower-garland, / a foot-armlet, a haṃsaka foot-ornament, an anklet, and small bells,

sanskrit_iast:
sukhapaṭṭamiti proktā alaṅkārāḥ suśobhanāḥ |
catvāriṃśadamī proktā loke vede tu saukhyadāḥ || 22 ||
meaning:
सुखपट्टमिति प्रोक्ता अलङ्काराः सुशोभनाः |
चत्वारिंशदमी प्रोक्ता लोके वेदे तु सौख्यदाः || 22 ||
text_mt: and the sukhapaṭṭa headband: these beautiful ornaments are proclaimed; / these forty, granting pleasure in the world and in the Veda, are declared.

sanskrit_iast:
alaṅkārapradānena caturvargaprasādhanam |
eteṣāṃ pūjanaṃ kṛtvā pradadyādiṣṭasiddhaye || 23 ||
meaning:
अलङ्कारप्रदानेन चतुर्वर्गप्रसाधनम् |
एतेषां पूजनं कृत्वा प्रदद्यादिष्टसिद्धये || 23 ||
text_mt: By the giving of ornaments, the four aims of life are accomplished; / having performed worship to these, one should offer [them] for the attainment of one's desired ends.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣāṃ daivatamuccārya pūjayet tu vicakṣaṇaḥ |
śirogatāni vā dadyāt sauvarṇāni tu sarvadā || 24 ||
meaning:
तेषां दैवतमुच्चार्य पूजयेत् तु विचक्षणः |
शिरोगतानि वा दद्यात् सौवर्णानि तु सर्वदा || 24 ||
text_mt: Having pronounced their deity, a wise man should worship them; / or one should always give golden [ornaments] that go upon the head,

sanskrit_iast:
cūḍāratnādikānīha bhūṣaṇāni tu bhairava |
graiveyakādihaṃsāntaṃ sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ ca vā || 25 ||
meaning:
चूडारत्नादिकानीह भूषणानि तु भैरव |
ग्रैवेयकादिहंसान्तं सौवर्णं राजतं च वा || 25 ||
text_mt: namely, ornaments such as crest-gems, O Bhairava; / from the choker down to the haṃsaka foot-ornament, [they should be] golden or silver.

sanskrit_iast:
nivedayet tu devebhyo nānyat taijasambhavam |
ītiraṅgādi saṃjātaṃ pātropakaraṇādikam || 26 ||
meaning:
निवेदयेत् तु देवेभ्यो नान्यत् तैजसम्भवम् |
ईतिरङ्गादि संजातं पात्रोपकरणादिकम् || 26 ||
text_mt: One should offer them to the gods, and none born of other metals; / vessels, utensils, and so forth made of lead, tin, and such—

sanskrit_iast:
dadyādāyasavarjaṃ tu bhūṣaṇaṃ na kadācana |
ghaṇṭācāmaraumbhādipātropakaraṇādikam || 27 ||
meaning:
दद्यादायसवर्जं तु भूषणं न कदाचन |
घण्टाचामरौम्भादिपात्रोपकरणादिकम् || 27 ||
text_mt: one may offer, but iron is excluded; an ornament [of iron] must never [be given]; / vessels, utensils, and so forth such as bells, chowries, and water-jars,

sanskrit_iast:
tadbhūṣaṇāntare dadyādayastmāt tadupabhūṣaṇam |
sarvaṃ tāmramayaṃ dadyād yat kiṃcid bhūṣaṇādikam || 28 ||
meaning:
तद्भूषणान्तरे दद्यादयस्त्मात् तदुपभूषणम् |
सर्वं ताम्रमयं दद्याद् यत् किंचिद् भूषणादिकम् || 28 ||
text_mt: one should offer among other ornaments, for that secondary ornament comes from iron; / whatever ornament or the like [one offers], one should offer entirely of copper.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvatra svarṇavat tāmramarghyapātre tato'dhikam |
pūjārghyapapātranaivedyādhārapātraṃ ca pānakam || 29 ||
meaning:
सर्वत्र स्वर्णवत् ताम्रमर्घ्यपात्रे ततोऽधिकम् |
पूजार्घ्यपपात्रनैवेद्याधारपात्रं च पानकम् || 29 ||
text_mt: Copper is everywhere like gold, and for the arghya vessel, even superior to it; / a worship-vessel, an arghya vessel, a food-offering base vessel, and a drinking-vessel

sanskrit_iast:
audumbaraṃ sadā viṣṇoḥ prītidaṃ toṣadaṃ tathā |
tāmre devāḥ pramodante tāmre devāḥ sthitāḥ sadā || 30 ||
meaning:
औदुम्बरं सदा विष्णोः प्रीतिदं तोषदं तथा |
ताम्रे देवाः प्रमोदन्ते ताम्रे देवाः स्थिताः सदा || 30 ||
text_mt: made of copper always brings pleasure and delight to Viṣṇu; / the gods rejoice in copper; the gods are always present in copper.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvaprītikaraṃ tāmraṃ tasmāt tāmraṃ prayojayet |
svopayoge naraḥ kuryād devānāmapi bhairava || 31 ||
meaning:
सर्वप्रीतिकरं ताम्रं तस्मात् ताम्रं प्रयोजयेत् |
स्वोपयोगे नरः कुर्याद् देवानामपि भैरव || 31 ||
text_mt: Copper brings delight to all; therefore, one should employ copper; / a person should use it for his own use and also for that of the gods, O Bhairava.

sanskrit_iast:
grīvordhvadeśe raupyaṃ tu na kadācicca bhūṣaṇam |
prāvāraḥ pānapātraṃ ca gaṇḍako gṛhameva ca || 32 ||
meaning:
ग्रीवोर्ध्वदेशे रौप्यं तु न कदाचिच्च भूषणम् |
प्रावारः पानपात्रं च गण्डको गृहमेव च || 32 ||
text_mt: Silver is never an ornament for the area above the neck; / an outer cloak, a drinking-cup, a gaṇḍaka vessel, a house,

sanskrit_iast:
paryaṅkādi yadanyacca sarvaṃ tadupabhūṣaṇam |
yomayamṛte kāṃsyamṛte yadbhūṣaṇaṃ bhavet || 33 ||
meaning:
पर्यङ्कादि यदन्यच्च सर्वं तदुपभूषणम् |
योमयमृते कांस्यमृते यद्भूषणं भवेत् || 33 ||
text_mt: a couch, and whatever else [there is]—all that is a secondary ornament; / whatever ornament is made without iron, without bell-metal,

sanskrit_iast:
svarṇaraupyasya cābhāve tvadhaḥ kāye niyojayet |
eteṣāṃ bhūṣaṇādīnāṃ yad dātuṃ śakyate naraiḥ || 34 ||
meaning:
स्वर्णरौप्यस्य चाभावे त्वधः काये नियोजयेत् |
एतेषां भूषणादीनां यद् दातुं शक्यते नरैः || 34 ||
text_mt: in the absence of gold and silver, one may place on the lower body; / of these ornaments and the like, whatever men are capable of giving,

sanskrit_iast:
tat tad dadyāt sambhave tu sarvameva pradāpayet |
caturvargapradaṃ vitthaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ sarvasaukhyadam || 35 ||
meaning:
तत् तद् दद्यात् सम्भवे तु सर्वमेव प्रदापयेत् |
चतुर्वर्गप्रदं वित्थं भूषणं सर्वसौख्यदम् || 35 ||
text_mt: that they should offer, and if possible, they should present everything; / such ornament grants the four aims of life and provides all comfort.

sanskrit_iast:
tuṣṭipuṣṭiprītikaraṃ yathāśaktīṣṭaye sṛjet |
idaṃ vā bhūṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ sarvadevasya tuṣṭidam || 36 ||
meaning:
तुष्टिपुष्टिप्रीतिकरं यथाशक्तीष्टये सृजेत् |
इदं वा भूषणं प्रोक्तं सर्वदेवस्य तुष्टिदम् || 36 ||
text_mt: Producing contentment, nourishment, and delight, one should offer it according to one's capacity for [the fulfillment of] desires; / this ornament is declared to give satisfaction to all the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
gandhaṃ ca samyak śṛṇutaṃ putrau vetālabhairavau |
cūrṇīkṛto vā ghṛṣṭo vā dāhākarṣita eva vā || 37 ||
meaning:
गन्धं च सम्यक् शृणुतं पुत्रौ वेतालभैरवौ |
चूर्णीकृतो वा घृष्टो वा दाहाकर्षित एव वा || 37 ||
text_mt: And listen attentively to fragrance, O two sons, Vetāla and Bhairava! / Either pulverized, or ground, or extracted by burning,

sanskrit_iast:
rasaḥ sammardajo vāpi prāṇyaṅgodbhava eva vā |
gandhaḥ pañcavidhaḥ prokto devānāṃ prītidāyakaḥ || 38 ||
meaning:
रसः सम्मर्दजो वापि प्राण्यङ्गोद्भव एव वा |
गन्धः पञ्चविधः प्रोक्तो देवानां प्रीतिदायकः || 38 ||
text_mt: or juice born from crushing, or arising from the limb of a living creature— / fragrance is declared to be of five kinds, granting delight to the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
gandhacūrṇaṃ gandhapatraṃ cūrṇaṃ sumanasastathā |
praśastagandhayuktānāṃ patracūrṇāni yāni tu || 39 ||
meaning:
गन्धचूर्णं गन्धपत्रं चूर्णं सुमनसस्तथा |
प्रशस्तगन्धयुक्तानां पत्रचूर्णानि यानि तु || 39 ||
text_mt: Scent-powder, scent-leaves, and the powder of flowers— / whatever leaf-powders there are endowed with praised fragrance,

sanskrit_iast:
tāni gandhavahāni syuḥ sagandhaḥ prathamaḥ smṛtaḥ |
ghṛṣṭo malayajo gandhaḥ sacūrṇīkṛtameruṇā || 40 ||
meaning:
तानि गन्धवहानि स्युः सगन्धः प्रथमः स्मृतः |
घृष्टो मलयजो गन्धः सचूर्णीकृतमेरुणा || 40 ||
text_mt: they are fragrance-bearers; this fragrant [class] is remembered as the first; / ground fragrance is born of Malaya, reduced to powder with Meru,

sanskrit_iast:
aguruprabhṛtiścāpi yasya paṅkaḥ pradīyate |
gandho dṛṣṭvāmaghṛṣṭo'yaṃ dvitīyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ || 41 ||
meaning:
अगुरुप्रभृतिश्चापि यस्य पङ्कः प्रदीयते |
गन्धो दृष्ट्वामघृष्टोऽयं द्वितीयः परिकीर्तितः || 41 ||
text_mt: and aloe wood and others, whose paste is offered; / this fragrance, seen as ground, is proclaimed as the second.

sanskrit_iast:
devadārvagurupadmagandhasārānta candanāḥ |
priyādīnāṃc a yo dagdhvā gṛhyate dāhajo rasaḥ || 42 ||
meaning:
देवदार्वगुरुपद्मगन्धसारान्त चन्दनाः |
प्रियादीनांच् अ यो दग्ध्वा गृह्यते दाहजो रसः || 42 ||
text_mt: Deodar, aloe wood, padmagandhi, and sandalwood ending with essence of scent, / and priya and others: the juice born from burning that is collected after burning them,

sanskrit_iast:
sadāhākarṣito gandhastṛtīyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ |
sugandhakaravībilvagandhīni tilakaṃ tathā || 43 ||
meaning:
सदाहाकर्षितो गन्धस्तृतीयः परिकीर्तितः |
सुगन्धकरवीबिल्वगन्धीनि तिलकं तथा || 43 ||
text_mt: that fragrance extracted by burning is proclaimed as the third; / fragrant karavīra, fragrances of bilva, as well as tilaka,

sanskrit_iast:
prabhṛtīnāṃ raso yo'sau niṣpīḍya parigṛhyate |
sasammardodbhavo gandhaḥ sammardaja itīṣyate || 44 ||
meaning:
प्रभृतीनां रसो योऽसौ निष्पीड्य परिगृह्यते |
ससम्मर्दोद्भवो गन्धः सम्मर्दज इतीष्यते || 44 ||
text_mt: and the like: whatever juice of these is obtained by pressing out, / that is fragrance born of crushing, and is called 'crushing-born'.

sanskrit_iast:
mṛganābhisamudbhūtastatkoṣodbhava eva vā |
gandhaḥ prāṇyaṅgajaḥ prokto modadaḥ svargavāsinām || 45 ||
meaning:
मृगनाभिसमुद्भूतस्तत्कोषोद्भव एव वा |
गन्धः प्राण्यङ्गजः प्रोक्तो मोददः स्वर्गवासिनाम् || 45 ||
text_mt: Arisen from the musk of a deer, or produced from its musk-pouch, / that fragrance is called 'born from the limb of a living creature', giving joy to the inhabitants of heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
karpūragandhasārādyāḥ kṣode ghṛṣṭe ca saṃsthitāḥ |
candrabhāgādayaścāpi rase paṅke ca saṅgatāḥ || 46 ||
meaning:
कर्पूरगन्धसाराद्याः क्षोदे घृष्टे च संस्थिताः |
चन्द्रभागादयश्चापि रसे पङ्के च सङ्गताः || 46 ||
text_mt: Camphor, sandalwood, and the like exist in powder and when ground; / Candrabhāgā and others also join in juice and in paste.

sanskrit_iast:
gandhasāraṃ arvarasaṃ gandhādau ca prayujyate |
mṛganābhirbhaved ghṛṣṭaścūrṇo'pyanyasya yogataḥ || 47 ||
meaning:
गन्धसारं अर्वरसं गन्धादौ च प्रयुज्यते |
मृगनाभिर्भवेद् घृष्टश्चूर्णोऽप्यन्यस्य योगतः || 47 ||
text_mt: Essence of scent, all juices, are employed in perfumes and the like; / musk is ground, and also becomes a powder when joined with another [substance].

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ sarvaṃ tu sarvatra gandho bhavati pañcadhā |
ghṛṣṭādibhāvādanyonyaṃ gandhaḥ prītikaraṃ paraḥ || 48 ||
meaning:
एवं सर्वं तु सर्वत्र गन्धो भवति पञ्चधा |
घृष्टादिभावादन्योन्यं गन्धः प्रीतिकरं परः || 48 ||
text_mt: Thus everywhere, all fragrance becomes fivefold; / from the state of being ground and so on, mutually, fragrance brings supreme delight.

sanskrit_iast:
gandhasya vistaro bhedaḥ proktaḥ kālīyakādayaḥ |
sarvaḥ pañcavidheṣveva praviṣṭo bhavati kṣaṇāt || 49 ||
meaning:
गन्धस्य विस्तरो भेदः प्रोक्तः कालीयकादयः |
सर्वः पञ्चविधेष्वेव प्रविष्टो भवति क्षणात् || 49 ||
text_mt: The extensive division of fragrance, such as kālīyaka and others, is described; / all of it enters in an instant into these five kinds alone.

sanskrit_iast:
gandho malayajo yastu daive pitrye ca sammataḥ |
tasya paṅko raso vāpi cūrṇo vā viṣṇutuṣṭidaḥ || 50 ||
meaning:
गन्धो मलयजो यस्तु दैवे पित्र्ये च सम्मतः |
तस्य पङ्को रसो वापि चूर्णो वा विष्णुतुष्टिदः || 50 ||
text_mt: The fragrance born of Malaya which is approved in rites for gods and ancestors— / its paste, its juice, or its powder gives satisfaction to Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
sarveṣu gandhajāteṣu praśasto malayodbhavaḥ |
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena dadyānmalayajaṃ sadā || 51 ||
meaning:
सर्वेषु गन्धजातेषु प्रशस्तो मलयोद्भवः |
तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन दद्यान्मलयजं सदा || 51 ||
text_mt: Among all kinds of perfumes, sandalwood is the most praised; / therefore, one should always offer sandalwood with every effort.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛṣṇāguruḥ sakarpūraḥ sahito malayodbhavaiḥ |
vaiṣṇavīprītido gandhaḥ kāmākhyāyāśca bhairava || 52 ||
meaning:
कृष्णागुरुः सकर्पूरः सहितो मलयोद्भवैः |
वैष्णवीप्रीतिदो गन्धः कामाख्यायाश्च भैरव || 52 ||
text_mt: Black agallochum along with camphor, combined with sandalwood, / is a perfume pleasing to Vaiṣṇavī and to Kāmākhyā, O Bhairava.

sanskrit_iast:
kuṅkumāgurukastūrīcandrabhāgaiḥ samīkṛtaiḥ |
tripurāprītido gandhastathā caṇḍyāśca śasyate || 53 ||
meaning:
कुङ्कुमागुरुकस्तूरीचन्द्रभागैः समीकृतैः |
त्रिपुराप्रीतिदो गन्धस्तथा चण्ड्याश्च शस्यते || 53 ||
text_mt: With equal parts of saffron, agallochum, musk, and camphor, / a perfume pleasing to Tripurā and likewise to Caṇḍī is commended.

sanskrit_iast:
daivatoddeśapūrveṇa gandhaṃ sampūjya sādhakaḥ |
devāyeṣṭāya vitaret sarvasiddhipradaṃ sadā || 54 ||
meaning:
दैवतोद्देशपूर्वेण गन्धं सम्पूज्य साधकः |
देवायेष्टाय वितरेत् सर्वसिद्धिप्रदं सदा || 54 ||
text_mt: Having first worshiped the perfume with reference to the deity, / the practitioner should offer it to their chosen deity; it always grants all perfections.

sanskrit_iast:
gandhena labhate kāmān gandho dharmapradaḥ sadā |
arthānāṃ sādhako gandho gandhe mokṣaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ || 55 ||
meaning:
गन्धेन लभते कामान् गन्धो धर्मप्रदः सदा |
अर्थानां साधको गन्धो गन्धे मोक्षः प्रतिष्ठितः || 55 ||
text_mt: Through perfume one attains desires; perfume always bestows righteousness; / perfume achieves wealth; liberation is established in perfume.

sanskrit_iast:
ayaṃ vāṃ kathito gandhaḥ putrau vetālabhairavau |
puṣpāṇi devyā vaiṣṇavyāḥ priyāṇi śṛṇu samprati || 56 ||
meaning:
अयं वां कथितो गन्धः पुत्रौ वेतालभैरवौ |
पुष्पाणि देव्या वैष्णव्याः प्रियाणि शृणु सम्प्रति || 56 ||
text_mt: This perfume has been told to you both, O two sons Vetāla and Bhairava. / Now hear of the flowers dear to the goddess Vaiṣṇavī:

sanskrit_iast:
bakulaiścaiva mandāraiḥ kundapuṣpaiḥ kuruṇṭakaiḥ |
karavīrārkapuṣpaiśca śālmalaiścāparājitaiḥ || 57 ||
meaning:
बकुलैश्चैव मन्दारैः कुन्दपुष्पैः कुरुण्टकैः |
करवीरार्कपुष्पैश्च शाल्मलैश्चापराजितैः || 57 ||
text_mt: With bakula, mandāra, kunda flowers, and kuruṇṭaka, / with karavīra, arka flowers, śālmali, and aparājitā,

sanskrit_iast:
damanaiḥ sindhuvāraiśca surabhī kuruvakaistathā |
latābhirbrahmavṛkṣasya dūrvāṅkuraiśca komalaiḥ || 58 ||
meaning:
दमनैः सिन्धुवारैश्च सुरभी कुरुवकैस्तथा |
लताभिर्ब्रह्मवृक्षस्य दूर्वाङ्कुरैश्च कोमलैः || 58 ||
text_mt: with damana, sindhuvāra, fragrant kuruvaka, / with creepers of the palāśa tree, and with tender shoots of dūrvā grass,

sanskrit_iast:
mañjarībhiḥ kuśānāṃ ca bilvapatraiḥ suśobhanaiḥ |
pūjayed vaiṣṇavīṃ devīṃ kāmākhyāṃ tripurāṃ tathā || 59 ||
meaning:
मञ्जरीभिः कुशानां च बिल्वपत्रैः सुशोभनैः |
पूजयेद् वैष्णवीं देवीं कामाख्यां त्रिपुरां तथा || 59 ||
text_mt: with spikes of kuśa grass, and with very beautiful bilva leaves, / one should worship the goddess Vaiṣṇavī, Kāmākhyā, and likewise Tripurā.

sanskrit_iast:
anyāśca yā śivāprītyai jāyante puṣpajātayaḥ |
tā imāḥ śṛṇu kathyante mayā vetāla bhairava || 60 ||
meaning:
अन्याश्च या शिवाप्रीत्यै जायन्ते पुष्पजातयः |
ता इमाः शृणु कथ्यन्ते मया वेताल भैरव || 60 ||
text_mt: And whatever other varieties of flowers exist for the pleasure of Śivā, / hear them as they are spoken by me, O Vetāla and Bhairava:

sanskrit_iast:
mālatī mallikā jātī yūthikā mādhavī tathā |
pāṭalā karavīraśca javā tarkārikā tathā || 61 ||
meaning:
मालती मल्लिका जाती यूथिका माधवी तथा |
पाटला करवीरश्च जवा तर्कारिका तथा || 61 ||
text_mt: Mālatī, mallikā, jasmine, yūthikā, and mādhavī, / pāṭalā, karavīra, hibiscus, and tarkārikā;

sanskrit_iast:
kubjakastagaraścaiva karṇikāro'tha rocanā |
campakābhrātakau bāṇo barbarā mallikā tathā || 62 ||
meaning:
कुब्जकस्तगरश्चैव कर्णिकारोऽथ रोचना |
चम्पकाभ्रातकौ बाणो बर्बरा मल्लिका तथा || 62 ||
text_mt: kubjaka, tagara, karṇikāra, and rocanā, / campaka, āmrātaka, bāṇa, barbarā, and mallikā;

sanskrit_iast:
aśoko lodhratilakau aṭarūṣaśirīṣakau |
śamīpuṣpaṃ ca droṇaśca padmotpalabakāruṇāḥ || 63 ||
meaning:
अशोको लोध्रतिलकौ अटरूषशिरीषकौ |
शमीपुष्पं च द्रोणश्च पद्मोत्पलबकारुणाः || 63 ||
text_mt: aśoka, lodhra, tilaka, aṭarūṣa, and śirīṣa, / the flower of śamī, droṇa, the lotus, blue water-lily, baka, and aruṇa;

sanskrit_iast:
śvetāruṇastrisandhye ca palāśaḥ khadirastathā |
vanamālā'tha sevantī kumudo'tha kadambakaḥ || 64 ||
meaning:
श्वेतारुणस्त्रिसन्ध्ये च पलाशः खदिरस्तथा |
वनमालाऽथ सेवन्ती कुमुदोऽथ कदम्बकः || 64 ||
text_mt: the white and red trisandhyā, the palāśa, and khadira, / the vanamālā, sevantī, white water-lily, and kadamba;

sanskrit_iast:
cakraṃ kokanadaṃ caiva taṇḍilo girikarṇikā |
nāgakeśarapunnāgau ketakyañjalikā tathā || 65 ||
meaning:
चक्रं कोकनदं चैव तण्डिलो गिरिकर्णिका |
नागकेशरपुन्नागौ केतक्यञ्जलिका तथा || 65 ||
text_mt: the cakra, red lotus, taṇḍila, and girikarṇikā, / nāgakeśara, punnāga, ketakī, and añjalikā;

sanskrit_iast:
dohadā bījapūraśca nameruḥ śāla eva ca |
trapuṣī caṇḍabilvaśca jhiṇṭī pañcavidhāstathā || 66 ||
meaning:
दोहदा बीजपूरश्च नमेरुः शाल एव च |
त्रपुषी चण्डबिल्वश्च झिण्टी पञ्चविधास्तथा || 66 ||
text_mt: dohadā, bījapūra, nameru, and śāla, / the trapuṣī, caṇḍabilva, and five kinds of jhiṇṭī.

sanskrit_iast:
evamādyuktakusumaiḥ pūjayed varadāṃ śivām |
apāmārgasya patraṃ tu tato bhṛṅgārapatrakam || 67 ||
meaning:
एवमाद्युक्तकुसुमैः पूजयेद् वरदां शिवाम् |
अपामार्गस्य पत्रं तु ततो भृङ्गारपत्रकम् || 67 ||
text_mt: With such flowers as mentioned, one should worship the boon-granting Śivā. / The leaf of the apāmārga, and then the bhṛṅgāra leaf;

sanskrit_iast:
tato'pi gandhinopatraṃ valāhakamataḥ param |
tasmāt khadirapatraṃ tu vañjulastavaka stathā || 68 ||
meaning:
ततोऽपि गन्धिनोपत्रं वलाहकमतः परम् |
तस्मात् खदिरपत्रं तु वञ्जुलस्तवक स्तथा || 68 ||
text_mt: furthermore, the leaf of fragrant [grass], and valāhaka after that; / then the leaf of khadira, and a cluster of vañjula;

sanskrit_iast:
āmraṃ tu bakagucchaṃ tu jambupatraṃ tataḥ param |
bījapūrasya patraṃ tu tato'pi kuśapatrakam || 69 ||
meaning:
आम्रं तु बकगुच्छं तु जम्बुपत्रं ततः परम् |
बीजपूरस्य पत्रं तु ततोऽपि कुशपत्रकम् || 69 ||
text_mt: mango, a bunch of baka, and then the rose-apple leaf; / the leaf of bījapūra, and also the kuśa leaf;

sanskrit_iast:
dūrvākuraṃ tataḥ proktaṃ śamīpatramataḥ param |
patramāmalakaṃ tasmādāmalaṃ patramantataḥ || 70 ||
meaning:
दूर्वाकुरं ततः प्रोक्तं शमीपत्रमतः परम् |
पत्रमामलकं तस्मादामलं पत्रमन्ततः || 70 ||
text_mt: then dūrvā sprouts are prescribed, and after that the śamī leaf; / the leaf of the āmalaka, and lastly the pure leaf.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvato bilvapatraṃ tu devyāḥ prītikaraṃ matam |
puṣpaṃ kokanadaṃ padmaṃ javā bandhuka eva ca || 71 ||
meaning:
सर्वतो बिल्वपत्रं तु देव्याः प्रीतिकरं मतम् |
पुष्पं कोकनदं पद्मं जवा बन्धुक एव च || 71 ||
text_mt: Above all, the bilva leaf is considered pleasing to the goddess. / As for flowers, the red lotus, the lotus, hibiscus, and bandhūka [are pleasing].

sanskrit_iast:
patraṃ bilvasya sarvebhyo vaiṣṇavītuṣṭidaṃ matam |
sarveṣāṃ puṣpajātīnāṃ raktapadmamihottamam || 72 ||
meaning:
पत्रं बिल्वस्य सर्वेभ्यो वैष्णवीतुष्टिदं मतम् |
सर्वेषां पुष्पजातीनां रक्तपद्ममिहोत्तमम् || 72 ||
text_mt: Of all [leaves], the leaf of the bilva is considered to give delight to Vaiṣṇavī; / of all varieties of flowers, the red lotus is supreme here.

sanskrit_iast:
raktapadmasahasreṇa yo mālāṃ samprayacchati |
bhaktiyukto mahādevyai tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu || 73 ||
meaning:
रक्तपद्मसहस्रेण यो मालां सम्प्रयच्छति |
भक्तियुक्तो महादेव्यै तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु || 73 ||
text_mt: Whoever, endowed with devotion, offers to the Great Goddess / a garland of a thousand red lotuses, hear the meritorious fruit of that:

sanskrit_iast:
kalpakoṭisahasrāṇi kalpakoṭiśatāni ca |
sthitvā mama pure srīmāṃstato rājā kṣitau bhavet || 74 ||
meaning:
कल्पकोटिसहस्राणि कल्पकोटिशतानि च |
स्थित्वा मम पुरे स्रीमांस्ततो राजा क्षितौ भवेत् || 74 ||
text_mt: Having dwelt in my city for thousands of tens of millions of kalpas, / and hundreds of tens of millions of kalpas, that glorious one will then become a king on earth.

sanskrit_iast:
