text_mt: ending in the dative case for "ray" (raśmaye), and the wife of the deity (svāhā) according to rule— / this is taught as the limb-seed-syllable, which grants all desires, of the Sun.

sanskrit_iast:
padmāsanaḥ padmakaraḥ padmagarbhasamadyutiḥ |
saptāśvaḥ saptarajjuśca dvibhujo bhāskaraḥ sadā || 48 ||
meaning:
पद्मासनः पद्मकरः पद्मगर्भसमद्युतिः |
सप्ताश्वः सप्तरज्जुश्च द्विभुजो भास्करः सदा || 48 ||
text_mt: Seated on a lotus, holding a lotus in his hand, having a radiance like the interior of a lotus, / possessing seven horses and seven reins, the Sun has two arms always.

sanskrit_iast:
vartulaṃ maṇḍalaṃ cāsya aṣṭapatrasamanvitam |
aṅguṣṭhāgrāṅgulīnāṃ ca hṛdādīnāṃ tathā ca ṣaṭ || 49 ||
meaning:
वर्तुलं मण्डलं चास्य अष्टपत्रसमन्वितम् |
अङ्गुष्ठाग्राङ्गुलीनां च हृदादीनां तथा च षट् || 49 ||
text_mt: And his circle is round, endowed with eight petals, / and with the tips of the thumbs and the fingers, and likewise the six beginning with the heart,

sanskrit_iast:
aṅgamantreṇa sahita upānte vahnisaṃyutaḥ |
sarvanyāse samuddiṣṭo mantraḥ sarvaphalapradaḥ || 50 ||
meaning:
अङ्गमन्त्रेण सहित उपान्ते वह्निसंयुतः |
सर्वन्यासे समुद्दिष्टो मन्त्रः सर्वफलप्रदः || 50 ||
text_mt: along with the limb-mantra, joined with fire (vahni) at the end, / this mantra, declared for all ritual placements (nyāsa), grants every fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
hṛcchirastu śikhāvarmanetrāsyodarapṛṣṭhataḥ |
bāhvoḥ pāṇyorjaṅghayostu pādayoścāpi vinyaset || 51 ||
meaning:
हृच्छिरस्तु शिखावर्मनेत्रास्योदरपृष्ठतः |
बाह्वोः पाण्योर्जङ्घयोस्तु पादयोश्चापि विन्यसेत् || 51 ||
text_mt: One should place [them] on the heart, head, crest, armor, eyes, mouth, belly, back, / the two arms, the two hands, the two shanks, and also on the two feet,

sanskrit_iast:
jaghane ca samastāni kramānmantrākṣarāṇi ca |
ramāccottarataḥ proktaḥ pūjane parikīrtitaḥ || 52 ||
meaning:
जघने च समस्तानि क्रमान्मन्त्राक्षराणि च |
रमाच्चोत्तरतः प्रोक्तः पूजने परिकीर्तितः || 52 ||
text_mt: and all the syllables of the mantra on the loins in due order. / From the beginning toward the north, it is taught and celebrated in worship.

sanskrit_iast:
visarjanaṃ tathaiśānyāṃ vidyādyā dalaśaktayaḥ |
nirmālyadhṛk tattvacaṇḍo māṭharādyāstu pārśvayoḥ || 53 ||
meaning:
विसर्जनं तथैशान्यां विद्याद्या दलशक्तयः |
निर्माल्यधृक् तत्त्वचण्डो माठराद्यास्तु पार्श्वयोः || 53 ||
text_mt: Likewise, the dismissal is in the northeast, and the petal-śaktis are Vidyā and the others; / Tattvacaṇḍa is the bearer of the remains of the offering, while Māṭhara and the others are at the two sides.

sanskrit_iast:
bījamuttaratantrasya pūrvataḥ pratipāditam |
anena vidhinā tattve pūjayitvā narottamaḥ || 54 ||
meaning:
बीजमुत्तरतन्त्रस्य पूर्वतः प्रतिपादितम् |
अनेन विधिना तत्त्वे पूजयित्वा नरोत्तमः || 54 ||
text_mt: The seed-syllable of the Uttaratantra has been explained previously. / Having worshipped on Tattva according to this rule, the best of men,

sanskrit_iast:
sa kāmānakhilān prāpya ihaloke pramodate |
sukhī śeṣe tathā gacched bhāskarasyālayaṃ prati || 55 ||
meaning:
स कामानखिलान् प्राप्य इहलोके प्रमोदते |
सुखी शेषे तथा गच्छेद् भास्करस्यालयं प्रति || 55 ||
text_mt: having attained all desires, rejoices in this world; / being happy, at the end he goes likewise to the abode of the Sun.

sanskrit_iast:
nātidūre bhāskarasya dakṣiṇasyāṃ śubhāhvayaḥ |
tasyordhvasānau vasati liṅgaṃ śāṃkaramuttamam || 56 ||
meaning:
नातिदूरे भास्करस्य दक्षिणस्यां शुभाह्वयः |
तस्योर्ध्वसानौ वसति लिङ्गं शांकरमुत्तमम् || 56 ||
text_mt: Not far to the south of the Sun lies [the peak] named Śubha; / on its upper ridge dwells the excellent liṅga of Śaṅkara.

sanskrit_iast:
parivārya sadā yānti mahākāyāstu vānarāḥ |
parivāryāvatiṣṭhante sevamānāśca śaṅkaram || 57 ||
meaning:
परिवार्य सदा यान्ति महाकायास्तु वानराः |
परिवार्यावतिष्ठन्ते सेवमानाश्च शङ्करम् || 57 ||
text_mt: Monkeys of huge bodies constantly go surrounding it, / and they stay around it, attending upon Śaṅkara.

sanskrit_iast:
trisrotāyāṃ naraḥ snātvā yaḥ paśyet tu śubhācale |
mahātmānaṃ mahādevaṃ kāmamiṣṭaṃ labhennaraḥ || 58 ||
meaning:
त्रिस्रोतायां नरः स्नात्वा यः पश्येत् तु शुभाचले |
महात्मानं महादेवं काममिष्टं लभेन्नरः || 58 ||
text_mt: The man who, having bathed in the Trisrotā, beholds on the Śubha mountain / the great-souled Mahādeva, that man will obtain his cherished desire.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ pūrvaṃ suranadī nāmnā sukumamālinī |
kṣīrodākhyāparā tasmāt te gate dakṣiṇasrave || 59 ||
meaning:
ततः पूर्वं सुरनदी नाम्ना सुकुममालिनी |
क्षीरोदाख्यापरा तस्मात् ते गते दक्षिणस्रवे || 59 ||
text_mt: East of that is the divine river named Sukumamālinī; / another beyond it is called Kṣīrodā; both of them flow southward.

sanskrit_iast:
ete api mahārāja puṇyatoye'mṛtasrave |
tayoḥ snātvā naro yāti śaṅkarasyālayaṃ prati || 60 ||
meaning:
एते अपि महाराज पुण्यतोयेऽमृतस्रवे |
तयोः स्नात्वा नरो याति शङ्करस्यालयं प्रति || 60 ||
text_mt: These two also, O great king, have sacred waters and flow with nectar; / having bathed in the two, a man goes to the abode of Śaṅkara.

sanskrit_iast:
tato'pi pūrvato devī līlākhyā cāparā nadī |
yasyāṃ snātvā mahānadyāṃ śivalokāya gacchati || 61 ||
meaning:
ततोऽपि पूर्वतो देवी लीलाख्या चापरा नदी |
यस्यां स्नात्वा महानद्यां शिवलोकाय गच्छति || 61 ||
text_mt: East of that also is another divine river named Līlā; / having bathed in which great river, one goes to the world of Śiva.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ pūrvaṃ śivā caṇḍī caṇḍikākhyā mahānadī |
niryāti dhavalākhyāt tu parvatāt sumanoharāt || 62 ||
meaning:
ततः पूर्वं शिवा चण्डी चण्डिकाख्या महानदी |
निर्याति धवलाख्यात् तु पर्वतात् सुमनोहरात् || 62 ||
text_mt: East of that, the auspicious and fierce great river called Caṇḍikā / issues from the delightful mountain named Dhavala.

sanskrit_iast:
śivaliṅgadvayaṃ tatra nātidūre vyavasthitam |
golokaṃ cātha śṛṅgaṃ ca krośamātrāntare sthitam || 63 ||
meaning:
शिवलिङ्गद्वयं तत्र नातिदूरे व्यवस्थितम् |
गोलोकं चाथ शृङ्गं च क्रोशमात्रान्तरे स्थितम् || 63 ||
text_mt: A pair of Śiva-liṅgas is situated there not far away; / Goloka and Śṛṅga stand at a distance of merely one krośa.

sanskrit_iast:
caṇḍikāyāṃ naraḥ snātvā āruhya dhavaleśvaram |
dakṣiṇaṃ sāgaraṃ vīkṣya pṛṣṭvā golokasaṃjñakam || 64 ||
meaning:
चण्डिकायां नरः स्नात्वा आरुह्य धवलेश्वरम् |
दक्षिणं सागरं वीक्ष्य पृष्ट्वा गोलोकसंज्ञकम् || 64 ||
text_mt: A man having bathed in the Caṇḍikā, ascended Dhavaleśvara, / and looked toward the southern ocean, having touched the one named Goloka,

sanskrit_iast:
tato'vatīrya ca punaḥ śṛṅgiṇaṃ bhūmipīṭhakam |
śivapūjāvidhānena pūjayitvā maheśvaram || 65 ||
meaning:
ततोऽवतीर्य च पुनः शृङ्गिणं भूमिपीठकम् |
शिवपूजाविधानेन पूजयित्वा महेश्वरम् || 65 ||
text_mt: and then having descended again to the ground-seat of Śṛṅgin, / having worshipped Maheśvara according to the rite of Śiva-worship,

sanskrit_iast:
aśvamedhasya yajñasya phalaṃ samprāpya mānavaḥ |
sarvān kāmānavāpyeha dehānte śivatāṃ vrajet || 66 ||
meaning:
अश्वमेधस्य यज्ञस्य फलं सम्प्राप्य मानवः |
सर्वान् कामानवाप्येह देहान्ते शिवतां व्रजेत् || 66 ||
text_mt: that human being obtains the fruit of an horse-sacrifice, / and having attained all desires in this world, at the end of the body he attains the state of Śiva.

sanskrit_iast:
etā yāḥ kathitā nadyaḥ sarvā vai dakṣiṇasravāḥ |
tasmādīśānakāṣṭhāyāṃ parvato gandhamādanaḥ || 67 ||
meaning:
एता याः कथिता नद्यः सर्वा वै दक्षिणस्रवाः |
तस्मादीशानकाष्ठायां पर्वतो गन्धमादनः || 67 ||
text_mt: All these rivers that have been mentioned indeed flow south; / in the north-eastern direction from there is Mount Gandhamādana,

sanskrit_iast:
yatra bhṛṅgāhvayaṃ liṅgaṃ śivasyāste mahattaram |
sa eva parvataśreṣṭhaḥ prāptaḥ kṣetrasya paścime || 68 ||
meaning:
यत्र भृङ्गाह्वयं लिङ्गं शिवस्यास्ते महत्तरम् |
स एव पर्वतश्रेष्ठः प्राप्तः क्षेत्रस्य पश्चिमे || 68 ||
text_mt: where the most great liṅga of Śiva named Bhṛṅga resides; / that best of mountains has reached the west of the sacred field.

sanskrit_iast:
dhṛtvā brahmaśilāṃ devīṃ sāvitraṃ pratigāminī |
gandhamādanakasyānte bhṛṅgeśasya padadvayam || 69 ||
meaning:
धृत्वा ब्रह्मशिलां देवीं सावित्रं प्रतिगामिनी |
गन्धमादनकस्यान्ते भृङ्गेशस्य पदद्वयम् || 69 ||
text_mt: Having sustained the divine stone of Brahmā, which goes toward the solar [shrine], / at the end of Gandhamādana are the two feet of Bhṛṅgeśa.

sanskrit_iast:
sravadgaṅgājalaṃ cāste kuṇḍaṃ tatrāntarālakam |
antarālakakuṇḍe tu snātvā pītvā ca tajjalam || 70 ||
meaning:
स्रवद्गङ्गाजलं चास्ते कुण्डं तत्रान्तरालकम् |
अन्तरालककुण्डे तु स्नात्वा पीत्वा च तज्जलम् || 70 ||
text_mt: And there is a pool with flowing Gaṅgā water, the Antarālaka; / having bathed in the Antarālaka pool and having drunk its water,

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛṅgeśasya tato dṛṣṭvā śilāsaṃsthaṃ padadvayam |
pūjayitvā mahābhṛṅgaṃ gāṇapatyamavāpnuyāt || 71 ||
meaning:
भृङ्गेशस्य ततो दृष्ट्वा शिलासंस्थं पदद्वयम् |
पूजयित्वा महाभृङ्गं गाणपत्यमवाप्नुयात् || 71 ||
text_mt: and then having seen the two feet of Bhṛṅgeśa situated upon the stone, / having worshipped Mahābhṛṅga, one will attain the state of a leader of Gaṇas.

sanskrit_iast:
śambhupādasamudbhūtamantarāladṛśākaram |
vṛṣadhvajapadānāṃ tvaṃ saṃyojaya mahāvṛṣa || 72 ||
meaning:
शम्भुपादसमुद्भूतमन्तरालदृशाकरम् |
वृषध्वजपदानां त्वं संयोजय महावृष || 72 ||
text_mt: "Arisen from the foot of Śambhu, producing sight of the intermediate space, / unite [me], O great bull, with the feet of the bull-bannered god!"

sanskrit_iast:
ityanena tu mantreṇa snānaṃ kṛtvāntarājale |
bhṛṅgadevaṃ tataḥ paśyet kubjapīṭhāntavāsinam || 73 ||
meaning:
इत्यनेन तु मन्त्रेण स्नानं कृत्वान्तराजले |
भृङ्गदेवं ततः पश्येत् कुब्जपीठान्तवासिनम् || 73 ||
text_mt: Having bathed in the intermediate water with this mantra, / one should then behold the god Bhṛṅga, who dwells at the edge of Kubjapīṭha.

sanskrit_iast:
maṇikūṭasyātha girergandhamādanakasya ca |
madhye sravati lauhityo brahmaṇāgnisamutthitaḥ || 74 ||
meaning:
मणिकूटस्याथ गिरेर्गन्धमादनकस्य च |
मध्ये स्रवति लौहित्यो ब्रह्मणाग्निसमुत्थितः || 74 ||
text_mt: Now, between the mountain Maṇikūṭa and Gandhamādana, / the Lauhitya, sprung from the fire of Brahmā, flows.

sanskrit_iast:
arṇāśāyā dakṣiṇasyāṃ lauhityo nāma sāgaraḥ |
maṇikūṭaḥ sthitaḥ pūrve hayagrīvo hariryataḥ || 75 ||
meaning:
अर्णाशाया दक्षिणस्यां लौहित्यो नाम सागरः |
मणिकूटः स्थितः पूर्वे हयग्रीवो हरिर्यतः || 75 ||
text_mt: South of Arṇāśā is the ocean named Lauhitya; / Maṇikūṭa is situated in the east, where Hari is Hayagrīva.

sanskrit_iast:
sa hayagrīvarūpeṇa viṣṇurhatvā jvarāsuram |
nihatya sa hayagrīvaḥ krīḍāyai yatra saṃsthitaḥ || 76 ||
meaning:
स हयग्रीवरूपेण विष्णुर्हत्वा ज्वरासुरम् |
निहत्य स हयग्रीवः क्रीडायै यत्र संस्थितः || 76 ||
text_mt: Having slain the demon Jvara in the form of Hayagrīva, / having killed him, Hayagrīva stayed there for sport.

sanskrit_iast:
hatvā jvaraṃ tathā viṣṇustatra vāsamathākarot |
naradevāsurādīnāṃ yathā bhavati vai hitam || 77 ||
meaning:
हत्वा ज्वरं तथा विष्णुस्तत्र वासमथाकरोत् |
नरदेवासुरादीनां यथा भवति वै हितम् || 77 ||
text_mt: Having slain Jvara, Viṣṇu then made his residence there, / so that the welfare of men, gods, demons, and others would indeed come to pass.

sanskrit_iast:
jvareṇāpīḍita tanurjvaraṃ hatvā mahāsuram |
sarvalokahitārthāya so'gadasnā namacaret || 78 ||
meaning:
ज्वरेणापीडित तनुर्ज्वरं हत्वा महासुरम् |
सर्वलोकहितार्थाय सोऽगदस्ना नमचरेत् || 78 ||
text_mt: With his body afflicted by the fever (jvara), having slain the great demon Jvara, / he performed a medicinal bath for the sake of the welfare of all the worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
agadasnānasambhūtaṃ saṃjātaṃ ca ahāsaraḥ |
tasya svayaṃ hayagrīvo nāma cakre'punarbhavam || 79 ||
meaning:
अगदस्नानसम्भूतं संजातं च अहासरः |
तस्य स्वयं हयग्रीवो नाम चक्रेऽपुनर्भवम् || 79 ||
text_mt: A great lake came into being produced by that medicinal bath; / Hayagrīva himself gave it the name Apunarbhava.

sanskrit_iast:
na punarjāyate yasmāt tatra snātvā narottamaḥ |
apunarbhavasaṃjñaṃ tat sarastu parikīrtitam || 80 ||
meaning:
न पुनर्जायते यस्मात् तत्र स्नात्वा नरोत्तमः |
अपुनर्भवसंज्ञं तत् सरस्तु परिकीर्तितम् || 80 ||
text_mt: Because the best of men is not born again after bathing there, / that lake is therefore proclaimed by the name Apunarbhava.

sanskrit_iast:
maṇikaṭācale viṣṇurhayagrīvasvarūpadhṛk |
śatavyāmapramāṇena vistareṇaiva śobhitam || 81 ||
meaning:
मणिकटाचले विष्णुर्हयग्रीवस्वरूपधृक् |
शतव्यामप्रमाणेन विस्तरेणैव शोभितम् || 81 ||
text_mt: Viṣṇu, bearing the form of Hayagrīva on Mount Maṇikūṭa, / is adorned with an extent of one hundred vyāmas in width.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmāt pūrve bhadrakāmaḥ parvatastu trikoṇakaḥ |
yatra kālahayo nāma śivaliṅgo vyavasthitaḥ || 82 ||
meaning:
तस्मात् पूर्वे भद्रकामः पर्वतस्तु त्रिकोणकः |
यत्र कालहयो नाम शिवलिङ्गो व्यवस्थितः || 82 ||
text_mt: East of that is the triangular mountain Bhadrakāma, / where the Śiva-liṅga named Kālahaya is situated.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyāsanne dakṣiṇasyāmapunarbhavakuṇḍakam |
apunarbhūḥsarastīre parvate bhadrakāmade || 83 ||
meaning:
तस्यासन्ने दक्षिणस्यामपुनर्भवकुण्डकम् |
अपुनर्भूःसरस्तीरे पर्वते भद्रकामदे || 83 ||
text_mt: Near it, to the south, is the Apunarbhava pool, / on the bank of the Apunarbhū lake, on the wish-granting mountain Bhadra.

sanskrit_iast:
haravīthīti vikhyātā śilā brahmasvarūpiṇī |
tatra yogī mahādevo yogajño dhyānatatparaḥ || 84 ||
meaning:
हरवीथीति विख्याता शिला ब्रह्मस्वरूपिणी |
तत्र योगी महादेवो योगज्ञो ध्यानतत्परः || 84 ||
text_mt: There is a stone famed as Haravīthī, having the nature of Brahman; / there, Mahādeva, the yogin who knows yoga, is absorbed in meditation.

sanskrit_iast:
yaṃ dṛṣṭvā yogavān martyo mṛto mokṣamavāpnuyāt |
tasyāmeva śilāyāṃ tu gokarṇo nāma śaṅkaraḥ || 85 ||
meaning:
यं दृष्ट्वा योगवान् मर्त्यो मृतो मोक्षमवाप्नुयात् |
तस्यामेव शिलायां तु गोकर्णो नाम शङ्करः || 85 ||
text_mt: Seeing him, a mortal possessing yoga attains liberation upon death. / On that very stone is the Śaṅkara named Gokarṇa,

sanskrit_iast:
gokarṇo nihato yena andhakasya sakhā purā |
gokarṇasya tathaiśānyāṃ kedāraḥ śambhurantataḥ || 86 ||
meaning:
गोकर्णो निहतो येन अन्धकस्य सखा पुरा |
गोकर्णस्य तथैशान्यां केदारः शम्भुरन्ततः || 86 ||
text_mt: by whom Gokarṇa, the friend of Andhaka, was slain in ancient times. / Likewise, in the northeast of Gokarṇa is Śambhu Kedāra at the end.

sanskrit_iast:
tato'ndhakasamaḥ proktaḥ kamalākarabhogadhṛk |
yatrāsti śambhuḥ kedāraḥ sa girirmadanāhvayaḥ || 87 ||
meaning:
ततोऽन्धकसमः प्रोक्तः कमलाकरभोगधृक् |
यत्रास्ति शम्भुः केदारः स गिरिर्मदनाह्वयः || 87 ||
text_mt: After that is proclaimed the one equal to Andhaka, enjoying the lotus pond; / the mountain where Śambhu Kedāra is located is named Madana.

sanskrit_iast:
tatraiva kamalaḥ proktaḥ sa mahātmālayapradaḥ |
snātvā'punarbhavajale dṛṣṭvā gokarṇayoginau || 88 ||
meaning:
तत्रैव कमलः प्रोक्तः स महात्मालयप्रदः |
स्नात्वाऽपुनर्भवजले दृष्ट्वा गोकर्णयोगिनौ || 88 ||
text_mt: Right there Kamala is proclaimed, who grants the abode of that great soul; / having bathed in the water of Apunarbhava and seen the two yogins Gokarṇa [and Śambhu],

sanskrit_iast:
kedārakamalau dṛṣṭvā muktirmādhavadarśane |
dṛṣṭvā tu mādhavaṃ devaṃ tataḥ kāmaṃ vilokayet || 89 ||
meaning:
केदारकमलौ दृष्ट्वा मुक्तिर्माधवदर्शने |
दृष्ट्वा तु माधवं देवं ततः कामं विलोकयेत् || 89 ||
text_mt: having seen Kedāra and Kamala, liberation comes upon seeing Mādhava; / having seen the god Mādhava, one should then behold Kāma.

sanskrit_iast:
kāmaṃ vilokya tatrastho nirīkṣedapunarbhavam |
evaṃ kṛtvā pīṭhayātrāmanena kramayogataḥ || 90 ||
meaning:
कामं विलोक्य तत्रस्थो निरीक्षेदपुनर्भवम् |
एवं कृत्वा पीठयात्रामनेन क्रमयोगतः || 90 ||
text_mt:
Beholding Kāma, standing there, one should gaze upon Apunarbhava.
Having thus made the pilgrimage of the pīṭha according to this sequence,

sanskrit_iast:
sapta pūrvān sapta parānātmānaṃ daśa pañca ca |
pitṛnuddhṛtya tridivaṃ nayet sa puruṣottamaḥ || 91 ||
meaning:
सप्त पूर्वान् सप्त परानात्मानं दश पञ्च च |
पितृनुद्धृत्य त्रिदिवं नयेत् स पुरुषोत्तमः || 91 ||
text_mt:
Seven ancestors, seven descendants, and fifteen [generations of] ancestors
for oneself—delivering them, that best of men shall lead them to heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
viṣṇusthānasamudbhutā punarbhavaharīśvara |
pāpaṃ hara svargahetorjitasaṅgamahodadhe || 92 ||
meaning:
विष्णुस्थानसमुद्भुता पुनर्भवहरीश्वर |
पापं हर स्वर्गहेतोर्जितसङ्गमहोदधे || 92 ||
text_mt:
“O lord, arisen from Viṣṇu's abode, remover of rebirth!
Remove sin for the sake of heaven, O ocean that overcomes worldly attachment!”

sanskrit_iast:
anenaiva tu mantreṇa snāyād vīro'punarbhave |
hayagrīvasya tantraṃ tu puraiva pratipāditam || 93 ||
meaning:
अनेनैव तु मन्त्रेण स्नायाद् वीरोऽपुनर्भवे |
हयग्रीवस्य तन्त्रं तु पुरैव प्रतिपादितम् || 93 ||
text_mt:
With this very mantra, a hero should bathe in Apunarbhava.
The tantra of Hayagrīva, however, has already been explained previously.

sanskrit_iast:
rūpaṃ śṛṇu mahārāja cintayet tasya yādṛśam |
karpūrakundadhavalaḥ sitapadmoparisthitaḥ || 94 ||
meaning:
रूपं शृणु महाराज चिन्तयेत् तस्य यादृशम् |
कर्पूरकुन्दधवलः सितपद्मोपरिस्थितः || 94 ||
text_mt:
Hear, O great king, the form in which one should contemplate him:
white as camphor and the kunda flower, seated upon a white lotus,

sanskrit_iast:
caturbhujaḥ kuṇḍalādinānālaṅkārabhūṣitaḥ |
varadābhayahastastu vāmahastadvayena tu || 95 ||
meaning:
चतुर्भुजः कुण्डलादिनानालङ्कारभूषितः |
वरदाभयहस्तस्तु वामहस्तद्वयेन तु || 95 ||
text_mt:
four-armed, adorned with various ornaments such as earrings,
having hands granting boons and protection with his two left hands,

sanskrit_iast:
pustakaṃ sitapadmaṃ ca dhatte hastadvaye'pare |
śrīvatsakaustubhoraskaḥ kvacicca garudāsanaḥ || 96 ||
meaning:
पुस्तकं सितपद्मं च धत्ते हस्तद्वयेऽपरे |
श्रीवत्सकौस्तुभोरस्कः क्वचिच्च गरुदासनः || 96 ||
text_mt:
and holding a book and a white lotus in his other two hands,
with the Śrīvatsa and Kaustubha on his chest, and occasionally seated upon Garuḍa.

sanskrit_iast:
sarva uttaratantroktaḥ kramo grāhyaḥ prapūjane |
viṣvakseno hayārestu nirmālyadhṛgvisarjane || 97 ||
meaning:
सर्व उत्तरतन्त्रोक्तः क्रमो ग्राह्यः प्रपूजने |
विष्वक्सेनो हयारेस्तु निर्माल्यधृग्विसर्जने || 97 ||
text_mt:
The entire procedure declared in the Uttaratantra should be adopted in worship.
Viṣvaksena is the receiver of the remnants at the dismissal of the enemy of the horse.

sanskrit_iast:
śilārūparpaticchannaḥ sadāste garuḍadhvajaḥ |
krīḍamāno'tha gandharvaiḥ sthito lokahitāya ca || 98 ||
meaning:
शिलारूपर्पतिच्छन्नः सदास्ते गरुडध्वजः |
क्रीडमानोऽथ गन्धर्वैः स्थितो लोकहिताय च || 98 ||
text_mt:
Concealed in the form of a stone, Garuḍa-bannered [Viṣṇu] ever abides,
sporting with the gandharvas and remaining for the welfare of the world.

sanskrit_iast:
hayagrīvasya mantrasya siddhirlakṣadvayena tu |
yāvakaiḥ pāyasairājyairhomaṃ kurvan puraścaret || 99 ||
meaning:
हयग्रीवस्य मन्त्रस्य सिद्धिर्लक्षद्वयेन तु |
यावकैः पायसैराज्यैर्होमं कुर्वन् पुरश्चरेत् || 99 ||
text_mt:
Attainment of the mantra of Hayagrīva comes through two hundred thousand [repetitions].
One should perform the preparatory rite, offering oblations with barley, milk-rice, and ghee.

sanskrit_iast:
ekenaiva tu rājendra puraścaraṇakarmaṇā |
iṣṭasiddhimavāpyeha viṣṇulokamavāpnuyāt || 100 ||
meaning:
एकेनैव तु राजेन्द्र पुरश्चरणकर्मणा |
इष्टसिद्धिमवाप्येह विष्णुलोकमवाप्नुयात् || 100 ||
text_mt:
By just one rite of preparation, O lord of kings,
having obtained desired success here, one attains the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
mantraistu pañcavaktrāṇāṃ pañcamūrtīḥ sadārcayet |
pūrve tatpuruṣādīnāṃ kāmādīn pūjako dvijaḥ || 101 ||
meaning:
मन्त्रैस्तु पञ्चवक्त्राणां पञ्चमूर्तीः सदार्चयेत् |
पूर्वे तत्पुरुषादीनां कामादीन् पूजको द्विजः || 101 ||
text_mt:
With the mantras of the five-faced [Śiva], the twice-born worshipper should always worship
the five forms: Kāma and the others in the east, [beginning with] Tatpuruṣa and the rest.

sanskrit_iast:
kāmastatpuruṣo jñeyo yogīśānaḥ prakīrtitaḥ |
aghoro hyatha gokarṇaḥ kedāro vāmadevakaḥ || 102 ||
meaning:
कामस्तत्पुरुषो ज्ञेयो योगीशानः प्रकीर्तितः |
अघोरो ह्यथ गोकर्णः केदारो वामदेवकः || 102 ||
text_mt:
Kāma is to be known as Tatpuruṣa; the Yogin is proclaimed as Īśāna;
Gokarṇa is indeed Aghora; Kedāra is Vāmadeva;

sanskrit_iast:
sadyojātastu kamalāmantraistaistaiḥ prapūjayet |
parvataścaiva kedāraḥ śivagaṅgā tu tu kālikā || 103 ||
meaning:
सद्योजातस्तु कमलामन्त्रैस्तैस्तैः प्रपूजयेत् |
पर्वतश्चैव केदारः शिवगङ्गा तु तु कालिका || 103 ||
text_mt:
and Kamala is Sadyojāta; one should worship each with its respective mantra.
Kedāra is the mountain, and Kālikā is the Śivagaṅgā.

sanskrit_iast:
hayagrīvasya pūrvasyāṃ kedārasya tu paścime |
chāyābhogāhvayasthānaṃ purī bhogavatī tathā || 104 ||
meaning:
हयग्रीवस्य पूर्वस्यां केदारस्य तु पश्चिमे |
छायाभोगाह्वयस्थानं पुरी भोगवती तथा || 104 ||
text_mt:
To the east of Hayagrīva, but to the west of Kedāra,
is the place named Chāyābhoga, as well as the city of Bhogavatī.

sanskrit_iast:
yo gacchenmaṇikūṭākhyāt kautukācca punarbhavam |
sa sarvatīrthayātrāṇāṃ phalamāpnoti mānavaḥ || 105 ||
meaning:
यो गच्छेन्मणिकूटाख्यात् कौतुकाच्च पुनर्भवम् |
स सर्वतीर्थयात्राणां फलमाप्नोति मानवः || 105 ||
text_mt:
A person who goes from Maṇikūṭa out of curiosity to Apunarbhava
attains the fruit of pilgrimages to all sacred fords.

sanskrit_iast:
jyaiṣṭhe māsi site pakṣe pañcadaśyaṣṭamīṣu ca |
snātvā'punarbhavajale yaḥ paśyed vidhivaddharim |
sa sarvaṃ kulamuddhṛtya viṣṇusāyujyamāpnuyāt || 106 ||
meaning:
ज्यैष्ठे मासि सिते पक्षे पञ्चदश्यष्टमीषु च |
स्नात्वाऽपुनर्भवजले यः पश्येद् विधिवद्धरिम् |
स सर्वं कुलमुद्धृत्य विष्णुसायुज्यमाप्नुयात् || 106 ||
text_mt:
In the month of Jyaiṣṭha, in the bright fortnight, on the fifteenth and eighth days,
one who bathes in the water of Apunarbhava and beholds Hari according to rule,
delivering his entire lineage, attains communion with Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
jyeṣṭhaṃ tu sakalaṃ māsaṃ nityaṃ paśyet tu yo harim |
harau vilīnatāṃ yāti sa sarvaiḥ sahitaḥ kulaiḥ || 107 ||
meaning:
ज्येष्ठं तु सकलं मासं नित्यं पश्येत् तु यो हरिम् |
हरौ विलीनतां याति स सर्वैः सहितः कुलैः || 107 ||
text_mt:
He who continually beholds Hari throughout the entire month of Jyeṣṭha
goes to dissolution in Hari together with all his family lines.

sanskrit_iast:
etat te kathitaṃ puṇyaṃ maṇikūṭāhvayaṃ param |
vārāṇasīto hyadhikaṃ siddhavidyādharārcitam || 108 ||
meaning:
एतत् ते कथितं पुण्यं मणिकूटाह्वयं परम् |
वाराणसीतो ह्यधिकं सिद्धविद्याधरार्चितम् || 108 ||
text_mt:
This supreme, auspicious [place] named Maṇikūṭa has been told to you,
greater even than Vārāṇasī, worshipped by siddhas and vidyādharas.

sanskrit_iast:
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvipro maṇikūṭasya nirṇayam |
sa sarvavedasya phalaṃ prāpnotyeva na saṃśayaḥ || 109 ||
meaning:
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्विप्रो मणिकूटस्य निर्णयम् |
स सर्ववेदस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्येव न संशयः || 109 ||
text_mt:
Whatever brāhmaṇa reads or listens to this determination of Maṇikūṭa,
he surely obtains the fruit of all the Vedas; there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast: iti śrīkālikāpurāṇe aṣṭasaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ || 78 ||
meaning: इति श्रीकालिकापुराणे अष्टसप्ततितमोऽध्यायः || 78 ||
text_mt: Thus ends the seventy-eighth chapter in the glorious Kālikāpurāṇa.

sanskrit_iast: ekonāśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ
meaning: एकोनाशीतितमोऽध्यायः
text_mt: The seventy-ninth chapter.

sanskrit_iast: aurva uvāca -
meaning: और्व उवाच -

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ pūrvaṃ mahārāja darpaṇo nāma parvataḥ |
kubero yatra vasati dhanapālaiḥ samaṃ sadā || 1 ||
meaning:
ततः पूर्वं महाराज दर्पणो नाम पर्वतः |
कुबेरो यत्र वसति धनपालैः समं सदा || 1 ||
text_mt:
East of that, O great king, is the mountain named Darpaṇa,
where Kubera ever dwells along with the guardians of wealth;

sanskrit_iast:
yasminnāste madhyabhāge rohito rohitākṛtiḥ |
yasmiṃllohādikaṃ spṛṣṭaṃ svarṇatāṃ yāti tatkṣaṇāt || 2 ||
meaning:
यस्मिन्नास्ते मध्यभागे रोहितो रोहिताकृतिः |
यस्मिंल्लोहादिकं स्पृष्टं स्वर्णतां याति तत्क्षणात् || 2 ||
text_mt:
in whose central region rests Rohita in the form of a rohita fish,
and upon which iron and other [metals], once touched, immediately become gold;

sanskrit_iast:
yatrātidūre sravati darpaṇo nāma vai nadaḥ |
himādriprabhavo nityaṃ lauhityasadṛśaḥ phalaiḥ || 3 ||
meaning:
यत्रातिदूरे स्रवति दर्पणो नाम वै नदः |
हिमाद्रिप्रभवो नित्यं लौहित्यसदृशः फलैः || 3 ||
text_mt:
where, not very far away, flows the river named Darpaṇa,
arising from the snowy mountain, always equal to the Lauhitya in its fruits.

sanskrit_iast:
samutpannaṃ hi lauhityaṃ sarvairdaivagaṇairhariḥ |
sarvatīrthodakaiḥ samyak snāpayāmāsa taṃ sutam || 4 ||
meaning:
समुत्पन्नं हि लौहित्यं सर्वैर्दैवगणैर्हरिः |
सर्वतीर्थोदकैः सम्यक् स्नापयामास तं सुतम् || 4 ||
text_mt:
For when Lauhitya was born, Hari, together with all the hosts of gods,
bathed that son thoroughly with the waters of all sacred fords.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya snānasamudbhūtaḥ pāpadarpasya pāṭanaḥ |
tenāyaṃ darpaṇo nāma purā devagaṇaiḥ kṛtaḥ || 5 ||
meaning:
तस्य स्नानसमुद्भूतः पापदर्पस्य पाटनः |
तेनायं दर्पणो नाम पुरा देवगणैः कृतः || 5 ||
text_mt:
Arisen from his bathing, it shatters the pride of sin;
therefore this [river] was named Darpaṇa of old by the hosts of gods.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmin snātvā nadavare yo'rcayed darpaṇācale |
kuberaṃ pratipattithyāṃ kārtike śuklapakṣake || 6 ||
meaning:
तस्मिन् स्नात्वा नदवरे योऽर्चयेद् दर्पणाचले |
कुबेरं प्रतिपत्तिथ्यां कार्तिके शुक्लपक्षके || 6 ||
text_mt:
Having bathed in that excellent river, he who worships Kubera on Mount Darpaṇa
on the first lunar day in the bright fortnight of Kārtika,

sanskrit_iast:
sa yāti brahmasadanamiha bhūtiśatairyutaḥ |
darpaṇād diśi pūrvasyāmagnimālāhvayau giriḥ || 7 ||
meaning:
स याति ब्रह्मसदनमिह भूतिशतैर्युतः |
दर्पणाद् दिशि पूर्वस्यामग्निमालाह्वयौ गिरिः || 7 ||
text_mt:
endowed with hundreds of splendors in this world, goes to the abode of Brahmā.
In the eastern direction from Darpaṇa is the mountain named Agnimālā,

sanskrit_iast:
sarpākāraḥ saptaśatavyāmadīrghodardha vistṛtaḥ |
tatra tiṣṭhati vai vahnirūrdhvabhāge'gnimaṇḍale || 8 ||
meaning:
सर्पाकारः सप्तशतव्यामदीर्घोदर्ध विस्तृतः |
तत्र तिष्ठति वै वह्निरूर्ध्वभागेऽग्निमण्डले || 8 ||
text_mt:
serpent-shaped, seven hundred fathoms long and half that in width.
There Fire indeed abides in the upper part, in the fire-circle.

sanskrit_iast:
sindūrapuñjasaṅkāśe cārudārūśilātale |
tasminnirindhano vahnirnityamadyāpi kāśate || 9 ||
meaning:
सिन्दूरपुञ्जसङ्काशे चारुदारूशिलातले |
तस्मिन्निरिन्धनो वह्निर्नित्यमद्यापि काशते || 9 ||
text_mt:
Resembling a heap of vermilion, on a charming stone surface of dāru wood,
fire without fuel shines there continually even today.

sanskrit_iast:
bhairavasya hitārthāya kāmākhyāparisevane |
pūrvameva sthitastatra sākṣād vahnirgaṇaiḥ saha || 10 ||
meaning:
भैरवस्य हितार्थाय कामाख्यापरिसेवने |
पूर्वमेव स्थितस्तत्र साक्षाद् वह्निर्गणैः सह || 10 ||
text_mt:
For the benefit of Bhairava, in attendance upon Kāmākhyā,
Fire was formerly situated there in person together with his hosts.

sanskrit_iast:
lauhityapāthasi snātvā tvagnimālāhvayaṃ girim |
āruhya vahniṃ sampūjya modate viṣṇumandire || 11 ||
meaning:
लौहित्यपाथसि स्नात्वा त्वग्निमालाह्वयं गिरिम् |
आरुह्य वह्निं सम्पूज्य मोदते विष्णुमन्दिरे || 11 ||
text_mt:
Having bathed in the water of the Lauhitya, climbing the mountain named Agnimālā
and worshipping Fire, one rejoices in the temple of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
purastādagnimālasya kuṇḍakaṃ vāruṇāhvayam |
tasya tīre giriśreṣṭho nāmnā kaṃsakaraḥ smṛtaḥ || 12 ||
meaning:
पुरस्तादग्निमालस्य कुण्डकं वारुणाह्वयम् |
तस्य तीरे गिरिश्रेष्ठो नाम्ना कंसकरः स्मृतः || 12 ||
text_mt:
In front of Agnimālā is a pool named Vāruṇa;
on its bank is the best of mountains, known by the name Kaṃsakara.

sanskrit_iast:
varuṇastatra vasati nityameva jalādhipaḥ |
tasmin kaṃsakare samyak pūjayitvā pracetasam || 13 ||
meaning:
वरुणस्तत्र वसति नित्यमेव जलाधिपः |
तस्मिन् कंसकरे सम्यक् पूजयित्वा प्रचेतसम् || 13 ||
text_mt:
Varuṇa, the lord of waters, dwells there perpetually.
Having properly worshipped Pracetas on that Kaṃsakara

sanskrit_iast:
snātvā ca vāruṇe kuṇḍe vāruṇaṃ lokamāpnuyāt |
ādyaṃ vyañjanamevātra pañcamasvarasaṃyutam || 14 ||
meaning:
स्नात्वा च वारुणे कुण्डे वारुणं लोकमाप्नुयात् |
आद्यं व्यञ्जनमेवात्र पञ्चमस्वरसंयुतम् || 14 ||
text_mt:
and having bathed in the Vāruṇa pool, one attains the world of Varuṇa.
The first consonant here, combined with the fifth vowel,

sanskrit_iast:
śambhucūḍāśikhāyuktaṃ kauveraṃ bījamucyate |
saptamo yaḥ pakārasya binduścandrārdhasaṃyutaḥ || 15 ||
meaning:
शम्भुचूडाशिखायुक्तं कौवेरं बीजमुच्यते |
सप्तमो यः पकारस्य बिन्दुश्चन्द्रार्धसंयुतः || 15 ||
text_mt:
joined with the crest of Śambhu's diadem, is declared to be the seed-syllable of Kubera.
The seventh [consonant] from the class of pa, with a dot and half-moon,

sanskrit_iast:
vahnibījamiti khyātaṃ tena vahni prapūjayet |
makārapañcamaḥ somabindunā vāruṇaḥ smṛtaḥ || 16 ||
meaning:
वह्निबीजमिति ख्यातं तेन वह्नि प्रपूजयेत् |
मकारपञ्चमः सोमबिन्दुना वारुणः स्मृतः || 16 ||
text_mt:
is renowned as the seed-syllable of Fire; with it one should worship Fire.
The fifth [consonant] from ma with a moon and dot is recalled as Varuṇa's [seed-syllable].

sanskrit_iast:
ebhirmantrairimān devān nityameva prapūjayet |
vāyukūṭo nāma giriḥ pūrvasyāṃ varuṇācalāt || 17 ||
meaning:
एभिर्मन्त्रैरिमान् देवान् नित्यमेव प्रपूजयेत् |
वायुकूटो नाम गिरिः पूर्वस्यां वरुणाचलात् || 17 ||
text_mt:
With these mantras one should continually worship these deities.
There is a mountain named Vāyukūṭa to the east of Varuṇa's mountain,

sanskrit_iast:
dvikhaṇḍo vāyubījena maṇḍalena samanvitaḥ |
vāyulokasthitaścandro yasmānniḥsṛtya mārutaḥ || 18 ||
meaning:
द्विखण्डो वायुबीजेन मण्डलेन समन्वितः |
वायुलोकस्थितश्चन्द्रो यस्मान्निःसृत्य मारुतः || 18 ||
text_mt:
divided into two, endowed with the wind-mandala bearing the seed-syllable of Wind,
where the moon situated in the world of Wind rests, from which the wind,

sanskrit_iast:
ūrdhvādhobhāgamāsādya nityaṃ vahati bhūpate |
tatra vāyuṃ samabhyarcya vāyulokamavāpnuyāt || 19 ||
meaning:
ऊर्ध्वाधोभागमासाद्य नित्यं वहति भूपते |
तत्र वायुं समभ्यर्च्य वायुलोकमवाप्नुयात् || 19 ||
text_mt:
reaching the upper and lower regions, blows continually, O protector of the earth.
Worshipping Wind there, one attains the world of Wind.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvaṃ vāyugireḥ śailaścandrakūṭa iti smṛtaḥ |
trikoṇaścandrasaṅkāśastadūrdhve candramaṇḍalam || 20 ||
meaning:
पूर्वं वायुगिरेः शैलश्चन्द्रकूट इति स्मृतः |
त्रिकोणश्चन्द्रसङ्काशस्तदूर्ध्वे चन्द्रमण्डलम् || 20 ||
text_mt:
East of Wind Mountain is the peak recalled as Candrakūṭa,
triangular, resembling the moon, and above it is the lunar orb.

sanskrit_iast:
dvitīyavargasyādyaṃ tu bindunā samalaṅkṛtam |
candrabījamiti proktaṃ tena candraṃ prapūjayet || 21 ||
meaning:
द्वितीयवर्गस्याद्यं तु बिन्दुना समलङ्कृतम् |
चन्द्रबीजमिति प्रोक्तं तेन चन्द्रं प्रपूजयेत् || 21 ||
text_mt:
The first [consonant] of the second class, adorned with a dot,
is declared as the seed-syllable of the Moon; with it one should worship the Moon.

sanskrit_iast:
adyāpi pratidarśe tu parvataṃ taṃ niśāpatiḥ |
pradakṣiṇīkarotyeva daśābhiścāpi khecaraiḥ || 22 ||
meaning:
अद्यापि प्रतिदर्शे तु पर्वतं तं निशापतिः |
प्रदक्षिणीकरोत्येव दशाभिश्चापि खेचरैः || 22 ||
text_mt:
Even today, on every new-moon day, the lord of the night
indeed circumambulates that mountain along with the ten sky-farers.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyaiva pūrvabhāge tu somakuṇḍāhvayaṃ saraḥ |
tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca naraḥ kaivalyamaśnute || 23 ||
meaning:
तस्यैव पूर्वभागे तु सोमकुण्डाह्वयं सरः |
तत्र स्नात्वा च पीत्वा च नरः कैवल्यमश्नुते || 23 ||
text_mt:
In its eastern part is the lake named Somakuṇḍa;
having bathed in it and drunk [from it], a person attains absolute liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
svargādavataraccandraḥ kāmākhyāsevane yadā |
tadā tadraśmisaṅghātānniḥsṛtāstoyarāśayaḥ || 24 ||
meaning:
स्वर्गादवतरच्चन्द्रः कामाख्यासेवने यदा |
तदा तद्रश्मिसङ्घातान्निःसृतास्तोयराशयः || 24 ||
text_mt:
When the Moon descended from heaven to attend upon Kāmākhyā,
then from the convergence of his rays masses of water poured forth.

sanskrit_iast:
taistoyairvāsavaḥ kuṇḍamakarodindracandrayoḥ |
madhye puṇyatame sthāne svayaṃ brahmaśilopari || 25 ||
meaning:
तैस्तोयैर्वासवः कुण्डमकरोदिन्द्रचन्द्रयोः |
मध्ये पुण्यतमे स्थाने स्वयं ब्रह्मशिलोपरि || 25 ||
text_mt:
With those waters Vāsava made a pool between Indra and Candra,
in the most sacred place, himself upon the rock of Brahmā.

sanskrit_iast:
candraraśmisamudbhuta candrakuṇdamahodadhe |
yaṃ yaṃ bhāvaṃ samāsādya tvaṃ candra kaluṣa hara || 26 ||
meaning:
चन्द्ररश्मिसमुद्भुत चन्द्रकुण्दमहोदधे |
यं यं भावं समासाद्य त्वं चन्द्र कलुष हर || 26 ||
text_mt:
‘O great ocean of the moon-pool, born from the rays of the moon,
whatever state he may attain, O moon, take away the blemish!

sanskrit_iast:
sudhāsravaṇamāhlāda tvaṃ candra kaluṣaṃ hara |
ityanena tu mantreṇa yaḥ snātvā candrapāthasi || 27 ||
meaning:
सुधास्रवणमाह्लाद त्वं चन्द्र कलुषं हर |
इत्यनेन तु मन्त्रेण यः स्नात्वा चन्द्रपाथसि || 27 ||
text_mt:
O flow of nectar, [source of] delight, O moon, take away the blemish!’
He who bathes in the water of Candra with this mantra,

sanskrit_iast:
candrakūṭaṃ samāruhya pūjayed yastu taṃ naraḥ |
avicchinnā santatistu sukāntā tasya jāyate || 28 ||
meaning:
चन्द्रकूटं समारुह्य पूजयेद् यस्तु तं नरः |
अविच्छिन्ना सन्ततिस्तु सुकान्ता तस्य जायते || 28 ||
text_mt:
and, having ascended Candrakūṭa, worships him,
his lineage becomes unbroken and lovely.

sanskrit_iast:
paratra candrabhavanaṃ bhittvā yāti paraṃ padam |
tīre tu candrakūṭasya nandano nāma vai giriḥ || 29 ||
meaning:
परत्र चन्द्रभवनं भित्त्वा याति परं पदम् |
तीरे तु चन्द्रकूटस्य नन्दनो नाम वै गिरिः || 29 ||
text_mt:
In the hereafter, piercing the realm of the moon, he goes to the highest abode.
On the bank of Candrakūṭa there is indeed a mountain named Nandana.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmin vasati śakrastu kāmākhyāsevane rataḥ |
pañcabhāvaṃ samāsādya sarvadeveśvaro hariḥ |
sevituṃ tridaśeśānīṃ satataṃ vartate naraḥ || 30 ||
meaning:
तस्मिन् वसति शक्रस्तु कामाख्यासेवने रतः |
पञ्चभावं समासाद्य सर्वदेवेश्वरो हरिः |
सेवितुं त्रिदशेशानीं सततं वर्तते नरः || 30 ||
text_mt:
On it dwells Śakra, devoted to serving Kāmākhyā.
Assuming the five states, Hari, the lord of all the gods,
always remains as a man to serve the ruler of the thirty [gods].

sanskrit_iast:
candrakūṭagireryāmyabhāge girijanārdanaḥ |
tasya yāmye tvadhobhāge aśvakrāntāhvayaṃ saraḥ || a ||
na tasya sadṛśaṃ tīrthamasti brahmāṇḍagocare |
jale sthale mṛtā ye'tra yānti brahma sanātanam || b ||
janārdanagirau viṣṇuḥ kūrmarūpasvarūpadhṛk |
śilāṁ bhittvā sthitastatra devagandharvasevitaḥ || c ||
meaning:
चन्द्रकूटगिरेर्याम्यभागे गिरिजनार्दनः |
तस्य याम्ये त्वधोभागे अश्वक्रान्ताह्वयं सरः || अ ||
न तस्य सदृशं तीर्थमस्ति ब्रह्माण्डगोचरे |
जले स्थले मृता येऽत्र यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् || ब् ||
जनार्दनगिरौ विष्णुः कूर्मरूपस्वरूपधृक् |
शिलाṁ भित्त्वा स्थितस्तत्र देवगन्धर्वसेवितः || च् ||

sanskrit_iast:
aśvakrāntajale snātvā pūjayitvā janārdanam |
vaṃśakoṭiṃ samuddhṛtya svayaṃ syāt puruṣottamaḥ || d ||
meaning:
अश्वक्रान्तजले स्नात्वा पूजयित्वा जनार्दनम् |
वंशकोटिं समुद्धृत्य स्वयं स्यात् पुरुषोत्तमः || द् ||
text_mt:
Having bathed in the waters of Aśvakrāntā and worshipped Janārdana,
he uplifts ten million [ancestors of his] lineage and becomes Puruṣottama himself.

sanskrit_iast:
candrakūṭasya tu girernandanasya tathā gireḥ |
pratidarśaṃ tathā candraḥ pradakṣiṇayati tridhā || 31 ||
meaning:
चन्द्रकूटस्य तु गिरेर्नन्दनस्य तथा गिरेः |
प्रतिदर्शं तथा चन्द्रः प्रदक्षिणयति त्रिधा || 31 ||
text_mt:
On every new moon, Candra circumambulates threefold
Mount Candrakūṭa and likewise Mount Nandana.

sanskrit_iast: candrakūṭajale snātvā samāruhyātha nandanam || 32 ||
meaning: चन्द्रकूटजले स्नात्वा समारुह्याथ नन्दनम् || 32 ||
text_mt: Having bathed in the waters of Candrakūṭa and then ascended Nandana,

sanskrit_iast:
ārādhya śakraṃ lokeśaṃ mahāphalamavāpuyāt |
nandanāt pūrvabhāge tu bhasmakūṭo mahāgiriḥ || 33 ||
meaning:
आराध्य शक्रं लोकेशं महाफलमवापुयात् |
नन्दनात् पूर्वभागे तु भस्मकूटो महागिरिः || 33 ||
text_mt:
and worshipped Śakra, the lord of the world, one would attain a great reward.
To the east of Nandana is the great mountain Bhasmakūṭa,

sanskrit_iast:
yaḥ svayaṃ bhargarūpaḥ sa sadā cecchāntamuttamam |
dakṣiṇe bhasmakūṭasya devī pīyūṣadhāriṇī || 34 ||
meaning:
यः स्वयं भर्गरूपः स सदा चेच्छान्तमुत्तमम् |
दक्षिणे भस्मकूटस्य देवी पीयूषधारिणी || 34 ||
text_mt:
which is Bharga's own form, ever most excellent and tranquil.
To the south of Bhasmakūṭa is the goddess who holds nectar,

sanskrit_iast:
urvaśī nāma vikhyātā śakraprītikarī sadā |
devairyat sthāpitaṃ pūrvamabhṛtaṃ bhojanāya vai || 35 ||
meaning:
उर्वशी नाम विख्याता शक्रप्रीतिकरी सदा |
देवैर्यत् स्थापितं पूर्वमभृतं भोजनाय वै || 35 ||
text_mt:
famed by the name of Urvaśī, who ever delights Śakra.
The nectar that was placed of old by the gods for their food,

sanskrit_iast:
kāmākhyāyāstadādāya svayaṃ tiṣṭhati corvaśī |
śilārūpo harastāṃ tu samāvṛtyaiva tiṣṭhati || 36 ||
meaning:
कामाख्यायास्तदादाय स्वयं तिष्ठति चोर्वशी |
शिलारूपो हरस्तां तु समावृत्यैव तिष्ठति || 36 ||
text_mt:
Urvaśī herself stands taking it for Kāmākhyā,
and Hara, in the form of a rock, remains surrounding her.

sanskrit_iast:
sā caivāmṛtarāśiṃ tu kṛtvā kiṃcana kiṃcana |
upasthāpayate nityaṃ kāmākhyāyonimaṇḍale || 37 ||
meaning:
सा चैवामृतराशिं तु कृत्वा किंचन किंचन |
उपस्थापयते नित्यं कामाख्यायोनिमण्डले || 37 ||
text_mt:
And taking a little of that mass of nectar again and again,
she continually offers it in the vulva-circle of Kāmākhyā.

sanskrit_iast:
sudhāśilāntarasthā tu urvaśīkuṇḍavāsinī |
urvaśībhasmakūṭasya madhye kuṇḍaṃ sadāvṛtam || 38 ||
meaning:
सुधाशिलान्तरस्था तु उर्वशीकुण्डवासिनी |
उर्वशीभस्मकूटस्य मध्ये कुण्डं सदावृतम् || 38 ||
text_mt:
Dwelling within the nectar-rock, Urvaśī resides in the pool;
between Urvaśī and Bhasmakūṭa the pool is always enclosed,

sanskrit_iast:
dvātriṃśaddhanurākīrṇaṃ pañcāśaddhanurāyatam |
tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca narā mokṣamavāpnuyāt || 39 ||
meaning:
द्वात्रिंशद्धनुराकीर्णं पञ्चाशद्धनुरायतम् |
तत्र स्नात्वा च पीत्वा च नरा मोक्षमवाप्नुयात् || 39 ||
text_mt:
thirty-two bows wide and fifty bows long.
Having bathed there and drunk [its water], a man attains liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
kāmākhyāyoniraiśānīṃ diśaṃ yāti sadaiva hi |
bhasmakūṭe praviśati urvaśīmapi yoginī || 40 ||
meaning:
कामाख्यायोनिरैशानीं दिशं याति सदैव हि |
भस्मकूटे प्रविशति उर्वशीमपि योगिनी || 40 ||
text_mt:
The vulva of Kāmākhyā always reaches into the north-eastern direction;
she enters into Bhasmakūṭa and also Urvaśī, the yoginī.

sanskrit_iast:
āpyāyitā cāmṛtena nityaṃ devī pramodate |
modayuktā mahādevī kāmena modate sadā || 41 ||
meaning:
आप्यायिता चामृतेन नित्यं देवी प्रमोदते |
मोदयुक्ता महादेवी कामेन मोदते सदा || 41 ||
text_mt:
Replenished with nectar, the goddess constantly rejoices;
filled with joy, the great goddess ever delights with Kāma.

sanskrit_iast:
bhasmakūṭasya caiśānyāṃ maṇikūṭo mahāgiriḥ |
maṇikarṇo nāma harastatra tiṣṭhati liṅgakam || 42 ||
meaning:
भस्मकूटस्य चैशान्यां मणिकूटो महागिरिः |
मणिकर्णो नाम हरस्तत्र तिष्ठति लिङ्गकम् || 42 ||
text_mt:
To the north-east of Bhasmakūṭa is the great mountain Maṇikūṭa;
there stands the liṅga of Hara named Maṇikarṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
sa sadyojātarūpastu maṇikarṇa itīritaḥ |
sadyojātasya mantreṇa pūjitavyaḥ sadāśivaḥ || 43 ||
meaning:
स सद्योजातरूपस्तु मणिकर्ण इतीरितः |
सद्योजातस्य मन्त्रेण पूजितव्यः सदाशिवः || 43 ||
text_mt:
That Maṇikarṇa is declared to have the form of Sadyojāta;
Sadāśiva is to be worshipped with the mantra of Sadyojāta.

sanskrit_iast:
candratīrthajale snātvā dṛṣṭvā candraṃ savāsavam |
maṇikarṇeśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā muktirbhasmācalaṃ gate || 44 ||
meaning:
चन्द्रतीर्थजले स्नात्वा दृष्ट्वा चन्द्रं सवासवम् |
मणिकर्णेश्वरं दृष्ट्वा मुक्तिर्भस्माचलं गते || 44 ||
text_mt:
Having bathed in the waters of the Candratīrtha and seen Candra along with Vāsava,
and having seen Maṇikarṇeśvara, liberation [is attained] when one has gone to the mountain of ashes.

sanskrit_iast:
śvetaḥ śvetāmbaradharo daśāśvo hemabhūṣitaḥ |
gadāpāṇirdvibāhuśca kartavyo baradaḥ śaśī || 45 ||
meaning:
श्वेतः श्वेताम्बरधरो दशाश्वो हेमभूषितः |
गदापाणिर्द्विबाहुश्च कर्तव्यो बरदः शशी || 45 ||
text_mt:
White, wearing white garments, with ten horses, adorned with gold,
holding a mace, two-armed and bestowing boons should Śaśin be made.

sanskrit_iast:
sahasranetro gaurāṅgo dvibhujo vāmahastagam |
vajraṃ gadāṃkuśaṃ dhatte dakṣiṇenāpi pāṇinā || 46 ||
meaning:
सहस्रनेत्रो गौराङ्गो द्विभुजो वामहस्तगम् |
वज्रं गदांकुशं धत्ते दक्षिणेनापि पाणिना || 46 ||
text_mt:
He is thousand-eyed, fair-limbed, two-armed; in his left hand
he holds a vajra, and with his right hand a mace and a goad.

sanskrit_iast:
airāvatagajasthastu bāṇatūṇīrabandhanaḥ |
dhanuśca kakṣe gṛhṇāti sevamāno maheśvarīm || 47 ||
meaning:
ऐरावतगजस्थस्तु बाणतूणीरबन्धनः |
धनुश्च कक्षे गृह्णाति सेवमानो महेश्वरीम् || 47 ||
text_mt:
Mounted on the elephant Airāvata, his arrows and quiver fastened,
he holds a bow at his side, serving Maheśvarī.

sanskrit_iast:
vakārānantaro varṇaścandrabindusamanvitaḥ |
śakrabījamiti proktaṃ śakraṃ tena prapūjayet || 48 ||
meaning:
वकारानन्तरो वर्णश्चन्द्रबिन्दुसमन्वितः |
शक्रबीजमिति प्रोक्तं शक्रं तेन प्रपूजयेत् || 48 ||
text_mt:
The syllable after the letter ‘va’, accompanied by the crescent and dot,
is declared to be the seed-syllable of Śakra; one should worship Śakra with it.

sanskrit_iast:
nadī sumaṅgalā nāma himaparvatanirgatā |
pūrvasyāṃ maṇikūṭasya sadā sravati śobhanā || 49 ||
meaning:
नदी सुमङ्गला नाम हिमपर्वतनिर्गता |
पूर्वस्यां मणिकूटस्य सदा स्रवति शोभना || 49 ||
text_mt:
A river named Sumaṅgalā, flowing forth from the mountain of snow,
flows always auspicious to the east of Maṇikūṭa.

sanskrit_iast:
maṇikūṭaṃ samāruhya yastāṃ paśyati vai nadīm |
sa gaṅgāsnānajaṃ puṇyamavāpya tridivaṃ vrajet || 50 ||
meaning:
मणिकूटं समारुह्य यस्तां पश्यति वै नदीम् |
स गङ्गास्नानजं पुण्यमवाप्य त्रिदिवं व्रजेत् || 50 ||
text_mt:
Ascending Maṇikūṭa, he who gazes upon that river
attains the merit born of bathing in the Gaṅgā and goes to heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
maṇikūṭācalāt pūrvaṃ matsyadhvajakulācalaḥ |
nirdagdho yatra madano haranetrāgninā punaḥ || 51 ||
meaning:
मणिकूटाचलात् पूर्वं मत्स्यध्वजकुलाचलः |
निर्दग्धो यत्र मदनो हरनेत्राग्निना पुनः || 51 ||
text_mt:
To the east of Mount Maṇikūṭa is the ancestral mountain Matsyadhvaja,
where Madana, having been burnt again by the fire of Hara's eye,

sanskrit_iast:
śarīraṃ prāpa tapasā samārādhya vṛṣadhvajam |
tatra matsyasvarūpastu kāmadeva samaṃsthita || 52 ||
meaning:
शरीरं प्राप तपसा समाराध्य वृषध्वजम् |
तत्र मत्स्यस्वरूपस्तु कामदेव समंस्थित || 52 ||
text_mt:
obtained a body through austerity by propitiating Vṛṣadhvaja.
There, having assumed the form of a fish, Kāmadeva settled,

sanskrit_iast:
adhityakāyāṃ pṛthivīṃ bīkṣamāṇaḥ samantataḥ |
nadī tu śāśvatī nāma tatrāste dakṣiṇasravā || 53 ||
meaning:
अधित्यकायां पृथिवीं बीक्षमाणः समन्ततः |
नदी तु शाश्वती नाम तत्रास्ते दक्षिणस्रवा || 53 ||
text_mt:
gazing all around at the earth on the plateau.
A river named Śāśvatī is there, flowing southward.

sanskrit_iast:
saraḥ kāmasaro nāma tatra śaile vyavasthitam |
śāśvatyāṃ vidhivatsnātvā pītvā āmasaro'mbhasi || 54 ||
meaning:
सरः कामसरो नाम तत्र शैले व्यवस्थितम् |
शाश्वत्यां विधिवत्स्नात्वा पीत्वा आमसरोऽम्भसि || 54 ||
text_mt:
A pool named Kāmasaras is situated on that mountain.
Having bathed according to rule in the Śāśvatī and drunk the water of Kāmasaras,

sanskrit_iast:
bimuktapāpaḥ śuddhātmā śivaloke mahīyate |
gandhamādanapūrvasyāṃ sukrānto nāma parvataḥ || 55 ||
meaning:
बिमुक्तपापः शुद्धात्मा शिवलोके महीयते |
गन्धमादनपूर्वस्यां सुक्रान्तो नाम पर्वतः || 55 ||
text_mt:
freed from sin, pure in self, he is exalted in the realm of Śiva.
To the east of Gandhamādana is the mountain named Sukrānta.

sanskrit_iast:
tatprānte vāsavaṃ kuṇḍaṃ vāsavāmṛtabhojanam |
yatra sthitvā dakṣiṇasyāṃ purā śakraḥ śacīpatiḥ || 56 ||
meaning:
तत्प्रान्ते वासवं कुण्डं वासवामृतभोजनम् |
यत्र स्थित्वा दक्षिणस्यां पुरा शक्रः शचीपतिः || 56 ||
text_mt:
At its edge is the pool of Vāsava, where Vāsava fed on nectar,
where in ancient times Śakra, husband of Śacī, standing in the south,

sanskrit_iast:
amṛtaṃ śrāntadehastu kāmarūpāntare papau |
snātvā tu vāsave kuṇḍe samāruhya sukāntakam || 57 ||
meaning:
अमृतं श्रान्तदेहस्तु कामरूपान्तरे पपौ |
स्नात्वा तु वासवे कुण्डे समारुह्य सुकान्तकम् || 57 ||
text_mt:
weary in body, drank the nectar within Kāmarūpa.
Having bathed in the pool of Vāsava and ascended Sukāntaka,

sanskrit_iast:
vāsavasya priyo bhūtvā śakralokamavāpnuyāt |
pūrvasyāṃ tu sukāntasya rakṣaḥkūṭāhvayo giriḥ || 58 ||
meaning:
वासवस्य प्रियो भूत्वा शक्रलोकमवाप्नुयात् |
पूर्वस्यां तु सुकान्तस्य रक्षःकूटाह्वयो गिरिः || 58 ||
text_mt:
becoming dear to Vāsava, he attains the realm of Śakra.
To the east of Sukānta is the mountain named Rakṣaḥkūṭa,

sanskrit_iast:
yatrāste satataṃ devo nir-ṛtī rākṣaseśvaraḥ |
khaḍgahasto mahākāyo vāme carmadharastathā || 59 ||
meaning:
यत्रास्ते सततं देवो निर्-ऋती राक्षसेश्वरः |
खड्गहस्तो महाकायो वामे चर्मधरस्तथा || 59 ||
text_mt:
where constantly resides the god Nirṛti, the lord of the rākṣasas,
with a sword in hand, gigantic in body, and holding a shield in his left [hand],

sanskrit_iast:
jaṭājūṭasamāyuktaḥ prāṃśuḥ kṛṣṇācalopamaḥ |
dvibhujaḥ kṛṣṇavāsāstu gardabhoparisaṃsthitaḥ || 60 ||
meaning:
जटाजूटसमायुक्तः प्रांशुः कृष्णाचलोपमः |
द्विभुजः कृष्णवासास्तु गर्दभोपरिसंस्थितः || 60 ||
text_mt:
endowed with matted locks, tall, resembling a black mountain,
two-armed, dressed in black garments, mounted upon an ass.

sanskrit_iast:
prāntopāntau binducandrasahitāvādireva ca |
nair-ṛtyaṃ kathitaṃ bījaṃ tena taṃ paripūjayet || 61 ||
meaning:
प्रान्तोपान्तौ बिन्दुचन्द्रसहितावादिरेव च |
नैर्-ऋत्यं कथितं बीजं तेन तं परिपूजयेत् || 61 ||
text_mt:
The initial along with the penult and the final [vowels], with dot and crescent,
is declared to be the seed-syllable of Nairṛta; with it one should worship him.

sanskrit_iast:
rakṣaḥkūṭaṃ samāruhya ni-ṛtiṃ rākṣaseśvaram |
yaḥ pūjayed vidhānena caṇḍikāṃ rākṣaseśvarīm || 62 ||
meaning:
रक्षःकूटं समारुह्य नि-ऋतिं राक्षसेश्वरम् |
यः पूजयेद् विधानेन चण्डिकां राक्षसेश्वरीम् || 62 ||
text_mt:
Having ascended Rakṣaḥkūṭa, he who worships Nirṛti, the lord of rākṣasas,
and Caṇḍikā, the queen of rākṣasas, according to the rule,

sanskrit_iast:
na tasya rākṣasebhyo'sti bhayaṃ nṛpa kadācana |
rākṣasāśca piśācāśca vetālā gaṇanāyakāḥ || 63 ||
meaning:
न तस्य राक्षसेभ्योऽस्ति भयं नृप कदाचन |
राक्षसाश्च पिशाचाश्च वेताला गणनायकाः || 63 ||
text_mt:
he has no fear from rākṣasas at any time, O king.
Rākṣasas, piśācas, vetālas, and troop-leaders,

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā puruṣaṃ rājan sarvadaiva prabibhyati |
rakṣaḥkūṭāt pūrvadiśi bhairava nāma mādhavaḥ || 64 ||
meaning:
तं दृष्ट्वा पुरुषं राजन् सर्वदैव प्रबिभ्यति |
रक्षःकूटात् पूर्वदिशि भैरव नाम माधवः || 64 ||
text_mt:
seeing that man, O king, are always afraid.
To the east of Rakṣaḥkūṭa is Mādhava named Bhairava,

sanskrit_iast:
pāṇḍunātha iti khyāto grāvarūpeṇa saṃsthitaḥ |
taṃ pāṇḍunāthaṃ satatamaṣṭākṣarabhavottaram || 65 ||
meaning:
पाण्डुनाथ इति ख्यातो ग्रावरूपेण संस्थितः |
तं पाण्डुनाथं सततमष्टाक्षरभवोत्तरम् || 65 ||
text_mt:
famed as Pāṇḍunātha, residing in the form of a rock.
That Pāṇḍunātha [one should worship] constantly, excellent through the eight-syllable [mantra].

sanskrit_iast:
tenaiva pūjayed devaṃ pāṇḍunāthāhvayaṃ harim |
varṇena raktagaurāṅgaṃ gadāpadmadharaṃ kare || 66 ||
meaning:
तेनैव पूजयेद् देवं पाण्डुनाथाह्वयं हरिम् |
वर्णेन रक्तगौराङ्गं गदापद्मधरं करे || 66 ||
text_mt:
With that very [mantra] one should worship the god Hari called Pāṇḍunātha,
whose body is reddish-white in complexion, holding a mace and a lotus in his hands,

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣiṇe cakraśaktī ca bāhubhyāmapi bibhratam |
caturbhujaṃ raktapadmasaṃsthitaṃ mukuṭojjvalam || 67 ||
meaning:
दक्षिणे चक्रशक्ती च बाहुभ्यामपि बिभ्रतम् |
चतुर्भुजं रक्तपद्मसंस्थितं मुकुटोज्ज्वलम् || 67 ||
text_mt:
and holding a discus and spear with his right arms,
four-armed, seated on a red lotus, radiant with a diadem,

sanskrit_iast:
kuṇḍale bibhrataṃ śuddhe śrīvatsoraskamuttamam |
namo nārāyaṇāyeti mūlabījena vā hareḥ || 68 ||
meaning:
कुण्डले बिभ्रतं शुद्धे श्रीवत्सोरस्कमुत्तमम् |
नमो नारायणायेति मूलबीजेन वा हरेः || 68 ||
text_mt:
wearing pure earrings, marked on his chest with the excellent Śrīvatsa;
or with the root seed-syllable of Hari: "Oṃ namo Nārāyaṇāya."

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ sampūjayed bhūpa caturvargasya siddhaye |
pāṇḍunāthasyottarasyāṃ brahmakūṭāhvayaṃ saraḥ || 69 ||
meaning:
एवं सम्पूजयेद् भूप चतुर्वर्गस्य सिद्धये |
पाण्डुनाथस्योत्तरस्यां ब्रह्मकूटाह्वयं सरः || 69 ||
text_mt:
Thus one should worship him, O king, for the attainment of the four goals of life.
To the north of Pāṇḍunātha is the lake called Brahmakūṭa,

sanskrit_iast:
brahmaṇā nirmitaṃ pūrvaṃ snānārthaṃ svargavāsinām |
āyāmena śatavyāmaṃ vistīrṇaṃ tvatadardhakam || 70 ||
meaning:
ब्रह्मणा निर्मितं पूर्वं स्नानार्थं स्वर्गवासिनाम् |
आयामेन शतव्यामं विस्तीर्णं त्वतदर्धकम् || 70 ||
text_mt:
created of old by Brahmā for the bathing of heaven-dwellers,
a hundred vyāmas in length and half of that in width,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ devalokāt samāgatam |
kamaṇḍalusamudbhūta brahmakuṇḍāmṛtasrava || 71 ||
meaning:
सर्वपापहरं पुण्यं देवलोकात् समागतम् |
कमण्डलुसमुद्भूत ब्रह्मकुण्डामृतस्रव || 71 ||
text_mt:
destroying all sins, holy, having descended from the world of the gods.
"O you who arose from the water-pot, flowing with the nectar of Brahmakuṇḍa,

sanskrit_iast:
hara me sarvapāpāni puṇyaṃ svargaṃ ca sādhaya |
ityanena tu mantreṇa snātvā tasmin sarojale || 72 ||
meaning:
हर मे सर्वपापानि पुण्यं स्वर्गं च साधय |
इत्यनेन तु मन्त्रेण स्नात्वा तस्मिन् सरोजले || 72 ||
text_mt:
remove all my sins, and secure [for me] merit and heaven!"
Having bathed in the waters of that lake with this mantra,

sanskrit_iast:
pāṇḍunāthaṃ ca sampūjya viṣṇusāyujyamāpnuyāt |
brahmakuṇḍajale snātvā pūjayitvā umāpatim || 73 ||
meaning:
पाण्डुनाथं च सम्पूज्य विष्णुसायुज्यमाप्नुयात् |
ब्रह्मकुण्डजले स्नात्वा पूजयित्वा उमापतिम् || 73 ||
text_mt:
and having worshipped Pāṇḍunātha, one attains union with Viṣṇu.
Having bathed in the waters of Brahmakuṇḍa and worshipped the lord of Umā,

sanskrit_iast:
vāyukūṭaṃ samāruhya muktimevāpnuyānnaraḥ |
pāṇḍunāthāt pūrvadiśi giriścitraharo hariḥ || 74 ||
meaning:
वायुकूटं समारुह्य मुक्तिमेवाप्नुयान्नरः |
पाण्डुनाथात् पूर्वदिशि गिरिश्चित्रहरो हरिः || 74 ||
text_mt:
having climbed Vāyukūṭa, a man certainly attains liberation.
To the east of Pāṇḍunātha is the mountain Citrahara, which is Hari,

sanskrit_iast:
satataṃ yatra ramate viṣṇurvārāharūpadhṛk |
tatastu nīlakūṭākhyaṃ kāmākhyānilayaṃ param || 75 ||
meaning:
सततं यत्र रमते विष्णुर्वाराहरूपधृक् |
ततस्तु नीलकूटाख्यं कामाख्यानिलयं परम् || 75 ||
text_mt:
where Viṣṇu, assuming the form of the Boar, ever delights.
Then there is the supreme abode of Kāmākhyā called Nīlakūṭa.

sanskrit_iast:
tatpūrvabhāge vasati brahmā brahmagiriḥ punaḥ |
brahmaśailasya pūrvasyāṃ bhūmipīṭhe vyavasthitam || 76 ||
meaning:
तत्पूर्वभागे वसति ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मगिरिः पुनः |
ब्रह्मशैलस्य पूर्वस्यां भूमिपीठे व्यवस्थितम् || 76 ||
text_mt:
In its eastern part Brahmā dwells, being the mountain Brahmagiri.
To the east of the mountain of Brahmā, situated on the ground-pīṭha,

sanskrit_iast:
cārunimnaśubhāvartaṃ kāmākhyānābhimaṇḍalam |
atrogratārārūpeṇa ramate parameśvarī || 77 ||
meaning:
चारुनिम्नशुभावर्तं कामाख्यानाभिमण्डलम् |
अत्रोग्रतारारूपेण रमते परमेश्वरी || 77 ||
text_mt:
is the navel-circle of Kāmākhyā, lovely, low, and auspiciously swirling.
Here the supreme goddess sports in the form of Ugratārā.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra tenaiva rūpeṇa pūjitavyā śubhātmikā |
tasyāstu bījaṃ pūrvasminnuttare pratipāditam || 78 ||
meaning:
तत्र तेनैव रूपेण पूजितव्या शुभात्मिका |
तस्यास्तु बीजं पूर्वस्मिन्नुत्तरे प्रतिपादितम् || 78 ||
text_mt:
There she, whose nature is auspicious, is to be worshipped in that very form.
Her seed-syllable was set forth earlier, in the north.

sanskrit_iast:
rūpaṃ śṛṇu naraśreṣṭha yena dhyeyā sadā śivā |
kṛṣṇā lambodarī dīrghā viralā raktadantikā || 79 ||
meaning:
रूपं शृणु नरश्रेष्ठ येन ध्येया सदा शिवा |
कृष्णा लम्बोदरी दीर्घा विरला रक्तदन्तिका || 79 ||
text_mt:
Hear her form, O best of men, in which the auspicious goddess is ever to be meditated upon:
black, pot-bellied, tall, with sparse red teeth,

sanskrit_iast:
caturbhujā kṛśāṅgī tu dakṣiṇe kartṛkharparau |
khaḍgaṃ cendīvaraṃ vāme śīrṣe caikajaṭā punaḥ || 80 ||
meaning:
चतुर्भुजा कृशाङ्गी तु दक्षिणे कर्तृखर्परौ |
खड्गं चेन्दीवरं वामे शीर्षे चैकजटा पुनः || 80 ||
text_mt:
four-armed, slender-bodied, with a chopper and a skull-bowl in her right [hands],
and a sword and a blue lotus in her left, having a single matted lock on her head,

sanskrit_iast:
vāmapādaṃ śavasyorvornidhāyāṅghriṃ tu dakṣiṇām |
śavasya hṛdaye nyasya sāṭṭahāsaṃ prakurvatī || 81 ||
meaning:
वामपादं शवस्योर्वोर्निधायाङ्घ्रिं तु दक्षिणाम् |
शवस्य हृदये न्यस्य साट्टहासं प्रकुर्वती || 81 ||
text_mt:
placing her left foot on the thighs of a corpse and resting her right foot
upon the chest of the corpse, uttering a loud, mocking laugh,

sanskrit_iast:
nāgahāraśiromālābhūṣitā kāmadā parā |
trikoṇaṃ maṇḍalaṃ cāsyā huṅkāraṃ madhyabījakām || 82 ||
meaning:
नागहारशिरोमालाभूषिता कामदा परा |
त्रिकोणं मण्डलं चास्या हुङ्कारं मध्यबीजकाम् || 82 ||
text_mt:
adorned with a necklace of snakes and a garland of heads, the supreme bestower of desires;
her maṇḍala is a triangle, with the syllable huṃ as its central seed.

sanskrit_iast:
dvāreśānāṃ yoginīnāṃ nāmānyasyāstu tantrake |
jñeyāni naraśārdūla yat proktaṃ vāmyagocare || 83 ||
meaning:
द्वारेशानां योगिनीनां नामान्यस्यास्तु तन्त्रके |
ज्ञेयानि नरशार्दूल यत् प्रोक्तं वाम्यगोचरे || 83 ||
text_mt:
The names of the guardian yoginīs of her doors are to be known from her tantra,
O tiger among men, as proclaimed in the left-hand tradition.

sanskrit_iast:
urvaśyāṃ vidhivat snātvā spṛṣṭvā pāṇḍuśilāṃ tathā |
nīlakūṭaṃ samāruhya punaryonau na jāyate || 84 ||
meaning:
उर्वश्यां विधिवत् स्नात्वा स्पृष्ट्वा पाण्डुशिलां तथा |
नीलकूटं समारुह्य पुनर्योनौ न जायते || 84 ||
text_mt:
Having bathed according to rule in Urvaśī, and having touched the stone Pāṇḍuśilā,
and ascended Nīlakūṭa, one is not born again in a womb.

sanskrit_iast:
purandarapurāyāte vārāṇasyāḥ halādhike |
sudhāsaṃkīrṇatoyaughaiḥ pāpa hara mamorvaśi || 85 ||
meaning:
पुरन्दरपुरायाते वाराणस्याः हलाधिके |
सुधासंकीर्णतोयौघैः पाप हर ममोर्वशि || 85 ||
text_mt:
"O you who have come from Indra's city, who are superior in plough-power to Vārāṇasī,
remove my sin, O Urvaśī, with your streams of water mingled with nectar!

sanskrit_iast:
amṛtasrāviṇī devī sudhaughaparipūraṇī |
amṛtenāmṛtaṃ me'dya dehi devi mamorvaśi || 86 ||
meaning:
अमृतस्राविणी देवी सुधौघपरिपूरणी |
अमृतेनामृतं मेऽद्य देहि देवि ममोर्वशि || 86 ||
text_mt:
O goddess flowing with nectar, brimming with a flood of ambrosia,
grant me immortality today with your nectar, O goddess, my Urvaśī!

sanskrit_iast:
purandarapriye devi vārāṇasyāḥ sadāmdhike |
lohityahradasaṃkīrṇe pāpaṃ hara manorvaśi || 87 ||
meaning:
पुरन्दरप्रिये देवि वाराणस्याः सदाम्धिके |
लोहित्यह्रदसंकीर्णे पापं हर मनोर्वशि || 87 ||
text_mt:
O goddess beloved of Indra, ever superior to Vārāṇasī,
mingled with the lake of the Lauhitya, remove my sin, O Urvaśī!"

sanskrit_iast:
ityebhiḥ stutibhirmantraiḥ snātvā puṇyorvaśījale |
sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇuloke viceṣṭate || 88 ||
meaning:
इत्येभिः स्तुतिभिर्मन्त्रैः स्नात्वा पुण्योर्वशीजले |
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो विष्णुलोके विचेष्टते || 88 ||
text_mt:
Having bathed with these mantras of praise in the holy water of Urvaśī,
freed from all sins, one disports in the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
urvaśī dvibhujā proktā svarṇakaṅkaṇadhāriṇī |
sauvarṇapātramamṛtasrāvaṇāya bibharti ca || 89 ||
meaning:
उर्वशी द्विभुजा प्रोक्ता स्वर्णकङ्कणधारिणी |
सौवर्णपात्रममृतस्रावणाय बिभर्ति च || 89 ||
text_mt:
Urvaśī is declared to be two-armed, wearing golden bracelets,
and holding a golden vessel for pouring out nectar,

sanskrit_iast:
śuklavastrā gauravarṇā pīnonnatapayodharā |
sarvāṅgasundarī śuddhā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā || 90 ||
meaning:
शुक्लवस्त्रा गौरवर्णा पीनोन्नतपयोधरा |
सर्वाङ्गसुन्दरी शुद्धा सर्वाभरणभूषिता || 90 ||
text_mt:
clothed in white garments, fair-complexioned, with plump and elevated breasts,
beautiful in all her limbs, pure, adorned with all ornaments.

sanskrit_iast:
etannāmādyakṣaraṃ tu mantramasyāḥ prakīrtitam |
umātantre tu gaditaṃ mantramasyāḥ prakīrtitam || 91 ||
meaning:
एतन्नामाद्यक्षरं तु मन्त्रमस्याः प्रकीर्तितम् |
उमातन्त्रे तु गदितं मन्त्रमस्याः प्रकीर्तितम् || 91 ||
text_mt:
The first letter of this name is proclaimed to be her mantra;
her proclaimed mantra was also declared in the Umātantra.

sanskrit_iast:
gaṇeśaḥ pūrvadvārasthaḥ kāmākhyāparvatasya tu |
tatraiva cāgnivetālaḥ sthito dvāri manoharaḥ || 92 ||
meaning:
गणेशः पूर्वद्वारस्थः कामाख्यापर्वतस्य तु |
तत्रैव चाग्निवेतालः स्थितो द्वारि मनोहरः || 92 ||
text_mt:
Gaṇeśa stands at the eastern gate of the mountain of Kāmākhyā;
and right there at the gate stands the charming Agnivetāla.

sanskrit_iast:
tayo rūpaṃ ca mantraṃ ca yathoktaṃ śambhunā purā |
tadahaṃ prativakṣyāmi mahārāja śṛṇuṣva me || 93 ||
meaning:
तयो रूपं च मन्त्रं च यथोक्तं शम्भुना पुरा |
तदहं प्रतिवक्ष्यामि महाराज शृणुष्व मे || 93 ||
text_mt:
Their form and mantra as told of old by Śambhu,
that I shall declare in turn; listen to me, O great king.

sanskrit_iast:
oṃ nama ulkāmukhāyeti mūlabījādisaṅgatam |
mantraṃ siddhagaṇeśasya dvārasthasya prakīrtitam || 94 ||
meaning:
ओं नम उल्कामुखायेति मूलबीजादिसङ्गतम् |
मन्त्रं सिद्धगणेशस्य द्वारस्थस्य प्रकीर्तितम् || 94 ||
text_mt:
"Oṃ, homage to Ulkāmukha"—combined with the primary seed-syllables and the rest—
is proclaimed to be the mantra of the Siddha-Gaṇeśa standing at the gate.

sanskrit_iast:
rūpaṃ tasya pravakṣyāmi gajavaktraṃ trilocanam |
lambodaraṃ caturbāhuṃ vyālayajñopavītinam || 95 ||
meaning:
रूपं तस्य प्रवक्ष्यामि गजवक्त्रं त्रिलोचनम् |
लम्बोदरं चतुर्बाहुं व्यालयज्ञोपवीतिनम् || 95 ||
text_mt:
I shall describe his form: elephant-faced, three-eyed,
pot-bellied, four-armed, wearing a serpent as a sacred thread,

sanskrit_iast:
śūrpakarṇa bṛhadgaṇḍamekadantaṃ pṛthūdaram |
dakṣiṇe tu kare daṇḍamutpalaṃ ca tathāpare || 96 ||
meaning:
शूर्पकर्ण बृहद्गण्डमेकदन्तं पृथूदरम् |
दक्षिणे तु करे दण्डमुत्पलं च तथापरे || 96 ||
text_mt:
with winnowing-basket ears, large cheeks, one tusk, and a broad belly;
in his right hand a staff, and in the other an utpala lotus;

sanskrit_iast:
laḍḍukaṃ paraśuṃ caiva vāmataḥ parikīrtitam |
bṛhattvākṣiptagaganaṃ pīnaskandhāṅghripāṇinam || 97 ||
meaning:
लड्डुकं परशुं चैव वामतः परिकीर्तितम् |
बृहत्त्वाक्षिप्तगगनं पीनस्कन्धाङ्घ्रिपाणिनम् || 97 ||
text_mt:
a sweetmeat and an axe are celebrated on his left side;
touching the sky by his vastness, with stout shoulders, feet, and hands,

sanskrit_iast:
yuktaṃ buddhikubuddhibhyāmadhastānmūṣakānvitam |
antrastu yādṛśaḥ proktaḥ pañcavaktrasya pūjane || 98 ||
meaning:
युक्तं बुद्धिकुबुद्धिभ्यामधस्तान्मूषकान्वितम् |
अन्त्रस्तु यादृशः प्रोक्तः पञ्चवक्त्रस्य पूजने || 98 ||
text_mt:
accompanied by Buddhi and Kubuddhi, attended by a mouse below.
As for the tantra that is prescribed for the worship of the Five-Faced One,

sanskrit_iast:
sa eva tantro grāhyastu tādṛgvidhiniṣedhanam |
dvibhujaḥ pīnavadano raktanetro bhayaṅkaraḥ || 99 ||
meaning:
स एव तन्त्रो ग्राह्यस्तु तादृग्विधिनिषेधनम् |
द्विभुजः पीनवदनो रक्तनेत्रो भयङ्करः || 99 ||
text_mt:
that very tantra is to be adopted, along with such rules and prohibitions.
[Agnivetāla] is two-armed, with a bloated face, red-eyed, terrifying,

sanskrit_iast:
churikāṃ dakṣiṇe pāṇau vāme rudhirapātrakam |
daṃṣṭrākarālavadanaṃ kṛśo dhamanisantataḥ || 100 ||
meaning:
छुरिकां दक्षिणे पाणौ वामे रुधिरपात्रकम् |
दंष्ट्राकरालवदनं कृशो धमनिसन्ततः || 100 ||
text_mt:
with a dagger in his right hand and a bowl of blood in his left,
with a face dreadful with fangs, emaciated, covered with a network of veins,

sanskrit_iast:
jaṭāṃ dīrghāṃ mūrdhni bibhradghorarāvayutastathā |
pacaturtho'gnibījena ṣaṣṭhasvaravibhūṣitaḥ || 101 ||
meaning:
जटां दीर्घां मूर्ध्नि बिभ्रद्घोररावयुतस्तथा |
पचतुर्थोऽग्निबीजेन षष्ठस्वरविभूषितः || 101 ||
text_mt:
bearing a long matted lock on his head, and uttering terrible roars.
The fourth [consonant] from pa, adorned with the seed of fire and the sixth vowel,

sanskrit_iast:
agnivetālabījo'yaṃ sarvatra bhayanāśakaḥ |
pūjayedagnivetālaṃ sarvatra bhayavāraṇam || 102 ||
meaning:
अग्निवेतालबीजोऽयं सर्वत्र भयनाशकः |
पूजयेदग्निवेतालं सर्वत्र भयवारणम् || 102 ||
text_mt:
is this seed-syllable of Agnivetāla, which destroys fear everywhere.
One should worship Agnivetāla, the warder-off of fear everywhere;

sanskrit_iast:
yaḥ pūjayet tasya punarbhūtādibhyo bhayaṃ nahi |
aṣṭānāmatha mantrāṇāṃ yoginīnāṃ kramannṛpa || 103 ||
meaning:
यः पूजयेत् तस्य पुनर्भूतादिभ्यो भयं नहि |
अष्टानामथ मन्त्राणां योगिनीनां क्रमन्नृप || 103 ||
text_mt:
for whoever worships him, there is no fear from ghosts and the like.
Now, O king, in the sequence of the eight mantras of the yoginīs,

sanskrit_iast:
śailaputrīpramukhyāṇāṃ mantrāṇyaṣṭākṣarāṇi tu |
vaiṣṇavītantrasaṃsthāni pūrvaproktāni tāni tu || 104 ||
meaning:
शैलपुत्रीप्रमुख्याणां मन्त्राण्यष्टाक्षराणि तु |
वैष्णवीतन्त्रसंस्थानि पूर्वप्रोक्तानि तानि तु || 104 ||
text_mt:
the eight-syllabled mantras of those headed by Śailaputrī
found in the Vaiṣṇavītantra were previously proclaimed;

sanskrit_iast:
śailaputryāstathā cāṅgamantraṃ prāk pratipāditam |
rūpaṃ tu naraśārdūla yoginīnāṃ viśeṣataḥ || 105 ||
meaning:
शैलपुत्र्यास्तथा चाङ्गमन्त्रं प्राक् प्रतिपादितम् |
रूपं तु नरशार्दूल योगिनीनां विशेषतः || 105 ||
text_mt:
likewise, the ancillary mantra of Śailaputrī was explained before.
As for the form of the yoginīs especially, O tiger among men,

sanskrit_iast:
pratyakṣareṇa bījena durgātantreṇa vā tvimāḥ |
netrabījenaiva pūjyā yoginyo nṛpasattama || 106 ||
meaning:
प्रत्यक्षरेण बीजेन दुर्गातन्त्रेण वा त्विमाः |
नेत्रबीजेनैव पूज्या योगिन्यो नृपसत्तम || 106 ||
text_mt:
these yoginīs are to be worshipped with the single-lettered seed-syllable or through the Durgātantra,
with the eye-seed-syllable itself, O best of kings.

sanskrit_iast:
kātyāyanīṃ pādadurgāṃ durgātantreṇa pūjayet |
tadeva pūjanaṃ rūpaṃ tatpūrvaṃ pratipāditam || 107 ||
meaning:
कात्यायनीं पाददुर्गां दुर्गातन्त्रेण पूजयेत् |
तदेव पूजनं रूपं तत्पूर्वं प्रतिपादितम् || 107 ||
text_mt:
One should worship Kātyāyanī, the Pādadurgā, through the Durgātantra;
that very worship and form was set forth previously.

sanskrit_iast:
kālarātryāstu mantreṇa kālarātriṃ prapūjayet |
kālarātryā rūpamantrau puraiva pratipāditau || 108 ||
meaning:
कालरात्र्यास्तु मन्त्रेण कालरात्रिं प्रपूजयेत् |
कालरात्र्या रूपमन्त्रौ पुरैव प्रतिपादितौ || 108 ||
text_mt:
One should worship Kālarātri with the mantra of Kālarātri;
the form and mantra of Kālarātri were indeed explained before.

sanskrit_iast:
mahāmāyātantramantraiḥ pūjayed bhuvaneśvarīm |
etāḥ sarvāstu yoginyaḥ kāmākhyāvat phalapradāḥ || 109 ||
meaning:
महामायातन्त्रमन्त्रैः पूजयेद् भुवनेश्वरीम् |
एताः सर्वास्तु योगिन्यः कामाख्यावत् फलप्रदाः || 109 ||
text_mt:
One should worship Bhuvaneśvarī with the mantras of the Mahāmāyātantra.
All these yoginīs grant fruits just like Kāmākhyā.

sanskrit_iast:
viśeṣo yatra naivokto rūpe tantre ca pūjane |
durgātantreṇa mantreṇa tatra pūjāṃ samācaret || 110 ||
meaning:
विशेषो यत्र नैवोक्तो रूपे तन्त्रे च पूजने |
दुर्गातन्त्रेण मन्त्रेण तत्र पूजां समाचरेत् || 110 ||
text_mt:
Where no specific rule is stated regarding the form, tantra, and worship,
one should perform the worship there with the mantra from the Durgātantra.

sanskrit_iast:
pratyekaṃ yoginīṃ yastu pūjayennarasattamaḥ |
sa sarvayajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti narasattama || 111 ||
meaning:
प्रत्येकं योगिनीं यस्तु पूजयेन्नरसत्तमः |
स सर्वयज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोति नरसत्तम || 111 ||
text_mt: The best of men who worships each yoginī individually, / O best of men, attains the fruit of all sacrifices.

sanskrit_iast:
nīlaśailasya pūrvasmin svarūpaṃ pratipāditam |
nābhimaṇḍalapūrvasyāṃ bhasmakūṭasya dakṣiṇe || 112 ||
meaning:
नीलशैलस्य पूर्वस्मिन् स्वरूपं प्रतिपादितम् |
नाभिमण्डलपूर्वस्यां भस्मकूटस्य दक्षिणे || 112 ||
text_mt: The true nature of the Nīlaśaila has been declared to the east; / to the east of the Nābhimaṇḍala, to the south of Bhasmakūṭa,

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvasyāṃ karpaṭo nāma parvato yamarūpadhṛk |
tatra yāmyaśilā kṛṣṇā nīlāñjanasamaprabhā || 113 ||
meaning:
पूर्वस्यां कर्पटो नाम पर्वतो यमरूपधृक् |
तत्र याम्यशिला कृष्णा नीलाञ्जनसमप्रभा || 113 ||
text_mt: to the east, is a mountain named Karpaṭa, bearing the form of Yama. / There lies a black rock of Yama, having the lustre of blue collyrium,

sanskrit_iast:
adhityakāyāṃ rājendra vyāmapañcasuvistṛtā |
pūjayet tatra śamanaṃ pāṇau daṇḍaṃ sadaiva yaḥ || 114 ||
meaning:
अधित्यकायां राजेन्द्र व्यामपञ्चसुविस्तृता |
पूजयेत् तत्र शमनं पाणौ दण्डं सदैव यः || 114 ||
text_mt: on the plateau, O king of kings, extending over five fathoms. / There one should worship Śamana, who always holds a staff in his hand,

sanskrit_iast:
dhatte tu pāṇinā nityaṃ prāṇidaṇḍasya sādhanam |
kṛṣṇavarṇa tu dvibhujaṃ kirīṭamukuṭojjvalam || 115 ||
meaning:
धत्ते तु पाणिना नित्यं प्राणिदण्डस्य साधनम् |
कृष्णवर्ण तु द्विभुजं किरीटमुकुटोज्ज्वलम् || 115 ||
text_mt: who constantly holds with his hand the instrument for punishing living beings, / black in colour, two-armed, radiant with a diadem and crown,

sanskrit_iast:
dadhataṃ cāsiputrīṃ ca vāmapāṇau sadaiva hi |
kṛṣṇavastraṃ sthūlapādaṃ bahirniḥsṛtadantakam || 116 ||
meaning:
दधतं चासिपुत्रीं च वामपाणौ सदैव हि |
कृष्णवस्त्रं स्थूलपादं बहिर्निःसृतदन्तकम् || 116 ||
text_mt: and always bearing a knife in his left hand, / wearing black garments, thick-footed, with teeth protruding outward,

sanskrit_iast:
hayābhayapradaṃ nityaṃ nṛṇāṃ mahiṣavāhanam |
pūjayet parayā bhaktyā yāmyabījena sādhakaḥ || 117 ||
meaning:
हयाभयप्रदं नित्यं नृणां महिषवाहनम् |
पूजयेत् परया भक्त्या याम्यबीजेन साधकः || 117 ||
text_mt: always granting fearlessness to horses and men, having a buffalo as his mount. / The practitioner should worship him with supreme devotion using the bīja of Yama.

sanskrit_iast:
upāntavargasyādiryo varṇo bindvindusaṃyutaḥ |
yamabījamiti khyātaṃ yamasya prītidāyakam || 118 ||
meaning:
उपान्तवर्गस्यादिर्यो वर्णो बिन्द्विन्दुसंयुतः |
यमबीजमिति ख्यातं यमस्य प्रीतिदायकम् || 118 ||
text_mt: The first letter of the penultimate consonant class, joined with a crescent and dot, / is known as the Yama-bīja, which bestows delight upon Yama.

sanskrit_iast:
anenaiva tu mantreṇa śamanaṃ pūjayet tu yaḥ |
karpaṭākhye'calavare nāpamṛtyumavāpnuyāt || 119 ||
meaning:
अनेनैव तु मन्त्रेण शमनं पूजयेत् तु यः |
कर्पटाख्येऽचलवरे नापमृत्युमवाप्नुयात् || 119 ||
text_mt: Whoever worships Śamana with this very mantra / on the excellent mountain named Karpaṭa shall not meet with untimely death.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvasyāṃ karpaṭākhyāt tu śailāccitra iti smṛtaḥ |
yaḥ pūrvabhāgaprānte'bhūddiśyāgneyyāmavasthitaḥ || 120 ||
meaning:
पूर्वस्यां कर्पटाख्यात् तु शैलाच्चित्र इति स्मृतः |
यः पूर्वभागप्रान्तेऽभूद्दिश्याग्नेय्यामवस्थितः || 120 ||
text_mt: To the east of the mountain named Karpaṭa is the one called Citra, / which stood at the edge of the eastern quarter, situated in the south-east direction.

sanskrit_iast:
pīṭhastu brahmagrāvastu sa prāk parvata ucyate |
tasmin vasanti satataṃ grahā nava yathecchayā || 121 ||
meaning:
पीठस्तु ब्रह्मग्रावस्तु स प्राक् पर्वत उच्यते |
तस्मिन् वसन्ति सततं ग्रहा नव यथेच्छया || 121 ||
text_mt: The seat, indeed the stone of Brahmā, was previously called a mountain; / on it the nine planets always dwell at their pleasure.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra tān pūjayed yastu sa nāpnotyāpadaṃ kvacit |
rūpaṃ mantraṃ ca sūryasya candrasya pratipāditam || 122 ||
meaning:
तत्र तान् पूजयेद् यस्तु स नाप्नोत्यापदं क्वचित् |
रूपं मन्त्रं च सूर्यस्य चन्द्रस्य प्रतिपादितम् || 122 ||
text_mt: Whoever worships them there never encounters misfortune. / The form and mantra of the sun and the moon have [already] been declared;

sanskrit_iast:
saptānāmitareṣāṃ tu mantraṃ rūpaṃ śṛṇuṣva me |
raktāmbaradharaḥ śūlī śaktimāṃśca gadādharaḥ || 123 ||
meaning:
सप्तानामितरेषां तु मन्त्रं रूपं शृणुष्व मे |
रक्ताम्बरधरः शूली शक्तिमांश्च गदाधरः || 123 ||
text_mt: now hear from me the mantra and form of the other seven. / Wearing red garments, holding a trident, possessed of a lance, and bearing a mace,

sanskrit_iast:
caturbhujo meṣaratho varado maṅgalo mataḥ |
pītāmbaradharaḥ śūlī pītamālyānulepanaḥ || 124 ||
meaning:
चतुर्भुजो मेषरथो वरदो मङ्गलो मतः |
पीताम्बरधरः शूली पीतमाल्यानुलेपनः || 124 ||
text_mt: four-armed, having a ram as his chariot, bestowing boons—such is Maṅgala considered to be. / Wearing yellow garments, holding a trident, anointed with yellow garlands and unguents,

sanskrit_iast:
haḍgacarmagadāpāṇiḥ siṃhastho varado budhaḥ |
svarṇagauraḥ pītavāsāḥ svarṇaparyaṃkasaṃsthitaḥ || 125 ||
meaning:
हड्गचर्मगदापाणिः सिंहस्थो वरदो बुधः |
स्वर्णगौरः पीतवासाः स्वर्णपर्यंकसंस्थितः || 125 ||
text_mt: holding a sword, shield, and mace in his hands, mounted on a lion, boon-granting is Budha. / Pale gold [in complexion], clad in yellow garments, seated on a golden couch,

sanskrit_iast:
mālāṃ kamaṇḍaluṃ daṇḍaṃ vāmena varadāyakam |
caturbhujaṃ ca sarvajñaṃ cintayed devatīrthakam || 126 ||
meaning:
मालां कमण्डलुं दण्डं वामेन वरदायकम् |
चतुर्भुजं च सर्वज्ञं चिन्तयेद् देवतीर्थकम् || 126 ||
text_mt: holding a rosary, water-pot, and staff, bestowing boons with his left [hand], / four-armed and omniscient—one should meditate on the teacher of the gods,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvairdevagaṇairnityaṃ amyamānaṃ manoharam |
śuklavastraṃ śuklavarṇaṃ śaṅkhanāgoparisthitam || 127 ||
meaning:
सर्वैर्देवगणैर्नित्यं अम्यमानं मनोहरम् |
शुक्लवस्त्रं शुक्लवर्णं शङ्खनागोपरिस्थितम् || 127 ||
text_mt: who is constantly praised by all the hosts of gods, captivating. / Clad in white garments, white in colour, standing upon a conch and a serpent,

sanskrit_iast:
caturbhujaṃ pāśamālāṃ pustakaṃ ca varābhaye |
kramād dakṣiṇavāmāyāṃ dhatte daityaguruḥ sadā || 128 ||
meaning:
चतुर्भुजं पाशमालां पुस्तकं च वराभये |
क्रमाद् दक्षिणवामायां धत्ते दैत्यगुरुः सदा || 128 ||
text_mt: four-armed, holding a noose, a rosary, a book, and [displaying the gestures of] boon and fearlessness / in order in the right and left [hands]—[thus] the teacher of the Daityas always holds.

sanskrit_iast:
indranīlanibhaḥ śūlī varado gṛdhravāhanaḥ |
āśabāṇāsanadharo dhyātavyo'rkasutaḥ sadā || 129 ||
meaning:
इन्द्रनीलनिभः शूली वरदो गृध्रवाहनः |
आशबाणासनधरो ध्यातव्योऽर्कसुतः सदा || 129 ||
text_mt: Resembling a sapphire, holding a trident, bestowing boons, having a vulture for his mount, / bearing a bow and arrows—thus should the son of Arka always be meditated upon.

sanskrit_iast:
kāmadevasyabījaṃ tu mantraṃ bhaumasya kīrtitam |
durgāyā netrabījasya yattu madhyāvaraṃ śubham || 130 ||
meaning:
कामदेवस्यबीजं तु मन्त्रं भौमस्य कीर्तितम् |
दुर्गाया नेत्रबीजस्य यत्तु मध्यावरं शुभम् || 130 ||
text_mt: The bīja of Kāmadeva is celebrated as the mantra of Bhauma. / That which is the auspicious middle consonant of Durgā's eye-bīja,

sanskrit_iast:
tanmantraṃ śaśiputrasya sarvakāmaphalapradam |
aṃkārapañcamādistu catuḥṣaṭsvarasaṃyutam || 131 ||
meaning:
तन्मन्त्रं शशिपुत्रस्य सर्वकामफलप्रदम् |
अंकारपञ्चमादिस्तु चतुःषट्स्वरसंयुतम् || 131 ||
text_mt: that is the mantra of the son of the Moon, granting the fruits of all desires. / The first [consonant] of the fifth class from the letter a, joined with the fourth and sixth vowels,

sanskrit_iast:
gaṇeśabījāntamidaṃ gurormantra prakīrtitam |
bindvindusaṃyutaṃ cāpi pūrvavarṇadvayaṃ punaḥ || 132 ||
meaning:
गणेशबीजान्तमिदं गुरोर्मन्त्र प्रकीर्तितम् |
बिन्द्विन्दुसंयुतं चापि पूर्ववर्णद्वयं पुनः || 132 ||
text_mt: ending with the bīja of Gaṇeśa—this is celebrated as the mantra of Guru. / And the previous two letters joined with a dot and a crescent,

sanskrit_iast:
saptamasvarasaṃyukto makārastvādirantaram |
prāntavargādyakṣaraṃ tu bindvindubhyāṃ samanvitam || 133 ||
meaning:
सप्तमस्वरसंयुक्तो मकारस्त्वादिरन्तरम् |
प्रान्तवर्गाद्यक्षरं तु बिन्द्विन्दुभ्यां समन्वितम् || 133 ||
text_mt: the letter ma joined with the seventh vowel as the initial and intermediate, / and the first syllable of the final consonant class endowed with a crescent and a dot—

sanskrit_iast:
bhavecchukrasya bījaṃ tu sarvakāmasamṛddhidam |
prāntavargādyakṣaraṃ tu candrabindusamanvitam || 134 ||
meaning:
भवेच्छुक्रस्य बीजं तु सर्वकामसमृद्धिदम् |
प्रान्तवर्गाद्यक्षरं तु चन्द्रबिन्दुसमन्वितम् || 134 ||
text_mt: this shall be the bīja of Śukra, bestowing the prosperity of all desires. / The first letter of the final consonant class, joined with a crescent and a dot,

sanskrit_iast:
ādyamantrasvaropetaṃ tadevetyādisaṃyutam |
śanaiścarasya mantro'yaṃ sarvadoṣavināśanaḥ || 135 ||
meaning:
आद्यमन्त्रस्वरोपेतं तदेवेत्यादिसंयुतम् |
शनैश्चरस्य मन्त्रोऽयं सर्वदोषविनाशनः || 135 ||
text_mt: accompanied by the vowel of the first mantra, joined with the same and so forth— / this is the mantra of Śanaiścara, destroying all blemishes.

sanskrit_iast:
binducandrasamāyuktaṃ nāmādyakṣarameva vā |
teṣāṃ sarvagrahāṇāṃ vai mantramaṅga prakīrtitam || 136 ||
meaning:
बिन्दुचन्द्रसमायुक्तं नामाद्यक्षरमेव वा |
तेषां सर्वग्रहाणां वै मन्त्रमङ्ग प्रकीर्तितम् || 136 ||
text_mt: Or the first syllable of their names, joined with a dot and crescent— / [that] is proclaimed as the mantra-limb of all those planets, O dear one.

sanskrit_iast:
śāntike pauṣṭike kṛtye ebhirmantrairgrahānimān |
pūjayet sarvadā dhīro bhūtikāmo mahāmatiḥ || 137 ||
meaning:
शान्तिके पौष्टिके कृत्ये एभिर्मन्त्रैर्ग्रहानिमान् |
पूजयेत् सर्वदा धीरो भूतिकामो महामतिः || 137 ||
text_mt: In rites of pacification and nourishment, the steadfast one desiring prosperity, / of great intellect, should always worship these planets with these mantras.

sanskrit_iast:
varadābhayahastaśca khaḍgacarmadharastathā |
siṃhāsanagataḥ kṛṣṇā rāhurdhīraḥ pracakṣyate || 138 ||
meaning:
वरदाभयहस्तश्च खड्गचर्मधरस्तथा |
सिंहासनगतः कृष्णा राहुर्धीरः प्रचक्ष्यते || 138 ||
text_mt: With hands granting boons and fearlessness, holding a sword and shield, / seated on a throne, black, Rāhu is declared to be wise.

sanskrit_iast:
dhūmravarṇo viśālākṣaḥ puccharūpī caturbhujaḥ |
khaḍgacarmagadābāṇapāṇiḥ ketuḥ śavāsanaḥ || 139 ||
meaning:
धूम्रवर्णो विशालाक्षः पुच्छरूपी चतुर्भुजः |
खड्गचर्मगदाबाणपाणिः केतुः शवासनः || 139 ||
text_mt: Smoke-coloured, large-eyed, having the form of a tail, four-armed, / holding a sword, shield, mace, and arrow in his hands, Ketu is seated on a corpse.

sanskrit_iast:
upāntādirdvādaśena svareṇa sahitaḥ punaḥ |
upāntaḥ pañcamenendubindubhyāṃ sahitāvubhau || 140 ||
meaning:
उपान्तादिर्द्वादशेन स्वरेण सहितः पुनः |
उपान्तः पञ्चमेनेन्दुबिन्दुभ्यां सहितावुभौ || 140 ||
text_mt: The first of the penultimate [class] accompanied by the twelfth vowel; again / the penultimate [consonant] with the fifth [vowel], both accompanied by the crescent and dot—

sanskrit_iast:
mantro'yamanulomena rāhoḥ ketorvilomataḥ |
ādyakṣaraṃ pūrvavad vā mantrayuktamathaitayoḥ || 141 ||
meaning:
मन्त्रोऽयमनुलोमेन राहोः केतोर्विलोमतः |
आद्यक्षरं पूर्ववद् वा मन्त्रयुक्तमथैतयोः || 141 ||
text_mt: this mantra in direct order is of Rāhu, and in reverse order of Ketu; / or the first syllable of each, as before, joined with the mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ citre śailavare pūjayitvā navagrahān |
abhīṣṭāllaṁbhate kāmāntaraḥ śāntiṃ tathottamām || 142 ||
meaning:
एवं चित्रे शैलवरे पूजयित्वा नवग्रहान् |
अभीष्टाल्लṁभते कामान्तरः शान्तिं तथोत्तमाम् || 142 ||
text_mt: Having thus worshipped the nine planets on the excellent mountain Citra, / a person attains desired wishes and supreme peace.

sanskrit_iast:
citrakūṭāt tu pūrvasyāṃ kajjalācala uttamaḥ |
sarvavidyādharādyāstu santyasmin devayonayaḥ || 143 ||
meaning:
चित्रकूटात् तु पूर्वस्यां कज्जलाचल उत्तमः |
सर्वविद्याधराद्यास्तु सन्त्यस्मिन् देवयोनयः || 143 ||
text_mt: To the east of Citrakūṭa is the excellent Kajjalācala; / on this are all classes of demigods, beginning with Vidyādharas.

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ parvataṃ samāruhya praṇamya sakalān surān |
svargaṃ yānti naraśreṣṭha iha cāpyatulāṃ śriyam || 144 ||
meaning:
तं पर्वतं समारुह्य प्रणम्य सकलान् सुरान् |
स्वर्गं यान्ति नरश्रेष्ठ इह चाप्यतुलां श्रियम् || 144 ||
text_mt: Having ascended that mountain and bowed to all the gods, / the best of men go to heaven, and here [on earth] obtain matchless fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
kajjalācalaśailāt tu pūrvasmiñchubhaparvataḥ |
śacyā sārdhaṃ purā reme yatra sakraḥ sureśvaraḥ || 145 ||
meaning:
कज्जलाचलशैलात् तु पूर्वस्मिञ्छुभपर्वतः |
शच्या सार्धं पुरा रेमे यत्र सक्रः सुरेश्वरः || 145 ||
text_mt: To the east of Mount Kajjalācala is the auspicious mountain / where formerly Śakra, the lord of the gods, sported with Śacī.

sanskrit_iast:
tatpūrvasyāṃ mahādevī nadī kapilagaṅgikā |
tasyāṃ snātvā naro gaṅgāsnānajaṃ phalamāpnuyāt || 146 ||
meaning:
तत्पूर्वस्यां महादेवी नदी कपिलगङ्गिका |
तस्यां स्नात्वा नरो गङ्गास्नानजं फलमाप्नुयात् || 146 ||
text_mt: To the east of that is the great goddess, the river Kapilagaṅgikā; / bathing in it, a man attains the fruit born of bathing in the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit_iast:
kāmākhyānilayāt pūrvaṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ tathā diśi |
vidyate mahadāvartaṃ bhuvi brahmabilaṃ mahat || 147 ||
meaning:
कामाख्यानिलयात् पूर्वं दक्षिणस्यां तथा दिशि |
विद्यते महदावर्तं भुवि ब्रह्मबिलं महत् || 147 ||
text_mt: To the east and likewise in the south direction from the dwelling of Kāmākhyā, / there exists a great whirlpool on earth, the great Brahmabila,

sanskrit_iast:
paṃcaviṃśatimānena yojanānāṃ nareśvara |
tasmādāyāti sunadī sitāmbho'pama oyabhāk || 148 ||
meaning:
पंचविंशतिमानेन योजनानां नरेश्वर |
तस्मादायाति सुनदी सिताम्भोऽपम ओयभाक् || 148 ||
text_mt: measuring twenty-five yojanas, O ruler of men. / From it comes forth a noble river of white waters, possessed of swift current.

sanskrit_iast:
ko brahmā kīrtito devairyasmāt tasya bilāt sṛtā |
gaṃgeva phaladā yasmāt tasmāt kapilagaṃgikā || 149 ||
meaning:
को ब्रह्मा कीर्तितो देवैर्यस्मात् तस्य बिलात् सृता |
गंगेव फलदा यस्मात् तस्मात् कपिलगंगिका || 149 ||
text_mt: Brahmā is called 'Ka' by the gods; because it issued from his chasm, / and because it yields fruit like the Gaṅgā, it is therefore Kapilagaṅgikā.

sanskrit_iast:
snātvā kapilagaṅgāyāṃ sarvamanvantareṣu ca |
naraḥ svargamavāpyādau brahmaloka tato vrajet || 150 ||
meaning:
स्नात्वा कपिलगङ्गायां सर्वमन्वन्तरेषु च |
नरः स्वर्गमवाप्यादौ ब्रह्मलोक ततो व्रजेत् || 150 ||
text_mt: Bathing in the Kapilagaṅgā in all manvantaras, / a man, having first attained heaven, goes from there to the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit_iast:
atītya tāṃ nadīṃ pūrvabhāge damanikāhvayā |
nadī mahākṛṣṇatoyā pāpasya damanī tathā || 151 ||
meaning:
अतीत्य तां नदीं पूर्वभागे दमनिकाह्वया |
नदी महाकृष्णतोया पापस्य दमनी तथा || 151 ||
text_mt: Passing that river, in the eastern region is the one named Damanikā, / a river with very black water, which subdues sin.

sanskrit_iast:
tato vṛddhāhvayā cābhūdaparā sariduttamā |
tasyā nadyāḥ pūrvabhāge gaṅgāvat phaladāyinī || 152 ||
meaning:
ततो वृद्धाह्वया चाभूदपरा सरिदुत्तमा |
तस्या नद्याः पूर्वभागे गङ्गावत् फलदायिनी || 152 ||
text_mt: Beyond it was another excellent river called Vṛddhā / in the eastern region of that river, yielding fruit like the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit_iast:
māghaṃ tu sakalaṃ māsaṃ snātvā muktimavāpnuyāt |
tathā damanikāyāṃ ca paraṃ nirvāṇamāpnuyāt || 153 ||
meaning:
माघं तु सकलं मासं स्नात्वा मुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् |
तथा दमनिकायां च परं निर्वाणमाप्नुयात् || 153 ||
text_mt: Bathing [there] for the entire month of Māgha, one attains liberation; / and likewise in the Damanikā, one attains supreme nirvāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ pūrve parā devī nāmnā sā sariduttamā |
mahatī divyayamunā yamunāvat phalapradā || 154 ||
meaning:
ततः पूर्वे परा देवी नाम्ना सा सरिदुत्तमा |
महती दिव्ययमुना यमुनावत् फलप्रदा || 154 ||
text_mt: To the east of that is another goddess, that excellent river by name, / the great divine Yamunā, granting fruits like the Yamunā.

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣiṇādrisamudbhūtā dakṣiṇodadhigāminī |
tasyāṃ tu kārtikaṃ māsaṃ snātvā muktimavāpnuyāt || 155 ||
meaning:
दक्षिणाद्रिसमुद्भूता दक्षिणोदधिगामिनी |
तस्यां तु कार्तिकं मासं स्नात्वा मुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् || 155 ||
text_mt: Arising from the southern mountain, flowing to the southern ocean; / bathing in it for the month of Kārtika, one attains liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
iha caivottamān bhogān bhāgadheyān pratiṣṭhitān |
tanmadhye bhairavo devo bharga sambhogasambhavaḥ || 156 ||
meaning:
